A silent extension found later is a ROW (and its binder site); the drift tests refuse an accepted row nothing names. Verdict DIVERGES -> CONFORMS.

notes: §7.3.4 GR3 'The state of compiler directives may be saved and restored with PUSH and POP directives. A 'stack' is maintained that the state of a directive may be pushed on to. subject: Compile-time arithmetic expressions
notes: kb/Work PB1369 (registrar 15a). Rule: 'The implementor shall define and document any rules restricting the precision and/or magnitude and/or range of permissible values for the intermediate results ... They shall also document which intermediate rounding method is used, if applicable' (--check 7.3.6.2 -> OK §7.3.6.2 2)). Precision/magnitude half: documented (28-29 digits, ~7.9E28) and enforced loudly -- 99999999999999999999999999 * 99999 -> COBOLNET1547 'exceeds the .NET decimal evaluation range ... §7.3.6.2 SR2' (unit Rejects_OverRangeSoleLiteral covers the sole-literal leg). Rounding half: DOCUMENTED WRONG. CONFORMANCE.md says 'division truncates toward the decimal precision'; System.Decimal division rounds the final digit (round-half-even), so CONSTANT AS 2 / 3 * 3 = 2 and 100 / 7 * 7 = 100 where the documented truncation yields 1 and 99 (probe p1.cob). Also the magnitude limit applied to an over-range OPERAND inside an expression (ParseLiteral TryParse failure) is reported as an SR1b 'shall be fixed-point numeric literals' violation instead of the documented SR2 limit (probe n16.cob), so the limit is misattributed in the diagnostic. A rule with two halves, one verified and one contradicted by probe -> DIVERGES. || editions (adjudicator): 2023 (Annex E.2 6): intermediate-result handling 'is now explicitly implementor defined') || code-location detail: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Expressions/CompileTimeExpressionEvaluator.cs#EvalArith (OverflowException catch; '/' via System.Decimal); src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Expressions/CompileTimeExpressionEvaluator.cs#ParseLiteral; docs/CONFORMANCE.md (Compile-time arithmetic mode determination)

subject: Compile-time arithmetic expressions
notes: Rule: 'The order of precedence and the rules for evaluation of compile-time arithmetic expressions are shown in 8.8.1' (cite.py --check 7.3.6.3 -> OK §7.3.6.3 1)). Precedence is carried by the shared arithmeticExpression grammar spine (additive > multiplicative > power > unary > primary); EvalArith folds each additive/multiplicative level LEFT TO RIGHT (§8.8.1.2 3) --check OK). Intermediates are not truncated (only the final result, at EvaluateArithmeticOperand). Probed with the pinned cobol.exe (probe/ctae/p1.cob, p2.cob, --std 2002/2014/2023): CONSTANT AS 2 + 3 * 4 = 14; 10 - 3 - 2 = 5; 12 / 2 * 3 = 18; (1 + 2) * 3 = 9; - 2 * - 3 = 6; 5 - 10 / 4 = 2 (2.5 untruncated intermediate); 7 / 2 + 0.5 = 4 (3.5 + 0.5, intermediate not truncated); >>IF 10 - 3 - 2 = 5 AND 12 / 2 * 3 = 18 selects; identical across editions. The unit Theory pins 2+3*4=14 and (2+3)*4-6/2=17 (spec-derived); the same-level left-to-right case has no test (probe only). || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (compile-time arithmetic in DEFINE/EVALUATE/IF directives and constant entries; not 1985)

subject: Compile-time arithmetic expressions
notes: kb/Work PB1369 (registrar 15a). Rule: 'The implementor shall define and document which mode of arithmetic is to be used when evaluating compile-time arithmetic' (--check 7.3.6.3 -> OK §7.3.6.3 2)). The code uses .NET System.Decimal (a mode 'unique for processing compile-time arithmetic expressions', which GR2 permits). The documentation exists (docs/CONFORMANCE.md) but is INACCURATE in three ways: (1) it calls the mode 'a standard fixed-point decimal mode ... chosen over the native binary runtime mode for portability (§7.3.6.3 GR2 NOTE)' -- the NOTE's 'standard modes of arithmetic' are standard-binary / standard-decimal (§8.8.1.5.3 --check OK: standard-decimal operations 'are performed as specified in ISO/IEC 60559:2020', decimal128, 34 digits); System.Decimal (96-bit, 28-29 digits, its own rounding) is neither, so the portability claim is false; (2) it states 'division truncates toward the decimal precision', but System.Decimal division ROUNDS the last digit: probe p1.cob CONSTANT AS 2 / 3 * 3 -> 2 and 100 / 7 * 7 -> 100 (truncating division as documented gives 1 and 99), same for >>DEFINE V3 AS 2 / 3 * 3 (>>IF V3 = 2 selects); (3) it names the evaluator 'DataBinder.Constants.cs EvalConstExpr' (no longer exists; the evaluator is CompileTimeExpressionEvaluator) and says 'today a multi-token directive operand binds only its first token -- a recorded Wave-D GAP', which is false (probe p2.cob: >>DEFINE V1 AS 7 / 2 evaluates to 3). A required documentation statement that does not describe the implemented mode does not satisfy 'define and document'. Separate edition note: E.2 6) says the previous standard required a specific mode; the compiler evaluates identically at --std 2014 (probe p2 at 2002/2014/2023), and VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE row 12 carries that gate as <!-- todo --> -- not this row's verdict, recorded as a dossier gap. || editions (adjudicator): 2023 (Annex E.2 6): the mode 'is now explicitly implementor defined'; earlier editions required a specific mode) || code-location detail: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Expressions/CompileTimeExpressionEvaluator.cs#EvalArith; docs/CONFORMANCE.md (Compile-time arithmetic mode determination)

subject: Compile-time arithmetic expressions
notes: Rule: 'The final result of the arithmetic expression shall be truncated to the integer part of the value as specified in 15.49, INTEGER-PART function, and the resultant value shall be considered to be an integer numeric literal' (--check 7.3.6.3 -> OK §7.3.6.3 3)). EvaluateArithmeticOperand applies decimal.Truncate (toward zero = INTEGER-PART) to an expression's final result only, and emits the integer text as the literal; a SINGLE numeric literal is reclassified (§13.10.3 SR1 / §7.3.11.4 GR5) and keeps its value. Probes: CONSTANT AS 7 / 2 -> 3, -7 / 2 -> -3 (toward zero, not floor), 1.5 + 1 -> 2, 0.9 + 0 -> 0; >>DEFINE V2 AS -7 / 2 then >>IF V2 = -3 selects; >>DEFINE V4 AS 1.5 keeps 1.5 (literal) while >>IF V4 + 0 = 1 selects; >>EVALUATE 9 / 4 >>WHEN 2 selects. Binder stores isInt from the integer text so the constant is an integer literal. Unit Theory pins '7 / 2' -> '3' (GR3, spec-derived); the negative toward-zero edge is probe-only.

subject: Compile-time boolean expressions
notes: kb/Work PB1370 landed (wave 66 h). Rule (cite.py --check 7.3.7.2 'Compile-time boolean expressions shall be formed in accordance with 8.8.2, Boolean expressions' -> OK §7.3.7.2 1)). The three divergences the adjudication measured are closed in the ONE model both lanes share: (a) a parenthesized boolean literal with no operator - §8.8.2 'a boolean expression enclosed in parentheses' (--check OK) - is recognized by boolExprAhead/boolArgAhead (ParenRunOpensOnBoolLiteral: a grouping-paren run opening on a BOOLLIT can only be boolean), so >>DEFINE X AS (B"101"), >>IF (B"1") = B"1" and >>EVALUATE (B"1") evaluate, and so do the runtime siblings IF (B"1") = F / IF F = (B"1") / INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN((B"1010")); (b) the shift count is held to Table 4's single identifier-or-literal by the shared ArithmeticFormationRules screen (rule 5 --check OK; rule 6 --check OK) and to an INTEGER literal by form (§5.5 2) a) --check OK; §8.3.3.3.2 'An integer literal is a fixed-point numeric literal that contains no decimal point' --check OK) - 1 + 1, 2 * 1, (1), - 1, 1.0, and a variable holding 1.5 are COBOLNET1619; (c) the directive stage asks the ONE BooleanOperatorGate (shared with VersionConformancePass), so a B-SHIFT-* in >>DEFINE / >>IF at 2002/2014 is COBOLNET0900 like its runtime twin (§E.2 3) --check OK); BooleanExpressionGateSiteDriftTests now requires both fragment sites to be gated instead of exempting them.

subject: Compile-time boolean expressions
notes: kb/Work PB1370 landed (wave 66 h). The refuted half is fixed in the ONE shared resolver: §8.8.2 7) b) 'The precedence of boolean shift operations ... is the same as that of the preceding operation, if any' (--check OK) and the ladder's '1st - negation (B-NOT)' (--check OK) make a B-NOT the preceding operation of a following shift, so A B-AND B-NOT B B-SHIFT-R 1 = A B-AND ((B-NOT B) B-SHIFT-R 1): 1010 B-AND B-NOT 0011 B-SHIFT-R 1 = 0010 (was 0100), in the compile-time fold AND the runtime COMPUTE (same resolver). The full ladder B-NOT > B-AND > B-XOR > B-OR is now pinned: B-NOT 1100 B-OR 0101 B-XOR 0110 B-AND 0011 = 0111 (both lanes). Combine/Not/Shift semantics unchanged (verified by the adjudicator).

notes: kb/Work PB1376 (w1012k). cite.py --check 7.3.14.4 'The implementor shall provide a warning mechanism that flags the incompatibilities potentially affecting existing programs' OK (GR1). The mechanism is the parse-tree pass FlagConformancePass emitting COBOLNET1620 (Warning) per flagged construct, documented in docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md and docs/CONFORMANCE.md A.1 item 79. Every option's warning is located: the walk-time detectors by the walk cursor, and the one directive-keyed detector (b, a >>TURN known only by its line) through FlagAtLine, which positions the diagnostic at the directive's own line. subject: FLAG-02 directive
notes: kb/Work PB1376 (w1012k). cite.py --check 7.3.14.4 'ALL: All of the options apply' OK (GR4 a, sub-item path mispathed by cite.py, kb/Work PB718). a) ALL fans out to every FLAG-02 option at fold time. b) head: the TURN-name set is exactly EC-ALL, EC-PROGRAM, EC-PROGRAM-ARG-OMITTED, EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND (EcProgramFamily); any TURN naming one, ON or OFF, is a candidate, and EACH is flagged at its own line: two qualifying directives in one source element are two located warnings (EcProgram_EachQualifyingTurnIsFlaggedAtItsOwnLine). A TURN written before an element's IDENTIFICATION DIVISION belongs to the element that follows it (SourceElementOf; 7.3.25.4 GR6). The b CONDITION (calls a function / invokes a method) is adjudicated on GR-7.3.14.4-L2.1 / -L2.2.

subject: FLAG-02 directive
notes: kb/Work PB1375 (w1012k). cite.py --check 7.3.14.4 'the source element calls any function, or' OK (GR4 b 1); 12.3.8.4 GR13 'intrinsic-function-name-1 may be specified as a function-identifier without being preceded by the keyword FUNCTION'. A source element is a source unit excluding its contained source units (3.164): the pass opens one per program, function, contained program, class, interface and method. A call is a FunctionCall node, a keyword-omitted function-identifier (the binder records its decision in DataBinder.ActivationSites at IntrinsicBinder.KeywordOmittedFunction, so the pass reads the bound fact instead of re-deriving it from syntax), or a function written inside a subscript (ReferenceResolver.IsFunctionBearing records its head token). A call inside a method now flags that method's TURN.

subject: FLAG-02 directive
notes: kb/Work PB1375 (w1012k). Row carries three halves. (1) GR4 b 2: cite.py --check 7.3.14.4 'the source element invokes any method' OK. INVOKE, an inline method invocation and an object-property reference (8.4.3.9.4 GR1: the occurrence invokes the get/set accessor; recorded by ReferenceResolver.OoTryBindPropertyReference in DataBinder.ActivationSites) mark the CURRENT source element, and a METHOD definition is a source element of its own (VisitMethodDefinition), so a TURN in a method that invokes is flagged and a TURN in a sibling method that invokes nothing is not. A contained program is its own element too: its calls do not count for its container. (2) GR4 c I-O-STATUS-07: CLOSE with WITH NO REWIND or UNIT (REEL equivalent per 14.9.6.3 SR2) flagged once. (3) GR4 d head: same-DDE test by symbol identity across plain and CORRESPONDING MOVE, resolved in the CONTAINED program's own scope (the unit map is keyed on the IDENTIFICATION DIVISION node a contained program shares with its synthetic programUnit).

subject: FLAG-02 directive
notes: kb/Work PB1375 (w1012k). cite.py --check 7.3.14.4 'the operands are of category alphanumeric-edited, or' OK (GR4 d 1); 8.4.3.3.4 GR6 a 'the category alphanumeric-edited is considered class and category alphanumeric'. An alphanumeric-edited self-move is flagged; a plain alphanumeric one is not; a reference-modified operand is category alphanumeric (IsRefModified, covering a refModPart, a captured depth-0-colon group and the qualified form), so it does not meet criterion 1. National-edited is deliberately excluded (the flag is narrower than 14.9.25.4 GR6 b by the printed text).

subject: FLAG-14 directive
notes: kb/Work PB1375 (w1012k). All twelve options (a-m) flag their GR4 population. (b) the CONSTANT entry's arithmetic-expression-1 is a compile-time arithmetic expression (7.3.6.1; 13.10.3 SR7) and is flagged through FlagOptions.IsFlaggableCompileTimeArithmetic, the one predicate the directive operands use. (e/f) every condition that tests the FILE STATUS item: a relation, an abbreviated combined relation (8.8.4.12.4 GR1), a level-88 condition-name, an EVALUATE subject/object pair and partial expression (14.9.13.3 SR2/SR8). (g/j/l) 13.18.8.4 GR2: BLANK WHEN ZERO on a numeric picture makes the item numeric-edited, and the unit's CURRENCY SIGN set reaches the analyzer. (m) 14.9.51.3 SR19 names END-OF-PAGE and NOT END-OF-PAGE separately, so a WRITE with only NOT AT END-OF-PAGE is flagged. (i) a function result's reference modification is not a data item's. Known advisory edge: an OO method body's operands are not name-resolved.

subject: LEAP-SECOND directive
notes: kb/Work PB1379 landed. subject: PAGE directive
notes: Rule: 'Comment-text-1 may contain any character in the compile-time computer's coded character set except for control characters as specified in Clause 6, Reference format, rule 3b.' (cite.py --check 7.3.19.3 -> OK §7.3.19.3 1)); §6.1 3b 'The implementor shall specify any control characters that terminate a free-form line...' (cite.py --check 6.1 -> OK §6.1 b)). Permission half verified by probe out/probe/page-directive/p2.cob (free form): comment-text with TAB, Latin-1 letters, CJK, the ASCII punctuation set incl. backslash and < >, and a FORM FEED is accepted and the program runs (OK). Exclusion half: the excluded characters are the ones that TERMINATE a line, and the preprocessor splits lines at CR/LF, so a terminating control character cannot lie inside comment-text-1 by construction — nothing further to diagnose. Side note (not this row's defect): docs/CONFORMANCE.md has no §6.1 rule 3b determination naming the line-terminating control characters (the only control-character determination is A.1-115, line sequential files); that obligation belongs to the §6.1 row. No golden puts non-ASCII or control characters in >>PAGE text, so test-ref is empty. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the §7.3 directive facility is post-85; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change to §7.3.19; COBOL-85 has no >> lines — derived edge, VCR Table 7 row 7.21)

subject: Character sets
notes: kb/Work PB547 (registrar 15b). Rule: "The number of bytes used in the memory of the computer to represent characters in the alphanumeric coded character set shall be the same for all characters in that coded character set; the number of bytes shall be determined at compile time." (cite.py --check 8.1.2 -> OK §8.1.2 1)). The byte count IS fixed at compile time (PicInfo.ByteWidth = 1 per DISPLAY position, DOC-A.1-209), but the SET it applies to is not bounded by it: the compiler admits any UTF-16 code unit into an alphanumeric item (DOC-A.1-33/188 declare the alphanumeric repertoire UTF-16) while every byte image carries one byte per position, so a character above U+00FF has no representation of that size. Three different losses measured at the pinned compiler: (a) mixed-usage REDEFINES codec - probe cs1/p2.cob: MOVE "€ABC" TO A1 (PIC X(4)), round trip through a REDEFINES PIC N(2) view, A1 reads back "¬ABC" and compares DIFF; p1.cob shows N1 decoded as U+AC41 U+4243 - CobolBits.NatReadWindow computes (char)((image[hi] << 8) | ...) which drops the code unit's high byte (U+20AC -> 0xAC) silently; (b) the sequential file channel substitutes '?' silently (open kb/Work PB690, PB547); (c) CONVERT ANUM->BYTE substitutes '?' and raises EC-DATA-CONVERSION (the documented disposition). One alphanumeric character, three byte images - the set is not represented in a uniform number of bytes. The file/'?' arm is owned by open kb/Work PB547 (analysis, inventory_rows GR-13.18.60.4-7) and PB690; the REDEFINES low-byte-truncation arm is new (see finding). Expected per spec: either the alphanumeric coded character set is restricted to what one byte represents (a character above U+00FF refused/diagnosed where it enters an alphanumeric item) or the alphanumeric size is widened so every member survives every storage image unchanged. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the alphanumeric/national coded-character-set split and these fixed-size rules arrive with ISO/IEC 1989:2002; 1985 has no national class)

subject: Character sets
notes: Rule: "The number of bytes used in the memory of the computer to represent characters in the national coded character set shall be the same for all characters in that coded character set; the number of bytes shall be determined at compile time." (cite.py --check 8.1.2 -> OK §8.1.2 2)). National = one UTF-16 code unit per position, BytesPerNational = 2 (a compile-time const, D-N1); every code unit U+0000-U+FFFF has a total 2-byte UTF-16BE image (PutNat/NatReadWindow are exact inverses for national content). NOTE 3 ("COBOL processes each fixed-size element of a character set as one character", --check OK) edge probed - cs1/p3.cob: LENGTH(N"😀€")=3 BYTE-LENGTH=6 (the surrogate pair is two positions), PIC N(4) BYTE-LENGTH 8; N"€A" in a PIC N(2) redefined as X(4) reads bytes 0x20 0xAC 0x00 0x41 (ORD 33 173 1 66) - uniform, lossless. No spec-derived test pins this rule; test-needed. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (national class introduced in ISO/IEC 1989:2002)

subject: Character sets
notes: kb/Work PB1397 (registrar 15b). Rule sentence 1: "The number of bytes used to represent a character of the national coded character set shall be equal to or greater than the number of bytes used to represent a character of the alphanumeric coded character set." (cite.py --check 8.1.2 -> OK §8.1.2 3)). National 2 >= alphanumeric 1 - holds; pinned by the golden l1_usage_display_character_size (LEQN line compares BYTE-LENGTH of X(1) and N(1)). The row text also carries the trailing implementor obligations: (i) hex literals not converted - probe cs1/p3.cob MOVE X"C1FF" gives ORD 194/256, raw bytes; compile-time = runtime set (UTF-16) so no literal conversion arises (A.1 item 34 conditional, not triggered) - OK; (ii) single SPACE/ZERO values - ' ' and '0' are the one value throughout, OK by reading; (iii) bits per byte (A.1 item 12) = 8, documented only in prose inside the USAGE BIT determination and BitLayout.cs, no DOC-A.1-12 row; (iv) "The implementor shall specify one and only one alphanumeric coded character value associated with each of the following COBOL elements" (--check OK) - A.1 item 32, required + documented - NOT documented anywhere in docs/ (no coded-character-value statement for SPACE/QUOTE/ZERO/editing characters, alphanumeric or national); (v) "the implementor shall specify any such additional characters that are prohibited from use as a currency symbol" (--check OK) - A.1 item 44, required + documented - ValidateCurrencyChar enforces only the §12.3.7.3 SR22/SR27 set (so the implementor-additional set is empty), and that choice is documented nowhere. Documentation halves (iv)/(v) missing => PARTIAL. The premise 'the alphanumeric character is 1 byte' is itself undermined by GR-8.1.2-1's divergence (PB547).

subject: COBOL character repertoire
notes: kb/Work PB1397 (registrar 15b). Rule: 'The implementor shall define a mapping of each basic letter, basic digit, basic special character, and extended letter of the COBOL character repertoire to one or more coded character sets.' (cite.py --check 8.1.3.2 -> OK 8.1.3.2 1)). What the code does: every source and copybook file is read by CompilationInputs.ReadAllText = File.ReadAllText(path) -- .NET BOM detection (UTF-8/UTF-16/UTF-32), defaulting to UTF-8, decoded into the one UTF-16 in-memory set (the D-N1 substrate). The mapping realized is 'one coded character set containing all characters' (ISO/IEC 10646), so the two-distinct-sets correspondence sentence is vacuous. HALF 1 (a mapping exists) holds for basic letters/digits/special characters. HALF 2 fails twice: (a) the mapping is DEFINED only in code -- docs/CONFORMANCE.md has no row for A.1 item 25 ('COBOL character repertoire (encoding of, mapping of, substitute graphics). This item is required. This item shall be documented', cite.py --check A.1 -> OK A.1 25)); grep of CONFORMANCE.md for source encoding / UTF-8 source / BOM finds nothing (DOC-A.1-25 is the separate catalog row carrying that documentation debt); (b) the rule names EXTENDED LETTERS in the mapping, and the lexer NAME_BODY admits only [a-z0-9_-], so no extended letter maps to a word character (see GR-8.1.3.2-4). Probe out/probe/repertoire/rlat1.cob: a Latin-1 byte 0xE9 inside a literal compiles clean and DISPLAYs EF BF BD (U+FFFD) -- the undocumented UTF-8 default silently replaces a non-UTF-8 byte, exactly what an A.1 item 25 determination must tell the user. No spec-derived test pins the mapping. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (Annex E lists no substantive change to 8.1.3.2 itself; E.2 items 4 and 14 change only the Annex B and Annex C tables 2014->2023)

subject: COBOL character repertoire
notes: kb/Work PB1397 (registrar 15b). Rule: 'If more than one encoding is permitted in a single compilation group, the implementor shall specify the control functions or other methods used for distinguishing between encodings.' (cite.py --check 8.1.3.2 -> OK 8.1.3.2 2)). Sentence 1 (mixed alphanumeric/national coded character sets) is VACUOUS: the repertoire maps to one set (UTF-16 in memory), so there is no shift mechanism to specify -- verified by reading ReadAllText. Sentence 2 IS live: each file (the source, and each copybook via CopyProcessor ~line 430 calling _inputs.ReadAllText independently) is decoded by its own BOM, so more than one encoding is permitted in one compilation group. Probe out/probe/repertoire/rmix.cob (UTF-8, no BOM) COPYing RCPY.cpy written UTF-16LE with BOM: compiles and runs, DISPLAY prints the e-acute correctly. The distinguishing method (per-file byte-order mark; absent a BOM, UTF-8) is nowhere specified in docs/CONFORMANCE.md (A.1 item 26, conditionally required on exactly this support). Sentence 3 (control functions are not part of the syntax) holds: the BOM is consumed by the decoder before the lexer. Mechanism present, specification absent -> PARTIAL. Same documentation mechanism as GR-8.1.3.2-1. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (no Annex E change)

subject: COBOL character repertoire

subject: COBOL character repertoire
notes: kb/Work PB1402: a) every Annex B character is in the UTF-16 compile-time set, so all are extended letters, admitted by the lexer's EXT_CHAR and screened per edition against Annex B.3 (2002/2014 = the 2023 annex with E.2 item 4 and E.3.3 items 4/5 reversed); b) uppercase extended letters fold by Annex C (CobolNames); c) the word length counts code points, so a combining character counts separately.

subject: COBOL character repertoire
notes: Rule: 'When an implementation does not provide a graphic representation of all characters of the COBOL character repertoire, substitute graphics may be specified by the implementor to replace the characters not represented.' (cite.py --check 8.1.3.2 -> OK 8.1.3.2 5)). A permission conditioned on a missing graphic. The source is decoded to UTF-16, which represents every Table 1 basic letter, digit and special character (all in ISO/IEC 646 IRV) and every Annex B character, so the antecedent is false and no substitute graphic is used or needed -- verified by reading ReadAllText and by the probes (rcase/rcase2 exercise the basic set incl. hyphen, quote, parentheses, period). No latitude exercised. Documenting 'substitute graphics: none' belongs to A.1 item 25 = DOC-A.1-25, the same missing CONFORMANCE.md row noted on GR-8.1.3.2-1; it does not make this permissive rule defective. CONFORMS-but-untested. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (no Annex E change)

subject: COBOL words
notes: kb/Work PB301. The prohibition is on ACCEPTING: a word ISO 8.9 reserves at edition E is refused in a user-defined-word slot AND in a system-name slot at E, and admitted at the editions 8.9 leaves it free. The gate is DERIVED, not listed - gen-cobol-words.ps1 computes it from reserved-words.json and CobolWordsDriftTests re-computes it independently, asserting set equality in BOTH directions and across BOTH halves (cobolWord under {userWordHere(W)}? and reservedGatedWord under its inverse), so neither a missing nor a stray gate survives. subject: Numeric literals
notes: "A literal shall contain at least one digit." (cite.py --check 8.3.3.3.2 -> OK §8.3.3.3.2 1)). Enforced by construction in the lexer: INT_BODY is [0-9]+, DEC_BODY is [0-9]+ '.' [0-9]+ | '.' [0-9]+, SIGNED_*LIT are [+-] followed by those bodies, and numericLiteralCore's comma alternatives (INTEGERLIT COMMA INTEGERLIT | COMMA INTEGERLIT) each carry an INTEGERLIT. No token or parser alternative forms a numeric literal from a bare sign or a bare decimal point, so a digitless 'literal' can only be a parse error. Structural rule; no probe needed beyond confirming the fragments. No dedicated negative golden -> test-ref empty. [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the formation/value rules are unchanged across editions; only the digit ceiling moves: 18 at COBOL-85, 1 through 31 from 2002 per the clause's lead paragraph)]

subject: Numeric literals
notes: kb/Work PB1445: ONE contiguity test (ArithmeticFormationRules.SignAbuts, on the tokens' stream indices, never GetText) answers rule 2 everywhere. subject: Numeric literals
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB99), RANGE DETERMINATION REPLACED 2026-08-31 by owner decision D-B (kb/Work PB156 + PB195 + PB276). 'a maximum of four digits' - COBOLNET1661 for a fifth (1.0E12345, which used to reach Roslyn as an overflowing C# double literal, CS0594). The IMPLEMENTOR-DEFINED maximum / minimum exponent VALUE is documented in CONFORMANCE.md Sec.7 A.1 item 82 and enforced at compile time, and it is now ONE range for every statement position: the DECIMAL128 range, about 1E-6176 to 9.99E+6144, in EVERY arithmetic mode (ExpressionBinder.CheckLiteral) - so 1.0E+400 evaluates and 1.0E+9999 / 1.0E-9999 are COBOLNET1661. ⛔ THE PER-POSITION SPLIT THIS REPLACED is what the previous note published: a literal in a NATIVE arithmetic expression or statement was screened against binary64 (about 4.9E-324..1.8E+308, so 1.0E+400 was rejected) while the identical program compiled under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL. Two rules remain, and they are different rules rather than different positions: a VALUE clause on a FLOAT-* item keeps the RECEIVER's binary form (Sec.13.18.63.3 SR2 - 'permissible values within the range indicated by the PICTURE clause or the USAGE clause', and a FLOAT-* subject has no PICTURE; DataBinder.FitsBinaryFloat, which is that screen's only surviving caller), and a VALUE on a fixed-point or floating-point numeric-edited item has no bound beyond the receiver's PICTURE (PIC 9E+9999 VALUE 1.0E+9999). The two lanes are witnessed SEPARATELY: pb99-floating-literal-range carries only the VALUE-clause entries and pb99-floating-literal-range-statement only the statement ones, because the negative harness asserts that SOME diagnostic contains COBOLNET1661 and a shared file let the VALUE entries satisfy it alone.

subject: Numeric literals
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB99), COMPLETED 2026-08-31 by owner decision D-B (kb/Work PB156 + PB195), and CORRECTED 2026-09-02 (kb/Work PB263 + PB264). D-B's claim recorded here was that the literal's value - significand x 10^exponent - is carried EXACTLY in EVERY position through ONE rendering, NumericRenderer.LiteralNum. THAT CLAIM WAS NOT TRUE OF TWO POSITIONS WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN, and this row's five goldens were all VALUE-clause or arithmetic-operand positions, so none of them could have contradicted it. The CALL argument lane and the INVOKE argument lane do not reach LiteralNum at all: they render operand text through the raw EmitText.UnscaledLit helper, which returned the literal's own source text as a binary64 Real NumX for the E-form. The generated C# then handed a double to ManagedPointer<long|Int128>.Cell(...) and did not compile - conforming source rejected by a raw Roslyn CS1503 with no COBOL diagnostic at all (measured both carrier arms). UnscaledLit now honours its own scaled-integer contract for BOTH notations via TryUnscaledParts, taking the (significand, power of ten) pair exactly and never expanding it to text; the CALL lane funnels both of its non-place arms through one carrier build, and the two new goldens pin the four-cell table (two notations x BY CONTENT / BY VALUE, all four displaying the same value) plus the INVOKE arm. The evidence set now covers the argument positions the word EVERY always claimed.

subject: National literals
notes: cite.py --check 8.3.3.5.3 "any character in the national coded character set that the implementor has designated for source code representation" -> OK (rule 2). STR_BODY admits every character except the delimiter and CR/LF; source text is read as UTF-8 so both dashes hold: an ASCII (alphanumeric-set) character and a character outside Latin-1 are each stored as one national (UTF-16) position. Probe p1: N"\u00e9\u6f22" MOVE/DISPLAY exact, LENGTH(N"\u00e9x")=2. The character set designation itself is Annex A.1 item 31 (documentation owned by that DOC row). [editions as adjudicated: COBOL-2002, COBOL-2014, COBOL-2023 (national literals are a COBOL-2002 introduction; absent from COBOL-85, where the construct is rejected COBOLNET0900 via Constructs.NationalData2002)]

subject: National literals
notes: cite.py --check 8.3.3.5.3 "Two contiguous quotation symbol characters matching the quotation symbol used in the opening delimiter" -> OK (rule 3). STR_BODY lexes '""' inside a quote-delimited body and '\'\'' inside an apostrophe-delimited one; Decode collapses the doubled OPENING delimiter only. Probe p1: N"A""B" -> A"B (LENGTH 3), N'A''B' LENGTH 3, VALUE N'a''b' -> a'b, and the non-matching quote N'A"B' is ordinary content (LENGTH 3). Second sentence (same coded character set representation as the opening quote): only the basic quotation mark/apostrophe are delimiters, so a doubled pair is necessarily in the opening delimiter's representation; a full-width quote is plain content. No spec-derived test pins the doubled delimiter inside N".." - test-needed. [editions as adjudicated: COBOL-2002, COBOL-2014, COBOL-2023 (national literals are a COBOL-2002 introduction; absent from COBOL-85, where the construct is rejected COBOLNET0900 via Constructs.NationalData2002)]

notes: cite.py --check 8.3.3.5.4 "If character-1 is not specified, the literal is a zero-length literal" -> OK (rule 3). subject: National literals
notes: kb/Work PB160 (registrar 15c). cite.py --check 8.3.3.5.4 "The implementor defines the result of specifying a hex-character-sequence-1 for which no corresponding character" -> OK (rule 5). Behaviour exists: DecodeHexGroups stores any 4-digit group verbatim as a UTF-16 code unit, so a group with no corresponding character (an unpaired surrogate, probe p1 LENGTH(NX"D800")=1) yields that code unit unchanged, no diagnostic, no exception. Half 2 (characters not a multiple of four bits) is vacuous: a UTF-16 unit is 16 bits. BUT the determination is undocumented: Annex A.1 item 97 (cite.py --check A.1 "Hexadecimal national literals (mapping for non-existing corresponding character)" -> OK - required, documented) and item 122 (digits per national character, SR5) have no DOC-A.1-97 / DOC-A.1-122 row in docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 (grep: absent). notes: Rule: 'The quote format represents one or more of the quotation mark character ' " ' in the computer's runtime coded character set. The word QUOTE or QUOTES shall not be used in place of a quotation symbol to bound a literal.' (cite.py --check 8.3.3.6.4 -> OK 8)). Second half: the lexer recognizes literal delimiters only as quotation symbols (§8.3.5 SR5); QUOTE is a figurative token (KindOf) with no delimiter role anywhere in the grammar, so it cannot bound a literal. No spec-derived test isolates the quote character; test-needed.

subject: Lexical elements
Lexical elements
notes: Rule 2 (cite.py --check 8.3.5 "The COBOL characters comma and semicolon, immediately followed by a space, are separators" OK 2)). kb/Work PB1394 LANDED (wave 73 group A): SeparatorRule, run post-lex over every token of the unit (all channels) from the source characters, reports a comma or semicolon not immediately followed by a space as COBOLNET2631 - DEFAULT-mode COMMA, SUBSCRIPT-mode SUB_COMMA / SUB_SEMICOLON, and the lone ';' that the lexer now keeps on the HIDDEN channel instead of skipping. The one space-less comma it leaves alone is a numeric literal's decimal point under DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA (a digit after it and a digit, sign, '(' or space before it - 12.3.7.4 GR14 a)), which the numeric-literal rules own. Negative: MOVE 1 TO N,M / N;M -> COBOLNET2631 at all four editions (they used to compile as two receivers and print 001001); positive: MOVE 1 TO N, M and N; M.

subject: Lexical elements
notes: Rule 3 (cite.py --check 8.3.5 "The COBOL character period, when followed by a space, is a separator" OK 3)). kb/Work PB1394 LANDED (wave 73 group A): SeparatorRule reports a DOT token not followed by a space (or the end of the text) as COBOLNET2632. A period inside a numeric literal or a PICTURE character-string is part of that token (DECIMALLIT / PIC_STRING), never DOT. Negative: DISPLAY N.DISPLAY M -> COBOLNET2632 at all four editions (it used to compile and print 005 and 007).

subject: Lexical elements
notes: Rule: 'Except when appearing in a picture character-string, the COBOL characters right parenthesis and left parenthesis are separators. Except in pseudo-text, parentheses may appear only in balanced pairs ... delimiting subscripts, a list of function or method arguments, a reference modifier, arithmetic or boolean expressions, or conditions.' (cite.py --check 8.3.5 OK §8.3.5 4)). Picture exception: PICMODE captures `X(5)`/`9(3)` as one PIC_STRING. Balance/position enforced by the parser: probes probe/lexical-elements/unbalparen.cob `COMPUTE N = (M + 1.` rejected; extraparen.cob `(M + 1))` rejected; parendisp.cob `DISPLAY (A).` rejected; subsp.cob `E (2)` / `E( 3 )` accepted. Pseudo-text exception: replparen.cob `REPLACE ==ZZ(== BY ==DISPLAY ==.` then `ZZ( "OK".` compiles and prints OK. All halves probed. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (§8.3.5 is common to all editions; Annex E lists no change to separators) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Preprocessor/CopyProcessor.cs#ReadReplaceOperand (the symbol was removed by kb/Work PB1350/PB1354; the successor that now implements the same step is named in its place (verdict untouched — the row is another note's)) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolLexer.g4#SUB_LPAREN (kb/Work PB2113 deleted the SUBSCRIPT lexer mode; OnDefaultLParen types every paren (REF_LPAREN, FNARG_LPAREN, LPAREN) from one balanced stack)

subject: Lexical elements
notes: Rule 5 (cite.py --check 8.3.5 "The opening delimiter shall be immediately preceded by a space, left parenthesis, or opening pseudo-text delimiter" OK 5)). kb/Work PB1394 LANDED (wave 73 group A): SeparatorRule asks every literal token of either lexer mode (LiteralTokens.Types, the set LiteralScreenDriftTests derives from the grammar) whether the character before its opening delimiter is a space, '(' or '==' and the character after its closing delimiter is a space, ',', ';', '.', ')' or '==', and reports COBOLNET2633 otherwise; touching literals are one report. The prefixed opening delimiters (X" N" B" NX" BX") are now always delimited as one token whatever their content (PB1441), so W"AB" beside an item W is IDENTIFIER + literal and reported, and X"GG" is a malformed hexadecimal literal (COBOLNET2630) rather than X + "GG". The parse-recovery guesses COBOL0301/COBOL0302 that stated the rule a second time are removed. Negative: DISPLAY "AB"N, MOVE"AB", IF "AB"=A -> COBOLNET2633 at all four editions.

subject: Lexical elements
notes: Rule: 'The separator space may optionally immediately follow any separator except the opening delimiter of a literal. A space following the opening delimiter of a literal is part of the literal and not a separator.' (cite.py --check 8.3.5 OK §8.3.5 9)). subject: Qualification
notes: kb/Work PB1476 (wave 1019 D). Rule 4's antecedent is DataItem.ReferencedByTypeClause, recorded from EVERY written TYPE clause (a storage item's, a linkage item's, another type declaration's member's) before anything expands. notes: cite.py --check 8.4.2.2.3 "LINAGE-COUNTER shall be qualified if more than one file description entry containing a LINAGE clause may be referenced within the source element in which the reference to LINAGE-COUNTER occurs" -> OK §8.4.2.2.3 8). subject: Subscripts
notes: PB1016 LANDED 2026-09-22: the DATA DIVISION reference - CONSTANT AS LENGTH OF data-name-2 (SS13.10) - now reaches the same ReferenceResolver.ScreenSubscriptArity every procedure-division reference takes; before, `01 KL CONSTANT AS LENGTH OF PLAIN(1).` over a non-table item compiled and KL was 7. The constant binder's private suffix walk is gone (ReadWritten), so a subscript hung off a qualification is screened too. SR2 has two halves - 'shall contain an OCCURS clause OR SHALL BE SUBORDINATE TO a data description entry that contains an OCCURS clause' - and the compiler wrote down only the first, as DataItem.IsTable. Both halves are now one predicate, DataItem.IsTableElement (= SubscriptArity > 0), read by the ONE declaration-informed '(' rule the three subscript-splitting callers share. POSITIVE: the 85 golden subscripts X, which carries no OCCURS clause of its own and is subordinate to one, in every reference position - a receiving operand of MOVE / ADD / COMPUTE / STRING / UNSTRING / INITIALIZE, a sending operand, a relative subscript, a reference-modification leftmost position, an intrinsic-function argument and a SEARCH ALL identifier-1. NEGATIVE: a subscript on an item satisfying NEITHER half is COBOLNET2096 at all four editions. Before kb/Work PB877 that violation drew COBOLNET0899 'not yet implemented' on the receiving side - a promise about permanently illegal source - and compiled clean and aborted at run time on the sending side, where 4.2.2 requires a compile-time mechanism.

subject: Subscripts
notes: The COUNT and the ORDER. DataItem.SubscriptArity is the count - one per OCCURS clause in the item's description, fixed or dynamic - and DataItem.SubscriptLevels() is the same walk as a list, outermost first, which is SR3's 'order of successively less inclusive dimensions'. Five hand-written copies of that ancestor walk were in the compiler; the drift test pins it to one. POSITIVE: the 85 golden writes one subscript per dimension in every position, including the two-dimensional Y2 OF Y-REC (X(1), 2) and the nested SEARCH ALL T-E (T-N (1), TX) whose witness value discriminates the outer occurrence. NEGATIVE: X (1, 2) on a one-dimensional element is COBOLNET2097 at all four editions. SR5's seven exceptions are all about OMITTING the subscript list and are decided by the owning binders (a SEARCH subject, a REDEFINES clause, an OCCURS KEY IS phrase, a SORT key or table subject, a screen entry's FROM/TO/USING phrase, a report SUM addend), so the screen deliberately fires only on a reference that WRITES subscripts.

notes: kb/Work PB1473 (discharged by PB1055's landing, re-probed on the w1012h build). cite.py --check 8.4.2.3.3 'as the rightmost or only subscript of a table in the table format of a SORT statement' -> OK §8.4.2.3.3 6). CobolTable.At is the ONE occurrence-number to element mapping and it is edition-independent - no edition branch - so the 1..n bound holds identically at every edition; ec_bound_subscript pins the NAMED condition under >>TURN EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT CHECKING ON with a USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION declarative and RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT. subject: Inline method invocation
notes: kb/Work PB1142 landed (w65c). cite.py --check 8.4.3.4.3 'Inline method invocation shall not be specified as a receiving operand.' OK. subject: Inline method invocation
notes: kb/Work PB1429 LANDED (w1014u). cite.py --check 8.4.3.4.3 'neither the predefined object reference NULL nor a universal object reference shall be specified' OK 2). NULL receiver -> COBOLNET2138 (pb428 negative); written universal -> COBOLNET2138 (pb428 negative); chained universal temp (A1 :: "UNIV" :: "GETNAME", UNIV RETURNING a universal reference) -> COBOLNET2138 (pb1429 negative; was the COBOLNET2362 internal error); chained class-typed temp still runs (pb428 case 6 -> ACCOUNT). subject: Inline method invocation
notes: kb/Work PB1428, LANDED (wave 59 with PB1548). Rule: 'The data item referenced in the RETURNING phrase of the invoked method's procedure division header shall not be described with the ANY LENGTH clause or with the ACTIVE-CLASS phrase.' (cite.py --check 8.4.3.4.3 -> OK §8.4.3.4.3 4)). The DIVERGES was the predefined NEW: OoBindImplicitNew synthesized an 'object-class-name ONLY' temp for `class :: "NEW"` and never applied SR4. subject: Inline method invocation
notes: kb/Work PB1425 (w1018d) closes the object-reference half the refuter recorded. "An inline method invocation references a temporary data item with the same class, category, and content as the temp-identifier that would be returned from the execution of the applicable form of INVOKE statement" (cite.py --check 8.4.3.4.4 -> OK §8.4.3.4.4 1)). The temp is an identifier wherever an object reference is asked: `SET U1 TO A1 :: "ME"` already compiled through SetSenders.Classify (PB1399/PB1929); `INVOKE A1 :: "ME" "WHO" RETURNING W` was COBOL0001 '::' and now invokes on the temp (§14.9.23.3 SR1 "Identifier-1 shall be an object reference", OK) -- `objectReference` (INVOKE's receiver, SET Format 5's sender, RAISE) gained `inlineMethodInvocation`, and its atom (the inline receiver) gained `functionCall`, so a function-identifier whose item is an object reference is a receiver and an inline identifier-1 too. The golden pins INVOKE through an inline temp and a chained segment, INVOKE through a typed and a universal function result, the keyword-omitted function, a function as inline identifier-1, and RAISE of an inline temp and of a function result caught by the class's declarative. A temp that is not an object reference is refused by the position's own rule naming the identifier as written (COBOLNET0824 / COBOLNET0848); a universal function result as inline identifier-1 is §8.4.3.4.3 SR2 (COBOLNET2138). [editions: the OO facility, 2002+]

subject: EXCEPTION-OBJECT
notes: kb/Work PB922 (wave 42) - RULE (cite.py --check 8.4.3.6.3 'EXCEPTION-OBJECT shall not be specified as a receiving operand'): OK, SR1. SR1 is a rule about EVERY receiving operand in the language, and only SET had an arm for it, so MOVE U TO EXCEPTION-OBJECT drew COBOLNET1639 ('is not defined - Check the spelling, or declare the item') beside COBOLNET0901 ('is a reserved word and cannot be used as a user-defined word') - two diagnostics that contradict each other, and neither of them the rule the program broke. Now screened at the ONE general receiving chokepoint, ExpressionBinder.ResolveReceiving, as COBOLNET2196 quoting SR1; SET's own arm draws the SAME code and its clause number was repaired from 8.4.3.6 (where cite.py --check FAILS) to 8.4.3.6.3. THE EDITION IS PART OF THE RULE and is measured on both sides: 8.9 reserves the word only from COBOL-2002, so at --std 85 EXCEPTION-OBJECT is an ordinary user-defined word and '01 EXCEPTION-OBJECT PIC X(4).' + 'MOVE "ABCD" TO EXCEPTION-OBJECT' is conforming source that runs (conformance:85/pb922_exception_object_user_word_85); the one predicate ReferenceResolver.IsExceptionObjectRegister carries spelling, form (8.4.3.6.2's general format is the bare word) and edition together, so no caller can hold a different opinion. editions names 2002 and later because that is where the prohibition applies at all.

subject: EXCEPTION-OBJECT
notes: kb/Work PB922 (wave 42) - RULE (cite.py --check 8.4.3.6.3 'EXCEPTION-OBJECT is implicitly described as class object and category object reference, as an external data item, and as a universal object reference'): OK, SR2. The STANDARD declares this name and no data description entry does, so a resolver that does not know it answers 'is not defined' about a name that is defined - which is what every sending reference got. DataBinder.ExceptionObjectRegister now carries SR2's implicit description (PicInfo.ObjectReferenceItem(ObjectRefDescriptor.Universal)) and ReferenceResolver resolves the bare word to an ExceptionObjectPlace over it, beside the CAPACITY and DEBUG-ITEM registers, so every class/category screen reads it like any other object-reference item and every caller inherits the answer. It is a VIEW, never storage: 8.4.3.6.4 GR2 gives the run unit ONE instance, which is the runtime's ExceptionState, and PlaceRenderer renders the read (fully qualified, because a reference to it needs neither the EC model nor a class and the conditional 'using' would otherwise leave the backend with CS0103 on generated C# the user cannot see). MEASURED at 2002 and 2023: IF EXCEPTION-OBJECT = NULL is legal source and true when no exception object is associated with the current exception (GR1); SET U TO EXCEPTION-OBJECT copies that reference; two references denote the same instance (GR2). SR2's 'as an external data item' is deliberately NOT carried as HasExternalClause - that flag drives the 13.18.22 EXTERNAL-store re-basing of a DECLARED record, and what the phrase asserts (one instance per run unit) is already realized by the single ExceptionState. ExceptionObjectPlace is registered in PlaceStorageFormSwitchDriftTests' storage-form roster, so a switch that meets it in a catch-all is a failing test.

subject: NULL object reference

The argument half is PB1137's (USING [BY CONTENT] NULL crosses as the null reference, pb1137_invoke_argument_forms). subject: NULL object reference
notes: "Predefined object reference NULL contains the null object reference value; this is a unique value defined by the implementor such that it is guaranteed to never reference an object." (cite.py --check 8.4.3.7.4 -> OK). In the typed-native model NULL is the .NET null reference, which by construction references no object. Probed at 2002 and 2023 (p4.cob): a NEW instance compares NOT = NULL. After `SET G H TO NULL`, G = NULL and H = NULL (both operand orders, NULL = G). A universal reference set TO NULL equals NULL and equals a typed reference holding NULL, so there is one unique null value across categories. INVOKE on a null reference raises EC-OO-NULL (conformance:2023/ec_oo_null_invoke, §14.9.23.4 GR5). conformance:2002/oo_universal_relation derives its expected values from this GR: the initial U = NULL, and after NEW U NOT = NULL.

subject: SELF and SUPER
notes: Rule (--check 8.4.3.8.3 'This identifier format may be specified only in a method definition' -> OK §8.4.3.8.3 1)). Every surface SELF/SUPER can appear on is guarded: INVOKE SELF|SUPER and the inline form (OoBindByReceiver: !host.InMethod || OoCurrentClass null -> COBOLNET0827), SET ... TO SELF (OoCurrentClass null -> 0867), RAISE SELF (EcBinder 0848). Probe probe/self-and-super/PSR1.cob in a PROGRAM: INVOKE SELF, INVOKE SUPER, MOVE SELF :: "M" TO X, RAISE SELF -> four targeted rejections citing SR1. Note: if F2 widens SELF to general identifier positions, those new positions need this same guard. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (OO predefined object references; absent from COBOL-85)]

subject: SELF and SUPER
notes: kb/Work PB1425 (registrar 15c). Rule (--check 8.4.3.8.3 'This identifier format shall not be specified as a receiving operand' -> OK §8.4.3.8.3 2)). Enforced structurally: no receiving slot (SET receivers are dataReference+, RETURNING, MOVE targets) admits the SELF/SUPER tokens. Probes probe/self-and-super/PSSETR.cob (`SET SELF TO O`) and PSRET.cob (`INVOKE PSRETA "NEW" RETURNING SELF`) both rejected. The diagnostic is the generic COBOLNET0901 "reserved word ... cannot be used as a user-defined word" rather than an SR2 citation (quality, not conformance). No spec-derived negative fixture found for this SR (SetFormatSelection.cs:232 comment only). || REFUTED: PARTIAL — No SR2 mechanism exists. Nine receiving-position probes each fail with COBOLNET0901 "'SELF' is a reserved word ... cannot be used as a user-defined word (ISO §8.9)": SET SELF TO NULL, RETURNING SELF, INITIALIZE SELF, SET SELF O / O SELF TO NULL, MOVE .. TO SELF, SET ADDRESS OF SELF, SET SUPER TO NULL and ACCEPT SELF. The source is rejected only because SELF/SUPER are not identifiers at all, which is the rejects-legal-source defect F2. The stated reason is also false: the source does not use SELF as a user-defined word, it uses a predefined-object identifier as a receiving operand. Nothing tests it. When F2 is fixed by admitting SELF/SUPER as identifier Format 6, every one of these positions would start compiling without a diagnostic. A verdict that depends on a separate defect staying unfixed, with no rule-owned diagnostic, is not CONFORMS. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (OO predefined object references; absent from COBOL-85)]

subject: SELF and SUPER
notes: kb/Work PB1425 (w1021a). "SUPER may be specified only as the object in an object-property identifier or as the object used to invoke a method with the INVOKE statement or an inline invocation of a method" (cite.py --check 8.4.3.8.3 -> OK 3)). notes: 'Identifier-1 shall be of category alphanumeric or national.' COBOLNET1960. The braced operand of ADDRESS OF FUNCTION arrives as ONE dataReference and the two arms are told apart at BIND, where the REPOSITORY function-specifier table and the item's resolved category are both facts: a word that is a declared function-prototype-name takes the prototype arm, anything else must resolve to an alphanumeric or national identifier. The positive leg is witnessed too - the 2023 golden drives the whole run-time lane through a PIC X(12) identifier-1.

subject: Function-address-identifier
notes: 'Function-prototype-name-1 shall be a function prototype specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph.' Resolved through DataBinder.UserFunctionNames - the REPOSITORY FUNCTION specifiers WITHOUT the INTRINSIC phrase - plus 8.4.6.6's other leg, 'the user-function-name of the containing function definition', so a self-referential function-pointer inside a function definition needs no repository entry. The SAME two legs the USAGE clause's TO phrase resolves, written once per operand kind. A word in neither leg is not silently accepted: it falls to SR1's identifier test and is refused COBOLNET1960.

subject: Function-address-identifier
notes: 'This identifier format shall not be specified as a receiving operand.' STRUCTURALLY SATISFIED, and the structure is the point: the function-address-identifier has exactly ONE grammar home, setFunctionAddressStatement's `TO ADDRESS OF? FUNCTION dataReference` tail, which is a SENDING position by construction. It appears in no receiving-operand rule anywhere in the grammar, so the rule cannot be violated by a parsable program and no screen is needed - the SR18/SR19 lesson in reverse (a rule with a structural answer needs no second copy of that answer in the binder). Compare 8.4.3.13's PROGRAM twin, whose SR4 is the same sentence and whose grammar home setEntryStatement is likewise sender-only.

subject: Function-address-identifier
notes: 'Function-address-identifier creates a unique data item of class pointer and category function-pointer that contains the address of a function identified by one of the following: a) the content of the data item referenced by identifier-1 b) function-prototype-name-1.' BOTH arms are live and both are witnessed: the 2014 golden takes the PROTOTYPE arm and the 2023 golden drives the IDENTIFIER arm three times. The 'unique data item of class pointer and category function-pointer' is the resolved FunctionPointer value the emitted site computes once and stores into every receiver - it is a value, never a declared item, which is why it has no PicInfo and why SR3 keeps it out of receiving positions. GR1's trailing sentence ('Identifier-1 shall reference a function prototype specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph') is a RUN-TIME fact about the identifier's CONTENT, not a compile-time screen on the identifier, and it is exactly what GR4 answers when the content names nothing.

subject: Function-address-identifier
notes: 'For a COBOL function, the address is that of the function identified by the externalized function-name in its FUNCTION-ID paragraph' - this implementation's function-pointer representation IS that name (ProgramTable.Node.CallName, the 11.5.4 GR1 AS literal when one is written and the declared word otherwise, kb/Work PB303), so the rule is satisfied by construction rather than by a conversion. 'For a non-COBOL function, the relation between the address and the associated function is defined by the implementor' - this implementation declares support for no non-COBOL function, which is published under A.1 item 210 (docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 7 DOC-A.1-210, the allowable-languages half); such a function has no run-unit registration, so GR4 - EC-FUNCTION-NOT-FOUND and the predefined address NULL - is the defined answer for one.

subject: Function-address-identifier
notes: 'When function-prototype-name-1 is specified, the function-address-identifier has the characteristics of a function-pointer restricted to function-prototype-name-1.' The rule's whole observable consequence is that the sender then enters 14.9.39.3 SR20's same-signature compare as a restricted function-pointer, and that is exactly how it is implemented: the prototype arm of BindSetFunctionAddress runs the SAME PrototypeSignatures.Same test the pointer-to-pointer arm runs, against the receiver's own prototype, and COBOLNET1959 names the mismatch. It is ALSO why the prototype arm needs no run-time GR14 screen of its own - the characteristics are known at bind - while the identifier-1 arm does.

subject: Function-address-identifier
notes: 'If the runtime system cannot locate the function, the EC-FUNCTION-NOT-FOUND exception condition is set to exist and the value of the address-identifier is the predefined address NULL.' BOTH halves are measured by the 2023 golden's NF-RAISED/B-NULL pair: the declarative runs AND the receiver takes NULL. The value is DEFINED by the rule, so the store happens whether or not checking is enabled and only the raise is checking-gated (14.6.13.1.4) - the opposite arrangement from 14.9.39.4 GR14, which NAMES its no-change outcome and therefore skips the store unconditionally. The two legs are written separately for that reason. EcBinder.QueryFor gained the BoundSetFunctionAddress arm in the SAME change set as the raise site, after the same gap was MEASURED on its BoundSetEntry sibling (a >>TURN EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND CHECKING ON over SET pp TO ENTRY 'NOSUCH' printed only 'AFTER SET' - the 8.4.3.13 GR4 raise had been dead since P10 Step 7).

subject: Report counters
notes: 'In the report section, PAGE-COUNTER and LINE-COUNTER may be referenced only in a SOURCE clause. In the procedure division, PAGE-COUNTER and LINE-COUNTER may be referenced in any context where an integer data item may appear.' TWO halves, and each has its own evidence. PROCEDURE DIVISION: the rule names no statement, so the counter is a receiving-capable PLACE resolved at the ONE receiving chokepoint rather than a permission granted per verb — ReportPageCounterPlace, reached from ExpressionBinder.ResolveReceiving, which every receiver funnels through; the positive golden exercises ten integer-data-item contexts (MOVE, ADD TO, SUBTRACT FROM, MULTIPLY BY, DIVIDE INTO, COMPUTE, ADD GIVING, INITIALIZE, INSPECT TALLYING, UNSTRING WITH POINTER) plus the sending direction in COMPUTE. Before kb/Work PB429 the receiving direction was refused wholesale (COBOLNET0899, 'legal ... not yet implemented'), and four verbs (INSPECT TALLYING, ACCEPT, UNSTRING's POINTER/TALLYING, STRING's INTO/POINTER) resolved their receivers through the SENDING resolver, so the chokepoint could not have reached them either; they now ask ResolveReceiving. REPORT SECTION: ReportSectionNameIn admits a counter only in a SOURCE clause and refuses it elsewhere - the negative golden writes one into a SUM addend, which SR6 of 13.18.54.3 refuses in its own words ('any identifiers it contains may reference entries in any section of the data division other than the report section') while the same program keeps a legal SOURCE IS PAGE-COUNTER in view.

subject: Condition-name
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 8.4.4.3 'Condition-name-1 shall be associated with a switch-name in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph.' OK, SR1). The only names SwitchCondOf admits as Format 1 are those registered in SwitchConditions, which is populated solely by BindImplementorNameEntry from a SPECIAL-NAMES switch-name entry whose implementor row is a Switch (a non-switch row with ON/OFF STATUS is COBOLNET2241, an unknown name registers nothing), plus InheritConfiguration from a containing program's SPECIAL-NAMES. A bare word that is neither a level-88 nor so associated is not a condition (probe n3: the switch's mnemonic-name SW1 used as a condition -> COBOLNET2318 naming §8.8.4.6). Positive runtime evidence in p1.cob at 85 and 2023 (see FMT-8.4.4.2). Resolution order level-88 before switch (NC211A) only matters for a name that is both, which is already non-conforming source under §8.3.2.2 uniqueness — not this rule's question.

subject: Local and global names

subject: Scope of names
notes: Rule: "If the program-name is that of an outermost program, that program-name may be referenced by statements included in any source element in the run unit." notes: kb/Work PB1042 (wave 1021 B2). §8.5.1.9.1 3): a dynamic-capacity table 'may be defined in any place, other than the file section, in which a fixed-capacity table may be defined and may be nested in any combination to the same number of levels as a fixed-capacity table'. subject: Variable-length data items
notes: PERMISSIVE rule: §8.5.1.11.3 says the resources 'MAY be freed automatically when' the listed event occurs, and 'The actual time when the resources used by a variable-length data item are freed is implementor-defined' (Annex A item 220: required, need not be documented). The only binding content is that freeing is unobservable ('this has no effect on the results of the execution of the program') and persistence equals a fixed-length item's. COBOL.NET's variable-length items are managed .NET objects: a dynamic-length item IS a System.String field (CobolDynString), a dynamic-capacity table IS a CobolDynTable<T> (T[] + count); reclamation is by the CLR GC once unreachable, so every listed event is honoured at a GC-determined time, which the implementor-defined timing admits. cite.py --check 8.5.1.11.3 "The resources used by a variable-length data item may be freed automatically when" -> OK; --check 8.5.1.11.3 "The actual time when the resources used by a variable-length data item are freed is implementor-defined" -> OK; --check 8.5.1.11.1 "The term variable-length data item refers to either a dynamic-capacity table or a dynamic-length elementary item" -> OK. Editions: the facility is ISO 2014+ (Annex E item 17 of 2023 records only the SET SIZE enhancement as new, so the items pre-exist in 2014). Event 1 (object finalized): OBJECT working-storage variable-length items are per-instance managed fields; they become unreachable with the instance and are collected with it. Probe probe/vldi/p2.cob (CLASS-ID CDYN, OBJECT WS with OCCURS DYNAMIC + DYNAMIC LENGTH; two instances, FILL on O1, SHOW both, SET O1 TO NULL): output 'CAP=0000000006 D=[HELLO]' / 'CAP=0000000001 D=[]' -- per-instance storage, no sharing, released with the instance. No spec-derived test pins OO-instance variable-length data (none exists; the freeing itself is unobservable).

Pinned twice: (1/3) ** 0 under PROHIBITED is exactly 1.00 (the CA5 sibling - the leak reinstated the pre-CA5 spurious EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION), and (A/B) ** 2 = 1 * (A/B) ** 2 = 11.1111 (the leak made multiplying by one change the value).

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB158, landed 2026-09-02). The rule is GR2's four-rank hierarchy (1st unary +/-, 2nd exponentiation, 3rd multiply/divide, 4th add/subtract). The IMPLEMENTATION was already correct and is unchanged: powerExpression puts a full unaryExpression in its base position, so `- 2 ** 2` binds as (-2)**2. What was PARTIAL was the EVIDENCE - rank 1 over rank 2 was pinned NOWHERE, and it is the one rank whose answer differs from every mainstream language, so a regression would have looked like normal behaviour. tests/conformance/2023/pb158_arith_precedence_spine now pins all four ranks in one labelled golden with every expected value derived from GR2/GR3 rather than from a run: R1 `- 2 ** 2` = 4 (rank 1 over 2), R2 `2 ** 3 * 4` = 32 (2 over 3), R3 `2 + 3 * 4` = 14 (3 over 4), R4 `2 ** 3 ** 2` = 64 (GR3 left fold), R7 `8 / 4 / 2` = 1 (GR3 left fold on /), and R5/R6 as the parentheses-vs-precedence discriminator. It also replaces the previous evidence's dependence on pb69 T11, where the precedence fact was INCIDENTAL to a golden about the Int128 carrier and would have vanished silently if that expression were ever rewritten.

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: Citation re-validated INDEPENDENTLY: `--check 8.8.1.2 "the order of execution of consecutive operations of the same hierarchical level is from left to right"` => OK §8.8.1.2 3). || UPHELD, with my own evidence rather than the adjudicator's. Derived first: every level left-folds, exponentiation included — the standard states no right-associativity exception for `**`, so `2 ** 3 ** 2` = (2**3)**2 = 64, not 512. READ: `ExpressionBinder.BindChain` is `foreach (var child in StatementBinder.Children(node)) { if (child is AddOpContext or MulOpContext) op = child.GetText()[0]; else { var x = BindExprCore(child, context); acc = acc is null ? x : new BoundBinary(acc, op, x); } }` — a strict left fold serving BOTH AdditiveExpressionContext and MultiplicativeExpressionContext; and `ExpressionBinder.BindPower` is `acc = BindExprCore(bases[0], context); for (int i = 1; i < bases.Length; i++) acc = new BoundPower(acc, BindExprCore(bases[i], context));` — the same left fold for rank 2. subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB158, landed 2026-09-02). The rule is Table 3's symbol-adjacency matrix. WHICH CELLS THE GRAMMAR CAN STILL PRODUCE WAS MEASURED, one probe program per cell, parsed through the real compiler rather than reasoned about: ten of the thirteen invalid cells are already hard parse errors ((ident,ident), (binop,binop), (binop,')'), (unary,binop), (unary,')'), ('(',binop), ('(',')'), (')',ident), (')',unary), (')','(')), and two more - (ident,'(') and its sibling - cannot form as an arithmetic PAIR at all because COBOL reads a '(' after an identifier as a subscript or reference-modifier. Exactly ONE cell was producible: (unary, unary). It is now screened by ExpressionFormationPass over the shared frontend rule, covering all THREE evaluating arms (ExpressionBinder.BindExprCore, CompileTimeExpressionEvaluator.EvalArith, and its SoleNumericLiteral reclassification probe, which used to fold `- - 5` to the literal 5). The screen reads TOKEN POSITIONS, not the tree, because SS8.3.3.3.2 rule 2 makes an ADJACENT sign part of the numeric literal - `- -2` is the PERMISSIBLE (unary, literal) pair while `- - 2` is the invalid one, and in the default lexer mode both emit MINUS MINUS INTEGERLIT. notes: CONFORMS as of 2026-08-03 (fix-queue PB28, landed this session). Rule 6 has three parts. r6a (zero base requires exponent > 0) and r6c (negative base requires an integer exponent) are mandatory 'shall' requirements setting EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION, Fatal in Table 14. BEFORE the fix the STANDARD-DECIMAL arm enforced both (CobolDec.Pow) and EVERY NATIVE arm enforced neither, so the same program answered differently depending only on whether an ARITHMETIC clause was present: 0 ** 0 returned 1 (IEEE's convention, not COBOL's) and -2 ** 0.5 returned 0 (Math.Pow yields NaN and the quantizer made it zero), both with an ON SIZE ERROR phrase present and NOT taken. Checked in the same pass rather than left to be discovered as a fourth leg.

notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS 2026-08-31 (owner decision D-C; kb/Work PB167). r2a-r2d were already exact (binary square-and-multiply over Mul, which for exponents 1-4 performs the printed equivalent expressions digit-for-digit); PB145 had closed every measured wrong answer in the escapes. What remained was r2e's own constraint on the DEVELOPMENT: 'Operands used in the development of that value shall be in SDIDI form. All additions, subtractions, multiplications and divisions performed in the development of the result shall be performed in accordance with the corresponding rules in ISO/IEC 60559:2020' (cite.py --check verified) — and the development went through IEEE binary64 (Math.Pow on the non-integer arm, a Math.Log10 decomposition on the past-loop-bound escape), so it satisfied neither shall and the two arms were two DIFFERENT approximations of the same value. There is now ONE development, exp(operand-2 x ln operand-1), carried entirely on CobolDec Add/Sub/Mul/Div with argument reduction (ln: decimal exponent split + three exact square roots + the atanh series; exp: reduction by n*ln10 so the 10^n factor is an EXACT decimal exponent shift, then the Taylor series), plus one chosen special case: at |operand-2| = 1/2 the equivalent expression is FUNCTION SQRT(operand-1), whose standard-decimal value Sec.15.84.4 r2 fixes EXACTLY, so b ** 0.5 and SQRT(b) agree by construction (they DISAGREED before). CobolDecPowDevelopmentTests scans CobolDec.cs and fails if any binary64 transcendental returns. ⛔ TWO DEFECTS IN THAT FIRST LANDING WERE FOUND BY ITS OWN REVIEW FLEET AND FIXED IN THE SAME WAVE. (1) kb/Work PB267 - the past-loop-bound escape rebuilt the exponent from TryIntegerValue's magnitude, which CLAMPS at long.MaxValue, so every exponent past 2**63-1 was silently replaced by 9223372036854775807: (1 + 10**-33) ** 1.0E+20 answered a flat 1.0000000000000 where 1.0000000000001 is owed, and 0.9999999999999999 ** 1.0E+25 answered a silent 0 where the value is below the decimal128 range entirely. PowMagnitude now carries the exponent OPERAND (an SDIDI holds |operand-2| exactly, so there was never anything to reconstruct), and PowCore screens the ORDER of p x ln b before forming it so an out-of-range product takes Sec.8.8.1.5.2 r2's own two names rather than Mul's clamp, which would say OVERFLOW in both directions. ⚠ The disposition is NOT 'a clamped exponent with |base| != 1 is out of range': the closest SDIDI value to one is 1 +/- 10**-33 and (1 + 10**-33) ** 10**20 is in range, so that screen would be PB145's spurious size error again. (2) kb/Work PB269 - the logarithm's three-square-root argument reduction carries u = m^(1/8) at 34 SIGNIFICANT digits about 1, so Sub(u, One) cancelled away log10(1/delta) of them: measured 17.05 correct digits at the worst point of |m-1| <= 1/4 and EXACTLY ZERO at m = 1 + 10**-33, where the first root rounds back to 1 and ln m came out 0. LnReduced now takes the same atanh series over delta = m - 1 directly inside that band (Sub(m, One) is exact there), which measures 32.74 digits at the same worst point and uses no square root at all. WHAT IS CLAIMED, precisely: an r2e-conforming SDIDI development, NOT 34 correct digits

subject: Standard-decimal arithmetic
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS 2026-08-31 (owner decision D-C; kb/Work PB167), CORRECTED THE SAME DAY (kb/Work PB266). r3: 'When operand-2 is less than zero, the result shall be equivalent to the evaluation of the arithmetic expression (1 / (operand-1 ** FUNCTION ABS (operand-2)))' (cite.py --check verified, both halves). This is an EQUIVALENCE and not implementor latitude - r2's latitude is scoped 'When the value of operand-2 is greater than zero' - and under Sec.8.8.1.5.2's per-operation 34-digit rounding the reciprocal form is a DIFFERENT value from exp(-|p| x ln b): it carries one extra correctly-rounded division and no negated exp argument. ⛔ THE FIRST LANDING'S NOTE CLAIMED THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THE CODE DID, in both of its sentences. It said the development 'develops every other negative exponent through the same SDIDI exp/ln core as the positive one, so the r3 identity holds by construction rather than by luck'; measured, it held in 21% of sampled cases, BY LUCK (2 ** -0.25 answered ...4762332146 where 1 / (2 ** 0.25) is ...4762332141). It also said 'the INTEGER arm has honoured it whole since PB145'; the past-loop-bound escape carried the sign INSIDE the exponent, so r3 held below |n| = 500000 and broke above it - a discontinuity at the loop bound. And no pin on the row could see either: pb167's two negative legs and MinusHalfExponent were all -1/2 (the one exponent PowCore short-circuited), pb145's B ** NN and MinusOne_...PastLongRange are base -1 (the |b| = 1 parity shortcut), and HalfPastTheLoopBound uses a POSITIVE exponent. THE CONSTRUCTION NOW: r3's reciprocal is written ONCE, at the top of Pow, over PowMagnitude(b, |operand-2|) - so every arm below it is r3-correct by construction, PowCore needs no -1/2 twin to keep in step, and the divergence is closed at the 34th significant digit where a relation between two SDIDI intermediates and an exact cancellation could both see it (pb167's R3GEN / R3PW7 / R3FAR / R3NEAR / R3DLT legs, and a 10-row unit theory spanning the non-integer, in-bound-integer and past-bound arms). ⚠ ONE VISIBLE CONSEQUENCE, pinned: an out-of-range negative exponent now takes its EC name from r3's own expression rather than from where the final value lands, because the operation that leaves the range is the INNER power. 2 ** -600000 reports EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW and 0.5 ** -600000 EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW; before the hoist they answered the other way round (pb145's R3OVER / R3UNDR legs). ⚠ r3 is an IDENTITY requirement, not an accuracy one, and honouring it COSTS accuracy here: the true 34-digit 2**-0.25 is ...4762332149, so the reciprocal form is 8 ulp out where the direct form was 3. That is why the fix is the literal expression and never a tolerance.

subject: Simple relation conditions
notes: Equal-length comparison in all three of its parts: equality when every pair matches (pb297 T01/T02/T03/T07/T12), the first unequal pair deciding (T15 differs at position 1, T11 at position 1), and the higher-collating operand being the greater one (T09 U+00FF over the low value; T08 shows two equal operands are neither less nor greater). The 2002 golden runs the same determination under a non-native PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE (U01-U03). WHICH OPERANDS REACH THIS RULE is now observed too, and that is what the prior evidence missed: the sentence says an alphanumeric operand may be compared 'to another operand treated as class alphanumeric for the purposes of comparison', which 8.8.4.2.5 makes a numeric integer operand compared with an alphanumeric one - and no golden held a numeric item, so a regression that answered such a relation WITHOUT the program collating sequence was invisible to the corpus (kb/Work PB741; NIST NC215A SEQ-TEST-GF-6/-7 was the sole witness). pb297 U11-U16 add the numeric anchor - LOW-VALUE, an ALL literal, the alphanumeric-literal twin that must agree, a signed anchor (14.9.25.4 GR6a drops the operational sign through 8.8.4.2.5's move) and a four-digit anchor - and the unit drift test pins the whole category matrix, so the numeric-vs-alphanumeric selection cannot silently become a numeric comparison again. The 'two zero-length operands are equal' sentence is pinned by conformance:2023/ref_mod_zero_length, not here.

subject: Simple relation conditions
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 8.8.4.2.8 "Two zero-length operands are equal" -> OK §8.8.4.2.8 1)): equal-length boolean operands compare position by position, leftmost first, equal iff every pair is equal; two zero-length operands are equal. Code: a relation whose collating class is Boolean renders `CobolString.Compare(l, r, pad: '0') op 0` (ConditionRenderer.RenderRelationalCore); a boolean-EXPRESSION relation renders CobolBool.Equal; the figurative arm threads the same pad. Both are positionwise first-difference loops over the D-B1 '0'/'1' substrate, so usage (DISPLAY vs BIT) does not enter. Ordering operators never reach the runtime: CheckRelationalOperands raises COBOLNET0844 (boolean relations are equality-only under §8.8.4.2.2 Format 2), so the 'no ordering' reading of this rule (which, unlike 8.8.4.2.10, names no greater operand) is honoured. Zero-length: Compare/Equal on two empty strings return 0/true by reading (and CobolBoolTests InlineData("","",true)). Probe E:\Temp\claude\E--CobolSharp\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d2\out\probe\srcp2\bool1.cob / bool2.cob (--std 2023 and 2002): B3D(DISPLAY) = B3B(BIT) same value -> Y; B\"10\" = B\"101\" -> N; B3 NOT = B5X -> Y; BIT group (GROUP-USAGE BIT, §8.8.4.2.1 treats it as an elementary bit item) = BIT item -> Y; B-AND expression relation -> Y; >>IF cce B\"10\" = B\"100\" -> Y; EVALUATE subject/object -> correct; level-88 VALUE B\"11\" over 110 -> TRUE. Aside (not this rule): `01 G USAGE BIT.` over PIC 1 subordinates is correctly an ALPHANUMERIC group (only GROUP-USAGE BIT makes a bit group), so comparing it with a boolean draws COBOLNET0844. Test: CobolBoolTests.Equal_ZeroExtends asserts equal-length equality/inequality and the two-empty-operands case from the rule text; the item-vs-item carrier (CobolString.Compare pad '0') is covered by unit:CobolStringPadTests.Compare_PadZero_ZeroExtends. subject: Simple class condition
notes: kb/Work PB571. All three arms of SR1 are screened at the ONE class-condition operand screen, which every spelling of the condition reaches (the IF form, 14.9.13.3 SR5's identifier-less form, and the EVALUATE selection subject's own class test, which used to be bound by a separate copy). The class list is asked through ItemCategory.IsIndexMessageTagObjectOrPointer for a data-item reference - the population that also answers for MESSAGE-TAG and FUNCTION-POINTER, whose entries never gain a PicInfo - and through IntrinsicArgumentRules.ClassOf for the operand shapes that are not one (an index-NAME, an intrinsic of 15.2 item 6's index class, the NULL predefined address). The variable-length group arm delegates to ReferenceResolver.HasVariableLengthSubordinate, which IS 8.5.1.12.1's definition. The strongly-typed-group arm keeps the COBOLNET1533 strong-typing family's own code (that family is split by rule) and the other two are COBOLNET2200; the split is stated in the code so it is not re-argued.

subject: Simple class condition
notes: kb/Work PB64 T5 (2026-08-19): a class condition whose alphabet-name-1 names an ALPHABET … IS LOCALE [locale-name] — of EITHER class (alphanumeric, or FOR NATIONAL) — is COBOLNET1669 locale-alphabet-not-a-charset: a LOCALE alphabet defines a collating sequence only (§12.3.7.4 GR7, Table 6), so it names no coded character set a class condition could test membership of. DataBinder.IsLocaleAlphabet is the ONE predicate; the same rule family (§12.3.7.3 SR16g / SR17d — the IN phrases of SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS and CLASS; §13.18.13.3 SR1/SR2 — CODE-SET) awaits those phrases binding at all (kb/Work PB110). Rule --check verified at 8.8.4.4.3 2).

subject: Simple class condition
notes: kb/Work PB590. SR3's list - alphabet-name-1, ALPHABETIC, ALPHABETIC-LOWER, ALPHABETIC-UPPER, BOOLEAN, class-name-1 - is the set of ClassConditionModel rows carrying ClassOperandRule.UsageDisplayOrNational, and NUMERIC is deliberately absent from it because SR8 states the same rule with a category escape. The predicate reads the operand's OPERAND picture (DataItem.OperandPic), so a bit or national GROUP answers as the elementary item 13.18.29.4 GR1b/GR2b makes it; a null picture is an ordinary alphanumeric group or a picture-less leaf and fails OPEN, which is the direction a screen must fail. Measured: `01 BT PIC 1(4) USAGE BIT. IF BT IS BOOLEAN` draws COBOLNET2202 where it previously compiled. The rule has no edition axis - the class condition and every alternative in its list except BOOLEAN exist at COBOL-85, and BOOLEAN is unreachable as a keyword below 2002 because it is not a reserved word there.

subject: Simple class condition
notes: kb/Work PB571. SR4 names THREE categories and only the BOOLEAN one was screened, so `IF <numeric item> IS ALPHABETIC` compiled and ran. All three are now one predicate. SR4 names class-name-1 and NOT alphabet-name-1, which is why the two user-defined-word alternatives carry DISTINCT kind tags: sharing one tag would have made this rule reject `IF <numeric item> IS <alphabet-name>`, which the standard admits and the 85 golden's F line pins.

subject: Simple class condition

subject: Simple class condition

notes: kb/Work PB1477 LANDED (wave 68 T). subject: Abbreviated combined relation conditions
notes: kb/Work PB1390 landed (wave 68 s). Rule 1): the omission of the subject (cite.py --check 8.8.4.12.1 "The omission of the subject of the relation condition, or" OK). BindAbbreviatedRelation inserts the carried subject; with none (after a class/sign/88/boolean condition, GR1's termination) it is now COBOLNET2552 (was the COBOLNET2319 internal-error net). notes: kb/Work PB1391 LANDED (wave 1005 D).
