subject: Conditional expressions
notes: kb/Work PB1432 LANDED (wave 68 T). Rule: cite.py --check 8.8.4.13 "The constituent connected conditions within a hierarchical level are evaluated in order from left" -> OK 8.8.4.13 1) ("... terminates as soon as a truth value for it is determined"). The order and short-circuit were already right (BindFlatSequence -> C# && / ||; a non-first operand's pre-ops ride a per-evaluation lambda). The mechanism that defers a non-first operand's steps failed on one legal shape: under >>TURN EC-ALL CHECKING ON a function-bearing subscript's 15.4 temporary STORE in that operand rendered its size-error RESUME landing as `goto __xfer` inside the lambda (CS0159), so `IF WS-A = 0 OR EL(FUNCTION TRC("C", 1)) = 1` and `IF WS-A = 1 OR EL(FUNCTION INTEGER(ONE / Z)) = 1` were rejected by the backend; hoisted before a FIRST operand the same landing fell back into the IF (14.9.33.4 GR2 a) 1. and NOTE 1 place it after the END-IF; measured: subscript 0 -> fatal EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT). Every drained step is now BoundStatement.OperandEvaluation; StatementEmitter.EmitStatement opens DispatchState's operand-evaluation scope and the ONE landing (ResumeTransfer) unwinds to the statement's BoundActivationSite. Measured on 2002/pb1432_operand_eval_resume: OR-T (no ACT-C), ACT-D OR2-T, DECL-ZD AFTER-A, DECL-ZD AFTER-B, C-T AFTER-C.

subject: Conditional expressions
notes: CONFORMS (kb/Work PB987, w54f). 'Values are established for arithmetic expressions and functions if and when the conditions containing them are evaluated': arithmetic expressions and intrinsic functions render inline inside the C# condition, so C#'s && / || short-circuit (8.8.4.13 1)) and the loop's re-test reach them per evaluation; every HOISTED activation - a user-defined function, an inline method invocation, a function-bearing subscript's temp store (DataBinder.PendingPreOps) and, since PB987, an object-property GET (DataBinder.OoPendingPropertyOps) - is drained by the per-evaluation window it was written in (UdfBinder.Mark marks BOTH lists): a PERFORM UNTIL / VARYING UNTIL condition, a SEARCH WHEN, an EVALUATE object, a non-first AND/OR operand, a VARYING BY / AFTER FROM operand, and runs at each evaluation or not at all. Negated conditions render as C# negation of the inner condition, evaluated when reached. Before PB987 a property reference in PERFORM UNTIL P OF S > 3 was fetched once for the whole loop (K=09 where the rule gives K=03). Witnesses: pb987_property_per_evaluation (UNTIL, AND/OR short-circuit, EVALUATE WHEN order, SEARCH WHEN, VARYING BY), udf_per_eval, pb17_function_subscript.

FIX: the ONE cross-run-unit verdict is Table19.Cell. FileConnector.Open takes RunUnitFileLock before OpenCore on an existing file (after the body on one it created): the OPEN publishes its Table 19 column (Table19.Column) as a SHARED open-file-description region lock (fcntl F_OFD_SETLK) on one byte at 2^62 + the column's wire number and tests, with F_OFD_GETLK, the columns its request row refuses (Table19.Cell == UnsuccessfulOpen) for another holder; a holder is refused with 61 (9.1.13.9 1)) and the file is untouched (14.9.27.4 GR25). A non-COBOL process that takes no lock meets only the share mode (Annex A.1 item 75). Rules 1) and 3) were CONFORMS and remain so: rule 1 is FileShare.None plus the NoOtherAnyMode column, rule 3 refuses nothing. The in-run-unit half (Table 19 via the PhysicalFileTable) was already CONFORMS.

subject: Polymorphism
notes: CONTEXT (applies to every 9.3.5.3 row): the seven items define the METHOD RESOLUTION SIGNATURE. The feature that DISTINGUISHES methods by it (overloading) is optional -- cite.py OK 9.3.5.3 7) 'Parametric polymorphism is an optional feature' -- and is NOT claimed (docs/CONFORMANCE.md 5 A.4.10 item 3; refused COBOLNET0822 in OoClassTable.Build, both instance and factory arms). But the signature is consumed by MANDATORY rules: cite.py OK 8.4.6.5 'The methods declared in an object class definition shall have unique method resolution signatures', OK 11.7.3 3) 'If the OVERRIDE phrase is specified, there shall be a method with the same method resolution signature', OK 11.7.3 9) (conformance of an inherited/implemented same-named method). inventory-schema.json derived-verdicts.oo-optional-items-only deliberately EXCLUDES these rows and asks for per-row adjudication, so no selector covers them. COBOL.NET's signature is the degenerate one (the NAME: roster key ExternalizedName) and the remaining components are enforced as SR9 conformance by OoConformance.ValidateOverrideSignatures -> MethodConformanceMismatches -> DescriptionMismatch (COBOLNET0829); for any program that does not overload, a component is conforming iff that comparator rejects every override the component distinguishes. Probes: out/probe/polymorphism/p*.cob, pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023 default. Rule: cite.py OK 9.3.5.3 1) 'The method name'. The name (the externalized name, PB303 roster key) IS the implemented signature: TryAddMethod/TryAddFactoryMethod refuse a second same-named method (COBOLNET0822 -- for identical parameters that is exactly 8.4.6.5's duplicate-signature error; for differing parameters it is the declined overloading), and MarkRoster pairs an override with its base by that key (0838 when OVERRIDE finds no base, 0837 when a same-named base method lacks OVERRIDE per 11.7.3 SR4a). Probe p1 (sub OVERRIDE M, PIC X(4) vs base PIC 9(4)) pairs by name and is rejected 0829. No spec-derived test targets this component as such (conformance:negative/oo-parametric-polymorphism witnesses the overloading decline, not this row). || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the OO module, and with it the method resolution signature, is a COBOL-2002 introduction -- Annex D.19.5.4.3 describes parametric polymorphism as part of the OO facility; none before 2002)

notes: Rule: 'if the identified object is a factory object, the method invocation will resolve to a factory method' (cite.py --check 9.3.6 -> OK §9.3.6 1)). subject: COBOL compilation group
notes: Rule: 'Compiler directives may appear in a structured compilation group as specified in 7.3, Compiler directives.' (cite.py --check 10.6.2 -> OK §10.6.2 5)). The substance is §7.3.3 SR8 'A compiler directive may be specified anywhere in a compilation group, in source text or in library text' (OK §7.3.3 8)) and §7.3.4 GR2 compile-stage directives 'processed in the order encountered in the structured compilation group' (OK §7.3.4 2)) with GR5 'applies to all of the source text and library text that follows' (OK §7.3.4 5)). Directives are line-level text processed by the preprocessor chain before the parse, so no source-unit boundary blocks them. PROBES (pinned cobol.exe, E:\Temp\claude\E--CobolSharp\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d2b\out\probe\cg): two_programs_directive.cob - >>DEFINE between END PROGRAM and the next PROGRAM-ID, >>IF/>>ELSE/>>END-IF inside the second unit, >>SOURCE FORMAT FREE after the last unit -> prints DEF / ONE (correct). dir_class_free.cob - >>DEFINE before the first unit (a CLASS-ID), >>IF inside a factory method, >>SOURCE FORMAT FREE between the class and a free-form program, >>SOURCE FORMAT FIXED between two programs -> CLS-DEF / FREE-DEF / FIXED-AGAIN (correct). turn_between.cob - a compilation-stage directive >>TURN EC-SIZE-ZERO-DIVIDE CHECKING ON between two units: unit 1 (before it) continues after DIVIDE BY 0, unit 2 (after it) terminates with EC-SIZE-ZERO-DIVIDE fatal -> order-of-encounter across units is honoured. The §7.3.3 SR8 exceptions (a)-(c) and the per-directive placement rules (e.g. PUSH/POP ALL, PushPopAllPlacementPass) are their own rows. Covering test: golden 2002/pb246_sqrt_absolute_value_and_domain writes >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON between END PROGRAM PB246SQRTABS and PROGRAM-ID PB246SQRTON and its spec-derived .out depends on it applying to the following unit only. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (compiler directives and the structured compilation group are post-85; §7.3 / §10.6)

subject: COBOL compilation group
notes: kb/Work PB1086: Rule: 'Compilation of a program prototype definition or a function prototype definition generates information required for the external repository, as specified in 8.13, External repository.' (cite.py --check 10.6.3 -> OK §10.6.3 1)). §8.13: 'Whether the information is taken from a prototype or a definition, the information stored in the external repository about the signature of a program or a function is the same.' (OK §8.13); 'The implementor shall provide a mechanism that allows the user to specify whether to update the external repository when a compilation unit is compiled.' (OK §8.13); and '... whether to flag differences in prototypes and definitions in the compilation group from the information in the external repository.' (OK §8.13). WHAT THE CODE DOES: a prototype's signature (LINKAGE formals + RETURNING) is generated and consumed IN-GROUP only - BinderDriver.BuildProgramDetailsTable (programs, GR10 b)) and the user-function table (functions) - so a caller in the SAME compilation group gets the prototype's details (witnessed by conformance:2002/udf_prototype and PB894's goldens). That half is met. The other half is not: this implementation declares its external repository to be the run-unit program registry (BinderDriver.cs:913/945, PrototypeSignatures.cs:32, docs/COBOLNET_INTERPROGRAM_DESIGN.md), and ProgramEmitter.cs:632 skips every prototype ('a prototype registers no runtime module - the separately-compiled definition does (§10.6.3 GR1)') - so compiling a prototype contributes NOTHING to that repository; the §10.6.3 GR1 citation there is used to justify the opposite of what GR1 says. PROBE proto_only.cob (PROGRAM-ID. CGPO IS PROTOTYPE. with LINKAGE A / PROCEDURE DIVISION USING A. / END PROGRAM CGPO.) compiles clean at 2023 and emits a module with no repository record; a later separately-compiled caller naming CGPO in its REPOSITORY therefore takes §12.3.8.4 GR10 c) with a NULL signature (PrototypeSignatures: 'An UNRESOLVED prototype conforms'), so no compile-time conformance check against that prototype is possible. Neither §8.13 mechanism (update / flag differences) exists: the CLI (--help) has no repository option and src has no repository store. Not owned by any kb/Work note (PB612/PB817/PB989 mention the external repository only as GR10 c)'s fallback). Verdict PARTIAL: in-group generation verified; generation for the external repository across compilations absent. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (prototype definitions and the external repository §8.13 are post-85) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/BinderDriver.cs#BuildProgramDetailsTable (BuildProgramDetailsTable is deleted by kb/Work PB989; GroupRepository.ProgramDetails is the in-group search)

notes: cite.py: OK §10.7.4 '1) An end marker indicates the end of the specified source unit.' subject: INITIALIZE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-09-02 (PB152), COBOLNET1727. 'Hexadecimal-alphanumeric literal' is a DEFINED TERM and the screen is written to it, not to a paraphrase: 8.3.3.2.2 gives the alphanumeric literal exactly two general formats - format 1 ("..." / '...') and format 2 (X"..." / X'...') - and 'hexadecimal-alphanumeric' names FORMAT 2, so a one-character format-1 literal such as "Z" is NOT admitted however short it is. One byte is exactly two hexadecimal digits (8.3.3.2.3 SR5). Before the screen the decoder took raw[0] for ANY shape, so INITIALIZE ALL TO "AB" silently became 'A'. The 2026-08-30 analysis that scoped this work carried the paraphrase 'a one-character alphanumeric OR one-byte hex literal', which would have shipped an under-reject; the printed page (PDF 307 / folio 277) was rendered and read to settle it. PB151's own golden pb151_options_fill was written with the format-1 spelling and is repaired to X"51" by this landing - 0x51 IS 'Q', so its expected output is unchanged byte for byte.

subject: INITIALIZE clause

subject: INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING clause
notes: kb/Work PB1511: Rule (cite.py --check 11.9.11.2 "If native arithmetic is in effect, the rounding rules that apply to intermediate data items are defined by the implementor" -> OK, rule 1; companion cite.py --check 8.8.1.3 "The implementor shall specify techniques used for native arithmetic" -> OK). What the code defines under NATIVE: (i) fixed-point operands on a scaled Int128, EXACT for the 14.7.7 31-digit composite (no intermediate rounding); (ii) a quotient NESTED in a larger expression computed at receiver/operand scale + DivGuardDigits (14) with TRUNCATION (NumericRenderer.cs ~615-651); (iii) any float operand -> IEEE binary64 (.NET round-to-nearest-even); (iv) a Dec-carried operand (float literal, float numeric-edited sender, integer power) -> the SDIDI lane rounded per the OPTIONS INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING mode (IntermediateMode in CombineCore), so the clause DOES reach native statements on that lane (kb/Work PB274 landed; CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-82 says so). The implementor has defined the rules and the implementation is deterministic. WHY PARTIAL: the published determination the rule depends on (CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-123 'Native arithmetic - techniques used, intermediate data item') says 'a nested quotient carries up to 14 guard fraction digits and rounds once, at the final transfer' - the guard-digit TRUNCATION (a second, intermediate rounding) is not stated, nor is the binary64 lane's rounding rule, and the INTERMEDIATE-ROUNDING-on-the-Dec-lane rule is stated only inside DOC-A.1-82 (a floating-literal item). The rule is implemented but only partly stated where a user would look. PB298's IntermediateRounding row is answerable from this read: the field IS consumed (NumericRenderer.IntermediateMode; IntrinsicRenderer 125/127/1031; NumericRenderer 163/568-571/857). No spec-derived test pins a native intermediate ROUNDING decision (l1_native_arithmetic_intermediate pins Int128 exactness, not rounding) -> test-ref empty. Editions follow the clause (2014,2023).

subject: INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING clause
notes: || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph
notes: Two rules in one row. (1) SR17 c)5 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'The number of characters specified shall not exceed the number of characters in the native national character set or, when the IN phrase is specified, the number of characters in the character set referenced by alphabet-name-4.' -> OK 17) 5.). The code path is shared with b5: the distinct count is checked against inSet.OrdinalCount under IN. Every national IN set (NATIVE/UTF-16 65,536; UCS-4/UTF-8 1,112,064; a literal-phrase national alphabet, which contains every native character) is at least as large as the 65,536-character native repertoire that members are drawn from, and no national code-name exists (PB793). notes: kb/Work PB702 (claimable since kb/Work PB324 landed; the row stayed GAP with an empty verdict while GR-12.4.5.3-3 already named the same goldens). RULE: 'Data-name-1 shall reference an alphanumeric data item and shall not be subordinate to the file description entry for file-name-1.' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.2 'Data-name-1 shall reference an alphanumeric data item and shall not be subordinate to the file description entry for file-name-1' -> OK, §12.4.5.2 7)). TWO HALVES, AND BOTH ARMS OF EACH ARE MEASURED. CODE: DataBinder.ResolveAssignUsing is the single site. Half 1 (category) is IsAlphanumericDataItem — an elementary PIC X item, or a group with no GROUP-USAGE clause, which 13.18.29.4 GR3 makes 'an alphanumeric group item'; category-ALPHABETIC (PIC A) is excluded because 8.8.4.2.4's 'A class alphabetic operand shall be treated as though it were an operand of class alphanumeric' is a COMPARISON rule and not a category identity, and bit/national groups are excluded by GroupUsage. An unresolvable name takes the same arm (there is no alphanumeric data item to reference), COBOLNET1810. Half 2 (subordination) walks item.Parent up to the root and fires COBOLNET1811 if any ancestor is one of THIS file's record descriptions — 'subordinate to the file description entry' means anywhere under a record description of that FD, which is the reading 9.1.21 corroborates ('The USING phrase references an alphanumeric data item whose content at the time an OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement for that file is executed uniquely identifies the specific physical file to be accessed'), because an operand inside the file's own record area is overwritten by every READ of that file. MEASURED on this worktree's build (c34f01ad): `cobol pb324-assign-using-not-alphanumeric.cob --std 85` -> 'error COBOLNET1810: file ''NF1'': ASSIGN … USING ''WS-NUM'' shall reference an alphanumeric data item - ''WS-NUM'' is a category-numeric item (ISO 12.4.5.2 SR7)'; `cobol pb324-assign-using-in-own-record.cob --std 2023` -> 'error COBOLNET1811: file ''NF2'': ASSIGN … USING ''N2-NAME'' shall not be subordinate to the file description entry for ''NF2'' (ISO 12.4.5.2 SR7)'. Both negative goldens carry `*> reject-at: 85 2002 2014 2023`, so the REJECTING arm is asserted at every edition. The ACCEPTING arm — the complement, which a rejection test can never measure — is conformance:2023/pb324_assign_using_dynamic and conformance:85/pb324_assign_using_85, both of which name a WORKING-STORAGE `PIC X(20)` item outside the FD and run to a spec-derived expected output. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 85 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023. §12.4.5.2 carries no edition marker on SR7 and Annex E records no change to the ASSIGN clause; the compiler enforces the rule through one ungated site and both negatives are pinned as rejecting at all four editions. This is the band GR-12.4.5.3-3 was landed at for the same clause and the same goldens. NOT CLAIMED HERE, and separately observed: this compiler does not gate the ASSIGN … USING SPELLING itself at 1985 (probed: `cobol tests/conformance/85/pb324_assign_using_85.cob --std 85` compiles silently). Whether the USING spelling is writable at 1985 is GR-12.4.5.3-3's landed adjudication and a question about the ASSIGN clause's introduction, not about SR7 — SR7 is either enforced or vacuous at that edition, never violated. || 2026-09-06 (landing train 19, kb/Work PB742+PB743): the code-location's second half moved. subject: File control entry
notes: LANDED 2026-10-05 (kb/Work PB773). RULE (--check 12.4.5.2 13): "Format 4 shall be specified only for a sort-merge file. The associated file description entry shall be a sort-merge file description entry." DETERMINATION: §12.4.5.1 prints Format 4 as SELECT [OPTIONAL], ASSIGN and [[ORGANIZATION IS] SEQUENTIAL] and nothing else, so an SD's file control entry is Format 4. Format 4 is a SUBSET of Format 3 (checked against the printed diagrams by the drift test), so an entry on an FD can never specify Format 4 alone and neither sentence can be broken from the FD side; the enforceable obligation is the SD's, and it is enforced clause by clause with each clause reported by exactly ONE row: a clause only one format prints names that format (SR8 Format 1, SR9 Format 2, SR11 Format 3), and a clause several formats print and Format 4 does not (ACCESS MODE, FILE STATUS, LOCK MODE, RESERVE, SHARING) is SR13's own row (FileControlKeyRules.Rules, Entry role, ScreenedOn SortMerge, COBOLNET1900). Re-measured before the fix on the pin's probes: FILE STATUS, ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL, ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL, SHARING, RESERVE, LOCK MODE and RECORD DELIMITER on an SD all compiled clean; SELECT OPTIONAL and ORGANIZATION IS [RECORD] SEQUENTIAL on an SD remain legal (Format 4 prints them).

subject: File control entry
notes: ALL FOUR SENTENCES OF GR3 MEASURED. (1) The TIMING lead - "The association occurs at the time of execution of an OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement that referenced file-name-1" - is FileRegistry.OpenCore's single Associate call, ahead of the Table-19 arbitration and OUTSIDE the RETRY loop (the content is read once per statement, not once per attempt); the SORT/MERGE implicit opens reach the same dispatch through CobolFile.OpenInput/OpenOutput. pb324_assign_using_dynamic moves two different names into data-name-1 and reads both files back through ONE connector, and its DELB=00 leg proves DELETE FILE acts on the association the last OPEN established rather than re-resolving. (2) GR3 a) - device-name-1/literal-1 "in the source unit that specifies the OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement" - is the non-dynamic arm of FileConnector.Associate(spec, dynamic), which the emitter feeds with the EXECUTING unit's own ASSIGN target rather than with whatever was registered first. (3) GR3 b) - data-name-1 "in the runtime element that executes the OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement" - is the dynamic arm, and the two PB673 goldens are what discriminate it: pb673_external_assign_executor has TWO programs describing ONE external file connector (13.18.22.4 GR4 a), the second activating LAST and the first executing the OPEN, and pins that the record lands in the EXECUTOR's file (CHKB=05, CHKA=00, READA=AAAAA); pb673_recursive_assign_linage does the same across ACTIVATIONS of one RECURSIVE unit whose data-name-1 is in LOCAL-STORAGE (CHKI=05, CHKO=00). Before kb/Work PB673 both answered with the last INSTALLER's data item, silently, at status 00. (4) The closing sentence - the statement is unsuccessful when the association cannot be made - is 9.1.13.6 item 2's '31', pinned by pb324_assign_using_dynamic's BLANK=31 leg. The CONTENT rules that decide when it cannot be made are GR4's implementor determination, adjudicated on its own row (docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-73 / DOC-A.1-10). EDITIONS, PER BRANCH (kb/Work PB746): GR3's lead sentence, a) and the closing sentence govern the ASSIGN TO clause at every edition; b) exists only where its phrase does, and the USING phrase is a COBOL-2002 introduction (kb/Work PB746): Annex E never names it, so it predates 2023, and GnuCOBOL 3.2's per-standard dialect files date it at 2002 (cobol85.conf assign-using-variable: unconformable; cobol2002.conf and cobol2014.conf: ok; cobc -std=cobol85 refuses `ASSIGN USING`) - constructs row assign-using-2002, VCR row 7.27; below 2002 the phrase is COBOLNET0900 on both arms (conformance:negative/pb746-assign-using-below-2002). b) rides conformance:2002/pb746_assign_using_2002 at its introducing edition. subject: General
notes: kb/Work PB692. "The DYNAMIC and RANDOM phrases shall not be specified for a sequential file" is a FILE CONTROL ENTRY rule, so it is enforced on the entry, in DataBinder.BindFileControl beside the clauses it relates, and not on any verb: it constrains the entry whether or not the file is ever read, written or started. Before this it had no enforcement anywhere (grep for the section number returned only generated-parser noise) and `SELECT F ASSIGN TO "f" ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM.` compiled and ran clean. BOTH PHRASES are screened, not just the one the repro wrote (negatives pb692-access-random-organization-sequential and pb692-access-dynamic-organization-sequential are the same entry with RANDOM and with DYNAMIC). ALL THREE SEQUENTIAL SPELLINGS are under it: an explicit ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL, LINE SEQUENTIAL (12.4.5.10.3 GR2 puts the phrase in the ORGANIZATION clause, that clause is written only in the Format 3 entry, and 12.4.5.2 SR11 says "Format 3 shall be specified only for a sequential file or a report file"), and the OMITTED clause, which 12.4.5.10.3 GR6 makes "sequential organization with the RECORD SEQUENTIAL phrase" - the omitted case is the shape a screen keyed on a written clause would miss, and negative pb692-access-dynamic-organization-omitted pins it. The predicate is FileModel.IsSequential, the one spelling of sequential organization, shared with the 12.4.5.9 SR2 screen beside it. Edition-invariant: no docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md row touches 12.4.5.5, ANSI X3.23-1985's sequential I-O file control entry likewise offered no ACCESS MODE but SEQUENTIAL, and each 4-edition negative asserts COBOLNET1858 at 85/2002/2014/2023 (the LINE SEQUENTIAL negative names 2023 ALONE because ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL is a COBOL-2023 introduction - at 85, 2002 and 2014 that source is rejected by kb/Work PB688's organization gate, COBOLNET0900, and this rule never gets to speak; the positive witness is a 2023 program for the same reason). The COMPLEMENT was measured, not assumed: a static scan of all 1483 SELECT entries under tests/ found the four cells this screen rejects EMPTY and every legal cell populated except LINE SEQUENTIAL with an explicit ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL, which had zero witnesses - conformance:2023/pb692_line_sequential_access_sequential is that missing positive. subject: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause
notes: RE-SITED 2026-09-06 (kb/Work PB699); rule unchanged. RULE (--check 12.4.5.6.3 1): "Data-name-1 and data-name-2 shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses." Same move as the RECORD KEY twin: the screen is a row of FileControlKeyRules' table, run at the ENTRY from DataBinder.ResolveFiles, and its subject list is FileModel.AlternateKeyNames - the clauses AS WRITTEN - rather than the resolved AlternateKeys, because a clause whose data-name-1 resolves to nothing is absent from the resolved list. As for the RECORD KEY twin, data-name-2 belongs to the SOURCE phrase, which the grammar does not admit and docs/CONFORMANCE.md 2 row 40 declines.

subject: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause
notes: LANDED 2026-09-06 (kb/Work PB743). RULE (--check 12.4.5.6.3 2): "Data-name-1 and data-name-2 shall be defined as a data item of category alphanumeric or national within a record description entry associated with the file-name to which the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause is subordinate." The prime key's twin, worded the same way with the same two obligations, and landed in the same change for the same reason. The asymmetry this closes was visible inside ONE method: KeyedIoBinder.KeyedValidateFile already wrote a CATEGORY screen for the RELATIVE key (12.4.5.13.3 SR2, an unsigned integer) and none for either record key. Both arms are now rows of FileControlKeyRules sharing this rule-id, screened at the ENTRY from DataBinder.ResolveFiles, over the clauses AS WRITTEN (FileModel.AlternateKeyNames) rather than the resolved AlternateKeys - a clause whose data-name-1 resolves to nothing is absent from the resolved list and is exactly the case the location arm speaks about. Boundary measured: a category-alphanumeric alternate key WITH DUPLICATES inside the record is accepted at all four editions, and the relative key's own category rule (which REQUIRES the unsigned integer this rule forbids) is measured beside it so the two cannot leak into each other.

subject: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause
notes: LANDED 2026-10-05 (kb/Work PB1073). RULE (--check 12.4.5.6.3 3): "Data-name-1 and data-name-2 shall not reference a variable-length data item." §8.5.1.11.1: a variable-length data item is "a dynamic-capacity table or a dynamic-length elementary item". FileControlKeyRules.Rules (AlternateRecordKey role) asks the key operand's IsDynamicLength attribute (COBOLNET0863). The dynamic-capacity-table arm is a key under OCCURS and SR1's row reports it (a dynamic-capacity table cannot be in a record at all, COBOLNET1526), so the row does not say the same fact twice; a GROUP containing a dynamic-length item is a variable-length GROUP, which the standard names separately where it means to forbid one (§12.4.5.8.3 SR3, §13.10.3 SR12) and does not name here, so it is accepted (the minimum-record-size rule, SR5, bounds it). Re-measured before the fix: probe sr3.cob compiled exit 0 and WRITE returned '00'.

subject: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause
notes: LANDED 2026-10-05 (kb/Work PB1073). RULE (--check 12.4.5.6.3 4): "Data-name-1 shall not reference an item whose leftmost byte position corresponds to the leftmost byte position of the prime record key, or of another alternate record key. This restriction does not apply in the case where either key is specified using the SOURCE phrase." FileControlKeyRules.Rules (AlternateRecordKey role, COBOLNET0863) compares each alternate clause's RecordLayout.KeyWindowInFile offset with the prime key's and with every OTHER alternate clause's (the operand carries its clause ordinal, so two clauses naming one item each violate it). The SOURCE exemption exempts a form this compiler declines (Annex A.3 item 40, COBOLNET1954), so no operand reaches the row through it. Positions are compared as the fixed-run offset plus whether a variable-length member precedes the key. Re-measured before the fix: sr4prime, sr4alt and sr4dupsame all compiled exit 0.

subject: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause
notes: CONFORMS, unchanged in substance and re-homed by kb/Work PB802 - the ALTERNATE-key twin of GR-12.4.5.12.4-3, carrying a SECOND requirement that one does not: 'The number of alternate record keys for the file shall also be the same as that used when the physical file was created.' Both halves are recorded and compared. IndexedConnector.DeclaredKeys puts every alternate key's window, DUPLICATES phrase, 12.4.5.6.4 GR6 SUPPRESS WHEN value and collating sequence into the FRAMED STORE'S HEADER in declaration order (the order key numbers are assigned in) - no longer into a .cbattr sidecar beside the file, but into the file itself, which is where GnuCOBOL's ISAM format keeps the same information. The SUPPRESS WHEN value is length-prefixed in the header rather than delimiter-separated, because GR6 admits any figurative-constant or literal value, including one carrying a NUL or a line ending; a legal COBOL program therefore cannot write a store its own next OPEN refuses. FixedFileAttributes.Conflicts compares the key COUNT before the descriptors, so an added or missing alternate index is itself the 14.9.27.4 GR10 file attribute conflict condition and the OPEN is unsuccessful with '39'. The descriptor's scope and its derivation are the same as GR-12.4.5.12.4-3's, and so is the COBOLNET_KEYCHECK=OFF opt-out (on by default; documented at DOC-A.1-129). Pinned by open_fixed_attribute_conflict_ix step I3 (a connector whose prime key agrees but which declares an ALTERNATE RECORD KEY the file was never built with gives '39') and by the unit test for the count requirement on its own - a description that simply OMITS the alternate, every key it does declare agreeing.

subject: LOCK MODE clause
notes: cite.py --check 12.4.5.9.4 6) 'Execution of any I-O statement except START releases any previously locked record in that file for that file connector' OK. Mode selection: MapLockMode sets Multiple only when the MULTIPLE token is present. So both `LOCK ON RECORD` (explicit single) and an omitted LOCK ON phrase (implicit single) give single locking, as the rule states. Release: ReleasePriorRecordLocks is the one site (skipped only when meta.Multiple). It runs at the top of ReadShared, ReadKeyedShared (l.1396), WriteShared (l.1428), RewriteShared (l.1455, except target) and DeleteShared (l.1499, except target), so it is tied to execution, not success (PB338 landed). The mutating verbs' 'except target' comes from their own statement rules (§14.9.35.4 GR12 a), §14.9.10.4 GR7 a)): the target's lock is released at completion instead. START is not routed through any release. CLOSE and UNLOCK release everything. Probe rt1.cob phase 1: A (AUTOMATIC single) read 1, then read 2, and B's read of 1 went from '51' to '00' (READ releases). A re-locked 1 and then did a WRITE of record 21; B's read of 1 was '00' (WRITE releases). The START exemption is witnessed by conformance:2023/l1_start_no_record_locks. conformance:2023/pb338_read_releases_prior_lock witnesses the READ release on all three organizations. unit:CobolFileLockTests.WriteShared_WithLock_LocksTheWrittenRecord_AndSingleLockingReleasesItOnTheNextWrite covers WRITE. The 'only one record locked at a time' consequence follows because every non-START statement releases first. kb/Work PB671 (open) owns the '§12.4.5.9 GR6' mis-citations (FileModel.cs:18, CobolFile.cs:296, PhysicalFileTable.cs:128 are sibling sites). subject: ORGANIZATION clause
notes: kb/Work PB688 (LANDED 2026-09-05). RULE: "The LINE SEQUENTIAL phrase specifies that the file organization is line sequential. Line sequential organization is a permanent logical file structure in which a record is identified by a predecessor-successor relationship established when the record is placed into the file. Each record in a line sequential file is terminated by an implementor-defined line delimiter. The range of allowable characters in a line sequential file is implementor-defined." cite.py --check 12.4.5.10.3 'The LINE SEQUENTIAL phrase specifies that the file organization is line sequential' -> OK 12.4.5.10.3 2). THE EDITION: the phrase is a COBOL-2023 introduction - the Foreword's list of the main changes this third edition makes over ISO/IEC 1989:2014 names "Line Sequential file organization" (specs/ISO_COBOL.md, the Foreword; Annex E carries no item for it, and it is NOT derivable from VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md, which has no 85->2002 row set). It is a PHRASE of the sequential organization and not a fourth organization: cite.py --check 9.1.7.1 'There are three file organizations: sequential, relative, and indexed' -> OK, and 9.1.7.2 splits the sequential one into its record- and line-delimited types - the { LINE | RECORD } inner choice of the 12.4.5.10.2 general format. MEASURED on the built cobol.exe: before, a SELECT with ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL compiled CLEAN at --std 85 (exit 0, .dll emitted); after, COBOLNET0900 at 85, 2002 and 2014 and clean at 2023. DataBinder.MapOrganization is the one recognition site (both grammar parents - the file control entry and the FD clause list - flow through the ONE VersionConformancePass.ParseArm.VisitOrganizationClause arm, pinned by the two negatives). subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "The RECORD DELIMITER clause may be specified only for variable-length records" is NOT enforced, and the licence is express rather than inferred. §4.2.6 ¶3, second sentence: "Although this warning mechanism shall identify processor-dependent elements that are not supported, it is not required to diagnose syntax errors within this unsupported syntax" (cite.py --check OK). The clause is unsupported whole — docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 26 for the STANDARD-1 arm (Annex A.3 item 26) and §7 A.1 item 150 for the feature-name arm — and COBOLNET1778 names it at every edition, which is the obligation §4.2.6 ¶3 does impose. Enforcing SR1 anyway was considered and REJECTED as a rejects-legal-source risk, not skipped: SR1's own NOTE makes variable-length-ness partly an implementor determination (A.1 items 147-148, both still open), and §9.1.7.2 makes a LINE SEQUENTIAL file's records variable with no RECORD clause written at all, so a test keyed on FileModel.Varying would refuse legal source in order to enforce a rule the standard excuses. The golden's four files are all SR1-legal (RECORD IS VARYING), so nothing here depends on the unenforced case.

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "The implementor shall specify the names available for use as feature-name-1" is DISCHARGED, and discharged in the negative: the set specified is EMPTY, filed as docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 Annex A.1 item 150. That is a specification and not an omission — A.1's preamble classes item 150 as optional and defines the class as "Optional: The element may be provided at the implementor's option" (cite.py --check A.1 OK). The compiler agrees with the register: every spelling written in the feature-name-1 position draws COBOLNET1778 naming the clause as unsupported, so no word is silently accepted as a delimiter selector and §12.4.5.11.4 GR4 never has a method to look up. The DOC row for the same obligation is DOC-A.1-150, whose verdict differs by design — that row asks whether the OPTIONAL ELEMENT is provided (it is not), this row asks whether the implementor answered the question (it did).

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "Any method used shall not be reflected in the record area or the record size used within the function, method, or program" is the rule that makes this implementation's method admissible, and the golden measures it directly. Records of 3 and 8 bytes are written to four variable-length files and read back; §13.18.43.4 GR15 stores the byte count of the record just read into the DEPENDING item, and the count read back is 03 then 08 on every file — the 4-byte little-endian length prefix (Annex A.1 item 151) is stripped before the record area is filled and never enters a record size the program can see. The DEPENDING item is deliberately forced to 99 before each READ so the measurement is GR15's stored count and not the leftover MOVE that sized the WRITE, and the displayed text is reference-modified to the reported length so nothing depends on what a short READ leaves in the tail of the area.

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "If STANDARD-1 is specified, the external medium shall be a tape drive" is unsatisfiable here and the non-support is documented: docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 26, whose ground is Annex A.3 item 26 — "The STANDARD-1 phrase of the RECORD DELIMITER clause is dependent upon a reel type of device" — and §4.2.6, which makes the decision to claim a processor-dependent element the implementor's, requires the absence to be specified in user documentation (this row), and adds that "Language elements that pertain to specific processor-dependent elements for which support is not claimed need not be implemented" (all cite.py --check OK). COBOL.NET provides no reel device at all — the same determination §2 rows 28-30 and 33-34 already record for CLOSE REEL/UNIT and OPEN WITH NO REWIND. The row closes on a DIAGNOSIS, not on silence: COBOLNET1778 is raised at bind for every occurrence at 85/2002/2014/2023, in both the IS and the optional-word-omitted spelling.

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "If STANDARD-1 is specified, the method used for determining the length of a variable-length record shall be that specified in ISO/IEC 1001:2012, 7.1.2" rides GR2's decline: the method is the tape-interchange framing of a standard this implementation neither implements nor could exercise, having no reel device (docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 26, Annex A.3 item 26). §4.2.6's "Language elements that pertain to specific processor-dependent elements for which support is not claimed need not be implemented" is the carry-over licence — the §4.2.6 analogue of Annex A.4.1's second paragraph, and it is what reaches from item 26's PHRASE to this rule. What happens instead is §12.4.5.11.4 GR5's implementor method, documented as Annex A.1 item 151 in §7. Witnessed by the named decline at every edition rather than by silence.

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause

The licence is NOT Annex A.3 — item 26 reaches only the STANDARD-1 phrase — but Annex A.1 item 150, which the standard classes as optional ("This item is optional"), read with A.1's preamble ("Optional: The element may be provided at the implementor's option") and §4.2.7's obligation to identify what is claimed. docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 A.1 item 150 records the determination as "Not provided.", which is exactly the shape owner decision kb/Work PB280 Q1 (2026-09-02) closes as DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT through the `a1-optional-not-provided` selector. subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "If the RECORD DELIMITER clause is not specified, the method used for determining the length of a variable-length record is specified by the implementor" — specified, and now documented, as Annex A.1 item 151 in docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7: a 4-byte little-endian binary length prefix per record for record sequential, relative and indexed files (one implementation, RecordFraming, shared by every organization), and the line delimiter for LINE SEQUENTIAL, which is §9.1.7.2's own rule. The licence to add a header at all is §9.1.7.2 ("In record sequential files the length of each record is determined by any information the implementor may add to the record on the physical storage medium (such as record length headers)"); the §9.1.13.6 "externally-defined boundaries" sentence that RecordFraming's header used to cite is the I-O status 34 rule about writing past a FILE's end and was corrected in this change set. GR5's ANTECEDENT is witnessed directly: golden file F4 writes no RECORD DELIMITER clause, draws no diagnostic (asserted as the complement) and reads its 3- and 8-byte records back at those lengths.

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "At the time of a successful execution of an OPEN statement, the record delimiter is the one specified in the RECORD DELIMITER clause in the file control entry associated with the file-name specified in the OPEN statement" — no delimiter is established at OPEN, because neither alternative of the clause is supported (GR2/GR3 by Annex A.3 item 26 and §4.2.6; GR4 by Annex A.1 item 150 and §4.2.7). §4.2.6's "Language elements that pertain to specific processor-dependent elements for which support is not claimed need not be implemented" carries the decline to this rule. notes: RE-SITED 2026-09-06 (kb/Work PB699); rule unchanged. RULE (--check 12.4.5.12.3 1): "Data-name-1 and data-name-2 shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses." The screen MOVED from KeyedIoBinder.KeyedValidateFile - which ran on the first KEYED VERB naming the file, so an entry whose prime key sat under OCCURS compiled with zero diagnostics when the procedure division only OPENed and CLOSEd it (measured) - to FileControlKeyRules, one table keyed by organization and key role, run from DataBinder.ResolveFiles over every declared file. conformance:negative/pb699-record-key-occurs-entry-only is the discriminator against the older pb354 case, which contains a READ. subject: RECORD KEY clause
notes: LANDED 2026-09-06 (kb/Work PB743) - the CATEGORY arm, which is what earns the verdict PB699 deliberately withheld. RULE (--check 12.4.5.12.3 2): "Data-name-1 and data-name-2 shall reference a data item of category alphanumeric or category national within a record description entry associated with the file-name specified in this file control entry." ONE sentence, TWO obligations joined by the word "within": a CATEGORY and a LOCATION. PB699 implemented the LOCATION half and left the row without a verdict rather than over-claiming; measured with only that half live, an indexed file whose RECORD KEY was PIC 9(5) compiled clean, ran, and wrote '00' - it built an index on an operand the standard forbids as a key. Now TWO ROWS carry this rule-id, one per arm, and FileControlKeyRuleDriftTests.ARuleWithTwoObligations_HasARowForEachArm re-derives the split FROM THE PRINTED SENTENCE so a rule that grows a third obligation reddens instead of shipping two thirds. The category predicate is ItemCategory.IsAlphanumericOrNational - the ONE 8.5.2 category reader, extracted from DataBinder in the same change and now shared with 12.4.5.2 SR7's ASSIGN ... USING screen - which admits an alphanumeric group item (13.18.29.4 GR3: "If a GROUP-USAGE clause is not specified or implied ... that group item is an alphanumeric group item") and a GROUP-USAGE NATIONAL group, and refuses alphabetic (PicInfo.IsAlphabetic; the storage model folds PIC A into PicCategory.Alphanumeric, so a bare category comparison would have passed it), numeric, numeric-edited, boolean and the PICTURE-less usages. Alphanumeric-edited has no PicCategory member and is therefore admitted - the established posture for a category screen here (RecordLayout.CategoryOfItem, 14.9.41.3 SR6 b) 2.): the screen rejects what the rule NAMES, never what the model cannot classify. DATA-NAME-2 is the SOURCE phrase's operand and has no reachable spelling (docs/CONFORMANCE.md 2 row 40 declines A.3 item 40), and SR2's third sentence ("All occurrences of data-name-2 shall be of the same category") is about it alone.

subject: RECORD KEY clause
notes: CONFORMS, unchanged in substance and re-homed by kb/Work PB802. The rule - 'The data description of data-name-1 or data-name-2 as well as their relative location within a record shall be the same as that used when the file was created' (note: 'the file', not 'the physical file'; 12.4.5.6.4 GR3 is the one worded 'the physical file', and the inherited quotation that gave both the same wording is corrected here) - states a requirement and no consequence where it is written; 14.9.27.4 GR10's file attribute conflict condition is the mechanism that detects a violation. WHAT CHANGED: the prime key's descriptor is no longer written into a .cbattr catalog sidecar beside the data file but into the framed store's own HEADER, which RecordFraming.WriteStore stamps from the writing connector's DeclaredAttributes on every persist - so the file itself carries its key geometry, as a real ISAM file does, and nothing exists beside it that could outlive it. FixedFileAttributes.Conflicts compares it on every later OPEN and a mismatch is the unsuccessful OPEN with I-O status '39' (9.1.13.6 item 7). THE RECORDED DESCRIPTOR IS THE KEY'S WINDOW PLUS ITS COLLATING SEQUENCE, and that is the whole of 'the data description ... as well as their relative location' this implementation can act on: 12.4.5.12.3 SR2 confines a record key to category alphanumeric or category national, 12.4.5.12.4 GR1 makes key equality a relation condition under the file's collating sequence (recorded by weights - FixedFileAttributes.Fingerprint), and both native sequences are one code-unit ordinal over the UTF-16 substrate (CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-33 / DOC-A.1-188), so two descriptions sharing a window and a sequence order every key value identically whatever their category. NEW: the comparison of the key table alone can be turned off for a run by COBOLNET_KEYCHECK=OFF, GnuCOBOL's COB_KEYCHECK opt-out under this repository's naming, documented as part of the A.1 item 129 determination (DOC-A.1-129) - by default it is on, so the rule is enforced unless a run explicitly asks otherwise. Pinned by open_fixed_attribute_conflict_ix step I2 (a six-byte prime key window over a file created with a four-byte one gives '39') and by the unit theory's prime-window arm.

Covering test: conformance:2002/pb354_start_generic_key_ok case K2 STARTs by an item at the prime key's identical byte positions in a SECOND record description and its expected record is derived from this GR (and §14.9.41.3 SR6 a). || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The data-name-1 half is verified and holds in every shape probed, but the rule names 'data-name-1 OR data-name-2'. The data-name-2 half (the SOURCE key form) is refused by COBOLNET1954 as the Annex A.3 item 40 decline. notes: kb/Work PB643 (landed, wave 1020 B). cite.py --check 12.4.5.14.3 "If the RESERVE clause is specified, the number of input-output areas allocated is equal to the value of integer-1" -> OK §12.4.5.14.3 1); "If the RESERVE clause is not specified, the number of input-output areas allocated is specified by the implementor" -> OK. Measured before the fix (probe E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/w1020b/probes/r1.cob, r4.cob): RESERVE 1 and RESERVE 4 both let a sibling reader see 64 of 100 64-byte records written under SHARING WITH READ ONLY (the 4,096-byte host buffer whatever the clause said). After: RESERVE 1 AREA 064, RESERVE 2 AREAS 000, 100 after CLOSE, 100 under SHARING WITH ALL OTHER (conformance:2002/pb643_reserve_areas_visibility, 2002/2014/2023 identical); every organization round-trips through its areas at 85 (conformance:85/pb643_reserve_areas_all_organizations). subject: SHARING clause
notes: GR1 (cite.py --check 12.4.5.15.3 OK): "The SHARING clause specifies the sharing mode to be used for the file unless it is overridden by the SHARING phrase of the OPEN statement. This clause also specifies whether record locks have an effect. Additional details are specified in 9.1.15". THREE halves, each verified: (a) clause sets the mode — DataBinder MapSharing -> FileModel.Sharing -> EmitSharingRegistration -> FileRegistry.RegisterSharing; SharedOpenAttempt uses `sharingOverride ?? registered meta.Sharing ?? ImplementorDefaultSharing`. Probe p1.cob: clause NO OTHER on A -> second connector's OPEN INPUT = 61; clause READ ONLY on B -> another INPUT = 00, EXTEND = 61 (§9.1.15 1)/2), cite.py OK). (b) override — OpenShared passes hasSharingOverride ? sharingOverride : null (§9.1.15 "The SHARING phrase on an OPEN statement overrides the SHARING clause", cite.py OK). Probe: clause NO OTHER + OPEN INPUT SHARING WITH ALL OTHER -> other INPUT open 00; clause ALL OTHER + OPEN SHARING NO OTHER -> other INPUT open 61. (c) record-lock effect — LocksEffective returns false when the EFFECTIVE (post-override) open sharing is NoOther (§9.1.15 1) "Record locks are ignored"; 2)/3) "Record locks are in effect"). Probe p2.cob: READ ONLY + LOCK MODE MANUAL, A READ WITH LOCK then B plain READ -> 51 (locks in effect under READ ONLY); ALL OTHER in-effect covered by conformance:2002/file_sharing (READB=51). The NO OTHER 'ignored' arm is verified by reading only — it is essentially unobservable, since exclusive access excludes any second connector that could meet the lock. Side note (not this rule's defect): FileModel.cs line 13 doc comment says the implementor default is 'COBOL.NET: ALL OTHER' while the runtime's ImplementorDefaultSharing is null/undetermined (kb/Work PB321/PB322) — stale comment. No kb/Work note owns open rows here; PB319 (landed) removed a duplicated §14.9.27.3 SR8 check from the SELECT binder; re-confirmed absent (DataBinder.cs ~1110-1125) and the SR8 check fires only at OPEN (probe: COBOLNET1512 at the OPEN of F-D, not the SELECT).

subject: SAME clause
notes: OWNER DECISION, kb/Work PB371, 2026-09-02 — CONFORMS + a witness pinning the refusal. §12.4.6.4.3 SR11: "A file or record area that is subject to an APPLY COMMIT clause shall not be specified with another file or record area that is not subject to an APPLY COMMIT clause." The SAME clause (§12.4.6.4) is CLAIMED and supported; the antecedent is the APPLY COMMIT clause, Annex A.4.3 item 2, refused by name (COBOLNET1709). No accepted program can put a file in an APPLY COMMIT clause, so the rule cannot be violated. ⛔ NOT DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT — the verdict field would speak about SAME, a claimed facility; see the `commit-and-rollback-only` selector, which names this row among its exclusions. Editions 2023: the APPLY COMMIT clause is a COBOL-2023 addition (Annex E.3.2 item 2). kb/Work PB666 (w1031 group G): the PB371 vacuity holds only in the strict lane - COBOLNET1709 is PermissiveInert, so under --permissive the fixture's SAME clause mixing subject and non-subject files on a file subject to an APPLY COMMIT clause compiled with zero errors. The rule is now enforced in its own right in both lanes: DataBinder.ScreenApplyCommitSubject (COBOLNET2974), the one report for the family. cite.py --check 12.4.6.4.3 11) OK. Witness: ApplyCommitSubjectRuleTests compiles the negative fixture under --permissive and asserts COBOLNET2974 naming this rule.

subject: SAME clause
notes: The existing golden cites GR1: files under SAME AREA are opened strictly one at a time and each keeps its own records (sharing is unobservable; §14.9.6.4 7)).

subject: SAME clause
notes: cite.py --check 12.4.6.4.4 "A logical record in the shared memory area is a logical record of each file open in the output mode and of the most recently-read file open in the input mode" -> OK GR2; cite.py --check 12.4.6.4.4 "This is equivalent to an implicit redefinition of the area with records aligned on the leftmost byte position" -> OK GR2. BindIoControl chains each listed file's first record as an implicit RedefinitionKind.SameRecordArea redefinition of the first listed file's record (the multi-01 FD mechanism) and records SameRecordAreaPeers for out-of-line records (D-FRA). Probe gr2_mixed (SEQUENTIAL X(4) / RELATIVE X(2)+X(6) / LINE SEQUENTIAL X(10)): MOVE to F3-REC shows F1=ABCD F2A=AB F2B=CDEFGH (leftmost alignment across unequal lengths); MOVE to F1-REC shows F3=WXYZEFGHIJ; after READ F2 F1-REC=1234, after READ F1 F2-A=WX (most-recently-read file's record occupies the area). Availability sentence (area available while any member open) and the most-recently-read sentence pinned by conformance:85/pb235_same_record_area_close (spec-derived, CLOSE GR7 + this GR2); RELEASE interplay by conformance:2023/l1_release_same_record_area. The 'only one file also in a file-area SAME clause may be open' sentence is a program constraint (no specified check). Residual: a record shape with a byte-window residue is still refused loud COBOLNET0899 (DataBinder ByteWindowResidueOf; since PB981 pointer/dynamic-length/national shapes ride, so no conforming shape is known to reach it) - noted, not a measured defect. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the SAME clause is base I-O-CONTROL language in every edition; no Annex E change entry names it)]

subject: SAME clause
notes: OWNER DECISION, kb/Work PB371, 2026-09-02 — CONFORMS + a witness pinning the refusal. §12.4.6.4.4 GR3: "The file and record area of a file subject to commit and rollback may not be shared with another such file or record area unless it has been closed, a commit or a rollback has been executed and the APPLY COMMIT clause for the file has been deactivated." ⚠ ITS SHAPE IS NOT SR-12.4.6.4.3-11'S and it therefore gets its OWN witness: SR11 forbids mixing a commit-subject file with one that is NOT subject, while GR3 says "another SUCH file" — BOTH files subject to commit and rollback. The SAME clause (§12.4.6.4) is CLAIMED and supported; the antecedent is the APPLY COMMIT clause (ISO §12.4.6.3), Annex A.4.3 item 2, refused BY NAME by COBOLNET1709, so no file is ever subject to the facility and the rule cannot be violated. ⛔ NOT DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT: the verdict field would speak about SAME, a claimed facility, and §4.2.7 discharges non-support through user documentation that declines commit and rollback — never SAME. The `commit-and-rollback-only` derived selector names this row among its exclusions for that reason. Editions 2023: the APPLY COMMIT clause is a COBOL-2023 addition (Annex E.3.2 item 2).

subject: SAME clause
notes: cite.py --check 12.4.6.4.4 "The extent of such allocation shall be specified by the implementor" -> OK GR4 b). GR4 a)/b) are storage-reuse PERMISSIONS (sort work storage 'is available for reuse'; non-sort file areas 'may be allocated as needed'), c) says non-sort files' areas do NOT share with each other. subject: Constant entry
notes: kb/Work PB1231 (w1007c), extended by kb/Work PB1941 (w1032a). cite.py --check 13.10.3 "The length of data-name-1 or data-name-2 shall not be dependent, directly or indirectly, upon the value of constant-name-1" -> OK SR4. The constant table is not filled in declaration order: every constant entry is declared before anything binds (DataBinder.DeclareDataEntries), FindConstant binds one on demand, and a length phrase may measure an item described later. A later RECORD is bound out of source order (BindLaterRecords); since PB1941 a later entry of the record STILL BEING DESCRIBED is bound ahead at the granularity of its own entry (BindLaterEntriesOfOpenRecord: the entry and its subordinates, plus each group entry between it and its nearest bound ancestor, linked to that ancestor and attached by the walk at their source position; a group bound alone is completed before it is measured, CompletePreboundGroup). The circular shapes are refused BY NAME: `01 K CONSTANT AS LENGTH OF W. 01 W PIC X(K).` (IsBeingDescribed), `01 G. 05 G1 PIC X(KG). 01 KG CONSTANT AS LENGTH OF G.` (IsDescriptionOpen), a constant cycle through a length phrase (ReportConstantCycle), and inside an open record `01 R. 05 A PIC X(K). 05 W. 10 WA PIC X(K). 01 K CONSTANT AS LENGTH OF W.` -> COBOLNET1547 '... (ISO 13.10.3 SR4)' (negatives pb1231-constant-length-cycle, pb1941-constant-length-cycle-open-record at 2002/2014/2023). The legal neighbours compile: A is X(7) with W in a later record, and inside one open record R: K = LENGTH OF W OF G = 7, KG = LENGTH OF G = 20 (G holds Z PIC X(K): G depends on K, never on KG), KT = BYTE-LENGTH OF TE (2) = 2, R = 57 (golden pb1941_constant_length_inside_open_record). Residue (not SR4's rule, the forward-reference service, kb/Work PB1941): an operand SUBORDINATE to the very entry whose description references the constant (`05 A OCCURS K. 10 W PIC X(4).`) is COBOLNET0899 constant-length-operand-bound-later.

subject: Data description entry
notes: kb/Work PB513 - LANDED (wave 39). SR14's permitted set is now ONE constant, DataClauseKinds.TypeCoPermitted, read over the entry's WRITTEN clause set (DataDescriptionEntryCst.WrittenClauses) exactly as SR12's SameAsCoPermitted is, and the guard sits in BindEntry beside SR12's: COBOLNET2150, which NAMES the offending clause instead of restating the permitted list. subject: Data description entry
notes: kb/Work PB488 -- the row was CONFORMS-BUT-UNTESTED and this landing supplies the spec-derived witnesses, one per arm. LEVEL-NUMBER 1: RegisterTypeDecl rejects a TYPEDEF root whose Level is not 1 (COBOLNET1529, 'a type declaration shall be a level-01 record-description entry') and BindEntries' non-root arm rejects item.IsTypedef on any entry that lands under an open parent (COBOLNET1529, 'the TYPEDEF clause shall be specified only in a level-01 record-description entry'), so the level-77 spelling (pb488-typedef-level-77) and the subordinate spelling (pb488-typedef-subordinate) are both refused. DATA-NAME FORMAT OF THE ENTRY-NAME CLAUSE: RegisterTypeDecl rejects a null CobolName -- an omitted or FILLER entry-name, the OTHER format of the entry-name clause (13.18.20) -- with COBOLNET1529 and returns without registering, so no anonymous type-name can exist (pb488-typedef-filler). Each negative was measured to carry COBOLNET1529 at 2002, 2014 and 2023; below 2002 the TYPEDEF clause draws its own introduction gate instead, which is why the row's editions are 2002,2014,2023. The WELL-FORMED spelling is exercised positively by 2023/pb488_condition_name_associations_ok, whose `01 T IS TYPEDEF STRONG.` / `01 V TYPE T.` pair compiles and whose member is moved and read through the TYPE reference -- so the rule is pinned in both directions rather than only by rejections.

subject: Data description entry

subject: Data description entry
notes: kb/Work PB488 LANDED. BOTH obligations of SR24 now have a site, in ONE place. (1) THE ASSOCIATION SENTENCE. BindEntries tracks `lastDescribed` -- the entry the level-88 entry IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWS, which is the rule's own subject -- instead of the level stack's top. The two coincide for every entry that opens or extends the level hierarchy and DIVERGE exactly for the entries that never enter the stack: a level-66 alias, a 13.10 constant entry, and the start of a section. Those divergences were the measured wrong answers. An 88 with no preceding entry describing a data item now draws COBOLNET1977 instead of being dropped silently and surfacing as a run-time NotImplementedCobolFeatureException. (2) THE EIGHT EXCLUSIONS are ONE TABLE, DataBinder.Sr24Exclusions -- one row per letter in the standard's order carrying the standard's words -- walked by ConditionalVariableExclusion, which returns the first matching row; the diagnostic COBOLNET1976 names the letter and quotes it. a) holds by construction (the 88 arm leaves `lastDescribed` alone, so a run of consecutive 88s shares one conditional variable, which is the rule's own plural) and the drift test verifies the predicate directly, since no DataItem in the forest carries level 88. b) the level-66 alias is now handed to the screen instead of stepped over (BindRenames returns it). c) ItemCategory.IsAlphanumericGroup (3.11's four-exclusion definition, 13.18.29.4 GR3 -- NOT 'IsGroup with GroupUsage.None', which over-included a variable-length and a strongly-typed group, kb/Work PB947) plus a subordinate at any depth whose usage is not DISPLAY -- a bit or national GROUP member counts, 13.18.29.4 GR1/GR2 treating it as an elementary item of usage bit/national. d) any group with a JUSTIFIED or SYNCHRONIZED subordinate, AND the group's OWN SYNCHRONIZED clause: 13.18.55.3 SR1 permits it there and 13.18.55.4 GR1 makes it a description of the members, and the binder does not propagate the flag, so a members-only screen would miss `01 G SYNCHRONIZED.` entirely. e) resolved through 13.18.60.3 SR4's OWN predicate Sr4PhraseOf -- SR4's six USAGE phrases produce exactly SR24 e)'s four classes -- reading the WRITTEN clause as well as the resolved Pic, because MESSAGE-TAG and FUNCTION-POINTER never gain a PicInfo. f) DataItem.IsAnyLength. g) the DECLARATION-side TypedefStrong, sharing UnderStrongTypeDeclaration with 13.18.60.3 SR14, whose second arm is the same words; the second arm is confined to GROUP items, so an elementary member of a strong template may still be a conditional variable. h) delegates to VariableLengthCompatibility.IsVariableLength (the group kind c) now subtracts, so c) and h) are disjoint), which IS 8.5.1.12.1's definition -- a group with a dynamic-length elementary item or a dynamic-capacity table subordinate -- NOT an occurs-depending-on group, which the standard names separately (13.18.12.3 SR2 lists the three side by side). IT IS A POST-BIND PASS (BindPipeline, PassPhase.UsageResolved) and could not be a test inside BindCondition: four of the eight exclusions ask about the conditional variable's SUBORDINATES, and a condition-name on a group is written BEFORE them, so parent.Children is still empty at bind time. UNGATED across the four editions -- COBOL-85's own condition-name rule states the same exclusions for every shape COBOL-85 can write, and the later letters name constructs their own introduction gates already refuse below their edition. OVER-REJECTION MEASURED: all 80 corpus programs that write a level-88 entry (conformance + NIST) were recompiled and not one draws COBOLNET1976/1977. kb/Work PB947 LANDED: the lettered quotation is now pinned per letter (each pb488-cond-var-* .err names its letter, because every letter produces COBOLNET1976) and a variable-length group holding a non-DISPLAY member quotes h) and never c).

notes: kb/Work PB522 LANDED — the implication and its ANTECEDENT are both correct now. THE IMPLICATION itself was always right: UsageInheritancePass walks every group child of a group whose GroupUsage is set and applies `if (c.GroupUsage is GroupUsage.None) c.GroupUsage = item.GroupUsage;` BEFORE the recursive descent, so it is transitive; conformance:2023/pb79_group_usage_bit pins the direct arm (SUB-LEN=4, derived from 13.18.29.4 GR1b + 15.50.4 r1). WHAT WAS PARTIAL, AND IS NOW CLOSED: the antecedent 'subordinate to a bit group' was destroyed whenever the bit group arrived through a description COPY — DataItem.GroupUsage was absent from BOTH copy helpers (CopyEntryDescription, the shared 13.18.57.4 GR1 / 13.18.49.4 GR1 body, and CloneItem, the per-node subordinate clone), so `01 BDEF IS TYPEDEF GROUP-USAGE BIT. 02 BT1. 03 BB PIC 1(3) USAGE BIT.` + `01 VIA-BIT TYPE BDEF.` measured LEN-VIABIT=1 / LEN-BT1=1 where the spec requires 3 and 3, and the SAME AS twin measured LEN-BDST=1 / LEN-BG-DST=1 against a correct LEN-BSRC=5. GROUP-USAGE (13.18.29) is in NEITHER GR-1 exclusion list — 13.18.57.4 GR1 excludes only the level-number, name, alignment, GLOBAL, SELECT WHEN and TYPEDEF; 13.18.49.4 GR1 only the level-number, name, CONSTANT RECORD, EXTERNAL, GLOBAL, REDEFINES and SELECT WHEN — and 13.18.49.4 GR4 propagating a GROUP-USAGE from data-name-1's SUPERORDINATE confirms the clause is meant to travel. THE FIX is structural, at the ONE place the rule belongs: CopyEntryDescription is now the only copy and CloneItem funnels through it (its initializer carries identity, the renumbered level and the MemberOnly fields alone), and every stored DataItem property carries a [DescriptionCopy] classification with its citing reason, enforced behaviourally by unit:DescriptionCopyCompletenessDriftTests. notes: kb/Work PB501 LANDED, both arms. GR3 says a format-3 entry carries 'the name of the condition AND the value, values, or range of values associated with the condition-name', and a level-88 entry was never screened against its own general format, so an entry missing EITHER constituent reached the backend. Arm 1 (no value-clause, `88 NOVAL.`) was closed by kb/Work PB485/PB829 -- COBOLNET1747 from LevelNumberPass, re-measured on this worktree. Arm 2 (no condition-name, `88 VALUE 1.`) is closed here, in the same pass and under the same code, because it is the same rule's other half: 13.16.2 was RENDERED from the printed page (folio 364 / PDF p394) and format 3 prints condition-name-1 UNBRACKETED while format 4 brackets condition-name-2; format 4's licence to omit the name is not free-standing, since its value-clause is 13.18.63.2 format 5 whose figure ends in a REQUIRED { INVALID / VALID } choice. So a nameless 88 with no VALID/INVALID phrase is neither format and 13.16.3 SR24 leaves no third possibility. MEASURED on this worktree's own build at 85 and 2023: `88 VALUE 1.` and `88 VALUE 07.` -> COBOLNET1747 naming both formats (both compiled CLEAN and produced a .dll before -- BindCondition returns on a missing data-name and the entry evaporated). Over-rejection measured too: the legal format-3 spellings (single literal, THRU range, literal list, a condition-name over a GROUP conditional variable) all compile and evaluate correctly, and the format-4 spelling `88 VALUE 1 THRU 9 IS VALID.` still draws its own A.4.14 decline (COBOLNET1708), not this screen. RenderCondition88 is now TOTAL over an empty value set -- it rendered the two-character fragment `()`, so the generated source read `if (())` and the user got CS1525 against a .g.cs path; an empty association can only be false (13.16.4 GR3).

subject: ALIGNED clause
notes: 'The ALIGNED clause may be specified only for a bit group item or an elementary bit data item.' The subject predicate is BitLayout.IsBitItem - the SAME predicate 8.5.1.6.3's layout walk uses, since the rule asks the same question in the same words, so the rule that decides whether ALIGNED is legal and the walk that implements it cannot disagree. Adjudicated in a POST-FOREST pass, not BindEntry, because a group becomes a bit group by 13.16.4 GR1 inheritance which UsageInheritancePass settles. A violation clears IsAligned so the item lays out by the default rules under an already-failed compile. COBOLNET1942. kb/Work PB487.

subject: ALIGNED clause
notes: 'aligned on the first bit of the first available byte boundary. Implicit filler bits may be generated ... as described in 8.5.1.6.3.' One conjunct on THE one placement predicate: an ALIGNED subject never shares its predecessor's byte, and the round-up every caller already performs does the rest. The predicate was previously written out THREE times - BitLayout.ExtentBits, BitLayout.StartBitWithin and DataBinder.AssignClassOffsets - and is now a single method all three call, so an item's OFFSET, the group's EXTENT and a REDEFINES view of it cannot disagree. Golden derivation: 05 B1 PIC 1(4) BIT. 05 B2 PIC 1(4) BIT ALIGNED. occupies 12 bits padded by rule 4 to 16, so FUNCTION LENGTH is 2 where without ALIGNED it is 1 - measured 2.

subject: ALIGNED clause
notes: 'An ALIGNED clause specified for a multiple-occurrence data item applies to each occurrence of that item.' The per-occurrence STRIDE therefore rounds up to a byte while the WIDTH stays the declared bit count; the two were one number at every subscript site (ReferenceResolver, CallBinder, InitializeBinder, OdoModel, GroupValueSlicer) and are now split by BitLayout.StrideBits. RunBits counts stride x (n-1) + width, never stride x n, because 8.5.1.6.3 generates trailing filler only 'to advance alignment ... for the NEXT item'. Golden derivation: 05 T PIC 1(4) BIT OCCURS 3 ALIGNED. places occurrences at bits 0, 8, 16 for an extent of 20 padded to 24, so FUNCTION LENGTH is 3 where without ALIGNED it is 2 - measured 3, with each occurrence read back at its own value.

subject: BLANK WHEN ZERO clause
notes: kb/Work PB566 LANDED 2026-09-20. GR1 blanks on THE VALUE BEING STORED. The determination: 14.9.25.4 GR6 d)'s closing paragraph sends the store to 14.6.8, and 14.6.8.2 r4 transfers 'with zero fill or truncation on either end as required', so a sending value that truncates away to zero at EITHER end stores zero (13.18.8.1 says the same in one line). The guard used to test the raw (value, valueScale) sending pair before the mask rescale, so the MOVE arm rendered digits where the arithmetic arms - whose emitters hand Format a value already at the resultant's scale - blanked on identical items; it now sits AFTER the store rescale in the ONE shared formatter (CobolEdit.Render), testing the stored digit string, which is the same value rule 7 b)'s all-suppressed test beside it already read. Siblings swept the same way: CobolLocaleEdit.Format (r10's short-circuit now runs on r14's aligned value, and r15 b with it, both still before any locale is consulted); CobolEdit.Float's two arms already tested the stored value (the significand's leading digit is nonzero after normalization, and 14.9.25.4 GR6 d) 4 b treats an underflow as zero) and now say so. Measured on the golden at --std 85: low-order truncation (0.4 into PIC ZZZ9 and into PIC 9(3)), high-order truncation (100 into PIC 99 blanks, 101 shows '01'), a negative sender, a floating-currency mask, VALUE 0 initialization (13.18.63.4 GR8's NOTE), the INITIALIZE verb (14.9.20.4 GR6 c), and COMPUTE / MULTIPLY GIVING agreeing with MOVE on the same two items.

That arm is presently unobservable - national-form numeric data is refused upstream as a Phase-4a residue (COBOLNET0899 / DiagnosticCatalog.NationalData at PictureAnalyzer.cs:252, probe a5) - so this is a LATENT gap that will surface silently when national numeric lands, not a live wrong answer. subject: BLANK WHEN ZERO clause
notes: kb/Work PB509 LANDED 2026-09-20. BOTH ARMS NOW. The MOVE / de-editing arm was already right (14.9.25.4 GR6 d) 1: every digit position of an all-spaces image contributes zero, which IS GR3's zero). The relation arm was not: ConditionRenderer took the first arm whose operand IsString, and a numeric-edited operand is a string operand, so the whole relation became a character comparison and nothing asked whether the sender was blanked. THE DERIVATION for the reading implemented: GR1 says 'receiving operand' one rule earlier where GR3 says 'the object of an OPERATION', and 8.8.4.2.1 13) calls a relation's two operands its subject and its object; the MOVE receiver case is already legislated by 14.9.25.4 GR6 d) 1, and 8.8.1.1 admits only 'an identifier referencing a numeric data item' into an arithmetic expression - so the relation condition is the operation GR3 adds. GR3 naming a numeric-EDITED object is what settles that the comparison there is BY VALUE (8.8.4.2.4): giving the blanked item 'the value zero' changes nothing in a character comparison. subject: CODE-SET clause
notes: GR1 names the clause's purpose: alphabets used to convert medium-to-native on input and native-to-medium on output. DETERMINATION, documented (CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 27), and it is a PROPERTY OF THE SET rather than a list of phrase names in the file-description binder - CodedCharacterSet.Medium answers it once for every reference site. IDENTITY (claimed, no conversion emitted): NATIVE (12.3.7.4 GR7 d, by definition), STANDARD-1/STANDARD-2 (GR7 c - the native set's first 128 characters ARE ISO/IEC 646 IRV), UTF-16 (the D-N1 substrate) and the ASCII code-name (the same set as STANDARD-1). TRANSLATED (claimed, and real - kb/Work PB793): the EBCDIC code-name, whose GR7 i correspondence with the native set is IBM CCSID 37, converts every record crossing the medium. NOT-PROVIDED: a literal-phrase alphabet's remapped ordinals (GR7 k4 leaves that correspondence to the implementor and this one does not define it) and UTF-8 / UCS-4 as variable-width medium encodings are the DOCUMENTED Annex A A.3 item 27 non-support - COBOLNET1672, never a silent identity (the negative). Rule --check verified at 13.18.13.4 1).

subject: CODE-SET clause
notes: GR2 - on successful OPEN the coded character set used to represent alphanumeric data on the storage medium is alphabet-name-1's. The set is established for the CONNECTOR and constant thereafter, so it is registered once beside the connector (FileConnector.CodeSet, the FileConnector.NationalRecordArea pattern) rather than re-derived per record; for an identity set nothing is registered at all and the record channel is unchanged byte for byte. The EBCDIC golden observes it in both directions: the same physical file read back through a description carrying NO CODE-SET clause yields the medium's own code units (GR7's default), which is what shows the clause established a DIFFERENT set for the first connector.

subject: CODE-SET clause
notes: GR3 - with no SELECT WHEN clause among the record description entries (this grammar has none, so it is EVERY case here), the specified alphabet is used for code-set conversion of ALL data items in each record. The conversion is therefore applied to the whole record image at the medium boundary rather than item by item, which is the same thing for a record whose elementary items are all usage display - 13.18.13.3 SR3 a requires exactly that of a file whose CODE-SET names alphabet-name-1 and which has record description entries, and it is checked (COBOLNET1672). What is NOT converted is the framing this processor adds AROUND the record - the 9.1.7.2 record-length header of a VARYING or keyed file, and a line sequential file's delimiter - because that is not data of the record; the determination is published in CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 27.

subject: COLUMN clause
notes: Rule: printable-size = columns for the characters the PICTURE describes, or, with no PICTURE, the VALUE literal; one column per alphanumeric character (cite.py --check 13.18.14.4 'in the absence of a PICTURE clause, the literal specified in the VALUE clause' -> OK 3)). The emitter advances the horizontal counter by PrintItem.DisplayTextWidth. Probe p5.cob (2023) with each item followed by a relative '|': PIC 9(3)V99 -> 5 columns ('01234', V occupies none), PIC S999 SIGN LEADING SEPARATE -> 4 ('-012'), PIC -ZZ9.99 -> 7 ('- 12.34'), PIC S999 (embedded sign) -> 3, PIC N(2) -> 2: output '01234|-012|- 12.34|01K|AB|' - every boundary exact. Probe p1.cob: `COLUMN 3 VALUE "ABC"` (no PICTURE) occupied 3-5 and `COLUMN PLUS 2` then landed at 7. NOTE 1 is informative. No spec-derived golden isolates printable-size; test-needed. || Code sites (adjudicator detail): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/DataItem.cs#DisplayTextWidth; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/ReportWriterEmitter.cs#EmitFieldPlacements; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Reports.cs (line-width loop ~2690)

subject: COLUMN clause
notes: (kb/Work PB1220, wave 1005 A). ReportColumnSpec.AbsoluteLeftmost is the ONE computation of GR6 b)-d): LEFT integer-1; RIGHT integer-1 - size + 1; CENTER integer-1 - (size - 1) / 2 (odd and even formulas agree in truncating integer arithmetic). The golden derives RIGHT 10 x3 -> 8-10, CENTER 15 x3 -> 14-16, CENTER 20 x4 -> 19-22 from the quoted formulas before the run. subject: COLUMN clause
notes: Rule: a per-line horizontal counter = rightmost occupied column, zero at line start (cite.py --check 13.18.14.4 'At the start of the line, the horizontal counter is zero' -> OK 7)). EmitCompose declares `int __hc = 0;` per compose method (one per line) whenever any placement is relative; every placement updates it. Probe p1.cob line 3: the first printable item `COLUMN PLUS 3` landed at column 3 (0+3). pb951's derivation computes from the zero counter. || Editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (Format 1 multiple/relative/alignment forms); the absolute single-operand COLUMN NUMBER IS integer-1 form also 85. Annex E records no 2023 change to the clause.

subject: COLUMN clause
notes: Rule: integer-2 on the first printable item is its leftmost column; otherwise leftmost = horizontal counter + integer-2 (cite.py --check 13.18.14.4 'The position of the item's leftmost character is obtained by adding integer-' -> OK 8)). Emitter: `__hc += integer-2; Place(__hc)`. Probes: p1 line 1 'ABC' 3-5 then PLUS 2 -> 7; line 3 first item PLUS 3 -> 3; line 5 AA at 2-3 then PLUS 1 -> 4, and after absolute C at 12, PLUS 1 -> 13 (' AABB      CD'); p6 `COLUMN PLUS 1 PLUS 2 PLUS 1 PIC 9` -> '3 33'. All match GR8 arithmetic. NOTE 2 informative. || Editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (Format 1 multiple/relative/alignment forms); the absolute single-operand COLUMN NUMBER IS integer-1 form also 85. subject: COLUMN clause
notes: (kb/Work PB1220, wave 1005 A).
