notes: kb/Work PB547 — TWO OF THE THREE OBLIGATIONS HOLD OUTRIGHT; THE UNIFORM-SIZE CLAUSE HOLDS ONLY OVER THE LATIN-1 SUBSET OF WHAT THE ITEM ACTUALLY ADMITS, AND THE EXCESS IS LOST SILENTLY. HOLDS: "an alphanumeric coded character set shall be used" and "the data item is aligned on a character boundary" - probe q9 (--std 2023) gives BYTE-LENGTH == LENGTH == the declared positions for X(5), 9(5), S9(5) (an unseparate sign shares a digit position), A(5) and ZZ9; probe q71 shows a DISPLAY leaf never shares a byte and never pads (`X(1) 9(1) 1(1)BIT X(1)` is 4 bytes and G(1:1)/G(2:1)/G(4:1) read P/7/Q, i.e. the character leaves sit on byte boundaries and only the BIT leaf takes 8.5.1.6.3's own byte). HOLDS: "Each implementor shall specify the size and representation of characters stored for usage DISPLAY" - A.1 item 209 is the required item and docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-209 states it (one byte per character position, uniform at every length, no per-compilation-unit option), pinned by the spec-derived golden conformance:2023/l1_usage_display_character_size whose UNI leg measures 1/5/9 for X(1)/X(5)/X(9). WHAT IS PARTIAL - "Alphanumeric characters shall be represented in the storage of the computer as characters of UNIFORM SIZE equal to or less than the size of characters in the computer's national character set": the item admits characters the documented size cannot represent, so the size is not uniform across the item's own content. Measured (probe q50, --std 2023): `01 G. 05 A PIC X(3).` with `MOVE "A(U+00E9)(U+2603)" TO A` compiles, and FUNCTION ORD of A(1:1)/A(2:1)/A(3:1) returns 66/234/9732 - the item is holding U+00E9 and U+2603 as UTF-16 CODE UNITS, one per position, and the group image returns the same three values - while FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(A) is 3. At the byte boundary the third character is not represented at all: probe q72 writes that record to a SEQUENTIAL file and the file is exactly 3 bytes, 41 E9 3F - the snowman became '?'. Probe q80 repeats it under `>>TURN EC-ALL CHECKING ON` and FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS comes back BLANK, so the loss is SILENT. That contradicts the implementation's OWN decided disposition, which docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-33 records for the same substitution ("the serialization substitutes '?' (0x3F) and sets EC-DATA-CONVERSION ... never silent") - the CONVERT leg was given the EC and the record/file leg was not, the two-arm shape. The rule's own words are the test: a character in an alphanumeric item is either represented at the uniform size or it is not admitted; here it is admitted, carried at 2 bytes in memory and written at 1 with a substitution nobody is told about. See finding usage-p3/F1. NOTE the neighbouring tension the row does not itself resolve: DOC-A.1-209 says the alphanumeric character is ONE byte while DOC-A.1-188 and DOC-A.1-33 say "the native alphanumeric and national repertoires are UTF-16, one code unit per character position" - the two determinations disagree about the size of the very character GR7 asks the implementor to specify. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/DataItem.cs#DataItem.ElementaryByteWidth (the `_ => ElementaryImageWidth` DISPLAY arm - one byte per character position); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/PicInfo.cs#PicInfo.ByteForm (Usage.Display -> NumericByteForm.Zoned); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/BitLayout.cs#BitsPerCharacter; docs/CONFORMANCE.md#DOC-A.1-209; docs/CONFORMANCE.md#DOC-A.1-33 (the '?' substitution disposition) || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 85,2002,2014,2023 (USAGE DISPLAY, explicit or implied, is a COBOL-85 element and the implied default at every edition - 13.18.60.3 SR13 b)

subject: USAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB546 — THE SIZE THE IMPLEMENTOR SPECIFIED IS NOT THE SIZE THE STORAGE USES, AND THE DISAGREEMENT DISPLACES EVERY LEAF AFTER A NATIONAL ONE. What conforms: the head of the rule and the alignment - `01 N PIC N(4) USAGE NATIONAL.` reports FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH 8 and FUNCTION LENGTH 4 (probe q11), i.e. 2 bytes per national position, and 2 IS "a multiple of the size of characters in the computer's alphanumeric character set" (1, DOC-A.1-209); `01 M PIC N(4).` reports the same, so SR13 a's implied USAGE NATIONAL agrees; national values store, compare and display (conformance:2002/national_data). THE DIVERGENCE, minimal repro (probe q73, --std 2023): `01 G. 05 N PIC N(2) USAGE NATIONAL. 05 A PIC X(2).` with `MOVE N"AB" TO N` and `MOVE "YZ" TO A`. FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(G) = 6 and FUNCTION LENGTH(G) = 6 - so A is DECLARED at positions 5-6 - yet `G(3:2)` reads "YZ" and `G(5:2)` reads two spaces. The same wrong layout crosses a CALL: probe q52 passes G BY REFERENCE to a program whose linkage is `01 W PIC X(6)` and the callee reads ORD 66 67 90 91 33 33 = A,B,Y,Z,space,space; probe q25/q27 show the identical thing through a group MOVE. MECHANISM, located and named by the code itself: DataItem.ElementaryByteWidth answers `2 * ElementaryImageWidth` for Usage.National (the documented D-N1/D-N3 model) while DataItem.IsCharacterImage's comment says a national leaf "contribute[s] their CHARACTER positions to a group image (ImageWidth = Length - never byte-doubled for national)". Two widths for one item, and the consumers split: BYTE-LENGTH / LENGTH / the declared group size take ByteWidth, the image codec and every channel built on it take ImageWidth. DataItem.IsImageCapable's own doc comment asserts the opposite - "Width-wise the codec uses ImageWidth, which IS ByteWidth for every item that reaches an image - the ONE-WIDTH invariant" - and the drift test that guards it, ImageWidthIsStorageWidthTests, carves national out by name (NationalLeaf_IsExactlyTwoBytesPerPosition asserts ImageWidth 4 / ByteWidth 8 and calls it "the ONE sanctioned divergence"), so the invariant cannot catch this and never has. THE IMPLEMENTATION ALREADY KNOWS: the FILE-record channel refuses the same shape LOUD - probe q60 gives COBOLNET0899 "national data in a file record ... the record codec is single-byte and the national character is two bytes (Phase 4a residue; ISO 8.1.2 / 13.18.60.4 GR8)" - so one of the four byte channels is honest and three are silently wrong. What the rule requires: "National characters shall be represented in the storage of the computer as characters of a UNIFORM SIZE equal to or a multiple of the size of characters in the computer's alphanumeric character set" - one size, everywhere, and the implementor's specified size is 2. EXPECTED for the repro: BYTE-LENGTH(G) = 6 with N occupying bytes 1-4 as UTF-16 (00 41 00 42, the form DOC-A.1-33 names for the storage channel) and A at bytes 5-6, so G(5:2) reads "YZ". OWNERSHIP: no kb/Work note covers this. PB327 (open) owns the FILE channel only - the EXTERNAL FD record, the national key and the national space fill - and PB231 (open) the BASED/ALLOCATE refusal; both are REJECTS-LEGAL-SOURCE shapes, whereas this is the silent WRONG-ANSWER shape, and its exact twin PB188 (landed) is the same defect for a byte-form numeric leaf: "seeds a FOUR-character window over a TWO-byte item, silently shifting every following member of the group image". SECOND, SEPARATE GAP IN THIS ROW: the rule's closing sentence ("Each implementor shall specify the size and representation of characters stored for usage NATIONAL") is A.1 item 213, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md has NO DOC-A.1-213 row - the ledger runs 208, 209, 211, 215 and DOC-A.1-209 forward-references "row 213" for the 2-bytes-per-position figure it relies on. See finding usage-p3/F2. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/DataItem.cs#DataItem.ElementaryByteWidth (`Usage.National => 2 * ElementaryImageWidth`) vs src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/DataItem.cs#DataItem.IsCharacterImage / DataItem.ImageWidth (a national leaf contributes its CHARACTER positions - "never byte-doubled for national"); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/DataDivision/GroupImageCodec.cs; tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit/ImageWidthIsStorageWidthTests.cs#NationalLeaf_IsExactlyTwoBytesPerPosition (the divergence asserted as sanctioned) || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 2002,2014,2023 (USAGE NATIONAL and category national are post-1985: probe q65 gives COBOLNET0900 "national data (PICTURE symbol N / USAGE NATIONAL) requires COBOL-2002" at --std 85)

notes: The MESSAGE-TAG usage is the DATA half of the asynchronous messaging facility, a processor-dependent element (ISO 4.2.6; Annex A.3 item 4) this implementation does not provide - the owner decision is recorded in docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 4 item 1, alongside SEND/RECEIVE. "held in a binary format suitable for the machine" - ByteForm Binary, two's complement, widths 1/2/4/8 (probe p50 reads 0x01 0x02 for BINARY-SHORT 258 and 0xFF 0xFF for -1 and for UNSIGNED 65535). notes: RE-RECORDED 2026-09-05 (kb/Work PB598) — the SUBJECT of each sentence, which this row had right for what SR4 forbids and wrong for what it admits. SR4 is three sentences: a category sentence, then 'Alphanumeric literals in the VALUE clause of an elementary item shall not exceed the size indicated by an explicit PICTURE clause' and 'Alphanumeric literals in the VALUE clause of an alphanumeric group item shall not exceed the size of the group item'. The 2026-09-04 landing (PB206) closed both size sentences, which had silently TRUNCATED, and this row was recorded CONFORMS on that evidence — but the screen it landed was reached by the three level-88 call sites in BindCondition carrying the CONDITIONAL VARIABLE's size, so it also applied the elementary-item sentence to a subject neither sentence names. `01 XV PIC X. 88 XC VALUE "cd".` became COBOLNET1740, legal source rejected, and GnuCOBOL differential case syn_misc:388 flipped from AGREE_ACCEPT to WE_REJECT_THEY_ACCEPT. A Format-3 entry is `88 condition-name-1 value-clause .` (13.16.2), which admits no PICTURE clause, so no EXPLICIT picture indicates a size; SR33 makes that level-88 entry the subject of the entry; 8.5.1.3.2 item 3 gives a condition-name entry 'no true concept of level', so it is neither of 8.5.1.3.1's record subdivisions; and 13.18.63.4 GR19 gives it its conditional variable's characteristics only IMPLICITLY, which is exactly what 'explicit' excludes. The three subjects the rule addresses are now a TYPE, ValueSubject, built only by ForElementary / ForGroup / ForConditionName, so a call site cannot compose a size the standard does not give it. The category sentence is unaffected and still binds a condition-name (SR4 is an ALL FORMATS rule). And the standard defines what an oversize condition-name literal MEANS, which a size rule would make dead text: 8.8.4.5.3 item 2 sends the comparison to the relation-condition rules, so it never compares equal; 14.9.39.4 GR6 -> 13.18.63.4 GR7 -> 14.6.8.5 places it 'with space fill or truncation to the right'. The 85 golden pb598_condition_name_value_size derives every one of those answers from the rules before measuring them; the pb206 negatives and ConditionNameValueSizeTests.TheSizeSentencesStillBindAnElementaryAndAGroupSubject are the drift proof that withholding the size from a condition-name did not withhold it from the two subjects the sentences do name (that test was measured RED against a deliberately over-withholding build). A FIGURATIVE operand remains exempt by rule (8.3.3.6.4 GR2). Error at every edition: Annex E.2 item 27's 2023 size change is scoped to numeric-edited items (COBOLNET1570).

notes: LANDED 2026-09-13 (kb/Work PB506). THREE DELEGATIONS: TWO NOW CONFORM, THE THIRD IS VACUOUS IN FORMAT 4. SR17 (VALUE and VALUES are equivalent) — CONFORMS, one grammar production accepts both spellings and the 2023 golden writes `VALUES ARE`. SR11 sentence 1 (editing characters ARE used for a numeric-edited item when the literal is numeric) — CONFORMS: `03 COLUMN 46 PIC ZZ9 VALUE 12.` prints ` 12`. SR11 sentence 2 (editing characters for an alphanumeric-edited or national-edited item do NOT cause editing of the initial value) — NOW CONFORMS, and this was the divergence: `03 COLUMN 26 PIC XXBXX VALUE "AB CD".` printed `AB  C`, the literal run through the alphanumeric EDIT, and now prints `AB CD` as written. THE ROOT CAUSE WAS A ROUTING, NOT A MISSING CHECK: ReportWriterEmitter.FieldImage turned a FieldValueSource into move.ConvertSource(source, PrintItem) — the SOURCE clause's implicit MOVE, 13.18.53.4 GR1, a real clause answering a different question — and a MOVE applies exactly the transforms a VALUE excludes. A format-4 VALUE operand now renders through ValueInitializer.InitializerFrom, the SAME 13.18.63 recipe the working-storage (format 1) lane uses, reached via DataEmitter.ValueImageOf; the 2023 golden prints the report item AND its identical WORKING-STORAGE twin on adjacent lines for each shape, so the two lanes cannot drift apart unseen. SR25 (no format 3/4/5 VALUE in or under a CONSTANT RECORD entry) is VACUOUS in format 4: CONSTANT RECORD is a data-description clause (13.18.15) and the report group description entry's clause list does not contain it, so the shape SR34 imports SR25 to forbid cannot be written in the report section at all; SR25's own row owns its format-3/5 legs. EDITIONS: MEASURED at 2002, 2014 and 2023 (the three goldens); FieldImage and InitializerFrom carry no version predicate and the 85 leg is reasoned from that, the repetition and COLUMNS/SOURCES spellings used to reach it being 2002-gated (COBOLNET0900). Annex E carries no 2023 change to SR34.

notes: LANDED 2026-09-13 (kb/Work PB506). BOTH SENTENCES ENFORCED, AND THE OPERAND LIST EXISTS TO ENFORCE THEM AGAINST. Sentence 1 (a multi-operand VALUE requires a repeating entry or an entry subordinate to one) and sentence 2 (the operand count shall equal the entry's repetitions, or that number multiplied by the repetitions of successive higher repeating entries) are screened by ONE reader, ScreenRepeatingOperandCount, which computes the admissible counts as the PREFIX PRODUCTS of the repetition chain RepetitionChain reads off the report-entry scope stack — the entry's own count per 13.15.4 GR3 (EntryRepetitions: a COLUMN clause with more than one operand, else 1) then each enclosing entry's. A non-repeating frame contributes a factor of 1, so sentence 1 is exactly 'the full product is 1' and needs no separate special case, and the rule generalizes without edit on the day the report-group OCCURS and multiple LINE vehicles land (both stage COBOLNET0899 today, and an entry that staged loud is skipped rather than double-diagnosed). Diagnostic COBOLNET2012. MEASURED: `03 COLUMN 1 PIC X(3) VALUE "AAA" "BBB" "CCC".` (a non-repeating entry) and `03 COLUMNS ARE 1 6 11 PIC X(3) VALUES ARE "AAA" "BBB".` (3 repetitions, 2 operands) each draw COBOLNET2012 at 85, 2002, 2014 AND 2023 — SR35 carries no version proviso and Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change, so at 85 the COBOLNET0900 introduction gate for the multiple COLUMN vehicle is reported ALONGSIDE it, not instead of it. The LEGAL three-operand form compiles and prints AAA/BBB/CCC (the 2023 golden). BEFORE: both illegal shapes compiled clean and printed the same `AAA  AAA  AAA` as the legal one, because DataBinder.ExtractValue collapsed the whole list to item.GetText() and FieldValueSource held ONE string — no count could be compared with a repetition count because no count existed. The SIBLING ARM, 13.18.53.3 SR6, is the same rule written for the SOURCE clause and now rides the same reader (COBOLNET2013).

notes: kb/Work PB1010 (2026-09-22): both directions of 'if and only if'. subject: Scope of statements
notes: Rule: an explicit scope terminator terminates 'the most-recently preceding unterminated statement having the statement-name for which that scope terminator is defined' (cite.py --check 14.5.3.2 -> OK §14.5.3.2 1)). Implementation is structural: every Table-12 statement rule ends in an optional END_x token (END_ADD?, END_IF?, END_READ?, ...) and ANTLR's greedy optional binds the terminator to the INNERMOST open statement of that name. Probes: nested ADD ... ON SIZE ERROR ADD ... END-ADD END-ADD binds innermost (sc1 T5 -> 'T5 B-SE','T5 IN-A-SE','T5 END'); an inner ADD already implicitly terminated by the outer's NOT ON SIZE ERROR phrase is skipped and END-ADD closes the outer (sc1 T1); nested inline PERFORMs (sc4 U3 -> 8); END-IF closes the innermost IF only (sc1 T7, sc4 U9); an END-ADD whose ADD was already implicitly terminated by ELSE is rejected COBOL0306 (sc5). The golden's S2/S4 pin END-IF-to-nearest-IF (IF instance only). Observation, not a verdict change: the grammar/lexer also accept END-SORT and END-MERGE as terminators of SORT/MERGE (Core/CobolIO.g4:846,921) and END-INVOKE for INVOKE (PB758) although Table 12 defines none; `SORT E ASCENDING END-SORT` compiles and runs at 2023 with no diagnostic (sc2). The reservation is documented (CONFORMANCE.md D-RW1, §4.2.10) but no §4.2.10 3) warning flags the extension - see finding F1. probe dir out/probe/scope-of-statements (sc1/sc4/sc5, pinned cobol.exe; sc1 identical output at --std 85/2002/2014/2023, sc4 at 85 and 2023) [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (explicit/implicit scope termination is COBOL-85 surface; Annex E records no change to 14.5.3)]

subject: Scope of statements
notes: Rule: the explicit terminator also terminates 'any unterminated statements that appear between that statement-name and the explicit scope terminator' (cite.py --check 14.5.3.2 -> OK §14.5.3.2 2)). Mechanism: statementBlock : statement+ stops at any END_x token that cannot start a statement; each intervening rule's own END_y? is absent, so it closes implicitly and control returns up the rule stack to the rule owning END_x. Probes: IF ... ADD ON SIZE ERROR ... END-IF closes the ADD (sc1 T3 -> 'T3 SE','T3 AFTER-IF'); ADD ON SIZE ERROR IF ... END-ADD closes the IF (sc1 T4); PERFORM ... IF ... END-PERFORM (sc4 U1); EVALUATE WHEN IF ... END-EVALUATE (sc4 U2); SEARCH WHEN IF ... END-SEARCH (sc4 U7) - all as the rule requires, at 85 and 2023. (U1/U2/U7 place an undelimited conditional where a format writes imperative-statement; that acceptance is PB351's open under-reject, not this row.) No existing spec-derived test crosses an intervening unterminated statement: test-needed. probe dir out/probe/scope-of-statements (sc1/sc4/sc5, pinned cobol.exe; sc1 identical output at --std 85/2002/2014/2023, sc4 at 85 and 2023) [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (explicit/implicit scope termination is COBOL-85 surface; Annex E records no change to 14.5.3)]

subject: Scope of statements
notes: Rule: a single imperative statement not contained in another is terminated by 'a) any element that follows the exhaustion of the statement's syntax, or b) the next-encountered statement-name, or c) a separator period' (cite.py --check 14.5.3.3 -> OK §14.5.3.3 1) a)). Mechanism: sentence : statement+ DOT, each statement rule consumes exactly its own syntax, so the next statement keyword (b), the DOT (c), or a following element such as ELSE (a) ends it. Probes: 'DISPLAY "T8 A" DISPLAY "T8 B" MOVE 1 TO A DISPLAY A.' -> three separate statements (sc1 T8); every sentence in sc1/sc4 ends at its period. Reserved statement names cannot be absorbed as operands (§8.9 reservation), so no adversarial operand/statement-name collision exists. No spec-derived test targets this rule specifically: test-needed. probe dir out/probe/scope-of-statements (sc1/sc4/sc5, pinned cobol.exe; sc1 identical output at --std 85/2002/2014/2023, sc4 at 85 and 2023) [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (explicit/implicit scope termination is COBOL-85 surface; Annex E records no change to 14.5.3)]

subject: Scope of statements
notes: Rule: a contained imperative statement is terminated by 'a) any element that terminates an imperative statement not contained within another statement, b) the termination of the scope of any containing statement, or c) the next phrase of any containing statement' (cite.py --check 14.5.3.3 -> OK §14.5.3.3 2) for the c) text). Probes: (c) 'IF FLG = 2 DISPLAY ... MOVE 5 TO N ELSE DISPLAY ... MOVE 6 TO N.' -> ELSE ends the THEN-arm MOVE (sc4 U8 -> 'U8 ELSE','U8 6'); (b) the DISPLAY inside ON SIZE ERROR ends when END-IF ends the containing IF (sc1 T3) and when the period ends the containing ADD (sc4 U5 -> both DISPLAYs inside the phrase); (a) statement-name boundaries inside phrases (sc4 U5 'DISPLAY "U5 SE" DISPLAY "U5 SE2"'). The golden's S1 pins (c) for IF (inner THEN DISPLAY ended by ELSE). probe dir out/probe/scope-of-statements (sc1/sc4/sc5, pinned cobol.exe; sc1 identical output at --std 85/2002/2014/2023, sc4 at 85 and 2023) [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (explicit/implicit scope termination is COBOL-85 surface; Annex E records no change to 14.5.3)]

subject: Scope of statements
notes: Rule: 'for a conditional statement not contained within another statement, by a separator period' (cite.py --check 14.5.3.3 -> OK §14.5.3.3 3)). Mechanism: a phrase's statementBlock is statement+ and only DOT (or a phrase/terminator token) ends it, so every following statement up to the period belongs to the conditional phrase. subject: Scope of statements
notes: Rule: a contained conditional statement is terminated by the termination or next phrase of a containing statement; 'Any phrase encountered is the next phrase of the most-recently preceding unterminated statement with which that phrase may be syntactically associated. If all permitted occurrences of a phrase have already been specified for a given statement, a subsequent occurrence of that phrase is not syntactically associated with that statement' (cite.py --check 14.5.3.3 -> OK §14.5.3.3 4)). Mechanism: each conditional-phrase group allows each phrase at most once (e.g. arithmeticOnSizeError, readAtEnd, ifStatement's single ELSE), and ANTLR's greedy optional attaches a phrase to the innermost open rule that can still take it, returning outward otherwise - the rule's association order. Probes: nested IFs, second ELSE goes to the outer IF (sc1 T6 'T6 OUTER-ELSE', T6B 'T6B INNER-ELSE'); END-IF-terminated inner IF lets ELSE go outer (sc1 T7); ADD conditional inside IF ended by ELSE (sc1 T9); SEARCH inside IF ended by ELSE, both WHENs to SEARCH (sc4 U6 'U6 FOUND'); exhausted inner NOT ON SIZE ERROR passes the second NOT to the outer ADD (sc1 T1/T2). The golden's S1/S3 pin association and the 'already matched with an ELSE' exhaustion for IF. Reach note: §14.5.1 makes a conditional statement imperative only when delimited, and every Table-12 conditional phrase and EVALUATE/PERFORM body is written imperative-statement-n, so in a CONFORMING program the only containing statement a conditional can sit in unterminated is IF (§14.9.19.2 statement-1/-2), whose only later phrase is ELSE. The grammar over-admits phrase repetition/merging elsewhere (SEARCH ALL WHEN+ - PB446; READ Format 1 AT END with Format 2 INVALID KEY on one statement; WRITE EOP with INVALID KEY; CALL 'NOT ON OVERFLOW'), which could steal a phrase from an outer statement - but only in programs already non-conforming under PB351 (undelimited conditional in an imperative position). Those rows are owned by PB351/PB446; no separate scope defect. probe dir out/probe/scope-of-statements (sc1/sc4/sc5, pinned cobol.exe; sc1 identical output at --std 85/2002/2014/2023, sc4 at 85 and 2023) || REFUTED: CONFORMS with test-ref EMPTY (test-needed) — Implementation conforms: adjudicator sc1 T6 (IF IF ELSE ELSE, second ELSE to outer), refuter R2 (ELSE terminates a contained undelimited EVALUATE, both truth values), R3 (ELSE terminates contained READ AT END/NOT AT END), R8, E5 (third ELSE with both IFs exhausted rejected COBOL0307). But the golden does not pin the rule load-bearing branches: branch b) "next phrase of any containing statement" terminating a contained CONDITIONAL, and the exhaustion sentence, are never reached - in S2/S3/S4 every inner IF is END-IF terminated before the ELSE (so S3 is decided by the END-IF, not by the already-matched-ELSE exhaustion the adjudicator credits it with), and in S1 the inner IF is ended by the period. Only the association sentence (S1 dangling ELSE) is pinned. A deciding test: IF T IF F DISPLAY 1 ELSE DISPLAY 2 ELSE DISPLAY 3. with no END-IF (expect 2), plus IF F IF .. ELSE .. ELSE DISPLAY 3. (expect 3). [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (explicit/implicit scope termination is COBOL-85 surface; Annex E records no change to 14.5.3)]

Sentence 1, "For each dynamic-capacity table, except where the table is defined by an elementary entry with a VALUE clause, the capacity of the table is set to the minimum capacity specified in the corresponding OCCURS clause": ValueInitializer.FieldInit opens every CobolDynTable at `OccursSpec.InitialCap ?? 0` (13.18.38.4 GR16's minimum) and raises it only for the EXCEPTION, which is the 13.18.63.4 GR16 Format-2 derivation DataBinder.ResolveTableValues accumulates into DataItem.TableValueInitialCapacity. WITH FILLER ALL TO VALUE THEN TO DEFAULT". notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB603 (open). Rule: 'An implicit CLOSE statement without any phrases is executed for each file that is in the open mode. These implicit close statements shall be executed for all open files in the run unit, even when an error occurs during the execution of one or more of the CLOSE statements. Any exception processing procedures associated with these files are not executed.' (cite.py --check 14.6.11 -> OK, rule 2). Three halves: (1) every open file in the RUN UNIT - RunMain's finally calls _owner.Files.CloseAll() on normal, STOP RUN and abnormal exits (§14.6.12 path too), over the run-unit registry incl. instance-file connectors (DrainPendingObjectCloses) and files opened by a separately compiled module; pinned by RunUnitTerminationTests.ImplicitClose_ReachesFileOpenedBySeparatelyCompiledSub and AbnormalTermination_StillClosesOpenFiles (spec-derived: on-disk content is the observable). (2) 'even when an error occurs': FileConnector.Close maps IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException to status '30' and returns, so one failing close does not stop the loop - verified by reading, no test. (3) 'exception processing procedures ... are not executed': CloseAll calls the connector's Close directly, never the emitted CLOSE statement path that selects USE declaratives - verified by reading, no test. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The half that says the implicit CLOSEs 'shall be executed for all open files in the run unit, even when an error occurs during the execution of one or more of the CLOSE statements' is broken. FileConnector.Close contains only IOException and UnauthorizedAccessException. Any other close-time failure escapes FileRegistry.CloseAll's loop, which has no per-file guard, so every connector after it is never closed, its buffered data is lost, and the process dies with an unhandled .NET exception. I reached this with a user-level program: an indexed file with CODE-SET IS EBCDIC defers its CODE-SET conversion to the persist in IndexedConnector.CloseCore, and a record holding U+20AC makes CodeSetConversion.ToMedium throw InvalidOperationException. The implicit close of every open file and the not-running of the exception procedures do hold. The adjudicator verified the 'error' half only by reading, which missed the narrow catch. Separate lead: WRITE IX returned '00' for a record its CODE-SET cannot represent, because the conversion is deferred to CLOSE (§13.18.13.4 GR1/GR6 b).

subject: Exception conditions
notes: kb/Work PB77 + PB75 (2026-08-18): with checking for a fatal exception condition NOT enabled 'the implementor defines whether or not execution will continue, how it will continue, and how any receiving operands are affected'. COBOL.NET's determination for the arithmetic size error condition without a SIZE ERROR phrase (EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION, §14.7.5 no-phrase rule 4; A.1 item 70): execution continues and the resultant identifier receives the LOW-ORDER digits of the result aligned at its scale (CobolNum.Store's high-order truncation), for EVERY value carrier — SDIDI (CobolDec.ToUnscaled, PB74), the native exact family (Rescaled's unchecked arm), a binary64 (ToScaledUnchecked / FromDouble's unchecked form — the exact decimal expansion past the Int128 carrier). A non-finite binary64 landing in a fixed-point receiver stores ZERO. An INTERMEDIATE that cannot be formed at all (a standard-decimal intermediate past decimal128, a native value past the Int128 escape boundary in a value-semantics position, an exponentiation-rule violation, a zero divisor) has no result: execution does NOT continue — the run unit terminates abnormally, exit 1, naming the condition (PB75; it used to be a raw CLR crash, exit 127). Documented on CONFORMANCE.md (the item-70 row).

subject: Exception condition handling
notes: kb/Work PB1042 (wave 1021 B2) made rule 6 REACHABLE and gave it its raise site. 'When the internal format of a dynamic-capacity table, as defined by the implementor, is not correctly formed or does not agree with the corresponding OCCURS clause an EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE exception condition is set to exist.' Until PB1042 every table a program read was constructed from that program's own OCCURS clause (ValueInitializer, now the ONE construction DynTableNew for both storage lanes) or recreated into it (FromCurrentImage), so the rule was unreachable by construction. A cell-backed area (an EXTERNAL record described by two programs) now shares one table across descriptions, so every cell table reference carries the REFERENCING description's FROM minimum and element width (CellTableSegment) and StorageCell.DynTableAt asks agreement, the twin of CobolDynString.Agree for rule 5: a capacity below the minimum or elements of another width disagree, an area holding no table at the component is not correctly formed; with checking enabled the fatal condition is raised, with it off the result is undefined and the reference proceeds. The rules are §8.8.1.2 r6 a)/c) (--check 8.8.1.2 'the exponent shall have a value greater than zero' -> OK §8.8.1.2 6) a)). These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). notes: kb/Work/PB401.md - rule 1, 'When the range of values is defined by numeric literals, the range of values includes literal-1, literal-2, and all algebraic values between literal-1 and literal-2'. A numeric range lowers to the inclusive ALGEBRAIC pair `subject >= lo && subject <= hi` over the numeric channel, names no collating sequence, and sets NO exception condition in either direction - which is what makes rule 1 observably different from rule 2 and is measured as such: PBR10 (inverted numeric identifier ends: empty, no EC), PBR11 (arithmetic-expression ends 1+1 THRU 8+2 containing 5 algebraically), PBR12/PBR13 (literal ends both directions), and the golden's NUMINV/ARITH arms. The rule-1/rule-2 split is written down ONCE, as CollatingSelection.IsCollatedThroughRange over the range's class, so a site cannot implement one rule and leave the other to a second author; before it, an arithmetic-expression-ended range was classified ALPHANUMERIC (its operand answered 'no category') and took rule 2's collating treatment.

subject: ACCEPT statement
notes: 'DATE without the phrase YYYYMMDD ... unsigned elementary integer of usage display SIX digits', positions 1-2 = the two low-order digits of the Gregorian year, 3-4 = month 01-12, 5-6 = day 01-31. AcceptSource.Date() returns `n.Year % 100 * 10000L + n.Month * 100L + n.Day` -- the two low-order year digits weighted 10^4, the month 10^2, the day 10^0, exactly the printed positional layout. The SIX-digit width comes from the emitter: EmitAcceptTemporal maps AcceptKind.Date to ("AcceptSource.Date()", 6). .NET DateTime is proleptic-Gregorian, satisfying 'Gregorian calendar'. Pinned end-to-end by AcceptDifferentialTests.Date_FormatIsYYMMDD: clock 2026-06-10T14:30:45.67 into PIC 9(6) displays exactly '260610'. || UPHELD (verdict) with the mechanism corrected. I recomputed the layout for the zero-fill edges the test does not cover: 2026-01-05 -> 26*10000 + 1*100 + 5 = 260105, and 2005-01-05 -> 5*10000 + 105 = 50105 which renders '050105' at width 6, so the '01 through 12' / '01 through 31' two-position zero fill holds at both ends and the item stays unsigned. Clock provenance also checked: SystemClock.Now() returns DateTimeOffset.Now (Clock.cs:38-42) and AcceptSource.Now() takes `.DateTime`, i.e. the LOCAL wall clock, which is what 'provided by the system on which the ACCEPT statement is executed' requires -- not UTC. || REFUTED (evidence chain, not verdict): the adjudicator attributed the six-position zero fill in Date_FormatIsYYMMDD to `CobolNum.FormatUnsignedDisplayU(value, 6)`. That is not the path that test takes. Its receiver is PIC 9(6), so EmitAcceptTemporal enters `case { Category: PicCategory.Numeric, IsFloat: false }` (AcceptDisplayEmitter.cs:131-138), which stores `NumStore(call, "0", profile)` narrowed by ArithmeticEmitter.Narrow and never evaluates `sendImage` at all -- the six-digit zero-padded image the test observes is produced by the RECEIVER's own PIC 9(6) display rendering. FormatUnsignedDisplayU governs only the alphanumeric / alphanumeric-edited / group / ref-mod receivers. The rule is still met on both paths (I checked each), but the closing evidence for the conceptual item's own width is the X(4) DAY test, not this one.

notes: 'DAY-OF-WEEK ... unsigned elementary numeric integer ONE digit ... usage display. 1 represents Monday ... 7 represents Sunday.' AcceptSource.DayOfWeek() returns `((int)Now().DayOfWeek + 6) % 7 + 1`. Checked the remap against .NET's DayOfWeek (Sunday=0 .. Saturday=6) for every value: Sunday 0 -> (6%7)+1 = 7; Monday 1 -> (7%7)+1 = 1; Tuesday 2 -> 2; Wednesday 3 -> 3; Thursday 4 -> 4; Friday 5 -> 5; Saturday 6 -> (12%7)+1 = 6. subject: ADD statement
notes: READ: the grammar alternative `ADD (CORRESPONDING | CORR) dataReference TO dataReference roundedPhrase? arithmeticOnSizeError? END_ADD?` (CobolParserCore.g4:851) and CorrespondingBinder.BindAddCorresponding (25-29), `add.CORRESPONDING() is not null || add.CORR() is not null ? Bind(CorrVerb.Add, add.dataReference(), ...) : new BoundUnsupported(...)`. The two spellings are ONE grammar alternative and ONE boolean disjunction feeding ONE Bind call, so there is no second dispatch arm that could carry different behaviour -- the equivalence is structural rather than a pair of parallel code paths (the two-arm-dispatch failure shape does not apply here). Neither token is edition-gated: no ConstructRegistry row in tests/version-matrix/constructs.json mentions CORR or CORRESPONDING, and Annex E carries no ADD entry, so the batch default editions stand. TEST HONESTY: the golden cited exercises the CORRESPONDING spelling on ADD; the CORR spelling is exercised on SUBTRACT (conformance-test:CorrespondingDifferentialTests.SubtractCorr_TargetMinusSource_CorrToken), through the sibling alternative at CobolParserCore.g4:890 and the identical `sub.CORRESPONDING() is not null || sub.CORR() is not null` disjunction -- so the CORR-on-ADD spelling specifically has no test of its own. Adding `ADD CORR SRC TO DST` to an existing CORR golden would make the coverage exhaustive; nothing about the code makes it a risk. || UPHELD, with evidence the record did not have. The structural argument is only sound if the two spellings are also indistinguishable to the LEXER, which I checked rather than assumed: Core/CobolLexer.g4:455 `CORR : 'CORR' ;` and :459 `CORRESPONDING : 'CORRESPONDING' ;` are both UNCONDITIONAL token rules -- no `{isXXXX()}?` version predicate on either -- and ANTLR's maximal-munch keeps CORRESPONDING whole rather than splitting it into CORR + a word, so neither spelling can degrade into a data-name at any edition. notes: Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.9.3 "If the AFTER phrase is not specified, then the statement is processed as if an AFTER phrase were specified with arithmetic-expression-1 specified as zero."` -> OK, SR 2). Derived expectation first: bare CONTINUE must be EXACTLY equivalent to `CONTINUE AFTER 0 SECONDS`, which by GR1 means (a) no suspension, (b) no exception -- 0 is not less than zero, so EC-CONTINUE-LESS-THAN-ZERO cannot be set even under CHECKING ON -- and (c) execution continues with the next executable statement. The failure shape to look for is a bare CONTINUE that behaves OBSERVABLY differently from the AFTER-0 spelling under some ambient state. READ: ControlFlowBinder.BindContinue (ControlFlowBinder.cs:57-62) -- `if (cont.arithmeticExpression() is not { } secs) return new BoundNop();` -- and StatementEmitter.Visit(BoundNop) (StatementEmitter.cs:147) returns false emitting nothing, so control simply falls to the next emitted statement. COMPARED the two spellings for OBSERVABLE difference rather than assuming: the AFTER-0 leg emits `CobolTiming.ContinueAfter((double)(0L), true)` (checked-in generated output, tests/conformance/2023/continue_after.g.cs), and ContinueAfter with 0.0 takes neither the `seconds < 0.0` arm nor the `secs == 0` sleep -- it returns having touched nothing. Under `>>TURN ... CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION` the AFTER form additionally wraps itself in `ExceptionState.EnterStatement("CONTINUE", loc, ...)` / `ExitStatement` (exception_statement_ambient.g.cs:151-156), but that pair is SAVE-and-RESTORE (ExceptionState.cs:79-88) and nothing raises inside it, so LastStatement/LastLocation are identical afterwards to what a bare CONTINUE leaves -- FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT and FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION cannot tell the spellings apart. EcBinder gives BoundNop no EC wrapper and BoundContinueAfter one (EcBinder.cs:379-381), but since neither can raise, that is not observable either. So all three of (a)(b)(c) hold STATICALLY and the equivalence looks exact. EDITION: 2023 -- this syntax rule exists only because the AFTER phrase does (Annex E.3.3 item 14, specs/ISO_COBOL.md:43957); at 85/2002/2014 bare CONTINUE is the only form and 14.9.9.1 already governs it, so no per-edition split exists. || UPHELD, the code half: I re-ran the cite check myself and re-read BindContinue (ControlFlowBinder.cs:57-62), Visit(BoundNop) (StatementEmitter.cs:147) and ExceptionState.EnterStatement/ExitStatement (Runtime/Exceptions/ExceptionState.cs:79-88) independently; the save/restore argument holds, and I confirmed the one thing that could break it -- that EnterStatement touches ONLY _stmtName/_stmtLoc/_stmtLocNames and nothing raises between it and ExitStatement, so no ambient state differs. notes: kb/Work/PB405.md - LANDED. GR6 requires control to pass to 'an implicit CONTINUE statement immediately following the last explicit statement of the current paragraph, preceding any return mechanisms for that paragraph', and the NOTE names those return mechanisms as the ones associated with PERFORM, SORT and USE - an INLINE PERFORM is none of them, so an enclosing inline PERFORM has no standing to intercept the transfer. The statement-level and PERFORM-return halves were already right; the third arm - written INSIDE an inline PERFORM - emitted a bare C# `break`, which C# binds to the innermost breakable statement, so it left the PERFORM's lowered loop instead of the dispatcher's `switch (__pc)` and the paragraph then ran to its end (measured on this worktree's build: `IT 1 / IT 2 / TAIL-MAIN / NEXT` where GR6 requires `IT 1 / IT 2 / NEXT`). Repaired STRUCTURALLY rather than per statement: DispatchState.TransferOut/TransferJump is now the ONE renderer of a paragraph-leaving transfer (`__pc = t; goto __xfer;`) and EmitDispatchMethod plants the `__xfer:` landing between the switch and the at-exit tail-check, so no lowered container can capture any transfer and the fall-through epilogue - which is inside the case, before the label - can no longer overwrite a deliberately set target. Design doc D1a records the idiom; the drift test re-measures it over the GENERATED C# and is proved to flag the pre-fix emission. Positive witness: the 2002 golden measures GR6 inside an inline PERFORM at three placements (top level, under an out-of-line PERFORM, and with the section arm of GR7 alongside); the 85 negative pins the COBOL-2002 introduction (COBOLNET0900).

subject: EXIT statement

GR7 passes control to 'an unnamed empty paragraph immediately following the last paragraph of the current section, preceding any return mechanisms for that section'. Inside an inline PERFORM the emitted `break` left the loop, and the paragraph's fall-through epilogue then overwrote the `__pc = SectionEndPc + 1` the statement had set, so the section-exit target was discarded and every remaining paragraph of the section ran too (measured: `IT 1 / IT 2 / TAIL-S1A / S1B / S2A` where GR7 requires `IT 1 / IT 2 / S2A`). The statement now renders the pc assignment, then the section's OWN return mechanism (`if (__exitPc == SectionEndPc) return __pc;` - a C# return, which no container can capture, and which is what fires the PERFORM/SORT/USE return from a MID-section paragraph where the bounded loop's __atExit was captured for the current pc), then the uncapturable jump to the dispatcher landing. Re-derived rather than moved: the order is exactly GR7's 'preceding any return mechanisms'. The two SectionDifferentialTests remain the statement-level spec-pinned witnesses; the new 2002 golden adds the inline-PERFORM arm and the under-a-PERFORM section return.

notes: kb/Work PB397, corrected by kb/Work PB2610. A Format 1 GO TO followed by an IMPERATIVE statement in the same consecutive sequence of imperative statements (within a sentence's statements, or within one phrase of another statement) is refused (COBOLNET2967). A following CONDITIONAL statement (14.5.1: a conditional phrase written without its explicit scope terminator - an IF or EVALUATE with no END-, an ADD with ON SIZE ERROR and no END-ADD, a SEARCH, a READ AT END) ends that sequence, so the GO TO before it is accepted; a delimited scope statement is imperative (14.5.3.2) and is refused after the GO TO. Before PB2610 every following statement was refused, which rejected legal source at every edition. The Format 2 DEPENDING GO TO is not constrained; the 1985 target-less GO TO is that edition's Format 1 and is covered. One existing golden (85/pb413_go_to_out_of_inline_perform) wrote the GO TO beside a following DISPLAY on purpose and was corrected to put the GO TO in an IF phrase.

notes: Rule: 'An INITIATE statement that specifies more than one report-name-1 shall not be specified in an exception checking PERFORM statement.' (cite.py --check 14.9.21.3 -> OK §14.9.21.3 3)). CODE: over region B (imperative-statement-1 + every WHEN / WHEN OTHER / WHEN COMMON body + FINALLY) every descendant InitiateStatementContext with reportName().Length > 1 -> error COBOLNET1605. PROBES s1-s6 (2023): multi-name INITIATE in imperative-statement-1 (s1), a WHEN body (s2), FINALLY (s3), nested inside IF + inline PERFORM (s4), WHEN OTHER / WHEN COMMON (s6) -> COBOLNET1605 each; two single-name INITIATEs (s5) and a multi-name INITIATE AFTER END-PERFORM (s2, s6) accepted and run. An INITIATE of an ACTIVE report calls ExceptionState.ReportActiveError (raise gated by >>TURN) and returns; 'the execution of the INITIATE statement has no other effect' is unconditional, so GR1a-c do not re-run. The golden witnesses exactly that with a SUM counter: the refused second INITIATE does not re-zero it, so the control footing prints S=008 (4+4) rather than S=004. subject: MERGE statement
notes: Rule: data-names after KEY in decreasing significance regardless of KEY-phrase division; a) ASCENDING low->high, b) DESCENDING high->low, per relation-condition comparison; 'The words ASCENDING and DESCENDING are transitive across all occurrences of data-name-1 until another occurrence of the word ASCENDING or DESCENDING is encountered.' (cite.py --check 14.9.24.4 -> OK §14.9.24.4 3) and 3) b)). Code: grammar mergeKeyPhrase = ON? (ASCENDING|DESCENDING) KEY? dataReferenceList, so the direction word governs every data-name of its list (transitivity); BindMerge appends keys phrase by phrase in statement order (significance); KeyColumns.Compare walks keys most-significant first and negates for Descending; comparison per class (numeric algebraic, alphanumeric/national under the GR5 sequence) = relation-condition rules (GR5 itself is part 1 / PB678 landed). Probe probe/merge-p2/m1.cob `ON ASCENDING KEY M-A DESCENDING KEY M-B M-C` (M-B PIC 9, M-C PIC X): output A9Z*, A9Y, A5Q, A1Z, B5A* - M-A ascending, M-B descending, M-C descending by transitivity - identical at --std 85 and 2023. No spec-derived golden exercises a multi-key/DESCENDING MERGE (SortMergeDifferentialTests.Merge_EqualKeys_KeepUsingFileOrder is a legacy differential and does not qualify).

subject: MERGE statement
notes: Rule: equal-key records return a) 'Follows the order of the associated input files as specified in the MERGE statement.' b) 'Is such that all records associated with one input file are returned prior to the return of records from another input file.' (cite.py --check 14.9.24.4 -> OK §14.9.24.4 4) b)). Code: NextInput marks each USING stream's start in statement order; Merge picks the head with STRICT less-than, so an equal head never displaces an earlier stream, and within a stream records keep file order; a stream's equal-key run is fully drained before a later stream's equal record because the earlier stream's next equal head again wins the tie. Probe probe/merge-p2/m1.cob: key A9Z in F1(1 rec), F2(2 recs), F3(1 rec) -> A9ZF1-1, A9ZF2-1, A9ZF2-2, A9ZF3-1; key B5A F1 before F3 - both halves. notes: Rule: 'During the execution of the output procedure, no statement may be executed manipulating the file referenced by or accessing the record area associated with file-name-2 or file-name-3.' notes: kb/Work/PB427.md - LANDED. CheckStrongMove implements BOTH halves of SR2, and its 'same type' is now 8.5.3.1's, not a stand-in. 'Identifier-1 shall be SPECIFIED': a non-field sending operand yields sender==null and errors, so a literal sender is rejected (measured: MOVE "123456" TO P1 -> COBOLNET1533) and so is a FUNCTION sender (measured -> 1533). 'Described as a group item of the SAME type': StrongTypeModel.SameType is 8.5.3.1's clause verbatim - 'Two typed items are of the same type when: (1) the items are described with TYPE clauses that reference equivalent type declarations; or (2) the items are described as subordinate items in equivalent type declarations, starting at the same relative byte or bit position and having the same length in bytes or bits' - over EquivalentTypeDeclarations, which is the clause's own equivalence relation (same type-name, same presence or absence of EXTERNAL and STRONG, corresponding elementary items at the same relative position and length, each pair carrying the same ALIGNED / BLANK WHEN ZERO / DYNAMIC LENGTH / JUSTIFIED / PICTURE / SIGN / SYNCHRONIZED / USAGE clauses). Positions come from BitLayout.StartBitWithin, the ONE 8.5.1.6.3 cursor walk, so bit-bearing declarations are measured by the same law as their storage; the PICTURE/SIGN/USAGE conjunct is PicInfo's own record equality, so a later analysis axis is covered by construction rather than by a member list. THE TWO DEFECTS THE PRIOR PARTIAL RECORDED ARE BOTH CLOSED, EACH RE-MEASURED ON THE BUILT cobol.exe BEFORE AND AFTER. (a) FALSE ADMISSION: an outer program's '01 SHAPE-T TYPEDEF STRONG. 05 SA PIC X(6).' against a contained program's own '01 SHAPE-T TYPEDEF STRONG. 05 SB PIC 9(3). 05 SC PIC 9(3).' - before: MOVE OUTER-X TO INNER-Y compiled clean and ran, printing SB=[ABC] SC=[DEF] into two PIC 9(3) items; after: COBOLNET1533, because the declarations share only a NAME (conformance:negative/pb427-same-type-nonequivalent-declarations, conformance-test:TypedefStrongTests.MoveNonEquivalentSameNamedDeclarations_Rejected1533). (b) FALSE REJECTION: '01 NEST-T TYPEDEF STRONG. 05 OUTERG. 10 INNERG. 15 LEAFX PIC X(4).' with MOVE OUTERG OF N1 TO INNERG OF N2 - before: rc=70 COBOLNET1533; after: accepted and runs (both subordinate items start at relative bit 0 and are 32 bits long, which is alternative 2 exactly) (conformance:2002/pb427_same_type_by_position leg A, conformance-test:TypedefStrongTests.MoveSameOffsetDifferentlyNamedSubgroups_Accepted). The two criteria are now told apart by a PAIR of witnesses: paths differ and positions agree -> legal (MoveSameOffsetDifferentlyNamedSubgroups_Accepted); paths agree and positions differ -> refused (MoveSamePathDifferentPosition_Rejected1533, two equivalent declarations whose grouping differs so that G spans bits 0-31 in one and 16-31 in the other). Over-rejection is guarded in the same set: MoveEquivalentSameNamedDeclarationsAcrossElements_Accepted proves two source elements declaring EQUIVALENT same-named types still describe items of the same type, so the fix refuses the non-equivalent pair without refusing the equivalent one, and MoveSameLayoutDifferentPicture_Rejected1533 isolates the PICTURE conjunct (identical name, strength, layout, positions and lengths; X(3) against 9(3)). The mainline stays correct: a different strong type, a structurally identical UNTYPED group, a literal sender and a FUNCTION sender are all 1533, and IsStrongGroup still restricts the gate to GROUP receivers per 8.5.3.3 ('The only kind of items that may be strongly typed are group items'), so an elementary leaf subordinate to a strong record keeps its unrestricted field MOVE. EDITIONS: STRONG TYPEDEF is a 2002 introduction (ConstructRegistry typedef-def-2002), so the rule has no 85 surface - conformance:negative/pb427-same-type-below-2002 pins the floor (COBOLNET0900 at 85). 8.5.3.1's currency-symbol and DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA exceptions (GR-8.5.3.1-1 / -2) are not witnessed HERE and deliberately so: 12.3.3 SR1 forbids a contained program its own CONFIGURATION SECTION (measured: COBOLNET1643), so two type declarations reachable by one compile-time same-type test always share one CURRENCY SIGN and one DECIMAL-POINT setting - those exceptions are observable only between separately compiled elements sharing an EXTERNAL strongly-typed record, where 14.8.1 makes the conformance a RUNTIME check. The predicate implements them regardless (the analysis PicInfo carries is currency-canonicalized and decimal-point-resolved), and the two rows stay for the adjudication lane. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Validation/StatementValidation.cs#CheckStrongMove (kb/Work PB878 deleted StatementValidation.CheckStrongMove; SR2 is MoveTable16.StrongGroupRefusal, first link of the Validity chain, framed as COBOLNET1533 by MoveBinder.MoveCategoryLegality)

CobolNum.FromAlphanumeric now takes the rightmost 31 CHARACTER POSITIONS of the sending operand before the digit scan (the window is over positions, not digit characters: §14.6.13.2 lets a non-digit position contribute no digit while still occupying a position). The other five channels that shared the decode (reference modification, the group image, UNSTRING INTO, the numeric-edited arm, the current-record read) were repaired by the same change, at the ONE decode.

subject: OPEN statement
notes:
kb/Work PB325 (landed). RULE (--check 14.9.27.4 "'X' at an intersection indicates that the specified statement, used in the access mode given for that row, may be used with the open mode given at the top of the column"): Table 20 licenses each (statement, access mode, open mode) triple; every BLANK cell is an unsuccessful execution whose status 9.1.13.7 names -- item 7 '47' for READ/START not open input or I-O, item 8 '48' for WRITE (a: access sequential and not open extend/output; b: access random or dynamic and not open I-O/output), item 9 '49' for REWRITE/DELETE RECORD not open I-O. Table 20 was read from the PDF (page 709) as well as the transcription, because the load-bearing signal here is a BLANK CELL and the OCR of a blank is not self-evident: Random x WRITE and Dynamic x WRITE carry X under Output and I-O only, and the Extend column of both rows is empty.
IMPLEMENTATION. The ACCESS MODE is the sole branch discriminator and lives in ONE place, KeyedConnector.Access (the abstract base RelativeConnector and IndexedConnector now share); the open mode is only ever the screen that follows. Each connector's Write opens with 'bool sequentialRelease = Access == KeyedAccess.Sequential', takes item 8 a)'s arm when true and item 8 b)'s when false; SequentialConnector.Write carries item 8 a) directly (12.4.5.5.2 SR2 admits only ACCESS SEQUENTIAL for a sequential file); READ/START answer item 7 and REWRITE/DELETE item 9 in both keyed connectors and in SequentialConnector; the blank Random x START row is enforced one level up, at bind, by KeyedIoBinder.BindStart's 14.9.41.3 SR1 screen (COBOLNET0862).
EVIDENCE. conformance:2023/l1_table20_seq_relative and conformance:2023/l1_table20_indexed walk EVERY cell of Table 20 that conforming source can reach -- 4 open modes x {READ, WRITE, REWRITE, START, DELETE RECORD} over sequential, relative and indexed organizations at all three access modes, 139 observations, each expected value derived from Table 20 plus 9.1.13.7 items 7/8/9 and every one observed. conformance:negative/pb325-start-random-access pins the blank Random x START row on BOTH keyed organizations at all four editions. The Random/Dynamic x WRITE x Extend cell is UNREACHABLE from conforming source -- 14.9.27.3 SR2 confines the EXTEND phrase to sequential access -- so it is pinned at the runtime by unit:Table20WriteOpenModeTests, whose four defect facts go RED if the open mode is put back into the branch predicate (measured) while its eight control facts stay green.
WHAT WAS FIXED. RelativeConnector.Write and IndexedConnector.Write selected the branch with '_access == KeyedAccess.Sequential || Mode == FileOpenMode.Extend'; the disjunct routed a random- or dynamic-access connector opened EXTEND into the sequential-release branch, whose own screen accepts extend, so the WRITE appended a record and reported '00' where item 8 b) requires '48'. That made a run-time answer depend on a bind-time syntax rule (SR2) that is enforced nowhere -- kb/Work PB318 -- so the runtime is now correct independently of it.
EDITIONS: Table 20 is version-invariant; the DELETE RECORD row for a sequentially-accessed relative/indexed file and the dynamic access mode ride the relative/indexed I-O modules present at every edition adjudicated here, and the negative fixture was observed rejecting at 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023.

subject: OPEN statement
notes: CONFORMS, and RE-DECIDED without a change of verdict (kb/Work PB802, owner decision 2026-09-07 verbatim: 'Let's match GNUCobol's implementation in spirit. No sidecar of any type.'; it supersedes the catalog PB193 landed). GR10's comparison still runs on FileConnector.Open BEFORE OpenCore (GR25 leaves an unsuccessful OPEN's file unaffected and the creation arms truncate), still returns FileStatusCode.FixedAttributeConflict '39' (9.1.13.6 item 7), and both OPEN dispatch arms still reach it (the plain registry Open and the sharing-active SharedOpenAttempt). WHAT CHANGED IS WHERE THE FILE'S ATTRIBUTES COME FROM: there is no catalog and no sidecar of any type (NTFS alternate data streams were considered and rejected with it), so a physical file's 9.1.6 fixed file attributes are whatever ITS OWN BYTES record. THE VALIDATED SET IS THEREFORE A RULE RATHER THAN A TABLE - exactly what each organization's format encodes - realized as three overrides of ONE virtual, FileConnector.FixedAttributeConflict, each beside the format it reads, so an organization added later brings its own answer instead of needing a row in a switch (the hand-kept MediumFixesRecordLayout classification is deleted). (1) Fixed-length record sequential and line sequential encode NOTHING, so nothing is validated - 9.1.7.2 puts those lengths in the data and in the reading program, and 9.1.13.2 items 3, 5 and 7 answer the disagreement with the SUCCESSFUL '04', '06' and '09'; a uniform set was MEASURED WRONG in 2026-08 (six conforming corpus programs red, one into an infinite READ loop). (2) A RECORD VARYING record-sequential file encodes its record type in 9.1.7.2's own 'record length headers' - COBOL.NET's 4-byte little-endian prefix, by the method 12.4.5.11.4 GR5 leaves to the implementor - so a first prefix naming more bytes than the file holds is not a framed file and the declared VARIABLE record type contradicts the medium: '39'. A prefix that PARSES but falls outside the RECORD clause's bounds is NOT a conflict; that is item 3's '04' on the READ, which a '39' at the OPEN would make unreachable (golden step 16 pins exactly that boundary). (3) RELATIVE and INDEXED encode the organization, record type, minimum and maximum logical record size and the key table in the framed store's HEADER, which is IN the data file as GnuCOBOL's ISAM key definitions are; a store with no readable header is '39' (loud) rather than a silent misread, and a zero-byte file is the one tolerated exception. The key check has a documented runtime opt-out, COBOLNET_KEYCHECK=OFF (GnuCOBOL's COB_KEYCHECK), read once per run unit and registered in RuntimeConfig. HONEST COST, PINNED AS A DECISION: PB193's original probe - a RELATIVE file reopened INPUT through a SEQUENTIAL or LINE SEQUENTIAL FD - no longer answers '39' but '00' (golden step 3, with its READ and its comment), because a sequential file's format states nothing for the store to contradict; the reverse direction still answers '39' (golden step 13) and RecordLayoutNotice still reports the byte-count disagreement on stderr. Surveyed, not assumed: GnuCOBOL's testsuite has exactly two status-39 cases, 'variable-length SEQUENTIAL data integrity' and 'INDEXED undeclared keys' with its COB_KEYCHECK=OFF opt-out, and both are reproduced.

notes: kb/Work PB317. notes: kb/Work PB328, LANDED. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.27.4 'If the I-O phrase is specified, the file shall support the input and output statements that are permitted for the organization of that file when opened in the I-O mode': OK, 16)): 'If the I-O phrase is specified, the file shall support the input and output statements that are permitted for the organization of that file when opened in the I-O mode. The successful execution of an OPEN statement with the I-O phrase sets the open mode of the file connector referenced by file-name-1 to open in the I-O mode.' TWO halves. HALF 2 (the open mode is set) was already conforming: FileConnector.Open assigns Mode and sets _openMode from the success family. HALF 1 (the '37') was the defect. WAS: the only producer of '37' for a write-incapable file was the shared catch (UnauthorizedAccessException) around OpenCore, which fired for SEQUENTIAL only because that organization's I-O and EXTEND arms open write-capable streams; the relative and indexed I-O arms merely Attach() (a READ of the store), so writability was never probed. Probed on a worktree build at 17c11fd4 with three files created by the compiler and then made read-only (a real host attribute, not a simulation): OPEN I-O answered SEQ '37', REL '00', IDX '00' on the SAME condition; the keyed successes were then believed downstream (READ '00', REWRITE '00') and the loss surfaced only as a '30' at CLOSE on a file whose MD5 was unchanged. The identical omission made OPEN EXTEND answer SEQ '37', REL '00', IDX '00' where 9.1.13.6 6) a) 1. requires '37' (cite.py --check 9.1.13.6 'the EXTEND or OUTPUT phrase is specified but the file will not support write operations': OK, 6) a) 1.); OPEN OUTPUT was already '37' on all three because its keyed arm eagerly calls RecordFraming.WriteStore. NOW: the write-capability question is an OPEN-CONTRACT question, asked ONCE above the organizations. HostFile.PermitsWrite (IO/FileSupport.cs) asks the host for a writable handle (FileMode.Open + FileAccess.Write + FileShare.ReadWrite, nothing written) and answers false only on UnauthorizedAccessException; every other IOException propagates so 9.1.13.6 1)'s '30' stays mapped in the one place. FileConnector.Open calls it for I-O, EXTEND and OUTPUT on a Present file, after GR10's '39' and before OpenCore, so every organization -- including one added later -- inherits the answer instead of re-earning it. GR16 names no organization and Table 20 is why it cannot: REWRITE sits under the I-O column for sequential, random AND dynamic access, so 'supports the statements permitted in the I-O mode' entails write capability whatever the organization. RE-PROBED after the fix on the same three read-only files: OPEN I-O 37/37/37, OPEN EXTEND 37/37/37, OPEN OUTPUT 37/37/37 -- nine cells. OVER-FIRE MEASURED, not assumed: the same read-only files still OPEN INPUT '00' and READ their record on all three organizations (a read-only file supports everything Table 20 permits in the input mode), and a WRITABLE file still opens I-O '00' and rewrites on all three. GR25 ('If the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful, the file is not affected', cite.py --check 14.9.27.4: OK, 25)) holds through the probe: content MD5 and last-write time are identical after the refused open. INPUT IS DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THE PROBE and the exclusion is required, not an optimization -- probing write for INPUT would refuse an OPEN the operating environment carries out perfectly, and 9.1.13.6 6) a) 3.'s read-capability question is answered by the organization's own eager read (measured on all three: see GR-9.1.13.6-6). BOTH HALVES OF GR16 ARE COVERED, not just the one that was defective: the rule says the file must support the input AND output statements the I-O mode permits, and Table 20 lists READ under the I-O column beside REWRITE, so a file this process may WRITE but not READ is equally '37'. Measured with icacls /deny :(RD) -- read DATA only, so a raw write open still succeeds and HostFile.PermitsWrite accepts the file -- OPEN I-O answered '37' on sequential, relative and indexed, produced by the organization's own eager read rather than by the write probe; unit:FileAuthorityPresenceTests.OpenIo_PresentAndWritableButNotReadable_Is37 asserts the write-probe premise first so the two halves cannot be confused. COVERING TESTS: unit:FileAuthorityPresenceTests establishes the precondition for real (a read-only attribute on Windows, mode 0400 on Unix) and verifies it with a RAW write open rather than with the subject under test; its nine GR16 cells were shown to FAIL (7 of them -- the four keyed I-O/EXTEND cells, the two keyed OPTIONAL cells and the GR25 inertness assertion) with the check disabled, and the three sequential cells and three OUTPUT cells stayed green, which is exactly the two-arm fingerprint the defect had. unit:HostFileProbeDriftTests keeps the question singular: PermitsWrite is banned outside FileConnector and its call count in the OPEN contract is pinned at one. No conformance golden can reach this arm -- the corpus runner compiles a .cob and compares its output, with nowhere to express 'and first make this file read-only'. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023 -- GR16 is version-invariant and docs/CONFORMANCE.md determines the '37' family is emitted at every edition, ungated.

notes: RULE: 'Upon successful execution of the OPEN statement, the current volume pointer is set: a) To point to the first or only reel/unit in the physical file if INPUT or I-O is specified. b) To point to the reel/unit containing the last record in the physical file if EXTEND is specified. c) To point to the newly created reel/unit in the physical file for an unavailable file if EXTEND, I-O, or OUTPUT is specified.' cite.py --check 14.9.27.4: OK (§14.9.27.4 19)). notes: kb/Work PB370. The emitted sequence is exactly the rule's order. EmitOpen emits the registry call, then EmitStoreFileStatus (a — the value is placed in the I-O status), then EmitUseHook. Inside the generated __IoCheckEc the body runs: `ExceptionState.SetIo(__ec!, IsFatalIoStatus(__st), ...)` when the name's checking bit is on (b — the level-3 EC-I-O condition associated with the status value, mapped by ExceptionCatalog.IoEcOfStatus per §9.1.13.1), then `__EcPerform(__ec!, __f)` consults the installed Format-3 PerformFrame FIRST (c), and only if that returns NoMatch do the F1 file-name / open-mode USE tiers and the outward GLOBAL walk run (d). §14.9.28.4 GR17's 'Any USE declarative that would normally match the exception condition is ignored' is what makes c) exclude d), and the emitter's own comment states it. PROBE (out-b1/probe/open-gr25): OPEN INPUT of an absent non-optional file with a `USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION PROCEDURE ON FN` declarative → the declarative runs and reports status 35, and the file is NOT created (a + d, and 'the file is not affected'); the same OPEN inside `PERFORM ... WHEN EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR ... END-PERFORM` → the WHEN body runs and the declarative does NOT (c), after which the run unit terminates abnormally naming EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR — which is §14.9.28.4 GR20's own tail ('If the exception condition was fatal, execution continues as specified in 14.6.13.1.3'), not a defect. CONFORMS-but-untested: no existing spec-derived test pins the OPEN-specific a-b-c-d ordering (conformance:2023/f3_perform_handler_turn_off_all covers the Format-3 machinery but not through an I-O statement). || REFUTED: PARTIAL — REFUTED, downward to PARTIAL. The rule has a leading requirement and then four ordered actions: 'If the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful, THE FILE IS NOT AFFECTED and the following actions take place in the following order: a) ... b) ... c) ... d)'. VERIFIED HALF -- the a-b-c-d machinery is right and I could not break it. EmitOpen emits the registry call, then EmitStoreFileStatus (a), then EmitUseHook; inside __IoCheckEc the order is SetIo (b), then the F3 PerformFrame via RunTopFrame (c), then, only when no WHEN matched, the F1 file-name and open-mode USE tiers, the F3 __EcDispatch tier and the outward GLOBAL walk (d) -- which is what 14.9.49.4 GR6 requires. I also closed the leg the adjudicator left unexercised: its probe ran a FORMAT 1 USE only, but GR25 d) names 'USE FOR EXCEPTION or USE AFTER EXCEPTION', so I probed a FORMAT 3 declarative (USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR under >>TURN ... CHECKING ON) on an unsuccessful OPEN INPUT: it runs, with FS=35, EXCEPTION-STATUS=EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR and EXCEPTION-FILE=35FN. The 9.1.13.1 status->EC map in ExceptionCatalog.IoEcOfStatus matches the standard's list digit for digit. UNVERIFIED-AND-VIOLATED HALF -- 'the file is not affected'. The adjudication tested this in the only direction that cannot lose data (an absent file is not CREATED by a failing OPEN INPUT). I tested the destructive direction and it fails. Connector FA holds po.dat open INPUT under SHARING WITH NO OTHER; connector FB, a plain SELECT on the same physical file, executes OPEN OUTPUT. 9.1.13.9 1) a) and Table 19 (whose 'sharing with no other' existing column is 'Unsuccessful open' in EVERY request row) make that OPEN unsuccessful with status 61, so GR25's own consequent applies and the file shall not be affected. The compiler reports 00 and TRUNCATES po.dat to zero bytes -- the record 'KEEPTHIS01' is gone. That is wrong-answer-with-data-loss on legal source, and it is GR25's own text that is violated, not merely the detection rule's. I checked the counter-hypothesis before charging it: every unsuccessful OPEN the implementation DOES recognise leaves the file intact -- 61 on a sharing-active incoming connector returns before c.Open(mode) is ever called, 41 returns at the top of FileConnector.Open, and 35/37/30 all return before or from the failing stream construction (I confirmed 61 and 41 by probe with the content re-read intact, and the OS-level conflict variant gives 30 with the file intact). So the failure is confined to spec-unsuccessful opens the implementation misclassifies as successful, whose ROOT cause (FileRegistry.Open consults the physical-file table only when the INCOMING connector is sharing-active) is already booked DIVERGES under GR-14.9.27.4-22/-23 -- I am not re-booking that defect, I am recording that GR25's leading clause is therefore unsatisfied and was never measured. Two halves, one verified => PARTIAL by the rubric; not DIVERGES, because the four ordered actions that are the substance of the rule are correct and probed. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023 for sub-rules a) and d); sub-rules b) and c) ride the exception-condition facility and the Format-3 exception-checking PERFORM, 2002 introductions, so they are adjudicated at 2002 / 2014 / 2023.

notes:
kb/Work PB331 LANDED. RULE: 'The LOCK phrase shall not be specified in the same READ statement as the IGNORING LOCK phrase.' (cite.py --check 14.9.30.3 OK.) 'The LOCK phrase' means WITH LOCK and NOT WITH NO LOCK: the standard names them apart in this very statement - GR11 b) 'except when the NO LOCK phrase is specified' and GR11 d) 'the record lock ... is set only if the LOCK phrase is specified on the READ statement' (both cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 OK).
THE RULE NOW HAS A CHECK, AND IT IS THE RULE'S OWN SHAPE. `FileLockBinder.CheckIgnoringLock` raises COBOLNET1818 when the IGNORING LOCK alternative of 14.9.30.2's contention bracket is written together with WITH LOCK from the retention bracket, and NOT when it is written with WITH NO LOCK. Both READ arms reach it: SequentialIoBinder.BindRead and KeyedIoBinder.BindRead each bind the retention bracket first and pass it in, so the two-arm shape cannot be half-fixed. MEASURED at --std 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023: `READ SQF NEXT RECORD IGNORING LOCK WITH LOCK ...` -> `error COBOLNET1818: READ on file 'SQF': the LOCK phrase shall not be specified in the same READ statement as the IGNORING LOCK phrase (ISO 14.9.30.3 SR3)`, exit 70, at every edition.
WHAT THE PREVIOUS RECORD SAID, AND WHY IT WAS RIGHT TO CALL IT PARTIAL. notes: Rule text (cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 "the content of any data item, where any part of that data item lies beyond the range of the current record, is undefined" => OK 3)). The rule imposes NO requirement: it declares the content UNDEFINED, and it is registered as such in Annex A.2 item 41 (Undefined language element list — unlike A.1, A.2 carries no documentation obligation). COBOL.NET makes the choice DETERMINATE: FileConnector.Fit pads/truncates the physical record to the record-area width with SPACES, and SequentialIoEmitter.EmitImageInto stores that full-width image into FileModel.AreaRecord (the LARGEST record description, §13.4.2), so every position past the current record reads as a space. notes: RULE: 'If the IGNORING LOCK phrase is specified on the READ statement, the requested record is made available, even if it is locked.' cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'the requested record is made available, even if it is locked' -> OK 14.9.30.4 12). BOTH ARMS VERIFIED. Sequential: ReadShared guards the whole conflict block with `if (phrase != FileRecordLock.Ignoring && f.ReadEligible)`, so an IGNORING LOCK read falls straight through to f.Read and the locked record is delivered. Keyed: ReadLockGovern wraps only the conflict block in `if (phrase != FileRecordLock.Ignoring)`, and the physical read has already happened, so the record is likewise made available. ApplyReadLockDiscipline maps Ignoring to wantLock=false, so an IGNORING LOCK read neither acquires nor (under multiple locking) releases -- consistent with 14.9.30.3 SR3/SR4, which bar combining IGNORING LOCK with LOCK and bar it entirely under automatic locking. Grammar carries it (recordLockPhrase: IGNORING LOCK | WITH? NO LOCK | WITH? LOCK, ordered so WITH NO LOCK is not shadowed) and the 2002 introduction gate fires on the bound phrase (VersionConformancePass.GateStatement -> Constructs.RecordLockPhrase2002). notes: kb/Work PB341 LANDED. RULE: 'For an indexed file being sequentially accessed, records having the same duplicate value in an alternate record key that is the key of reference are made available in the same order, or, in the case of PREVIOUS, in the reverse order, in which they are released by execution of WRITE statements, or by execution of REWRITE statements that create such duplicate values.' VALIDATED: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 "records having the same duplicate value in an alternate record key that is the key of reference are made available in the same order" -> OK 26). WAS DIVERGES: KeyedRec carried ONE Arrival for the whole record and IndexedConnector.Rewrite collapsed its per-key loop into one altChanged bool, so a REWRITE that changed ANY alternate key repositioned the record last in the duplicate set of EVERY alternate key - contrary to 14.9.35.4 GR24 a) ('When the value of a specific alternate record key is not changed, the order of retrieval when that key is the key of reference remains unchanged', --check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)). MEASURED before the fix (probe pb341a.cob: 01/AA/PP and 02/AA/PP released in that order, then REWRITE of 01 changing only R-A1): the R-A2 walk answered 02 then 01. NOW: KeyedRec.Ordinals is a VECTOR - slot 0 the prime key, slot i+1 the i-th alternate; Write stamps one fresh ordinal into every slot (the record is released under every key at once, 14.9.51.4 GR40); Rewrite re-stamps ONLY the keys whose value or SUPPRESS WHEN state actually changed, and the changed test is KeyEq under the key's collating sequence per GR24's closing sentence ('The comparison used for determining changes to the key is based on the collating sequence for the file according to the rules for a relation condition', --check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)); Ordered(keyIndex) ties on THAT key's ordinal; PersistOrder writes the physical file in a topological order of the per-key duplicate orders so a reload - which can only give every key the file's own order - reproduces all of them. PINNED: conformance:2023/l1_rewrite_alt_key_order legs B and C (an untouched R-A2 keeps 01,02,03 while the changed R-A1 moves the record last in its new set) and leg D (both orders survive CLOSE/OPEN); the forward and reverse duplicate walks are pinned by conformance:2023/l1_read_alt_dup_walk and conformance:2023/l1_start_dup_set_entry. RESIDUE (a NEW, separate defect, not this rule's): the per-key orders can be made mutually CYCLIC by a REWRITE that moves one record into another's duplicate set under key A while both stay duplicates under key B, and no single sequence of record images can then carry both orders across a CLOSE - the physical framing has one order and the model has one per key. PersistOrder appends the cyclic residue in release order, which loses one key's repositioning.

notes: kb/Work PB341 LANDED. RULE: 'For an indexed file accessed through a given file connector, execution of a READ statement sets the file position indicator to the value in the key of reference. This value is compared with the value contained in the corresponding data item of the stored records in the file until the first record having an equal value is found. A format-2 random READ is not a sequential access, so 14.9.30.4 GR27's '02' never applies to it - it reports '00'.
