notes: kb/Work PB347 LANDED; closes the half kb/Work PB236 left open. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.32.3 'Record-name-1 shall be the name of a logical record in a sort-merge file description entry and it may be qualified.' -> OK, 14.9.32.3 1). BOTH DEFECTS THIS ROW CARRIED ARE NOW FIXED. (1) STAGE, closed by PB236: the rejection is a COMPILE-TIME COBOLNET1757 naming SR1, not a run-time NotImplemented.Run. (2) PREDICATE, closed here: seqIo.FileOfRecord tested CONTAINMENT -- it walked the reference's ancestry to its top-level 01 and asked whether THAT root was a file's record, so 'the reference lies somewhere INSIDE an SD record' passed, and `RELEASE SR-DATA` on a 05 item injected a record the program never released (measured before the fix on this worktree's own build: the output procedure returned R=[BBBbbbbb] AND R=[aaaaa   ], the second being SR-DATA's 5-byte image space-extended to the SD's 8). The rule now has ONE home for all three verbs that print record-name-1, StatementValidation.ResolveRecordName, which tests IDENTITY -- the reference IS a FileModel.Records entry -- and refuses a reference-modified one (see FMT-14.9.32.2). The containment walk survives only as the message: 'SR-DATA is subordinate to SRT-REC, which is the logical record of SRTF -- name that record, not one of its items'. The qualification half stays CONFORMS: `RELEASE SRT-REC OF SRTF` binds, pinned in both positive goldens. Edition-invariant -- the sentence is identical in 1985, 2002 and 2014, so no gate exists and each negative carries `*> reject-at: 85 2002 2014 2023`.

subject: RELEASE statement
notes: kb/Work PB348 LANDED. RULE (`--check 14.9.32.3 "If identifier-1 is a function-identifier, it shall reference an alphanumeric or national function."` => OK). WHAT WAS ABSENT: nothing screened the function's result class in this position. The FROM phrase of RELEASE, WRITE and REWRITE alike bound its operand through SequentialIoBinder.WriteSource, an unconditional three-way hand-off that INSPECTED NOTHING, so each verb's own phrase rule was applied by no one. WHAT IS THERE NOW: MoveBinder.BindFromPhrase applies the rule from a FromPhraseRules row, ONE PER VERB, because the three verbs name DIFFERENT SETS and a scalar column would reject legal source: RELEASE (14.9.32.3 SR2) and WRITE (14.9.51.3 SR4) admit an alphanumeric or national function, REWRITE (14.9.35.3 SR9, the FILE phrase not specified) also admits a boolean one. The FILE-phrase readings (14.9.51.3 SR10, 14.9.35.3 SR8) are unreachable: the FILE arm is Annex A.4.13 item 2 and is declined COBOLNET1706 earlier. The class is read off the BOUND operand through the SAME Table-16 sender position the category screen uses (MoveBinder.SenderPosition), which is what makes a folded FUNCTION LENGTH -- it reaches the binder as a plain numeric literal -- answer 'numeric' rather than 'unknown'. DIAGNOSTIC COBOLNET1914. MEASURED before: `RELEASE SRT-REC FROM FUNCTION LENGTH(WS-A).` compiled clean at 85, 2002 and 2023 and released R=[8       ]. MEASURED after: refused at every edition, and the WRITE and REWRITE siblings with it. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2002 . 2014 . 2023

subject: RELEASE statement
notes: kb/Work PB348 LANDED. RULE (`--check 14.9.32.3 "Identifier-1 or literal-1 shall be valid as a sending operand in a MOVE statement specifying record-name-1 as the receiving operand."` => OK). WHAT WAS ABSENT: the MOVE statement's own screens. They run at BIND time in MoveBinder -- the 14.9.25.3 Table-16 legality arms, the SR1 class-index test, the SR5 figurative edition gates and CheckStrongMove -- and RELEASE reached none of them, because SortBinder.BindRelease only bound the OPERAND and the implicit MOVE was FIRST CONSTRUCTED AT EMIT TIME (`SortEmitter.EmitRelease: move.Emit(new BoundMove(from, [rl.Record]))`), downstream of every one. DECISIVE PAIR, measured: `MOVE WS-NUM TO SRT-REC` (PIC 9(3) into PIC A(8)) drew COBOLNET0819 while the equivalent `RELEASE SRT-REC FROM WS-NUM` compiled clean and printed R=[123     ]. WHAT IS THERE NOW: BindFromPhrase routes the operand through MoveBinder.BindMoveOf -- THE one application of the MOVE statement's rules to a sender/receiver pair, shared with the explicit MOVE statement -- so the same rules reach the phrase by construction rather than by an edit, and the diagnostic names the statement the programmer wrote ('the implicit MOVE of RELEASE ... FROM to SRT-REC (ISO 14.9.32.4 GR4 a); 14.9.32.3 SR3)'). The drift test ImplicitMoveConstructionDriftTests keeps `new BoundMove` out of the I-O and sort emitters. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 . 2002 . 2014 . 2023

subject: RELEASE statement
notes: kb/Work PB348 LANDED. RULE (`--check 14.9.32.3 "Literal-1 shall not be a zero-length literal."` => OK). WHAT WAS ABSENT: the length test -- WriteSource routed literal-1 straight to host.Expr.LiteralOperand with no inspection. It was a missing APPLICATION, not a missing capability: the same BoundStringLiteral { Value.Length: 0 } predicate is applied in ControlFlowBinder (the STOP RUN / GOBACK status literal, COBOLNET1704), IntrinsicBinder, DataBinder.Switches and CallBinder, and the premise was proved rather than assumed -- `STOP RUN WITH ERROR STATUS "".` is rejected, so the compiler both lexes and models "" as a zero-length literal. WHAT IS THERE NOW: the rule rides the RELEASE row of FromPhraseRules and is applied by BindFromPhrase, diagnostic COBOLNET1915. It is RELEASE's rule ALONE -- neither 14.9.51.3 nor 14.9.35.3 states it for the FROM phrase -- which is why the rules table carries it as a nullable clause per verb rather than a screen every FROM phrase pays. The 1985 leg is outside the golden's reject-at header: at X3.23-1985 the FROM phrase admits only identifier-1, so a literal sender is refused by COBOLNET0871 before SR4 is reached. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2002 . 2014 . 2023

subject: RELEASE statement
notes: kb/Work PB349 (landed, wave 56). RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.32.4 'the EC-FLOW-RELEASE exception condition is set to exist' -> OK 14.9.32.4 1)). The sort store now carries the executing statement's procedure PHASE (CobolSort.Store.Phase, set by the emitted EnterProcedure before the INPUT PROCEDURE range and cleared by the sequence phase); the RELEASE STATEMENT renders CobolSort.ReleaseStatement, which raises EC-FLOW-RELEASE through ExceptionState.FlowReleaseError before releasing whenever no store exists for the SD or its phase is not Input. FatalAmbientGates row (EC-FLOW-RELEASE, FlowReleaseChecking) + QueryFor(BoundRelease) give the statement its >>TURN guard, so the condition reaches a USE declarative (14.6.13.1.3 item 5) or terminates (item 7). The implicit USING release keeps the unchecked Release primitive (it is not a RELEASE statement). Checking OFF: nothing is raised (14.6.13.1.1) and the release proceeds, except that a RELEASE with no SORT executing has no store to release to - the 14.6.13.1.3 item 8 implementor choice. Golden pb349_sort_merge_flow_ec: MAIN's RELEASE outside any SORT -> HANDLED=EC-FLOW-RELEASE, the record is not released, and the two RELEASEs inside IN-P raise nothing (negative control).

subject: RELEASE statement
notes: RULE (`--check 14.9.32.4 "The execution of a RELEASE statement causes the record named by record-name-1 to be released to the initial phase of a sort operation."` => OK 14.9.32.4 2). WHAT THE CODE DOES: SortEmitter.EmitRelease renders record-name-1's own character image and calls `CobolSort.Release(sd, image)`, which appends it to that SD's per-file image buffer in release order (CobolSort.cs:77) -- the buffer the SORT's sequence phase then orders and the RETURN phase drains, i.e. exactly the initial phase. The image is a C# string, so the store holds a snapshot: a later mutation of the record area cannot alter an already-released record. THREE LENGTH SHAPES READ AND VERIFIED, all three per 13.18.43.4 GR13 (`--check 13.18.43.4 "During the execution of a RELEASE, REWRITE, or WRITE statement, the number of bytes in the record is determined by the following conditions"` => OK 13.18.43.4 13): (a) fixed SD -- the named record's own width (probe out-b1/probe/base/base.cob returns AAAaaaaa / BBBbbbbb / CCCccccc in key order); (b) RECORD VARYING ... DEPENDING ON -- GR13a's length, emitted as `StrRefMod(image, 1, (int)dep)` (`--check 13.18.43.4 "If data-name-1 is specified, by the content of the data item referenced by data-name-1."` => OK 13.18.43.4 13) a)); (c) GR13c, a variable-occurrence record with no DEPENDING ON in the RECORD clause -- probe out-b1/probe/odo/odo.cob generates `CobolSort.Release("RELODO::SRTF", SRT_REC.AsImage().Substring(0, CobolTable.OdoExtentChars(CobolTable.Occ(WS_OCC), 1, 9, 6, 2, 1)))`, i.e. fixed portion 6 + 2 occurrences x 2 = 10 bytes, not the maximum. COVERING TEST is spec-derived (AssertSpec with expectations computed from the standard, not from the legacy oracle) and cites 14.9.32 GR2 in its own section header. EDITIONS: Annex E lists no substantive change to 14.9.32; the rule is edition-neutral in its own text.

subject: RESUME statement
notes: Rule: 'The RESUME statement may be specified only in a declarative or in an imperative statement in a WHEN phrase of an exception-checking PERFORM statement. In the latter case, the NEXT STATEMENT phrase shall be specified.' (cite.py --check 14.9.33.3 'In the latter case, the NEXT STATEMENT phrase shall be specified' -> OK §14.9.33.3 1)). BindResume asks the ONE bind-position probe ctx.Enclosing: InPerformWhen admits NEXT STATEMENT and refuses procedure-name with COBOLNET1610; outside any declarative (ordinary paragraph, imperative-statement-1, FINALLY) it refuses with COBOLNET0712. Both halves verified: the theory PBRS01-05 covers a WHEN phrase, a statement nested inside a WHEN phrase, imp-1 and FINALLY (rejected) and a plain paragraph (rejected), all with SR1-quoted expectations; Resume_AtProcedureNameInAWhenPhrase_IsRejected covers the second sentence; ExceptionConditionConformanceTests.Resume_OutsideDeclaratives_Diagnosed and PerformFormat3Tests' imp-1 case also pin 0712. PROBED in addition: RESUME NEXT STATEMENT in WHEN OTHER and in WHEN COMMON (both WHEN phrases of the general format) is admitted and runs (sr1w.cob -> SIZE / COMMON / END). A RESUME inside a WHEN phrase that is itself inside a declarative is treated under the WHEN branch (NEXT STATEMENT required) - a reading the text supports, since the statement is then 'in a WHEN phrase'.

subject: RESUME statement
notes: Rule: 'Procedure-name-1 shall be a procedure-name in the nondeclarative portion of the function, method, or program.' (cite.py --check 14.9.33.3 -> OK §14.9.33.3 3)). BindResume resolves procedure-name-1 through the ONE procedure-operand resolution (scoped to the source element, so a name of another program does not resolve) and refuses a target whose SECTION is declarative (target.IsDeclarative, PB433) with COBOLNET0714. PROBED with the pinned cobol.exe: RESUME AT a declarative paragraph (sr3_D2.cob) and RESUME AT the declarative section itself (sr3_D.cob) -> COBOLNET0714; RESUME AT an undeclared name (sr3_X9.cob) -> COBOLNET1639; RESUME AT a nondeclarative paragraph compiles and transfers (gr3b.cob). pb1010_method_declaratives exercises the method arm. subject: RESUME statement
notes: VERDICTED CONFORMS by kb/Work PB892. RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT's implicit CONTINUE: a) an exception-entered declarative returns -2 from __RunUse to the raise site, which completes the applicable statement - 1. the raising statement, 2. the CALL/INVOKE or the statement a function/inline invocation is written in (BoundActivationSite), 3. the lowest such statement. b) a declarative entered by a PERFORM in the nondeclarative portion (14.9.49.3 SR4) - 'the implicit CONTINUE statement immediately follows the last statement of the terminating procedure referenced in that PERFORM statement' - used to have NO landing: the ResumeSignal escaped every frame and the run unit died with an unhandled .NET exception (probe w48s/p6). BoundOutOfLinePerform.EntersDeclarative marks that PERFORM (range declarative, PERFORM not itself in a declarative) and ControlFlowEmitter.EmitPerformedRange catches ResumeSignal around the range: NEXT STATEMENT completes this execution of the range (the TIMES/UNTIL phrase goes on), procedure-name is GR3's GO TO. The golden covers TIMES, a SECTION range (the section's later paragraph is skipped), RESUME AT procedure-name, and the exception entry of the same declarative. The transcription dedents b) to column 0, so cite.py locates the b) text under '2) a) 3.'; it is GR2 b) in the printed standard. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/EmitterState.cs#OperandActivationResume (kb/Work PB1432 made the operand landing the ONE ResumeTransfer inside the operand-evaluation scope StatementEmitter.EmitStatement opens (OperandActivationResume became the private OperandEvaluationResume); the public method no longer exists)

subject: RETURN statement
notes: kb/Work PB236 (landed). RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.34.3 'File-name-1 shall be described by a sort-merge file description entry in the data division.' -> OK, 14.9.34.3 1). A SYNTAX rule, so the obligation is on the compiler at compile time (cite.py --check 4.2.2 'An implementation shall provide a warning mechanism that optionally may be invoked by the user at compile time to indicate violations of the general formats and the explicit syntax rules of standard COBOL.' -> OK). The predicate and the citation were already right at BindReturn; only the STAGE was wrong -- BoundUnsupported is not a diagnostic, StatementEmitter rendered it as NotImplemented.Run, and probe p14 (the same illegal RETURN on a paragraph the flow jumps over) compiled AND ran to normal completion. Both are now fixed, and the ONE test the old code wrote has been split into the TWO verdicts it was conflating: `!FilesByName.TryGetValue(...) || !file.IsSortMerge` answered 'there is no such file-name' (8.4.2.1) and 'the file exists but is described by an FD' (14.9.34.3 SR1) with one message, which told a user whose file was right there in the FILE SECTION that the name was undefined. The undeclared case now goes through StatementValidation.ResolveFile -> COBOLNET1639, and SR1 itself through CheckReturnFile -> COBOLNET1757. Measured on a build of this worktree, RETURN behind a GO TO: `error COBOLNET1757: RETURN 'F-IN' -- file-name-1 shall be described by a sort-merge (SD) file description entry in the data division (ISO 14.9.34.3 SR1); this file is described by an FD`. Witness: conformance:negative/pb236-return-file-not-sd for the prohibition, conformance:2002/pb64t1_sort_locale_snapshot for the admitted RETURN over a real SD.

subject: RETURN statement
notes: kb/Work PB337, LANDED. The RETURN twin of SR-14.9.30.3-1, and the SAME screen: SortBinder.BindReturn reaches it through MoveBinder.BindIntoPhrase with IntoPhraseRules.Return, so the two verbs cannot drift. The wording difference is carried on the rules row rather than in a second code path -- RETURN's arm a) reads 'If only one record description is subordinate to the sort-merge file description entry', with no record-less admission, because 13.4.6.3 SR2 requires a record description under an SD (and the binder already rejects one that has none), where 13.4.5.3 SR3 permits a record-less FD. Arm b) is the identical operand set, so it is the identical ItemCategory.IsAlphanumericOrNational call over identifier-1 and every SD record. Diagnostic COBOLNET1994. PRE-FIX MEASUREMENT: an SD with '01 S-REC' (an alphanumeric group) and '01 S-NUM PIC 9(6)' (elementary, category numeric) returned INTO an alphanumeric group compiled AND RAN on this worktree's own build, printing INTO=1ONE / INTO=2TWO; it now draws COBOLNET1994 at all four editions. The positive golden's case R is the RETURN over-reject guard -- an SD with TWO alphanumeric-group records into an alphanumeric group is ADMITTED by arm b) and returns its record unchanged.

subject: RETURN statement
notes: kb/Work PB337, LANDED. The RETURN twin of SR-14.9.30.3-2, split the same way: the COUNT -- 'there shall be exactly one record area subordinate to the SD for file-name-1' -- is CheckIntoReceiver's (COBOLNET1995), and the second sentence, 'This record area shall be a strongly-typed group item of the same type as identifier-1', is CheckStrongMove's over the implicit move's sender (COBOLNET1533, kb/Work PB348). subject: REWRITE statement
notes: A successful REWRITE releases the record to the operating environment, not to a buffer, and the OBSERVABLE content of that is what ANOTHER file connector over the same physical file then reads: OverwriteInPlace is the ONE in-place overwrite for both sequential framings (the record-sequential GR16/GR20 arm and the line-sequential GR17 arm validate differently and release identically), and it seeks to the record's byte anchor, writes, FLUSHES, and announces the release on the physical file's shared state (NoteRelease -> PhysicalFileTable.State.ReleaseGeneration) so no sibling connector's read-ahead can keep serving the superseded image. The keyed organizations release into the per-physical-file shared record store, which every attached connector sees the instant the mutation happens (kb/Work PB143). MEASURED, both goldens: over 300 records, reader R takes record 1, sibling W rewrites a later record to NEW and reports '00', and R's next reads are OLD then NEW on record-sequential FIXED width, RECORD VARYING, LINE SEQUENTIAL (2023 only), a CLAUSE-LESS pair, RELATIVE and INDEXED. The SHARING WITH ALL OTHER legs close W before R reads on, which is the reported shape; the CLAUSE-LESS leg instead re-fills R's read-ahead AFTER W's OPEN and reads with W STILL OPEN, because a change in the 9.1.15 union repostures - and therefore rebuilds and empties - the other connectors' handles, which for the undetermined-default spelling would hide the defect (measured: with the coherence rule injected out, that leg still printed NEW while the three ALL OTHER legs printed OLD). Before kb/Work PB753 the four sequential legs all read OLD while the physical file held NEW, with '00' from every statement. COBOL-85 has no file sharing, so the sibling observation cannot be made there; the release itself is the same code on every edition.

subject: REWRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB702 (the row PB341 made true and did not claim). RULE — all six obligations of GR24, each re-derived on this tree, never inherited: (a) 'When the value of a specific alternate record key is not changed, the order of retrieval when that key is the key of reference remains unchanged' (cite.py --check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)); (b) 'When the value of a specific alternate record key is changed … the record is logically positioned last within the set of duplicate records where the alternate record key value is equal to the same alternate key value in one or more records in the file based on the collating sequence for the file' (--check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)); (c) the FIRST SUPPRESS WHEN sub-rule, 'If the SUPPRESS WHEN phrase is specified in the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause and the value of the alternate record key is no longer equal to the literal specified in that phrase: 1. an access path to this record using this key of reference shall be provided, and 2. the record shall be logically positioned so that it will be found when accessed using the alternate record key' (--check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)); (d) the SECOND SUPPRESS WHEN sub-rule, 'If alternate record key suppression is specified for this alternate record key and the value of this alternate record key is now equal to its key suppression value: 1. the access path to the record using this alternate record key shall no longer be provided, and 2. the record shall be logically repositioned so that it will not be found when accessed using this alternate record key' (--check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)); (e) 'The comparison used for determining changes to the key is based on the collating sequence for the file according to the rules for a relation condition' (--check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)); (f) 'Any number of records may have the same alternate key value equal to its key suppression value without requiring the DUPLICATES phrase to be specified for that key. Key entries that are suppressed shall not cause a duplicate key condition to exist' (--check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)). CODE: IndexedConnector.Rewrite runs TWO passes over _alts and the order is load-bearing — pass 1 validates only (an early '22' must leave nothing repositioned), pass 2 applies GR24 while target.Image is still the REPLACED record so AltChanged compares against it. (a)/(b): the local AltChanged(i) is the ONE definition of 'this REWRITE changed alternate key i', and only the keys it answers true for take a fresh release ordinal off the monotone mint (Stamp(target, i, repositioned)), so an untouched key keeps its ordinal and Ordered(i) keeps its order, while a changed key sorts after every existing member of its new duplicate set. (e): AltChanged is KeyEq, the file's collating sequence, not an ordinal string compare. (c)/(d): AltChanged also returns true when IsSuppressed(image, i) != IsSuppressed(target.Image, i), so entering OR leaving suppression is a change of its own and re-stamps the key; the access path itself is Ordered(keyIndex)'s Where(r => !IsSuppressed(r.Image, keyIndex)) (12.4.5.6.4 GR6), which withdraws and restores the path from the key VALUE with no separate state to drift. (f): pass 1 does `if (IsSuppressed(image, i)) continue;` before the uniqueness test and also excludes suppressed records from the `exists` scan, so a suppressed entry can neither raise '22' on a non-DUPLICATES key nor be duplicated by one. MEASURED on this worktree's build (c34f01ad + this change) by conformance:2023/l1_rewrite_alt_key_suppress, whose 20 expected lines were WRITTEN FROM THE SPEC BEFORE THE FIRST RUN and matched byte for byte: leg B REWRITEs record 01's R-A1 to the suppression value 'XX' and the R-A1 walk drops from 01,03,02 to 03,02 at status '00' (d); leg C REWRITEs it back to 'AA' and the walk becomes 03,01,02 — the access path is restored (c 1.) and 01, which was FIRST in the AA set on release, comes back LAST (c 2. + b), with the REWRITE itself reporting '02' per 9.1.13.2 2 c); leg D REWRITEs two records to 'ZZ', the suppression value of an alternate key with NO DUPLICATES phrase, and both report '00' rather than the '22' a real duplicate would raise, after which the R-A2 walk finds only the one unsuppressed record (f); leg E re-walks after CLOSE/OPEN and both the restored position and the two withdrawn paths survive the physical file. conformance:2023/l1_rewrite_alt_key_order (kb/Work PB341) independently pins (a), (b) and (e) on two DUPLICATES alternate keys without suppression. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 85 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023 for (a), (b) and (e) — ALTERNATE RECORD KEY and its DUPLICATES phrase are ungated in this compiler (no constructs.json row), the clause carries no edition marker, and Annex E lists no change to 14.9.35; this matches the band the sibling rows GR-14.9.30.4-26 and GR-14.9.30.4-32 were landed at on the same golden. Sub-rules (c), (d) and (f) are 2023-ONLY: they exist only where SUPPRESS WHEN is writable, and SUPPRESS WHEN is a COBOL-2023 addition (cite.py --check E.3.3 'The SUPPRESS WHEN phrase may be specified as part of the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause' -> OK, item 42), gated by constructs.json row 'alternate-key-suppress-when-2023' (COBOLNET0900 below 2023) — so the 2023 golden is the only edition at which they CAN be measured, and they are vacuous, not unverified, at 85/2002/2014.

notes: kb/Work/PB447.md LANDED — the one contradicted proposition is now delivered, so all four of GR9's normative propositions hold and the row closes. WHAT CHANGED: Format 2 no longer rides Format 1's scan. The emitter's single advance-then-test loop was split into TWO lowerings derived from the two rules that disagree — ControlFlowEmitter.EmitSerialScan (GR4, which forms the new index value and then judges it, so an unsuccessful serial search still ends at N+1, the state GR4 contemplates in as many words) and ControlFlowEmitter.EmitAllScan (GR9, which tests the bound BEFORE advancing, so the index moves only onto an occurrence that exists). The WHEN arms stay in ONE shared emission (EmitSearchWhens) because GR1/GR2 are ALL FORMATS rules, and the AT-END funnel stays shared for the same reason (GR1 b). BoundSearch.FromStart was renamed IsAll: the flag now selects a lowering rather than tweaking one. MEASURED, same probes as the defect record: gr9_nomatch_index over OCCURS 5 printed ATEND KX=06 / READ K(KX)=[0] / AFTER KX=06 before and prints ATEND KX=05 / READ K(KX)=[9] / AFTER KX=05 after — an in-range setting whose subscript reads a real element. The occurs-depending shape is the sharper case because storage and table differ: a 3-of-5 ODO table leaves JX=3 and J(JX)=5, not 4 and a phantom. The empty-table leg is unchanged (JX=1, NO-MATCH) and is now correct BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by accident — EmitAllScan makes no probe when no permissible setting exists. 'The initial setting of the search index is ignored' is now covered by a test and not only by a probe (SearchAll_IgnoresTheInitialSettingOfTheSearchIndex SETs KX to 5 past the only match at occurrence 1 and still finds it), closing the gap the previous record named in ec_range_search. THE FORMAT-1 COUNTERPART IS PINNED TOO, in the same class (Serial_Unsuccessful_LeavesTheIndexOnePastTheTable asserts 6 of 5), so the bound cannot later be swept onto the format GR4 licenses for it. Assertions on the unsuccessful Format-2 exit are RANGE assertions, never equality: GR9's own 'the final setting of the search index is undefined' (Annex A undefined item 51) forbids pinning WHICH in-range occurrence is left, while 'At no time is it set to a value that exceeds ... the last element of the table' is what is pinned. The failure branch was exercised: with the advance restored to its pre-fix order, 13 of the class's 37 cases go red across all four editions and all three table shapes (fixed, occurs-depending, OCCURS DYNAMIC); the empty-table case stays green, which is why a suite without the range assertions held this open. notes: kb/Work/PB390.md — The rule's DISCRIMINATING case now decides it, at bind. §8.4.4.1: 'There are two kinds of condition-names' — the level-88 kind, associated with a conditional variable, and the SPECIAL-NAMES kind, associated with the on/off status of an implementor-defined switch — and SR6 admits only the first. A switch-status condition-name draws COBOLNET1757 quoting SR6 and pointing at Format 3 (SET mnemonic-name-1 TO ON|OFF, SR5, whose sibling refusal moved to bind time in the same change set); a word that names nothing draws COBOLNET1639. The old message was worse than late: it read 'SET SW-ON TO TRUE (not a condition-name)' while SW-ON IS a condition-name, denying the fact the rule turns on, and it was staged to a run-time abort so the program compiled and shipped. The satisfied half is pinned by the positive golden's `SET WS-FLAG-YES TO TRUE` (§14.9.39.4 moves the VALUE literal to the conditional variable: FLAG=Y). DETERMINATION, owner-overturnable: §8.4.4.1's closing sentence about the switch kind — 'This condition-name may also be used in a SET statement to set the associated switch' — was read as describing the ABILITY to alter the switch (through Format 3 on its mnemonic) rather than as admitting condition-name-1 into a SET format, because Format 3's general format, rendered from the printed page rather than the transcription (PDF p759), prints `{ mnemonic-name-1 } … TO { ON | OFF }` with no condition-name alternative, and Format 4's SR6 excludes the switch kind by name. Nothing that used to RUN is refused by this reading: the statement aborted the run unit before.

subject: SET statement
notes: kb/Work PB456. The receiver screen ('Identifier-3 shall be any item of class object that is permitted as a receiving item', with EXCEPTION-OBJECT refused per 8.4.3.6 SR1) was always complete and self-citing; the verdict rested on the statement never REACHING it. Format 5 used to be entered only when the sender was exactly one bare dataReference (OoExtractBareReference), so a literal or expression sender declined the re-route and dropped an object-reference receiver onto the Format-1 arithmetic path where no SET operand rule applied at all. Format 5 is now selected from the RECEIVING list, so every statement with an object-reference receiver reaches this screen whatever the sender looks like. WAVE-41 FINISHER: two more arms of the same rule. (a) The SENDER can now identify Format 5 where the receiving list could not: Format 1's identifier-1 brace admits any identifier, so SET N4 TO U selected Format 1 and the object sender reached the ARITHMETIC screen (COBOLNET0844, "'U' ... is not a numeric operand") while the rule the program broke was SR8. 8.8.1.1 admits only numeric operands in arithmetic-expression-1 and SR2 makes identifier-2 class index, so an item of class object is admissible in NO Format-1 sending position and is named by exactly one format's sending brace - SelectForTo picks it and SR8 refuses the receiver by name. (b) The receiver screen was ONE arm testing Resolve-or-category, so it stacked SR8 on top of the resolver's own COBOLNET1639 for an undefined name, and reported a FALSE 'not defined' for an INDEX-NAME receiver, which 13.18.38.3 SR7 permits in a SET statement and which is not a data reference at all; it is now three arms, one rule each. MEASURED at 2002/2014/2023: SET N4 TO U and SET IX TO U each draw exactly one COBOLNET0867.

notes:
kb/Work/PB388.md — Citations validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "an object reference described with an interface-name that identifies int-1 or an interface inheriting from int-1"` -> OK 10); `"if described without a FACTORY phrase, the objects of the specified class shall implement int-1"` -> OK 10); `"if described with a FACTORY phrase, the factory object of the specified class shall implement int-1"` -> OK 10).

FOUR OF THE FIVE ALTERNATIVES ARE IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED (probe file setp1_o2.py, --std 2023, one compilation group with interfaces IA / IB-inherits-IA / IZ and classes CB-implements-IA / CD-inherits-CB / CX):
- a) an interface sender that inherits int-1: `SET RA TO RB` (RA is OBJECT REFERENCE IA, RB is OBJECT REFERENCE IB, IB INHERITS FROM IA) COMPILES AND RUNS (p1a_iface_inherit -> OK). The negative control `SET RA TO RZ` is refused: COBOLNET0867 'interface IZ does not inherit interface IA' (p1b_iface_unrelated). OoConformance.cs:384-403 walks the inheritance closure, so a transitively-inheriting interface is admitted too.
- b2) a class sender WITHOUT a FACTORY phrase whose objects implement int-1: `SET RA TO OB` binds and the interface view is live - INVOKE RA "PING" prints PONG (p2a_class_impl). A SUBCLASS of the implementing class is admitted (p2c_subclass_impl -> PONG). A non-implementing class is refused: 'class CX does not implement interface IA (ISO 9.3.8.2/SET SR10)' (p2b_class_noimpl). The test is the section 11.8.4 GR2 transitive IMPLEMENTS closure.
- d) SELF: implemented at OoBinder.cs:920-926 and it is the ONE alternative in this whole rule that carries BOTH a positive and a negative spec-derived test - conformance:2002/oo_set_self_interface (expects PONG) and conformance:negative/oo-set-self-interface-not-implemented (both 'enabled' in tests/conformance/negative/manifest.json), a pair that differs only by the IMPLEMENTS clause.
- e) NULL: `SET RA TO NULL` compiles and runs (probe j2_null_iface -> OK); senderNull short-circuits every conformance test, which is right - NULL conforms to any object reference.

TWO ALTERNATIVES ARE UNREACHABLE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS PARTIAL:
- b1) a class sender described WITH a FACTORY phrase. `01 FB USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE FACTORY OF CB` is refused at DECLARATION: COBOLNET0899 'USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE FACTORY OF (a factory-object reference, ISO 13.18.60) is recognized but not yet implemented (the universal-reference wave)' (probe p3_factory_usage). The item then degrades to a UNIVERSAL reference and the SET draws a second, misleading error - 'a UNIVERSAL object reference does not conform to a typed receiver'. So the b1 leg of the rule (test the FACTORY closure rather than the instance closure) has no code and no reachable input. Note ObjectRefWideningMismatch calls `ImplementsClosure(sc, factory: false)` UNCONDITIONALLY (OoConformance.cs:381) - the factory/instance distinction b1-vs-b2 draws is not represented at all, so the day FACTORY OF lands, b1 will silently take b2's test unless this line is changed with it.

subject: SORT statement

subject: SORT statement
notes: kb/Work PB704 (2026-09-06): the phrase that BUYS this rule was unusable above COBOL-85 until this landing - ORDER is the format's own optional word (measured: on the printed page only DUPLICATES is underlined) but the grammar spelled it as a `cobolWord`, and the 8.9 funnel, which screens IDENTIFIER occurrences position-blind, refused it as a user-defined word from 2002 (8.9 reserves ORDER since 2002). ORDER is now a lexer token with a cobol-words.json nameSlot row, so the phrase parses at every edition and `01 ORDER PIC X.` still draws COBOLNET0901 at 2002+ (conformance:negative/pb704-order-as-data-name). All three arms are evidenced: a) the USING-file order and, within a file, the access order; b) the input procedure's RELEASE order; c) the table elements' pre-sort relative order. Both formats realize it as an unconditional STABLE sort - CobolSort.Sort ties on the buffer index (Format 1) and EmitTableSort emits a stable comparer (Format 2) - so GR4's undefined order is safely refined to the same one. Arm c) needs Format 2, which is 2002+; arms a) and b) hold at 85.

subject: SORT statement
notes: kb/Work PB678 (2026-09-05): the TWO sequences GR5 determines separately are now resolved as a pair (SortCollation) and selected per key by the key's CLASS through the one classifier CollatingSelection.Of - alphabet-name-1 (GR5a) or the alphanumeric program collating sequence (GR5b) for keys of class alphabetic and alphanumeric, alphabet-name-2 (GR5a) or the national program collating sequence (GR5b) for keys of class national, and NO sequence for the two classes GR5 names neither of (numeric, boolean). subject: SORT statement
notes: Rule: 'If an output procedure is specified, control passes to it after the file referenced by file-name-1 has been sequenced ... The compiler inserts a return mechanism after the last statement in the output procedure ... passes control to the next executable statement after the SORT statement ... The RETURN statements in the output procedure are the requests for the next record.' (cite.py --check 14.9.40.4 OK, GR14). EmitSort emits SortSort, then SortEnterProcedure(output: true) + the bounded dispatch of the output range, then the end label and SortClose, falling through to the next statement; RETURN pulls the next record by cursor (CobolSort.Return). Sorted records are delivered one per RETURN in pb440 (OUT=A/B/C) and in the spec-pinned conformance-test SortMergeDifferentialTests.Sort_InputOutputProcedures_MultiKeyMixedDirections; conformance:2023/pb367b_sort_use_not_normal shows control reaching the statement after the SORT. notes:
kb/Work PB354. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 4): 'Data-name-1 or record-key-name-1 shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses.' The rule has two operand legs (indexed and relative) and they behave differently.
INDEXED LEG -- ENFORCED, but only as a SIDE EFFECT and reported under the WRONG RULE. RecordLayout.OffsetOf bails to null when the item or any ancestor carries OCCURS ('if (p.Occurs is not null) return null;   // subject to OCCURS => no single fixed position'), so KeyIndexByPosition returns null and BindStart emits COBOLNET0862 '<name> neither names a record key nor begins at the leftmost character position of one with a length not greater than that key (ISO 14.9.41 SR6)'. PROBED (out-b1/probe/sr4-occ) with '05 IX-KEY. 10 IX-ELEM PIC X(3) OCCURS 2 TIMES.' and 'START IXF KEY IS = IX-ELEM (1)': rejected with exactly that message. The source IS refused, so no illegal program compiles -- but the message asserts something FALSE about this operand: IX-ELEM(1) DOES begin at IX-KEY's leftmost character position and IS shorter than it. The rule actually violated is SR4; OffsetOf's null collapses two distinct rejection reasons into one sentence, and a user reading it would look for the wrong problem.
RELATIVE LEG -- NO CHECK AT ALL. BindStart's relative arm tests only ReferenceEquals(operand.Item, file.RelativeKeyItem) (that is SR5), which is TRUE for a SUBSCRIPTED reference to the same DataItem. PROBED (same file): with '01 WS-RKT. 05 WS-RK PIC 9(4) OCCURS 3 TIMES.' and 'RELATIVE KEY IS WS-RK', the statement 'START RLF KEY IS = WS-RK (2)' compiles with NO diagnostic. That shape is reachable only through a file control entry that already violates 12.4.5.13.3 SR1 (--check: 'Data-name-1 shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses') -- and KeyedIoBinder.KeyedValidateFile implements 12.4.5.13's SR2 (unsigned integer, no P) and SR3 (not within a record of the file) but NOT its SR1, so nothing anywhere in the chain diagnoses it. The two missing checks cover for each other.
UNDER-REJECTS. TEST: none.

Both legs are pinned by their own negative fixture.

notes: kb/Work PB370. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR9 and GR9 b) / c)). NUMERIC COMPARISON (8.8.4.2.4): EmitStart renders the operand as `(long)(NumericRenderer.Align(num.FieldNum(sta.Operand), 0))` and calls CobolFile.StartRelative(name, op, rrn) — the RRN travels as a typed long, never a character image, so the comparison is numeric by construction. GR9 a) FORWARD SEARCH: RelativeConnector.Start walks the SortedDictionary keys ascending for '==' (ContainsKey), '>' and '>=' and breaks on the first hit. GR9 b) REVERSE SEARCH: '<' and '<=' walk the same ascending key order but KEEP the last satisfying key and break on the first non-satisfying one — which is the largest RRN satisfying the relation, i.e. the first record found searching the file in reverse. ConditionBinder.MapOperator maps NOT LESS -> '>=', NOT GREATER -> '<=', GREATER OR EQUAL -> '>=', LESS OR EQUAL -> '<='; '!=' is unreachable here (SR3 rewrite in BindStart), and no other spelling can fall through the switch, so there is no silent no-match arm. All six legal operators plus both boundary directions verified. EDITIONS: the reverse-search operators are A.3 item 39 processor-dependent elements (cite.py --check A.3 OK: 'the relational operators LESS, NOT GREATER, or LESS OR EQUAL in the START statement are dependent on the capabilities of the processor'); this processor supports them. NO CLOSING TEST: the only existing coverage is the legacy-baked conformance-test:KeyedIoDifferentialTests.Relative_StartKeyGreaterOrEqual_PositionsThenWalks (DifferentialGolden characterization, disqualified). CONFORMS-but-untested. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — REFUTED on the record's own editions claim. The forward/reverse SEMANTICS are right and I re-derived them independently: RelativeConnector.cs:340-355 walks a SortedDictionary<long,string> (KeyedStoreTable.cs:69), so '>'/'>=' break on the first ascending hit and '<'/'<=' keep the LAST satisfying key, which is the first found searching in reverse (GR9b); ConditionBinder.MapOperator (:798-810) folds NOT LESS -> '>=' and NOT GREATER -> '<=', matching the a)/b) split exactly. I even probed an operand shape the adjudicator never tried -- ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL, which SR1 admits -- and it is correct once the 14.9.51 GR29a sequential-WRITE renumbering to RRN 1/2/3 is accounted for. What does NOT hold is editions '85,2002,2014,2023'. GR9 b)'s operator set (LESS, NOT GREATER, LESS OR EQUAL) is not COBOL-85: the standard binds it to the READ PREVIOUS phrase in ONE sentence, A.3 item 39, as a single reverse-access processor-dependent capability, and GR9 is itself split into a) (the 85 set) and b) (the added set). The compiler gates the OTHER half of that same sentence -- READ ... PREVIOUS raises COBOLNET0900 at --std 85 (VersionConformancePass.cs:254, Constructs.ReadPrevious2002) -- and gates every other post-85 element of START (start-first-last-2002, start-with-length-2002, both with constructs.json rows). So at one of the four editions the record claims, the compiler silently accepts a construct that edition does not define and executes 2002 semantics for it. One arm of the rule verified at four editions, the other at three and ungated at the fourth => PARTIAL. notes: kb/Work PB370. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR17 e) 1.): 'The file position indicator is set to the value of the key of reference in the first logical record whose key satisfies the comparison'. IMPLEMENTATION: IndexedConnector.Start builds `Ordered(keyIndex)` — records sorted by (key-of-reference value under KeyCompare, then Arrival) with SUPPRESS WHEN records filtered out — then iterates FORWARD for '==','>','>=' and BACKWARD for '<','<=' (GR17 c/d) and stops at the first satisfying record, setting `_fpiKey = KeyOf(found.Image, keyIndex)` (the key VALUE, as the rule states) plus `_fpiArrival` (the duplicate-key disambiguator 9.1.8.2 needs to make arrival-order retrieval work; it adds resolution, it does not contradict the rule). GR17 e)'s operand orientation is right: `KeyCompare(part, value, keyIndex)` puts the RECORD'S extracted key on the left, matching 'with the second temporary area on the left hand side' (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK). The suppression sentence is honored by Ordered's `Where(r => !IsSuppressed(r.Image, keyIndex))`, and IsSuppressed returns false for keyIndex < 0 so the prime key is never suppressible. The partial-key truncation uses the WITH LENGTH count when present, else the operand's ImageWidth (EmitStart). OBSERVED (probe/idx-start/STPRB3, keys AAA100/BBB200/CCC300): implicit EQUAL 'BBB200' -> BBB200; '> BBB200' -> CCC300; '< BBB999' -> BBB200 (the LARGEST key below, proving the reverse search); 'NOT GREATER BBB999' -> BBB200; '>= AAA000 WITH LENGTH 3' -> AAA100. probe/idx-dup/STPRBB (alternate key WITH DUPLICATES, MM written by 05, 03, 09 in that arrival order): '>= MM' positions at 05 — the EARLIEST arrival of the duplicate set, and the walk gives 05, 03, 09; '< NN' positions at 09 — the LATEST arrival, i.e. the first satisfying record in reverse order. TESTS: conformance:2002/file_collating_seq pins START KEY IS >= 'M' under ALPHABET REV (expected 'START >= M UNDER REV:' then K=M, K=A, derived from 12.4.5.5.3 GR2c, not from any oracle); conformance:2023/altkey_suppress_when pins START KEY IS >= LOW-VALUES on a SUPPRESS-WHEN alternate key (expected 01/AA then 03/BB); conformance-test:KeyedOffsetSpecTests.Start_KeyOperandInSiblingRecord_MatchesByBytePosition asserts GOT=01 for START KEY = via a sibling-record operand, reasoned from 12.4.5.12.4 GR4 + 14.9.41.3 SR6b. subject: SUBTRACT statement
notes: The emitted shape is literally the rule's `(operand-2 - (operand-11 + ... + operand-1n))`: Fold builds the SUM node first and Combine subtracts it from the rendered FROM operand as one nested subtrahend - not a left-to-right `((op2 - op11) - op12)`. THE PARENTHESISATION IS MEASURED, NOT ONLY READ, and the measurement is spec-derived: under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL every operation rounds to 34 significant digits (8.8.1.5 / decimal128), so the two shapes disagree at the boundary. Probe k2 `SUBTRACT 0.00005 0.00005 FROM 1000000000000000000000000000000 GIVING R` (R PIC 9(31)) returned 999999999999999999999999999999 - the rule's grouping, whose intermediate 999...999.9999 is 34 digits exactly. A left-to-right fold would have rounded 999...999.99995 (35 digits) up to 1E30 at each step and stored 1000000000000000000000000000000. Ordinary cases: p2 `SUBTRACT 1 2 3 FROM 20 GIVING G1` = 14 and `SUBTRACT 1.5 2.5 FROM X GIVING G2 ROUNDED` = 6 from X=10.00; g6 several GIVING receivers each with its own ROUNDED; h1 the FROM operand as a data item (B unchanged - it is a SENDER here, not a receiver); g9/g10 a function-identifier in either sending position. The result is stored into EVERY identifier-3 (EmitGiving snapshots the value once when there is more than one receiver, 14.7.7 GR4 NOTE 3). The named golden is spec-derived (`SUBTRACT 1 FROM 5 GIVING C`, expectation 4 derived in its header) and pins the format-2 shape; it does not exercise several operand-1s, which k2/p2 do. STANDARD-BINARY IS A DECLARED NON-SUPPORT AND IS NOT MINE TO VERDICT (owner, D13): probe k3 shows `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY` rejected at compile time with COBOLNET0806 `a processor-dependent language element (ISO Annex A.3 item 2) for which support is not claimed (4.2.6)` plus COBOLNET0903 (obsolete as of COBOL-2023, Annex F.2 item 3). subject: UNLOCK statement
notes: RULE (two halves): 'Any record locks associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1 are released by the execution of the UNLOCK statement. The presence or absence of any record locks does not affect the success of the execution of the UNLOCK statement.' - cite.py --check 14.9.47.4 (first sentence) -> OK §14.9.47.4 1). CODE: FileRegistry.Unlock calls `PhysicalFileTable.ReleaseAllForConnector(st, name)` - keyed on the CONNECTOR name, which is exactly 'associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1' - then unconditionally `c.SetStatus(FileStatusCode.Success)`, so held locks and no locks give the same 00. The RECORD/RECORDS word is deliberately dropped (`_ = records;`), which is right: GR1 releases ALL locks and its NOTE routes single-record release to READ ... NO LOCK. BOTH HALVES MEASURED. (a) release: conformance:2002/file_sharing has A lock record 1 (READA=00), B blocked (READB=51), then `UNLOCK F-A` and B reads 00 (AFTER=00); file_sharing_seq shows the converse - B's UNLOCK does not disturb A's own lock (UNLB=00 then REWA=00/REWB51=51). (b) presence-or-absence: p1.cob UNLOCKs an OPEN sequential file that never held a lock -> 00, and p6.cob UNLOCKs twice in a row (AUTO-UNLA=00 then AUTO-UNLA2=00 with nothing left to release). (c) ALL LOCK MODES, not just MANUAL: p6.cob uses `LOCK MODE IS AUTOMATIC` on two RELATIVE connectors - the auto-lock taken by A's READ blocks B (AUTO-READB=51) and is released by `UNLOCK F-A` (AUTO-READB2=00), matching Table A.1's UNLOCK row, cite.py --check D.2.4.3.2 '| UNLOCK | Automatic -single - multiple Manual - single - multiple | | for all lock modes: - on all locked records |' -> OK (informative corroboration; GR1 is the normative source). NOT DOWNGRADED by the unregistered-connector path of findings [unregistered-keyed-connector]/[unlock-registry-entry-is-the-one-silent-fall-through]: a connector that was never registered was never opened, so it holds no record locks and GR1 is vacuous there - the observable failure on that path is the I-O status, which is why GR2 and GR3 carry it and this row does not.

What the record misses is the RULE'S SCOPE: GR5 is 'Within a given procedure division', and ISO 14.2.2 SR10 says Format 1 -- the procedure-division format that CARRIES the DECLARATIVES portion (14.2.1) -- 'may be specified in a source element if and only if that source element is a function definition, a function prototype definition, a METHOD DEFINITION, a program definition, or a program prototype definition'. A method definition therefore has a procedure division that may legally hold Format-1 USE statements (14.9.49.3 SR1 puts the USE statement in exactly that declaratives portion), and the compiler rejects EVERY declarative part inside a method unconditionally: StatementBinder.cs:239-242 -> COBOLNET0899 'DECLARATIVES inside a method (ISO 14.2.1) are recognized but not yet implemented (owning roadmap phase: Phase 3, OO port)'. That is a deferral rejecting legal source, not owner-documented non-support, so the rule is implemented for the program and function procedure divisions and NOT IMPLEMENTED for a method's. Two halves, one verified => PARTIAL. (The record's code-location, editions and empty test-ref are otherwise accurate and should be kept.) || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985/2002/2014/2023 (FORMAT 1). No Annex E entry touches it.

subject: USE statement
notes: kb/Work PB370. Rule text (cite.py --check 14.9.49.4 "the first one that occurs in the order of evaluation of the statement that causes the exception to exist" -> OK, GR 11). There is no explicit 'first condition' latch; the property is emergent - every raise site dispatches inline at the point the condition occurs, and a fatal raise throws out of the statement, so the first condition in evaluation order is the one that reaches __EcDispatch. `__af.Dispatched` additionally guarantees one dispatch per raise across nested guards (14.6.13.1.3 #7). PARTIAL because the adversarial shape is unverified and the emergent property is not robust to it: a statement in which the FIRST condition is nonfatal and a LATER one is fatal would dispatch on the later one, and there is no mechanism preventing it, because an enabled nonfatal condition raised from a runtime site never dispatches at all (ExceptionState.Set only records the last exception status - the nonfatal ambient gates EC-DATA-CONVERSION / EC-BOUND-OVERFLOW set a flag and nothing more). Whether a nonfatal condition must run the declarative is 14.6.13.1.4's rule, not this one, but it is what makes GR11 untested here. No spec-derived test asserts the ordering. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2002/2014/2023 (FORMAT 3). No Annex E entry touches it.

subject: USE statement
notes: CLOSED 2026-09-09 by the PB365/PB366 reconciliation - the row carried TWO measured defects, each mechanism owned one, and this is the first tree on which both cures exist together. Rule text (cite.py --check 14.9.49.4 'A declarative is selected for execution by analyzing the USE statements in a source element in the order in which they are specified' -> OK GR 14; 'is a factory object or instance object of object-class-name-1 or of a subclass of object-class-name-1' -> OK GR 14 a); 'all of the USE statements in the source element are analyzed again' -> OK GR 14 a) (its otherwise-clause); 'described with an IMPLEMENTS clause that references interface-name-1' -> OK GR 14 b)). || DEFECT 1, GR14 a)'s FACTORY arm, FIXED by kb/Work PB366: the factory object of class X is a distinct emitted type X__FACTORY deriving from the BASE class's factory (OoEmitter.EmitClassUnit / OoClassSymbol.FactoryCsName), never from X, so the selector's single `__obj is X` test was false for every factory exception object - silently, no declarative and no diagnostic. Measured before (probe: `01 FR USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE.` / `SET FR TO CF1.` / `RAISE FR.` against `USE AFTER EXCEPTION OBJECT CF1`) -> `AFTER` alone where the spec requires `F4-HANDLER / AFTER`; the instance control reached the handler. The cure is the census OoClassSymbol.FactoryOrInstanceCsTypes rendered as one C# or-pattern per entry, `__obj is X or X__FACTORY`; 'or of a subclass' rides C#'s `is` in EACH hierarchy because both mirror INHERITS. Witness conformance:2002/pb366_use_exception_object_factory walks five arms - an exact-class factory, a factory two declaratives match (source-order first-match plus 'no other declaratives are executed'), a SUBCLASS factory naming no declarative of its own, an INSTANCE object, and an unmatched factory falling to the 14.6.13.1.5 tail - and on the pre-fix tree arms 1, 2 and 3 printed no handler at all. || DEFECT 2, GR14 b) absent, FIXED by kb/Work PB365: an interface operand was rejected at bind with COBOLNET0859 (SR16's diagnostic answering SR17's question) and there was no second analysis pass over the USE statements at all. The selector is now TWO passes - EmitObjDispatchPass emits every object-class-name-1 entry in source order, then, only after all of them, every interface-name-1 entry - which is what 'otherwise, all of the USE statements in the source element are analyzed again and: b) ...' requires and which an interleaved single pass cannot express (an earlier interface entry would beat a later class entry). GR14 b)'s 'described with an IMPLEMENTS clause' is 11.8.4 GR2 (instance objects) / 11.4.4 GR2 (factory objects) as a CLOSURE - own IMPLEMENTS, an implemented interface's INHERITS, an inherited class's IMPLEMENTS - and the emitter renders each emitted HALF of a class with exactly that closure as its C# interface list, so one test against OoInterfaceSymbol.ImplementedCsTypes realises all three legs for both object kinds. Witness conformance:2002/pb365_use_eo_interface_two_pass, whose interface declarative is written FIRST and whose expected output (CLASS-CY, AFTER-1, IFACE, AFTER-2) is produced only by a selector that honours the pass boundary. || THE RECONCILED SHAPE (this change set): BoundDeclarative.Eo is the discriminated BoundEoOperand - BoundEoClass(OoClassSymbol) | BoundEoInterface(OoInterfaceSymbol) - carrying the RESOLVED SYMBOL, never a rendered C# type name, and each GR14 pass renders its own alternative's census. Both goldens were re-measured on the merged tree and match their .out byte-for-byte. pb366_use_exception_object_factory itself needed repair, not exemption: two of its class definitions inherited from PBFBASE with no REPOSITORY paragraph, which 11.3.3 SR2 forbids and PB365's 8.4.6.4 funnel now enforces. Format4UseObjectSelectorDriftTests asserts against the GENERATED C# that each alternative's census equals what the backend actually emits, that the selector tests every member, and that the class pass precedes the interface pass; both new detectors were fired against a deliberately broken census and a deliberately swapped pass order before being trusted. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2002/2014/2023 (FORMAT 4 - the exception-object / OO facility). No Annex E entry touches it.

subject: USE statement
notes: kb/Work PB370. Rule text (cite.py --check 14.9.49.4 "the predefined object reference EXCEPTION-OBJECT references the exception object" -> OK, GR 15). On BOTH paths that can enter a Format-4 declarative the register is set before the selector runs: EmitRaiseObject emits `ExceptionState.SetObject(<the RAISE operand>)` and then `__EcObjDispatch(ExceptionState.ExceptionObject)`; EmitPropagationPickup emits `SetObject(__po)` and then the selector. The covering case tests/conformance/2002/oo_ec_raise_object.cob enters the selected declarative and executes `SET U TO EXCEPTION-OBJECT` / `IF U NOT = NULL`, and the committed golden requires `BASE-HANDLER EXCEPTION-OBJECT` + `REGISTER-SET` - so the register is proven non-null and carrying the raised object on entry. Note the register is a run-unit-scoped single slot (ExceptionState.ExceptionObject) and a NAMED raise inside the declarative nulls it (Set sets ExceptionObject = null); that is 14.9.29.4 GR1's rule, and GR15 constrains only the state on ENTRY, which holds. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — Two independent defects in the record. (1) THE TEST-REF DOES NOT PIN THE RULE. GR15 says EXCEPTION-OBJECT 'references the exception object' -- an IDENTITY claim (ISO 8.8.4.2.15: the relation is true 'if the object referenced by identifier-3 is the same object that is referenced by identifier-4'). The cited conformance:2002/oo_ec_raise_object asserts only 'IF U NOT = NULL DISPLAY "REGISTER-SET"'; its golden line 'REGISTER-SET' is satisfied by ANY non-null object, so a regression that set the register to the wrong object -- SELF, a fresh instance, the activating program -- keeps that golden green. The row is NOT closed by it and the test-ref must be emptied; the missing assertion is one line (IF U = E). I measured the identity claim myself and it HOLDS on every entry path, so the program-level half of the rule is genuinely correct -- this is a coverage correction, not a behaviour finding. (2) A HALF THAT CANNOT BE ENTERED AT ALL. 'the associated declarative' is a declarative in a procedure division, and ISO 14.2.2 SR10 permits the DECLARATIVES-bearing Format 1 (14.2.1) in a METHOD DEFINITION; StatementBinder.cs:239-242 rejects every declarative part inside a method with COBOLNET0899 'recognized but not yet implemented (owning roadmap phase: Phase 3, OO port)' at both 2002 and 2023, so a Format-4 USE in a method -- the natural home for EC-OO handling -- is legal source the compiler refuses. Unlocated/unreachable half + verified half => PARTIAL. (Contributing, already owned by the record for GR14: the interface-name-1 arm of the associated declarative is rejected COBOLNET0859, so even in a program only the object-class arm of GR14 can ever deliver an entry for GR15 to constrain -- I confirmed that rejection. It does not by itself move GR15, because the register is written BEFORE the selector runs and is therefore arm-independent.) || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2002/2014/2023 (FORMAT 4). No Annex E entry touches it.

notes: 'The write file is the file referenced by file-name-1 or by the file-name associated with record-name-1.' (cite.py --check 14.9.51.3 OK, SR1). ResolveRecordName's identity test returns the FileModel whose Records contain the item (own files, then inherited GLOBAL FDs via FilesByName); that FileModel is the write file every later check (SR12/SR13/SR19/SR22, org reroute) and the BoundWrite/BoundKeyedWrite node use. The FILE file-name-1 arm is Annex A.4.13 declined (COBOLNET1706) so only the record-name arm is reachable. pb347_record_name_identity writes OUT-REC / OUT-REC OF OUTF and reads the records back from OUTF. [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (base WRITE statement; the 2023 text records no change to this rule in Annex E)]

subject: WRITE statement
notes: GAP -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB691). Rule text validated: cite.py --check 14.9.51.3 "If the organization of the write file is sequential, format 1 shall be specified" => OK 2). The rule is a FORMAT-SELECTION rule, and what it forbids is read off the formats: Format 1 (sequential) of 14.9.51.2 carries no INVALID KEY bracket at all -- only Format 2 (random) does -- so a WRITE on a sequential-organization file may not carry the phrase. It was PARSED AND DROPPED: SequentialIoBinder.BindWrite never called w.writeInvalidKey(), so the program compiled clean at every edition and NEITHER imperative ran, with no diagnostic on either severity axis. Measured with a CLI probe before the fix (WRITE ... INVALID KEY DISPLAY "W-IK" NOT INVALID KEY DISPLAY "W-NIK" on ORGANIZATION SEQUENTIAL printed only 'DONE 00' at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 and under --permissive), not inferred. It is the THIRD arm of one silent drop: PB144 screened REWRITE (SR-14.9.35.3-2), PB334 READ, and this one hid because the writeInvalidKey sub-rule was consumed by the KEYED binder only. Now screened through the ONE severity seam (StatementValidation.ScreenForbiddenPhrase -> COBOLNET1720, no new code): an ERROR under strict at all four editions, a WARNING under --permissive -- and, unlike the REWRITE arm as PB144 left it, the phrase is BOUND rather than dropped, because 9.1.14's final rule item 2 (cite.py --check 9.1.14 "If the I-O status indicates a successful completion, control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement or to the imperative-statement specified in the NOT INVALID KEY phrase if it is specified" => OK 2)) gives the NOT INVALID KEY imperative a live meaning even here. The INVALID arm is provably dead on this organization: 9.1.13.5's four invalid-key statuses '21'-'24' each name a relative or indexed file, so the emitter's status-first '2' branch can never fire -- dead, never rerouted. D9 CORPUS SWEEP RUN, NOT REASONED: a record-name -> FD -> SELECT organization mapping over all 459 NIST programs finds 77 WRITE ... INVALID KEY sites, every one of them on an INDEXED or RELATIVE file and ZERO on a sequential-organization file; all 459 then compiled at --std 85 with the screened compiler and NOT ONE drew COBOLNET1720; and the ~Nist conformance leg is byte-identical across the change (Passed! Failed: 0, Passed: 352, Total: 352, before and after). The screen is edition-invariant by construction (Removed keys on Permissive, never on edition) and measured so at 85/2002/2014/2023.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: GAP -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB909). Rule text validated: cite.py --check 14.9.51.3 "If the organization of the write file is indexed or relative, format 2 shall be specified" -> OK 3). Format 2 differs from Format 1 only by lacking the ADVANCING and END-OF-PAGE phrases (and admitting INVALID KEY, which SR2 screens on the other arm), so refusing those two phrases on a relative/indexed WRITE IS the rule. COBOLNET1720 in both lanes (Format 2 gives a print-control phrase no meaning to bind under --permissive); it used to be a COBOLNET1756 deferral and a run-unit abort.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: SR4: 'If identifier-1 is a function-identifier, it shall reference an alphanumeric or national function.' (--check OK). FromPhraseRules.Write = {Alphanumeric, National}; BindFromPhrase reads the function's category through MoveTable16.SenderPosition (so a constant-folded LENGTH still reads numeric) and raises COBOLNET1914. Same row serves the sequential and keyed arms. Probes: numeric (NUMVAL), integer (INTEGER, LENGTH) and boolean (BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER) rejected 1914; alphanumeric (UPPER-CASE, CURRENT-DATE) and national (NATIONAL-OF to PIC N) accepted. The screen is deliberately not applied to an inline method invocation (not a function-identifier, §8.4.3.1.2). pb348-write-from-integer-function rejects FUNCTION LENGTH at all four editions; the paired positive is conformance:2023/pb10_function_identifier_sending. [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 wherever a function-identifier can be written as identifier-1 (the national/boolean categories are post-1985)]

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB347. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.51.3 'Record-name-1 is the name of a logical record in the file section of the data division and may be qualified.' -> OK, 14.9.51.3 5). This is RELEASE 14.9.32.3 SR1 and REWRITE 14.9.35.3 SR1 written a third time, and all three now share ONE implementation, StatementValidation.ResolveRecordName. BOTH HALVES ARE WITNESSED. Name-of-a-logical-record: a subordinate item is refused (`WRITE OR-DATA` -> COBOLNET1757, naming OUT-REC as the record to write instead), a reference-modified record is refused (record-name-1 is a user-defined word per 8.3.2.2.25 and 5.2.4, not an identifier position per 8.4.3.3.3 SR5), and a WORKING-STORAGE 01 is refused with 14.9.51.3 SR1's reason -- 'The write file is the file referenced by file-name-1 or by the file-name associated with record-name-1' (--check OK) -- there being no file to name. May-be-qualified: `WRITE OUT-REC OF OUTF` binds and writes, pinned in both positive goldens. BEFORE THIS: all three were accepted with NO error. The subordinate and reference-modified forms drew nothing at all and emitted CobolFile.Write with the wrong operand and so the wrong record WIDTH; the WORKING-STORAGE form drew only the COBOLNET1756 DEFERRAL WARNING, which announces the COMPILER's gap for what is the source's error, and the program compiled. ISO 4.2.2 makes the compile-time indication mandatory. Edition-invariant: the sentence is identical in 1985, 2002 and 2014, so no gate exists and each negative carries `*> reject-at: 85 2002 2014 2023`.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.51.3 'The BEFORE and AFTER phrases shall not both be specified if the PAGE phrase is specified' -> OK 14.9.51.3 17). BOTH DIRECTIONS OBSERVED. The prohibition: tests/conformance/negative/pb712-write-before-after-page.cob writes `WRITE P-REC BEFORE AFTER ADVANCING PAGE` and is refused COBOLNET1910 at 2023. The complement (the pair WITHOUT the PAGE operand is legal, so the rule is a narrowing and not a ban): tests/conformance/2023/write_before_and_after.cob compiles and runs `BEFORE AFTER ADVANCING 3 LINES` and `AFTER BEFORE ADVANCING 2 LINES`. WHY SR17 EXISTS, which is what makes the check's placement correct rather than arbitrary: 14.9.51.4 GR25 g) and h) position the record 'before or after (depending on the phrase used) the device is repositioned' to the next page, and with both words written there is no phrase to depend on -- whereas GR25 e)/f), which govern the numeric and mnemonic operands, DO resolve the pair (f)'s second sentence puts its advance after the presentation). EDITIONS 2023: the pair itself is a COBOL-2023 introduction (Annex E.3.3 item 2; docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md row 45), so below 2023 this source is refused first by the introduction gate COBOLNET0900, evidenced by conformance:negative/pb712-write-before-after-below-2023 and conformance:negative/pb712-write-after-before-below-2023. kb/Work PB712 (LANDED 2026-09-06) is the note; before it the SR17 test was one arm of a malformed-pair check over a two-ADVANCING-phrase grammar 14.9.51.2 Format 1 never prints.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: GR10: 'If the locking mode of the write file connector is single record locking, any record lock associated with that file connector is released by the execution of the WRITE statement.' Every WRITE (sequential and keyed emitters both render FileWriteShared unconditionally) calls ReleasePriorRecordLocks before the operation; it returns early only for meta.Multiple (multiple record locking keeps its locks), otherwise ReleaseAllForConnector. Released 'by the execution' regardless of the write's outcome, which matches the rule text (no success condition). Organization-independent. The unit test asserts WA's WITH LOCK record 2 is released by the next WRITE under single locking. cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'any record lock associated with that file connector is released by the execution of the WRITE statement' -> OK rule 10. Record locking is a COBOL-2002 introduction (LOCK MODE clause).

subject: WRITE statement
notes: GR11: 'If record locks have an effect for the write file connector and the WITH LOCK phrase is specified or implied, the record lock associated with the record written is set when the execution of the WRITE statement is successful.' WriteShared: wantLock = phrase==WithLock && LocksEffective (LOCK MODE not None, not SHARING NO OTHER); lock set only when status[0]=='0' via _physical.LockRecord on c.LastWrittenRecordId. The 'implied' arm: the only source of an implied WITH LOCK is §9.1.16's 'implicit LOCK MODE IS AUTOMATIC WITH LOCK ON MULTIPLE RECORDS' for files subject to commit and rollback (cite.py --check 9.1.16 -> OK); APPLY COMMIT is refused by name (COBOLNET1709, CONFORMANCE.md A.4.3 Not claimed), so no compilable program reaches that arm — the same vacuity the owner recorded as CONFORMS for commit-antecedent rules (kb/Work PB371). Automatic locking does not lock on WRITE (§14.9.51.3 SR22 forbids the phrase; the concept text locks on READ). cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'the WITH LOCK phrase is specified or implied' -> OK rule 11.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: A successful WRITE releases the record to the operating environment, not to a buffer: SequentialConnector.ReleaseRecord is the ONE release point every write arm reaches, and for a file another connector shares it flushes the record out before the statement returns, which is what makes it visible to that connector's read and what stops the next append landing on top of it. The keyed organizations release into the per-physical-file shared record store, which every connector over the path sees. All three write arms release (the print-control arms never did).

subject: WRITE statement
notes: Annex A.2 item 64 (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'the content of the bytes that extend outside the end of record-name-1 are undefined' -> OK 13); 4.4 2) makes the run unit conforming. The content is a DOCUMENTED determination, docs/CONFORMANCE.md 3 D-WRT1 (owner decision 2026-10-01): a byte past record-name-1 is the record area's content at that position, a position no record description occupies is a space; the NUMBER of bytes stays ISO (13.18.43.4 GR13 a), GR6). Line sequential (GR21/GR22) and a varying file without DEPENDING (GR13 b) send record-name-1 itself. Pinned by the three goldens.

The WRITE's length decision is ONE member (WrittenLength) asked by both arms, and the bound (OutsideVaryingBounds) runs in both - the print-control arm (WriteAdvancingRecord, which a print/LINAGE file's plain WRITE is rerouted to) now receives the DEPENDING length through FileRegistry.WriteAnyOrg. Golden: VARYING 3 TO 8 DEPENDING ON VL, AFTER ADVANCING with VL=9 -> 44 and BEFORE ADVANCING with VL=2 -> 44, nothing written; plain VL=5 -> 00 and the file reads back one 5-byte record.
