subject: WRITE statement
notes: GR16: 'The RETRY phrase is used to control the behavior of the WRITE statement for files opened for file sharing for the case where resources needed to write a record are locked by another run unit. The I-O status is set in accordance with the rules in 14.7.9, RETRY phrase.' (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 -> OK rule 16). The antecedent is unpopulatable in this implementation: COBOLNET_FILES_DESIGN §14.7.9 GR2 determination (CONFORMANCE A.1 items 165/166) — every file and record lock is held by a connector of the executing run unit, and WRITE defines no record operation conflict. WriteShared therefore binds the RETRY phrase (grammar retryPhrase, GateRetryIntro 2002) and makes the first attempt decide. The one resource denial WriteShared CAN return, the §12.4.5.9 GR7 lock ceiling '53'/'54' from PreflightNewLock, bypasses RetryLoop — kb/Work PB707 (open) owns that as a where-the-rule-is-written defect, behaviour-identical today (no re-attempt within one run unit can clear the ceiling). No verdict-changing edge found.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: GR17: 'The successor relationship of a sequential file is established by the order of execution of WRITE statements when the physical file is created. The relationship does not change except when records are added to the end of a physical file.' (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 -> OK rule 17). The sequential connector appends each record to one forward-only writer (OUTPUT = FileMode.Create, EXTEND = append stream, PB739 made shared append re-seek to the end), so read-back order is write order; REWRITE overwrites in place (never reorders). Golden l1_open_extend_position's sequential leg reads back SEQ001, SEQ002, SEQ003 after an EXTEND append — the order of execution of the WRITEs.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: The EXTEND write-ordinal base is the record count present at OPEN, measured before this OPEN's own writer exists (kb/Work PB713); the goldens read the appended record back as the successor of the existing one on every organization and framing.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: Two sharing-active file connectors extending one physical file each append after every record present at the moment of the write: a participant's writer is HostFile.OpenConnectorWriteStream's SharedAppendStream, which repositions at the physical end before every write instead of at the .NET FileMode.Append offset captured once at open. The record's ordinal is minted from the shared PhysicalFileTable.State.ReleasedOrdinal, so the two connectors' releases are 2 then 3 rather than 2 twice. Only the relative ORDER of the two connectors' records is undefined by this rule; both goldens read all three records back on every organization and framing. COBOL-85 has no file sharing, so the rule's antecedent cannot arise there. kb/Work PB740 renamed the role to HostFile.OpenConnectorWriteStream and moved its shared-vs-plain choice onto the 9.1.15 file lock the connector's handle carries (FileLockPosture.AdmitsAnotherWriter) instead of onto whether the SELECT wrote a SHARING or LOCK MODE clause: the same change made two CLAUSE-LESS connectors openable EXTEND on one physical file for the first time, and keying the repositioning stream on a clause would have left exactly that pair anchoring two buffered writers at one offset. The rule and its evidence are unchanged; this row is re-recorded because the symbol it names moved.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB1192 (w61d). GR20 (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'When an attempt is made to write beyond the externally-defined boundaries of the physical file' -> OK 20)). The boundary of a sequential file is the host medium's capacity (Annex A.1 item 108, docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-108). HostFile.IsMediumBoundary classifies the host's refusal (Windows ERROR_HANDLE_DISK_FULL/DISK_FULL/FILE_TOO_LARGE/DISK_QUOTA_EXCEEDED; Unix EFBIG/ENOSPC/EDQUOT) and FileStatusCode.ForWriteFailure answers '34' (else '30'); SequentialConnector.Write, WriteAdvancing and Rewrite are the three entry points a record reaches the medium through and each wraps its body in that one catch, so the WRITE is unsuccessful with '34' instead of an escaping IOException. The writer buffers, so the refusal lands on the WRITE whose record fills the buffer. Witness: the classifier unit test, and an end-to-end WRITE loop on Linux /dev/full (ENOSPC by construction) that must end in '34'. IoStatusClass.WriteBoundary (SORT GR15 / MERGE GR12) now has a sequential producer.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB1191: the strip is keyed on the three things GR21 names. A FD whose RECORD clause has the DEPENDING phrase is untouched (GR22); the alphanumeric space is the space character only (U+00A0 survives); and a WRITE or REWRITE carries record-name-1's own category (FileModel.IsNationalRecord, rendered as nationalRecord: true), so an FD with a national and an alphanumeric record description writes each with its own space, never the area's flag.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB1191: a line sequential FD whose RECORD clause has the DEPENDING phrase registers RecordLengthFromDepending, so its records are written at data-name-1's length, trailing spaces kept.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB329 (LANDED 2026-09-05) built this rule's mechanism; kb/Work PB689 gave it a ROW. The row did not exist when PB329 landed -- an interior '## SEQUENTIAL FILES' heading truncated 14.9.51.4's rule block at GR16, so GR17-GR42 were never in the catalog and PB329's implementer had nothing to close. RULE: 'For a line sequential file, if the record area contains one or more characters that are not in the implementor-defined character set defined for a line sequential file, the execution of the WRITE statement is unsuccessful and the I-O status in the write file connector is set to 71.' cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'the execution of the WRITE statement is unsuccessful and the I-O status in the write file connector is set to 71' -> OK 14.9.51.4 23). MECHANISM: LineSequentialCharacterSet is the one executable copy of the Annex A.1 item 115 determination (docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-115: every character at or above U+0020 is a member, the C0 controls below it are not), and SequentialConnector.RecordAreaOutsideLineCharacterSet is the one call shape. BOTH write entry points consult it -- Write and WriteAdvancing -- ahead of every shape branch, because the rule is organization-scoped rather than shape-scoped, and ahead of any stream traffic because 9.1.13.10 item 1 requires the record area and the medium to be left unchanged. (There were THREE until kb/Work PB712, 2026-09-06, deleted WriteBeforeAndAfter: 14.9.51.2 Format 1 prints ONE ADVANCING operand, so the COBOL-2023 BEFORE AFTER pair is a placement and reaches WriteAdvancing like every other print-control write. The arm count fell; the coverage did not.) The test is CHARACTER-wise, not byte-wise: a national record area is walked two bytes at a time as UTF-16BE, so N"CD"'s 00 43 00 44 is two members and not two control characters. MEASURED on the built cobol.exe before PB329 landed: a line sequential WRITE of a record holding 0x00 reported STATUS=00 and left the byte on the medium; after, STATUS=71 and the file is 0 bytes. Goldens walk 09 (READ, 14.9.30.4 GR16), 71 (WRITE, THIS rule), 71 (REWRITE, 14.9.35.4 GR17d), the unchanged medium, and the set boundary (0x7F -> ordinal 128, 0xFF -> ordinal 256 are members) at 2023, the one edition the LINE SEQUENTIAL organization exists in. kb/Work PB688 (2026-09-05): ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL is a COBOL-2023 INTRODUCTION - the Foreword's list of the main changes this third edition makes over ISO/IEC 1989:2014 names "Line Sequential file organization", and 9.1.6 / 9.1.7.1 still name exactly three organizations with 9.1.7.2 splitting the sequential one into its record- and line-delimited types. The organization therefore does not exist below 2023 (the pass now rejects it with COBOLNET0900, registry row file-organization-line-sequential-2023), the 2002 and 2014 copies of the golden were deleted as programs no edition below 2023 can express, and this row's editions are 2023 alone.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work R43 (owner, 2026-09-24): an unsupported facility is unsupported entirely — item 3: a rule whose trigger can only arise through an unsupported capability closes as DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT, CONTINGENT: re-adjudicate if the capability is ever added (kb/Work PB1198 Q2). §14.9.51.4 GR24's reel/unit swap needs an end of reel/unit recognized inside a multi-volume physical file; COBOL.NET provides no reel or unit medium (docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 A.3 items 26, 28-30, 33-34; A.1 item 24), and the witness pins that every connector kind reports a non-unit or mass-storage category (§14.9.6.4 GR2 (a)/(d)), so no WRITE can recognize an end of unit. The READ twin GR-14.9.30.4-23 was closed earlier by an owner-signed §8 derivation.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB964 + PB1027. The omitted ADVANCING phrase acts as AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE (GR25), and PB1027 makes that LITERAL: SequentialConnector.WriteRecord reroutes it to WriteAdvancingRecord(lines: 1, before: false) in EVERY state of the device, for record sequential and line sequential files alike, so the two spellings are one path and write the same file byte for byte (PlainWriteAdvancingConformanceTests holds every three-write mix of plain/AFTER/BEFORE, with and without LINAGE). Before PB1027 it took BEFORE's placement (record, then its line end) whenever no line was open: no blank line after a BEFORE write, the first record of a LINAGE page one line high, a line sequential file travelling twice around an AFTER write. a) n lines = n line terminators; c) zero = a bare carriage return on an open line (overprint; R54); d) mnemonic = implementor-defined zero-line advance, the record always released; e)/f) BEFORE presents then advances, AFTER advances then presents; g) PAGE on a LINAGE file repositions to the next logical page; h) PAGE with no LINAGE = a form feed. Determination (docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 4, Annex A.3 item 37): a file supports vertical positioning when its description has a LINAGE clause or once an ADVANCING phrase has been written to it (SequentialConnector.SupportsVerticalPositioning); a file of which neither holds (an ordinary text or fixed-block data file written with plain WRITEs only) has nothing to position, so its plain WRITE is the record and its line end, with no leading empty line - the GnuCOBOL 3.2 default; the earlier note 'every sequential file supports vertical positioning' is withdrawn. b) (negative identifier) is undefined. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/SequentialConnector.cs#EmitLineSequentialRecord (kb/Work PB1027 deleted both: a plain WRITE on a file that supports vertical positioning is the explicit AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE path (WriteAdvancingRecord), so there is no placement question left to ask and no separate line sequential arm) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/SequentialConnector.cs#ImplicitAdvanceIsBefore (kb/Work PB1027 deleted both: a plain WRITE on a file that supports vertical positioning is the explicit AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE path (WriteAdvancingRecord), so there is no placement question left to ask and no separate line sequential arm)

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB686 + PB523 LANDED - THE CONDITION WAS ALREADY MEASURED; ARM a)'s REPOSITIONING SENTENCE IS NOW MEASURED TOO, ON BOTH ORDERINGS. What this row was PARTIAL for was named exactly: arm a) does not stop at the condition, it also says 'the device is repositioned to the first line that may be written on the next logical page and the logical record is presented on that line', and for any file with a LINES AT TOP phrase that first writable line is past the top margin, which 13.18.34.4 GR4's discarded operand made unreachable - the counter landed right and the device did not. Both are now decided in one place: PositionOnLogicalPage computes the condition and calls BeginNextLogicalPage, which travels the rest of the current page (unwritten body lines plus the bottom margin, GR5), re-evaluates the operands (13.18.34.4 GR6 b) 3, 'before the device is positioned and after all positioning on the current page') and steps one line onto the next page, leaving the device on its line 1 with the new top margin still to materialize. Bytes_TopAndBottomMarginsAreLinesOfTheLogicalPage pins the AFTER ordering ('the device is repositioned ... and the logical record is presented on that line' - the record after the wrap is on page-2 body line 1, physical line 11, not on the first line of the page and not on the line after the old body); Bytes_OverflowWithBeforePhrase_PresentsThenRepositions pins the BEFORE ordering ('the logical record is presented and the device is repositioned'), which was previously exercised only by nist:SQ201M and now has a spec-derived fixture. The a)/b) DISCRIMINATION and the c == page size boundary are unchanged and stay adjudicated in docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 4 ('DETERMINATION - the 14.9.51.4 GR26 a)/b) boundary at LINAGE-COUNTER = page size'), pinned by conformance:2023/pb686_linage_gr26_boundary and its 85 twin on BOTH arms of the FOOTING dispatch. RESIDUE, deliberately not folded in here: GR27's choice between EC-I-O-EOP-OVERFLOW and EC-I-O-EOP is GR-14.9.51.4-27's row and the EC subsystem is a later slice.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: GR28: 'If, during the successful execution of a WRITE statement with the NOT END-OF-PAGE phrase, the end-of-page condition does not occur, then after execution of the input-output operation, control is transferred to imperative-statement-2 of the NOT END-OF-PAGE phrase. If control is returned from imperative-statement-2, control is then transferred to the end of the WRITE statement.' (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 -> OK rule 28). EmitWrite snapshots the connector status before the FILE STATUS store and USE hook, then renders `if (successful && EndOfPage) {AT} else if (successful) {NOT}` — the NOT arm runs only on a successful write without the condition, after the operation, and falls to the end of the statement. Both orders of the phrases parse (writeAtEndOfPage choice indicators). Goldens conformance:2023/pb686_linage_gr26_boundary and conformance:85/pb686_linage_gr26_boundary_85 print 'NO-EOP' on exactly the writes that land inside the page body (spec-derived per the PB686 determination).

notes: kb/Work PB1192 (w61d). subject: WRITE statement
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'Subsequent records released to the operating environment have consecutively higher relative record numbers' -> OK 30)): in extend mode the first record gets highest-existing RRN + 1, later records get consecutive numbers, and the RRN is MOVEd into the RELATIVE KEY item. Code: extend mode can only be reached with ACCESS SEQUENTIAL (§14.9.27.3 SR2), and RelativeConnector.Write's sequential arm takes NextSequentialSlot() = Max(_st.Highest, _lastReleasedSlot) + 1. That is highest-existing + 1 for the first record and consecutive after it, because nothing else releases between two writes on an unshared file (GR31 covers the shared case). KeyedIoEmitter.EmitWrite then StoreArith's FileRelativeSlot into the key item when the status is successful: a MOVE-rule numeric store, with Truncation. Probe dir: out/probe/write-statement-p3/ (pinned adj-d1 cobol.exe). rel1.cob: OUTPUT writes RRN 1..3; a DYNAMIC connector adds RRN 5; OPEN EXTEND then writes 'E-OK 00 RK=6', 7, 8, 9 (consecutive, starting at highest+1), and the 5th write overflows RELATIVE KEY PIC 9 with 'E-INV 24'. The read-back walks 1,2,3,5,6,7,8,9. The test l1_open_extend_position is spec-derived: it seeds records 1 and 4 sparsely, and EXTEND gives RK=0005. It covers the first-record and MOVE sentences; the consecutive-subsequent sentence is witnessed only by the probe. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the rule is in every edition's relative/indexed WRITE text; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change to it)]

subject: WRITE statement

subject: WRITE statement
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'The data item specified as the prime record key shall be set by the runtime element to the desired value prior to the execution of the WRITE statement' -> OK 37)): the program sets the key before the WRITE. subject: WRITE statement
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'If the DUPLICATES phrase is not specified and the alternate key value is non unique, the execution of the WRITE statement is unsuccessful' -> OK 40)). Code: for each alternate key, `exists && !_alts[i].Dups` gives '22' and the record is not added. With DUPLICATES, the record is added with a fresh release ordinal under every key (ReleaseOrdinals), so a sequential walk returns duplicates in the order they were written. Probe dir: out/probe/write-statement-p3/ (pinned adj-d1 cobol.exe). idx1.cob: FU (ALTERNATE U-ALT, no DUPLICATES): U01/ZZ gives 'U1 OK 00', U02/ZZ gives 'U2 INV 22', and a random READ by ZZ still returns U01. Through FX/FR (X-ALT WITH DUPLICATES): K20, K30, K40, K50 are written sequentially and K05, K47 dynamically, all with alternate key AA, and START KEY = R-ALT then READ NEXT walks K20, K30, K40, K50, K05, K47. That is the write order, not prime-key order. The '02' of §9.1.13.2 2c accompanies each duplicate. The '22' that a SUPPRESSED alternate key raises today is a GR41 defect, not this rule's. No spec-derived golden is aimed at the WRITE side (l1_read_alt_dup_walk is a READ GR26 golden), so test-ref is empty. (b) IMPLICIT USAGE DISPLAY is modelled and is READ: IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs#StaticUsageOf answers Usage.Display for a nested intrinsic whose ResultCategory is Alphanumeric, and that is the axis §15.18.3 r2 (--check'd) and §15.19.3 r4/r5/r6/r7 key on, so the implicit usage is not decorative. (c) 'represented in the alphanumeric coded character set in effect when the function is referenced at runtime': the compiler has ONE runtime alphanumeric repertoire — UTF-16, one code unit per character position — recorded as a required-and-documented determination in docs/CONFORMANCE.md items 33 and 188, so 'the set in effect' is invariant and the sentence is satisfied by construction rather than left open. subject: Intrinsic functions
notes: LANDED (kb/Work PB124 wave 3): the space-separator boundary arm - a boolean expression connects every term with a B-operator (8.8.2 r1), so TWO ADJACENT OPERAND TERMS at depth 0 end the argument, and a B-operator found beyond belongs to a LATER argument. notes: CITATION re-derived mechanically: cite.py --check 15.3.3.6.1 'A minus sign to indicate that the common time portion of the data is adjusted upward by the offset values to represent UTC' -> OK, anchored on the rule marker '2)'. The MIRROR of rule 1, and I read both halves separately rather than inferring them from rule 1's arm. (1) PRODUCE-THE-CHARACTER. CobolDate.cs#EmitFormatted line 363 'char osign = offsetMinutes >= 0 ? '+' : '-'' writes '-' for a negative argument-4/argument-3, with the MAGNITUDE taken through Math.Abs at line 361 so the offset-hours/offset-minutes subfields carry the unsigned value the subformat wants. The negative value survives the emitter intact: IntrinsicRenderer.cs#RenderFormattedTime / #RenderFormattedDatetime pass the offset through ArgInt -> AsInt -> RuntimeApi.IntegerArg, a raising (not wrapping) narrowing to long, not through any absolute-value or unsigned carrier. Verified by golden: conformance:2023/pb11_datetime_format_grammar 'OFF-MIN=010000-2359' for FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss+hhmm" 3600 -1439) -- the format's placeholder is '+' and the DATA carries '-', which is precisely the shape §15.3.3.6.1 describes. (2) HONOUR-THE-MEANING (adjust UPWARD). EmitFormatted line 328 'secs -= offsetMinutes * 60m' with a NEGATIVE offset ADDS, then lines 329-330 roll the day. This is the direction NOTE 1 of rule 3 illustrates ('0514278124-0500' == '1014278124Z'), and CobolDate.cs#FormattedCurrentDate reproduces exactly that shape for a west-of-UTC system clock (offMin = -300 -> osign '-', oh 05, om 00, with now.TimeOfDay giving the LOCAL common time). (3) CONSUME-THE-CHARACTER. Analyze lines 513-515 accept '-' through the same single expression that accepts '+' ('if (c is not ('+' or '-')) { ... }' -- both signs take the identical no-op branch), and no downstream use is required: §15.79.4 and the §15.48.4 r1 NOTE (both --check OK, see GR-15.3.3.6.1-1) confine the returned values to the common-time / date subfields. Editions rationale identical to GR-15.3.3.6.1-1. || REFUTED: verdict CONFIRMED at CONFORMS, but TWO load-bearing claims in the note above are WRONG and the record is changed. This is a COMPOUND rule with FOUR normative obligations plus three informative NOTEs; I located and read the implementation of every one. (a) '0' IS A PERMITTED SIGN VALUE. notes: OVERTURNED PARTIAL -> NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION. The prior verdict rested on TWO edges it called unverified; I executed BOTH against the shipping binary, so its stated basis no longer holds - one edge is CORRECT and the other emits a value 15.21.3 forbids, with no conforming alternative available in the standard, which is an owner call, not a mechanical fix. "+" : "-") + Math.Abs(t.Offset.Hours).ToString("00") + Math.Abs(t.Offset.Minutes).ToString("00"). InvariantCulture pins the proleptic Gregorian calendar and ASCII digits (positions 1-4). VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, COBOL side: 'MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO WS-CD' (PIC X(21)) at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 -> '2026073010404830-0700'; FUNCTION LENGTH of the function = 0021. Receiver varied per the PB5 lesson - PIC X(30) space-pads to '...-0700         ', PIC X(8) truncates to '20260730', PIC N(21) carries all 21, and STRING ... DELIMITED BY SIZE contributes exactly 21 characters - so no receiver scale hides a layout defect. VERIFIED BY DIRECT EXECUTION OF THE SHIPPING METHOD (loaded src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/Cobol.Net.Runtime.dll and invoked CobolNet.Runtime.CobolDate.Format21 over fixed DateTimeOffsets, since TimeZoneInfo.Local reads the Windows registry and ignores TZ): +05:45 -> '2026073010331564+0545', -09:30 -> '...-0930', +12:45 -> '...+1245', 00:00 -> '...+0000', -12:00 -> '...-1200', +13:00 -> '...+1300'. So positions 20-21 (the prior pass's unverified edge (b)) are CORRECT for non-zero minute offsets, position 17 is correct on BOTH branches including the 'same as UTC' => '+' boundary, and the '-' branch reaches -14:00 too - CORRECTED 2026-08-31 from 'cannot exceed 12 because no TimeZoneInfo zone is below -12:00', which is true of the HOST ZONE TABLE and false of the value CURRENT-DATE reports: COBOLNET_CLOCK pins a DateTimeOffset directly and that type admits -14:00, so the departure is symmetric and the documentation names both signs. THE ONE OPEN POINT, now demonstrated rather than suspected: +14:00 -> '2026073010331564+1400'. 15.21.3 positions 18-19 state 'If character position 17 is '+', two numeric digits are returned in the range 00 through 13', and Math.Abs(t.Offset.Hours) is UNCLAMPED, so a run on a host whose TimeZoneInfo.Local is 'Line Islands Standard Time' / Pacific-Kiritimati (UTC+14, a zone Windows and IANA both ship) returns '14' there. The reason this is NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION and not DIVERGES: the standard's table offers NO in-range value for a +14 host, so no behavior conforms - emitting 14 (today) is an out-of-range implementor extension, clamping to 13 misreports the offset, and returning '0'/'00'/'00' means 'the system has no facility to provide the local time differential factor', which is false. Nothing in CobolDate.cs, docs/CONFORMANCE.md or the design docs records a decision, and the same unclamped expression also feeds WHEN-COMPILED (15.99.3, identical table). THE BARE OWNER QUESTION: on a host whose local UTC offset is +14:00, what shall CURRENT-DATE (and WHEN-COMPILED) return in character positions 17-19? CORRECTED FROM THE PRIOR RECORD: positions 13-14 do conform without qualification - 7.3.17.4 GR1 implies OFF when no LEAP-SECOND directive is written and GR3 then forbids >59, which .NET's 'ss' can never emit; GR2's ON case leaves >59 to the implementor, so ignoring the directive (it sits in ConditionalCompilationProcessor.KnownIgnoredDirectives) is conforming on both branches, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md's 'documented non-support' wording for >>LEAP-SECOND overstates the exposure for THIS rule. CORRECTED 2026-08-31 (the sentence this replaces was written before R21 and asserted the opposite): CurrentDate() reads the INJECTABLE seam - CobolDate.cs 'public static string CurrentDate() => Format21(RunUnit.Current.Clock.Now())' - so CURRENT-DATE, SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT, FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE and the windowing defaults observe ONE clock per run unit, the §15.100.3 r5 YEAR-TO-YYYY identity holds, and ClockSeamDriftTests is the source-form guard that no direct DateTime[Offset].Now read comes back. test-needed: (i) a unit test over CobolDate.Format21 with fixed DateTimeOffsets (+14:00, +13:00, -12:00, +05:45, -09:30, a zero-hundredths instant, a single-digit month/day) asserting every position's 15.21.3 range, and (ii) a conformance case pinning CURRENT-DATE through the injectable clock once that seam covers it. The only existing spec-derived test touching CURRENT-DATE (IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.WhenCompiled_CompileTimeConstant_PinnedToSpec, verified on disk) asserts only the ordering CURRENT-DATE >= WHEN-COMPILED and inspects NO character position of the CURRENT-DATE value, so it does not cover this rule and test-ref stays empty. || OWNER DETERMINATION RECORDED 2026-08-30 (answered via AskUserQuestion: "True offset"); NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION -> DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT. THE QUESTION THIS ROW CARRIED IS ANSWERED: on a host whose local UTC offset lies outside the rule's table, CURRENT-DATE and WHEN-COMPILED REPORT THE TRUE OFFSET. ONE DETERMINATION, BOTH ROWS: RV-15.21.3-1 and RV-15.99.3-1 share it because one formatter serves both (CobolDate.Format21) and §15.99.3 r1's table is character-for-character §15.21.3 r1's; the compile-time bake (IntrinsicBinder.CompileClock) and the run-time read (RunUnit.Current.Clock) are independent seams onto that one formatter, and the shared test asserts they agree rather than assuming it. WHAT THE ADJUDICATOR MISSED, and it is what makes this an owner DECISION rather than a bug: the standard itself classes this clause as processor-dependent. Annex A.3 item 2, validated verbatim - cite.py --check A.3 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' -> OK - and 4.5 NOTE, validated verbatim ('These factors can include the use of optional, processor-dependent, or implementor-defined language elements'), together mean a conforming implementation may fail to translate a compilation group that uses it without ceasing to conform. Annex F.2 additionally makes STANDARD-BINARY an obsolete feature, and it is F.2 ITEM 3 - not Annex E - that records the non-implementation: '3. STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' (cite.py --check F.2 'STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item' -> OK). CITATION REPAIRED 2026-08-31, and the error was worse than a wrong annex letter: the sentence as previously quoted here ('it has not been implemented ... by any COBOL provider', singular) is F.2 ITEM 5's, which is about the VALIDATE FACILITY - a real clause answering a different question (feedback_a_real_clause_can_answer_a_different_question). Item 3 also carries the reevaluation note that makes the decline REVISITABLE: 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). The non-support is already recorded at docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 2 ('| 2 | ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY | 11.9.5 | Not claimed | Obsolete feature (A.3 NOTE 1); the native/standard-decimal modes are provided |') - the DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT shape, a verdict only the owner may set, hence NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION. BARE QUESTION: should 15.27.3 rule 2 be recorded as discharged by the existing documented non-support of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY (Annex A.3 item 2 processor-dependence) rather than carried as an open inventory GAP? Identical to the already-adjudicated sibling RV-15.73.3-2 for PI; one decision should settle the whole 15.4.1 family. EDITIONS DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY OF INTRINSICCATALOG: the STANDARD-BINARY keyword of the ARITHMETIC clause is a COBOL-2014 addition (the 2002 clause offered NATIVE and STANDARD only; the compiler's own edition gate agrees - 'OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY.' at --std 2002 draws COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014 (targeting COBOL-2002)', re-run by me), so the rule's precondition cannot arise at 85 or 2002. TEST COVERAGE: none - no test references FUNCTION E under any arithmetic mode. The honest cover is a negative case pinning that FUNCTION E under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is refused BY MODE; a mode-only rejection test that never names E would not cover this row. || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOLNET0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).

No spec-derived test, and none constructible. || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). CITATIONS RE-VALIDATED BY ME: cite.py --check 15.48.3 "If argument-1 is a date format, the contents of argument-2 shall be a valid date in that format." -> OK (§15.48.3 4)). cite.py --check 15.3 "If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value" -> OK (§15.3 rule 14), and I read that paragraph IN FULL because it is what forecloses every escape from the finding below: "... results in an incorrect value for that argument OR FOR THE RETURNED VALUE according to the rules specified in the function definition ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist ... If the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist and checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled, the implementor defines the result of the function reference."

THE VALIDATION ITSELF IS CORRECT and I re-read every leg: CobolDate#Analyze walks the tokenized format against the data, requiring each in-data separator ('-', ':', 'W', 'T', 'Z') to appear, rejecting a non-digit, a short field and any trailing character (`if (pos != data.Length) return pos + 1;`), and range-checking every subfield with per-digit narrowing - year 1601..9999 (§15.3.1.3/.5/.7, "greater than 1600 and less than or equal to 9999"), month 1..12, day-of-month against DaysInMonth, day-of-year against the leap year, week against LongIsoYear, weekday 1..7. I checked LongIsoYear against §15.3.1.7's OWN formulation (53 weeks "if the year subfield represents a common year and January 4 of that year falls on Sunday, or if the year subfield represents a leap year and January 4 of that year falls on a Saturday or Sunday") and derived that it is equivalent to ISO 8601's Jan-1-Thursday / leap-Wednesday rule, which is what ISOWeek.GetWeeksInYear implements - so the week cap is right. A nonzero result becomes ExceptionState#ArgumentError, which I read: it sets EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION fatal when checking is enabled and otherwise returns 0 - exactly §15.3 rule 14's disposition.

THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). notes: VERDICT UPHELD, on stronger evidence than the original, with one citation corrected. CITATION FIX: the original note said '§8.8.4.2.2 makes two greatest-valued numeric arguments equal in algebraic value'; §8.8.4.2.2 is 'General format' and --check FAILS on that text. The clause is §8.8.4.2.4 (--check OK: 'For operands whose class is numeric, a comparison is made with respect to the algebraic value of the operands regardless of the manner in which their usage is described ... Zero is considered a unique value regardless of the sign'). WHY THIS SURVIVES THE ATTACK AT IMPLEMENTATION LEVEL RATHER THAN BY SAMPLING: leftmost-wins is a property of ExtremeIndex ALONE - `for (int i = 1; i < xs.Length; i++) { int c = cmp(xs[i], xs[k]); if (max ? c > 0 : c < 0) k = i; }` - and is independent of the comparator passed in, so it holds identically for all six MaxString/MinString overloads (native pad-compare, the ushort[] alphanumeric-PCS weights, and the NationalCollation variant) and for OrdMaxString/OrdMinString, which is the whole family in one place. The original evidence only exhibited SAME-CONTENT / DIFFERENT-LENGTH ties, which cannot distinguish leftmost-wins from a stable comparator; the refuter added a tie between DIFFERENT CONTENTS of EQUAL VALUE, which is what the rule is actually about, and it passes on the weights overload. The NUMERIC/INDEX half remains vacuous rather than unverified, and the argument is sound: §8.8.4.2.4 makes two greatest-valued numeric arguments equal in algebraic value (and makes signed and unsigned zero one value), §15.59.4 r3 confines the SIZE question to alphanumeric and national, and under standard arithmetic §15.4.1 puts the returned value in a mode-defined intermediate data item whose characteristics come from the mode rather than from the selected argument - so two tied numeric or index arguments have no observable difference in content to choose between. CONTINGENCY WORTH RECORDING: this rule governs which of the TIED arguments is returned; whether the tie is real is RV-15.59.4-1's question, and at the boundaries documented there the 'greatest value' premise is itself wrong. EDITION WINDOW as in AR-15.59.3-1, from Annex E only. EVIDENCE: PROBED, --std 2023. Every subfield satisfies §15.3.1.7: year 9999 is >1600 and <=9999; Jan 4 9999 is a Monday so 9999 is a 52-week ISO year and week 52 is inside the permitted 01..52; day-of-week 7 is inside 1..7. The expected result is +86399.00 — D.31.5.9 makes the date VALIDATED BUT DISCARDED for this function, so the integer date form is never needed here at all; Analyze computes it unconditionally at its `else if (hasWeek) integerDate = ISOWeek.ToDateTime(...)` leg, and ISO-9999-W52-7 falls on 10000-01-02, outside DateTime.MaxValue. Even on the most conservative reading (that the denoted date is out of range and r5 is therefore violated), §15.3 fixes the disposition as EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION or the implementor-defined result — never a raw CLR stack trace, which is neither a COBOL value nor a COBOL exception condition. Fix shape: bound-check the week-date reconstruction (and hand SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME a path that does not build integerDate at all). The rest of r5 is correct and was verified: the mandatory 'T' is required in the data (§15.3.3.7); the D.31.5.9 worked example `("YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm", "19950215T05142781+0500")` → +18867.81 with the offset correctly excluded; Feb-31 in the same format → the §15.3 default 0; the calendar boundary "99991231T235959" → +86399.00. test-needed. ⚙ FIXED AND CLOSED 2026-08-05 (fix-queue PB23). This row's ONLY divergence was the shared week-date reconstruction, and the row itself said so ("ONE ROOT CAUSE, ONE FIX"). CobolDate#Analyze no longer calls ISOWeek.ToDateTime: §15.3.1.7 fixes week 1 as "the week that includes January 4", so that week's Monday is computed directly and every later day is a plain integer offset from it — the arithmetic CANNOT overflow, which is the point, because the input is VALID and no tightening of the per-subfield range table could have prevented the fault. The result is then range-checked against §15.5.2's ceiling ("shall be greater than zero and shall be less than or equal to ... 3,067,671"), and ONLY the caller that must PRODUCE an integer date form reacts: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION through ExceptionState#ArgumentError per §15.3 rule 14's "incorrect value ... FOR THE RETURNED VALUE" arm (implementor-defined result 0 when checking is off), while TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME still answers 0 — §15.92.4 requires any non-zero answer to be "the ordinal character position at which the first error ... was detected", and no CHARACTER of "9999W526" is in error (the identical '6' in "2009W526" is valid) — and SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME still returns its seconds (§15.79.4 reads only the time subfields). THE TWO-DAY WINDOW THIS ROW RECORDS (d=6 AND d=7) IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not re-derived on paper: 9999-12-31 is ISO 9999-W52-5. notes: CLOSED by kb/Work PB246. Citation re-derived: cite.py --check 15.84.4 'the returned value is the absolute value of the approximation of the square root of argument-1' -> OK, rule 4 - and the rule's own lead-in is 'When native arithmetic is in effect', so CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs#Sqrt IS this rule's site and the SDIDI lane answers to r2 instead. THE APPROXIMATION HALF WAS ALREADY CONFORMING (Math.Sqrt is IEC 60559 correctly-rounded, and SQRT's Codomain.None is correct because 15.84.4 states no bound, so the FromDoubleBounded clamp must not apply). THE ABSOLUTE-VALUE HALF WAS NOT IMPLEMENTED AT ALL, only unreachable-by-argument: grep Abs over the file returned nothing. The rule does not say 'made non-negative when negative'; it says the returned value IS the absolute value, and IEEE abs clears the sign bit - |-0.0| is +0.0 while IEC 60559 mandates sqrt(-0) = -0 EXACTLY so that sqrt is not the absolute value there. Negative zero is therefore the unique input on which r4's phrase does work, it is a LEGAL argument-1 (15.84.3 r2 admits zero) that a COMP-1/COMP-2 item reaches by ordinary native underflow, and the receiver-less/float arm renders it unquantized through CobolFloat.Display, which is IEEE-faithful and prints the sign. subject: SUM function
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS 2026-09-05 (kb/Work PB252). THE PRIOR RECORD'S OWN LANE (b) DESCRIPTION WAS WRONG, and that is what this landing corrects. It read: '`case "SumScaled" or "RangeScaled"` takes AlignedArgs ... and calls CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#SumScaled (`Int128 s = 0; foreach (x) s += x`) ... the alignment is escape-checked (CobolNum.RescaleEscape), so an argument that cannot be represented in the Int128 intermediate raises the size-error condition instead of wrapping.' RescaleEscape bounds each ALIGNED ARGUMENT and says nothing about their SUM: `Int128.Abs(value) > Int128.MaxValue / Pow10Wide(toScale - fromScale)`. MEASURED on the compiler's own exe before the fix, inside the 31-digit cap: `P PIC S9(31) VALUE ALL '9'` beside `Q PIC SV9(7)`, `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION SUM(P P P Q) ON SIZE ERROR ...` -- each aligned argument (9.99e37) passes the per-argument bound (1.70e31 at scale 7), their sum 2.9999e38 exceeds Int128.MaxValue and wrapped to -4.028e37, which at scale 7 fits a 31-digit receiver, so the phrase was NOT taken and a SIGN-FLIPPED value was stored silently. The EAE's true value (3x10^31 - 3) needs 32 digits, so Sec.14.7.5 rule 3 makes the size error condition exist there with NO implementor latitude at all. FIX: the accumulator is now `checked` under one try for the whole loop and escapes through CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#SizeEscape -> CobolSizeError/EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW, which ArithmeticEmitter lands on the ON SIZE ERROR arm leaving the receiver unchanged (Sec.14.7.5 rule 1). GOVERNING CLAUSE CORRECTED IN THE SAME CHANGE: the message text had carried PB32's inherited 'ISO Sec.8.8.1.2 rule 7', which is a REAL clause answering a DIFFERENT question (arithmetic expressions are exempt from the composite-of-operands limit); the rule that makes this the size error condition is Sec.14.7.5 rule 5 -- 'if native arithmetic is in effect and the implementor defines that the range of values allowed for the intermediate data item is to be checked, when an arithmetic operation on the intermediate data item would cause the new value to be outside of the allowed range' (--check 14.7.5 -> OK). ALL THREE LANES NOW READ AND EACH IS THE Sec.15.88.4 r1 EAE: (a) standard modes -> SumDec on the SDIDI, left to right; (b) NATIVE fixed-point -> the checked Int128 accumulator, exact until the D1 boundary and then LOUD; (c) NATIVE with a float argument -> SumReal. Left-to-right accumulation is normative (Sec.8.8.1.2 rule 3, --check OK), so a partial sum that escapes the carrier IS an r5 size error even when later terms would bring the total back inside -- the modular cancellation the old unchecked `s += x` happened to deliver was two's complement's answer, not the standard's. CLOSING EVIDENCE: conformance:2002/pb252_native_carrier_boundary pins the r3 case (no latitude) and a control well inside the carrier; the drift test closes the whole exact-carrier entry-point set by reflection, so a new variadic exact function cannot ship unguarded. Both were verified to FAIL on the pre-fix build (SUM-R3-SIZE-ERROR=NO, RANGE-SIGN=NEGATIVE). EDITIONS: carried forward as adjudicated; the witness itself needs 31-digit items so it lives in the 2002 corpus (COBOL-85 caps fixed-point at 18 digits, COBOLNET0802).

subject: TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD function
notes: LANDED (kb/Work PB254). The PARTIAL was leg a's UPPER half, defeated above 2**63 by the intake, not by the body. CITATIONS RE-DERIVED MECHANICALLY, none inherited: cite.py --check 15.90.4 "less than 16 010 000 or greater than 99 999 999" -> OK (15.90.4 1) a)); --check 15.90.4 "The year is not within the range 1601 to 9999" -> OK (1) a) NOTE 1); --check 15.90.4 "The date is valid" -> OK (1) d) NOTE 4); --check 15.90.3 "Argument-1 shall be an integer" -> OK (15.90.3 rule 1); --check 15.3 "results in an incorrect value for that argument" -> OK (15.3 rule 14); --check 8.3.3.3.2 "fixed-point numeric literals of 1 through 31 digits" -> OK. THE DERIVATION. 15.90.3 r1 is the WHOLE argument rule and constrains nothing but integer-ness; 15.90.4 r1a is a CATCH-ALL over both directions, so the function is TOTAL over the integers and every integer argument has a defined verdict. 15.3 rule 14 sets EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION only when evaluation 'results in an incorrect value for that argument or for the returned value according to the rules specified in the function definition' - there is no such value here, so a conforming program may pass any integer and must receive a verdict, never an abort. THE DEFECT, re-probed on this tree before the fix, not inherited from the note: (a) FLOAT lane - 01 FBIG USAGE COMP-2, COMPUTE FBIG = 1.0E19, FUNCTION TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD(FBIG) printed 00, i.e. 1) d) 'The date is valid', where r1a requires 1; the body was CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs#TestDateYyyymmddReal = 'TryIntegerArg(...) ? CobolDate.TestDateYyyymmdd(n) : 0' and the literal ': 0' tail is the verdict for VALID. (b) CHECKING-ON lane - '>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON' with 01 BIG19 PIC 9(19) VALUE 9999999999999999999 terminated the run unit: 'abnormal run-unit termination: EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): the intrinsic integer argument 9999999999999999999 is outside the range the function can represent (ISO 15.3)' - on CONFORMING source. (c) NATIVE/Dec lane printed 01, the right code by COINCIDENCE ONLY: CobolIntrinsics.IntegerArg substituted the checking-off default 0 for the ARGUMENT and 0 lands in the same r1a arm (0 < 16 010 000); the coincidence evaporates under checking, which is lane (b). THE FIX is at the validator, never at the shared narrowing: CobolDate.TestDateYyyymmdd now takes Int128 and answers r1a before any conversion (past the guard the value is eight digits, so the int narrowing is exact); IntrinsicRenderer's 'case "TestDateYyyymmdd" or "TestDayYyyyddd"' arm takes the WIDE intake IntArgWide -> AsIntWide, which has no raise point and, unlike AsInt, carries the U (UInt128) carrier arm as well; TestDateYyyymmddReal classifies by r1a on the VALUE, so +/-infinity and every magnitude past the window answer 1 without narrowing, and the one input that is the value of no integer (a NaN) routes to the shared 15.3 raise site and substitutes the documented implementor-defined result 1, never the 0 that would call a non-date a valid date. STRUCTURE, so the next case is automatic: the intake width is now derived from the runtime body's DECLARED carrier (Int128 = total, long = bounded), and IntrinsicCarrierAgreementDriftTests.EveryTotalIntegerArgument_TakesTheWideIntake re-derives that pairing by reflection and fails when an arm and its body disagree. The guard was proven RED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS on the shipped renderer before being trusted: reverting this arm produced 'TestDateYyyymmdd: body declares Int128 ... but the arm narrows' plus its sibling, and a stray widening of the DateOfInteger/DayOfInteger/IntegerOfDate/IntegerOfDay arm (whose 15.5.2 domain IS bounded, so the 15.3 landing is right there) produced the opposite four. THE GOLDEN that closes the row is conformance:2002/pb254_total_integer_arguments, which pins r1a's UPPER half on every carrier an integer argument can arrive on - T1 100000000 -> 1; T2 99999999 -> 2, proving the bound is EXCLUSIVE and that r1a did not swallow the boundary (MOD(99999999 10000) = 9999 > 1299, so r1b fires); T3 a 19-digit LITERAL (8.3.3.3.2 requires 1..31 digits be accepted) -> 1; T4 a PIC 9(19) item -> 1; T5 a PIC 9(31) item -> 1; T6 the 15.3 type-6 arithmetic-expression witness P18 * 100 + 62 = 2**64 + 1 995 046 -> 1; T7 a FLOAT-LONG item holding 1.0E19 -> 1 - and it runs the whole program under >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON with an ARMED CONTROL, because a checking-ON leg proves nothing if the directive is inert: leg ARMED raises the condition deliberately from FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DAY, whose 15.5.2 argument form IS bounded, and the USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION declarative reports 'ARMED=EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION' before RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT leaves the receiver at its 99 preset. Every T value above was derived from the rule text first and then observed.

subject: TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes: CLOSED by kb/Work PB255. Citation re-derived: cite.py --check 15.92.4 'the value returned is the ordinal character position at which the first error in argument-2 was detected' -> OK, rule 1. The per-digit range NARROWING and the zero arm were already right and are undisturbed; the three residues are all closed. (1) THE OFFSET SUBFIELD BOUNDS WERE JUSTIFIED BY THE WRONG CLAUSE. Fld.OffHour and Fld.OffMinute share their switch arms with Fld.Hour and Fld.Minute and were the only bounds in the table with no citation, while the adjudication defended them from 15.3.3.3 - which governs the COMMON TIME format by its own words ('the minutes subfield of the data (corresponding to mm in a common time format)'). The clause that governs them is 15.3.3.6.2: cite.py --check 15.3.3.6.2 'The offset-hours subfield of the data associated with a basic or extended offset time format shall contain a value from 00 to 23 inclusive' -> OK and the offset-minutes twin -> OK. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). "+" : "-") + Math.Abs(t.Offset.Hours).ToString("00") + Math.Abs(t.Offset.Minutes).ToString("00")`. This is the SAME formatter CURRENT-DATE uses (§15.21.3's table is character-for-character the same table), which is why this row inherits that row's open owner question rather than getting an independent verdict. POSITION BY POSITION AGAINST THE RULE TEXT: 1-4 four Gregorian year digits - InvariantCulture pins the proleptic Gregorian calendar and ASCII digits, "yyyy" zero-pads to four; 5-6 "MM" 01-12; 7-8 "dd" 01-31; 9-10 "HH" 00-23; 11-12 "mm" 00-59; 13-14 "ss" - conforms on BOTH LEAP-SECOND branches (cite.py --check 7.3.17.4 "the implementor defines whether a value greater than 59" => OK §7.3.17.4 GR2, which leaves the ON-phrase maximum implementor-defined, and .NET's DateTimeOffset cannot represent a 60th second so "ss" never exceeds 59; LeapSecondDirectiveProcessor's own summary records the REPORTED side as answered "never" for WHEN-COMPILED by name); 15-16 "ff" hundredths 00-99, and the '00 when the system has no fractional facility' escape is unneeded since DateTimeOffset.Now carries sub-second precision; 17 - '+' on `Offset >= TimeSpan.Zero` (correctly INCLUDING the 'same as UTC' boundary the rule assigns to '+') and '-' otherwise, with '0' unreachable, which is right because .NET always provides the local time differential factor; 20-21 `Math.Abs(t.Offset.Minutes)` two digits 00-59. NOTE ON THE TRANSCRIPTION: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 34038 renders position 17's minus as U+2013 EN DASH (verified by codepoint scan); the emitted character is ASCII hyphen-minus, which is the only dash in the §8.1.2 COBOL character repertoire - an OCR artifact, not a divergence. THE OPEN POINT, and the reason this is not CONFORMS: positions 18-19 require '00 through 13' when position 17 is '+', and `Math.Abs(t.Offset.Hours)` is UNCLAMPED, so on a host whose local offset is +14:00 (Pacific/Kiritimati, 'Line Islands Standard Time' - a zone both Windows and IANA ship) the compiling host bakes '14' into positions 18-19. The standard's table offers NO in-range value for such a host, so no behavior conforms: emitting 14 is an out-of-range extension, clamping to 13 misreports the offset, and '0'/'00'/'00' asserts the false 'no facility' case. THIS IS ALREADY A REGISTERED OWNER QUESTION, NOT A NEW ONE: the inventory row RV-15.21.3-1 carries the identical finding and states 'the same unclamped expression also feeds WHEN-COMPILED (15.99.3, identical table)', and kb/Work/PB67.md (status: owner) closes with 'The separate CURRENT-DATE +14:00 spec-hole question (RV-15.21.3-1) remains its own decision'. D13 reserves the call to the owner. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation') has NO row in docs/CONFORMANCE.md - the determinations table jumps from nothing to item 112 (the 86,400 half). The substance is stated inside item 112's prose and in the prose at CONFORMANCE.md line 158, but the required, separately-documented item-111 determination for positions 13-14 does not exist as such. TEST NEEDED: a unit test over CobolDate.Format21 with fixed DateTimeOffsets (+14:00, +13:00, +00:00, -12:00, +05:45, -09:30, a zero-hundredths instant, a single-digit month/day) asserting every position's §15.99.3 r1 range. || OWNER DETERMINATION RECORDED 2026-08-30 (answered via AskUserQuestion: "True offset"); NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION -> DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT. THE QUESTION THIS ROW CARRIED IS ANSWERED: on a host whose local UTC offset lies outside the rule's table, CURRENT-DATE and WHEN-COMPILED REPORT THE TRUE OFFSET. ONE DETERMINATION, BOTH ROWS: RV-15.21.3-1 and RV-15.99.3-1 share it because one formatter serves both (CobolDate.Format21) and §15.99.3 r1's table is character-for-character §15.21.3 r1's; the compile-time bake (IntrinsicBinder.CompileClock) and the run-time read (RunUnit.Current.Clock) are independent seams onto that one formatter, and the shared test asserts they agree rather than assuming it. WHY NO ALTERNATIVE CONFORMS: the rule caps positions 18-19 at 00..13 under '+' and 00..12 under '-' (cite.py --check 15.21.3 'two numeric digits are returned in the range 00 through 13 indicating the number of hours that the local time is ahead of Coordinated Universal Time' -> OK; the same text --check'd against 15.99.3 -> OK), and for a +14:00 host the table names no value at all - emitting 14 leaves the range, clamping to 13 misreports what §15.21.1 defines as 'the ... local time differential factor provided by the system on which the function is evaluated' (--check -> OK), and '0'/'00'/'00' asserts position 17's 'the system ... does not have the facility to provide the local time differential factor' (--check 15.21.3 -> OK), which is false.
