subject: FLAG-02 directive
notes: kb/Work PB1374 (w1020f). Printed format rendered from the canonical PDF (p.100, folio 70): `>> FLAG-02 { ALL | { |EC-PROGRAM-EXCEPTIONS | I-O-STATUS-07 | MOVE-TO-SAME-NAME | RANGE-EXCEPTION-FOR-INDEX | TERMINATE-WITH-VARYING| } } { ON | OFF }` with FLAG-02, the five option words and OFF underlined and ALL and ON NOT. cite.py --check 5.2.3 'They are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats' OK; 5.2.6.3 'If one of the alternatives contains only optional words, that alternative is the default and is selected unless another alternative is explicitly specified' OK; 5.2.6.4 'any single alternative shall be specified only once' OK. FlagDirectiveLine.TryParse now takes the ON/OFF braces as optional (default ON) and the outer braces as ALL by default, so `>>FLAG-02`, `>>FLAG-02 ON` and `>>FLAG-02 OFF` are accepted (ALL ON / ALL ON / ALL OFF), and a repeated option word or repeated ALL, ALL combined with options, or an ON/OFF that is not the last word is COBOLNET1622. Before: the three forms were rejected and a repeated word silently merged. The same parse serves FLAG-14 (FMT-7.3.15.2). [editions: introduced 2014 (7.3.14.1), obsolete element at 2023 (7.3.14.1 NOTE) so it warns COBOLNET0903 and still works; refused below 2014 with COBOLNET0900]

subject: FLAG-14 directive
notes: kb/Work PB1374 (w1020f). Printed format rendered from the canonical PDF (p.102, folio 72): `>> FLAG-14 { ALL | { |twelve options| } } { ON | OFF }` with FLAG-14, every option word and OFF underlined and ALL and ON NOT (the spec figure note agrees; its closing sentence calling the ON/OFF braces 'required' contradicted its own first paragraph and is corrected in specs/ISO_COBOL.md). cite.py --check 5.2.3, 5.2.6.3, 5.2.6.4 and 7.3.15.4 'If ON is explicitly or implicitly specified for an option' OK. TryParse now accepts `>>FLAG-14 VALUE-ZERO`, `>>FLAG-14 ALL`, `>>FLAG-14 ON`, `>>FLAG-14 OFF` and a bare `>>FLAG-14` (ALL and ON are the defaults, 5.2.6.3), and refuses `>>FLAG-14 VALUE-ZERO VALUE-ZERO ON` (5.2.6.4) with COBOLNET1622. Before: the first five drew COBOLNET1622 and the repeat compiled clean. [editions: a 2023 introduction (7.3.15.1); COBOLNET0900 below 2023]

subject: IF directive
notes: kb/Work PB1363 + PB806. cite.py --check 7.3.16.2 'constant-conditional-expression-1 [ text-1 ]' OK (general format). Every part of the general format is now enforced: the constant-conditional-expression is required and fragment-parsed in every branch (COBOLNET1619; omitted branches by CheckCceSyntax), >>ELSE only after an open >>IF and at most once, >>END-IF required and closing the >>IF of its own text (COBOLNET2649), and neither >>ELSE nor >>END-IF takes an operand (COBOLNET1911, 7.3.3 SR3/SR4). The former retired witness (the frame stack with no phase) is gone.

subject: LEAP-SECOND directive
notes: { ON | OFF } with ON un-underlined in the printed format, so per 5.2.3 a bare >>LEAP-SECOND selects ON - the 'specified or implied' case 7.3.17.4 GR2/GR4 presuppose. Any other operand is COBOLNET1911. The 7.3.17.3 SR1 PLACEMENT rule is a different row and stays with the stage as COBOLNET1650.

subject: LISTING directive
notes: { ON | OFF } with ON un-underlined (rendered from the printed page, folio 78), so a bare >>LISTING selects it - which is what 7.3.18.3 GR4/GR5 call 'specifying or implying the ON phrase'. Any other operand is COBOLNET1911. The directive itself is a no-op under 7.3.18.3 GR1: this compiler produces no source listing.

subject: PAGE directive
notes: >> PAGE [ comment-text-1 ] - the operand is bracketed, so it is optional, and 7.3.19.3 SR2 states that comment-text-1 'is not checked syntactically'. The row's directiveOperand records that as form 'text' with the citation, so the absence of a content check is the standard's decision on the record rather than a gap. The directive is a no-op under 7.3.19.4 GR3 with no listing produced.

subject: POP directive
notes: { directive-name | ALL }, plain braces - exactly one shall be written. The admissible directive-names are DERIVED from the catalog itself minus 7.3.20.3 SR1's exclusions (EVALUATE, IF, PAGE, POP, PUSH), by ROW: >>POP WHEN is refused because WHEN is a word of the excluded EVALUATE directive. Anything else is COBOLNET1911.

subject: PROPAGATE directive
notes: { ON | OFF } with ON un-underlined, so a bare >>PROPAGATE selects ON; 7.3.21.4 GR4's OFF default is about omitting the DIRECTIVE, not about which alternative the format implies. Any other operand is COBOLNET1911 (kb/Work PB794 retired this directive's own COBOLNET0883). The runtime propagation SEMANTICS are separate rows and remain PHASE-13 residue; this row is the format.

subject: PUSH directive
notes: { directive-name | ALL }, plain braces - exactly one shall be written, with the admissible directive-names derived from the catalog minus 7.3.22.3 SR1's exclusions, by row. Anything else is COBOLNET1911.

subject: REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH directive
notes: { ON | OFF } with ON un-underlined, so a bare >>REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH selects ON. Any other operand is COBOLNET1911 (kb/Work PB794 retired this directive's own COBOLNET1576).

subject: SOURCE FORMAT directive
notes: >> SOURCE FORMAT IS { FIXED | FREE }, verified against the PRINTED page (folio 84): SOURCE, FIXED and FREE are underlined required words, FORMAT and IS are 5.2.3 optional words, and the braces are a plain required choice. The optional words are the row's optionalWords, so >>SOURCE FREE and >>SOURCE FORMAT IS FREE both select FREE; an operand that is neither, or none at all, is COBOLNET1911 and the line is still consumed (the reference format in effect carries on, since the directive selected none). kb/Work PB794. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Preprocessor/ReferenceFormatProcessor.cs#TryMatchDirective (kb/Work PB1361 (w70b) replaced the format-blind TryMatchDirective pre-scan with the in-order FormatSegments walk, which recognizes the directive by its word through CompilerDirectiveLine in the program-text area of the format in effect)

subject: TURN directive
notes: kb/Work PB1365 (wave 1019 B re-probe on a fresh build). The printed diagram (PDF p115) underlines TURN, CHECKING, OFF and LOCATION only, so ON and WITH are optional words (cite.py --check 7.3.25.4 'If the ON phrase is specified or implied' OK 6)). ParseTurn reads { exception-name [file-name]... }... CHECKING [ON] [[WITH] LOCATION] | OFF and ends the operand there: CHECKING / CHECKING WITH LOCATION / CHECKING LOCATION / CHECKING ON LOCATION all select ON (checking takes effect: pb1365_turn_checking_implied_on); CHECKING OFF WITH LOCATION, CHECKING ON JUNK, CHECKING JUNK, CHECKING WITH and a directive with no CHECKING are COBOLNET0718; EC-I-O ON / LOCATION as file-name-1 is COBOLNET0718 (SR-7.3.25.3-1); the exception-name/file-name ellipses accept several of each. All re-run: turn_ok / turn_impl / turn_impl_loc / turn_on_loc_nowith / turn_comment run, the rest are rejected.

subject: Alphanumeric literals
notes: Format 1 quote/apostrophe with character-1 optional (STR_BODY `(...)*`), Format 2 X"..."/X'...' with the hex sequence optional (HEXDIGITS `*`, caseInsensitive so x"4a" also lexes; 3.98 makes A-F equivalent to a-f). cite.py --check 8.3.3.2.2 "hexadecimal-alphanumeric" OK. Probe p1 (probe dir E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec/scratchpad/adj-d2/out/probe/anlit): 'it''s', "a""b", X'4142', x"4a4b", X"" all lex and decode ([it's][a"b][AB][JK][    ]). r03 golden rows 13/15/17/18 pin X"", X"4142", X'', X'4142' (both delimiters of Format 2, zero length); Format 1 apostrophe/quote parity is also pinned by conformance-test:ApostropheValueDifferentialTests.EmbeddedDelimiter_DecodesToOneCharacter_PerForm. The X"GG" (non-hex body) lexing hole is SR5's defect, recorded there. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2014, 2023 (Annex E itemizes the 2014->2023 delta and lists no change to 8.3.3.2, so the rule stands in both; the 1985/2002 edge is NOT derivable in-repo -- no 2002 or 1985 text is held)

subject: Boolean literals
notes: Format 1 B"[0|1]..."/B'...' and Format 2 BX"[hex]..."/BX'...' with the character sequence OPTIONAL under both delimiters. BOOL_BODY = 'B' '"' [01]* '"' | 'B' apostrophe [01]* apostrophe | 'BX' '"' HEXDIGITS '"' | 'BX' apostrophe HEXDIGITS apostrophe, HEXDIGITS=[0-9a-f]* (caseInsensitive lexer). Probes out/probe/boolean-literals/bl1 (B"0101", B'10', BX"...", BX'f0', VALUE BX'0f') and bl12 (B"", B'', BX'', BX"") all accepted with correct values. cite.py --check 8.3.3.4.2 "hexadecimal-boolean" OK. No spec-derived test exercises the apostrophe spelling of either format (r03 covers BX"..." only) -> test-ref empty. Doc drift (not a verdict issue): CobolLexer.g4 comments above BOOLLIT and near line 979 still say 'BX"..." (hex boolean) is deferred', and the HEXDIGITS comment says Format 1 is '[01]+' while the rule is [01]*. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (boolean literals are a COBOL-2002 introduction, gated COBOLNET0900 at --std 85 - probe bl7; the zero-length-literal introduction edge is not derivable from the in-repo 2023 text, whose Annex E lists only the 2014->2023 delta) retired-witness: conformance:2002/l1c02_boolean_literal_forms (the golden moved to the 2014 corpus: it writes a zero-length literal, a COBOL-2014 introduction gated by kb/Work PB895 (same program, same expected output))

subject: National literals
notes: Format 1 N"[character-1]..." / N'...' and Format 2 NX"[hex-character-sequence-1]..." / NX'...' are all one NATLIT token (NAT_BODY: 'N' STR_BODY | 'NX' '"' HEXDIGITS '"' | 'NX' '\'' HEXDIGITS '\''), HEXDIGITS is `*` so both formats admit zero length as the brackets require; lexer is caseInsensitive so n".." also lexes (prefix is not literal content, §8.1.3 case-equivalence). Probe p1: N"A""B", N'A''B', N"", n"xy", NX"00410042" in VALUE all compile and run correctly. The r03 golden pins NX both delimiters, zero-length NX"" and the F1 control N"CD". Content that is NOT hexadecimal inside NX".." is SR4's defect (silent split), not this format row. cite.py --check 8.3.3.1 "Hexadecimal digits are used to specify the value of the literal" -> OK. [editions as adjudicated: COBOL-2002, COBOL-2014, COBOL-2023 (national literals are a COBOL-2002 introduction; absent from COBOL-85, where the construct is rejected COBOLNET0900 via Constructs.NationalData2002)]

subject: Figurative constant values
notes: Formats 1-6 (ZERO/SPACE/HIGH-VALUE/LOW-VALUE/QUOTE with the optional ALL, ALL literal-1) are the figurativeConstant rule; Format 7 (symbolic-character-1) binds through the SPECIAL-NAMES SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS path. kb/Work PB71 made Format 6 total over the literal kinds.

subject: Qualification
notes: kb/Work PB1455 (landed w1014 group S). The misordered spelling (a subscript or reference modifier BEFORE a qualifier, `E (1) OF T`, `S (2:2) OF G`, and the same inside a SUBSCRIPT-mode capture, `X (E (1) OF T)`) is refused COBOLNET2776 at every edition by ExpressionFormationPass, once per parse tree; the grammar keeps the superset parse so the refusal names the rule (8.4.2.3.2 Format 1 `qualified-data-name-1 [ ( subscript ... ) ]`, 8.4.3.1.2 Format 3 `identifier-1 reference-modifier-1`, both cite.py --check OK). Sibling fixed: the subscript splitter asked SR2's '(' question of the LAST qualifier, so `X (E OF T OF G (2))` was split into two subscripts and refused COBOLNET2270; CannotBeSubscripted now takes the whole qualified name. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Validation/ExpressionFormationPass.cs#VisitSubscriptOrRefMod (kb/Work PB2113: a subscript's own identifier is a nested dataReference, so the one VisitDataReference screens its qualifier order) kb/Work PB2040 (w1031 group G): the format's other half - a file-name has NO qualified format; it appears only as the file-report-qualifier - was unenforced at the procedure-division file-name positions that share the dataReference production (OPEN, the SORT and MERGE subjects, SORT/MERGE USING and GIVING, FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE / EXCEPTION-FILE-N): they resolved the GLUED text, so `OPEN OUTPUT A OF B` opened a file named AOFB and `SORT S OF X` dropped the qualifier, both silently. StatementValidation.ResolveFile now takes the parse node and ScreenFileNameOperand refuses a qualified, subscripted, reference-modified or special-register operand (COBOLNET2972) at every edition. cite.py --check 8.4.2.2.2 'file-report-qualifier' OK.

subject: Subscripts
notes: The subscript general format has exactly THREE alternatives and each now has a witness. ALL - pb62 (the three ranges GR1a defers to; vacuous at 85, which has no function for which the subscript ALL is allowed). index-name-1 [{+|-} integer-1] - 85/index_name_r7_windows and pb170. arithmetic-expression-1 - pb136 for compound expressions and pb877_subscripted_subscript for the shape that had no vehicle until kb/Work PB877: an identifier operand carrying its OWN subscripts. 8.8.1.1 admits 'an identifier referencing a numeric data item' and 8.4.3.1.2 Format 2 makes that identifier a qualified-data-name-WITH-SUBSCRIPTS, so X(1) is an arithmetic-expression-1 - but the declaration-informed '(' splitter asked DataItem.IsTable, which is only the first half of 8.4.2.3.3 SR2, so the identifier's own '(' opened a SECOND subscript and every such reference failed arity. It was loud on the receiving side (COBOLNET0899) and a run-time abort on the sending side. Format 1 (qualified-data-name-with-subscripts) and Format 2 (qualified-condition-name-with-subscripts) are both covered: the golden subscripts data-names, and ResolveForItem - the condition-name path, whose subscripts identify the occurrence of the CONDITIONAL VARIABLE - applies the same SR2/SR3 screen. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/ReferenceResolver.cs#SplitSubscriptTokens (kb/Work PB2113: the subscript list is the grammar's subscriptList, read by SegmentsOf) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/ReferenceResolver.cs#MaterializeViaFragment (replaced: kb/Work PB2151 reads the position's parse node into a typed Position (BindPosition, MaterializePosition); RenderSegment and the text re-parse are deleted) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/ReferenceResolver.cs#RenderSegment (replaced: kb/Work PB2151 reads the position's parse node into a typed Position (BindPosition, MaterializePosition); RenderSegment and the text re-parse are deleted)

subject: Identifier
notes: kb/Work PB1425 (w1021a). The eleven identifier formats (cite.py --check 8.4.3.1.3 -> OK 2)-12)). Formats 1-4 and 8-11 were verified by the registrar's probes; Format 5 (object-view) landed w1019a, Format 6's qualified SUPER w1014 and SELF / SUPER as identifiers w1020c, and Format 7's identifier-3 is now any identifier (the dataReference chain split by ResolveObjectProperty, plus the propertyObject suffix for SELF, SUPER, a view, a function, NULL). Every format is spelled and bound. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/ReferenceResolver.cs#OoTryBindPropertyReference (the one-word property binder ReferenceResolver.OoTryBindPropertyReference is deleted by kb/Work PB1425 (w1021a): a property reference is resolved by ReferenceResolver.ResolveObjectProperty, which splits the chain and resolves identifier-3 through the ordinary resolver)

subject: Function-identifier
notes: [FUNCTION] {function-pointer-name-1 | function-prototype-name-1 | intrinsic-function-name-1} [ ( [ {argument-1 | OMITTED} ] ... ) ] - rendered PDF p157: the arguments are bracketed INSIDE the parentheses, so the empty list is legal on both the keyword route (functionCall's functionArgList?) and the keyword-omitted route (subscriptOrRefMod : subToken*, kb/Work PB969). An empty group after a DATA reference is refused by name, COBOLNET2309 (ReferenceResolver.ScreenEmptyParentheses). retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4#subscriptOrRefMod (kb/Work PB2113: the keyword-omitted argument list is the parsed subscriptPart, whose items are functionArguments)

subject: Reference-modification
notes: kb/Work PB1458 (closed by PB1407 wave 1019 C, the same code site). The PARTIAL was X(:2): the REQUIRED leftmost-position omitted was refused only by the COBOLNET2362 internal-error net. It is now COBOLNET2876 naming the 8.4.3.3.2 format identifier-1( leftmost-position : [ length ] ), for X (:2), X (: 2) and X (:) on a sending, receiving, relation and ADDRESS OF operand. T(1)( :2) and FUNCTION F (:2) never reach the resolver: the default-mode refModPart grammar rule requires the leftmost expression, so they are parse errors (COBOL0001). retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/ReferenceResolver.cs#LeftmostPositionOmitted (kb/Work PB2113: every reference modifier is the parsed refModPart/refModSpec, read by the one ReadRefMod) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4#subscriptOrRefMod (kb/Work PB2113: every reference modifier is the parsed refModPart/refModSpec, read by the one ReadRefMod)

subject: Inline method invocation
notes: kb/Work PB1430 landed (wave 1032 F). Format rendered from the canonical PDF page 163 (printed folio 133): {object-class-name-1 | identifier-1} :: literal-1 [ ( {arithmetic-expression-1 | boolean-expression-1 | identifier-2 | literal-2 | OMITTED} ... ) ]. The bracket makes the parenthesised group optional, but the argument forms are a BRACE whose ellipsis repeats inside the one pair (cite.py --check 5.2.6.3 'one of the alternatives contained within the braces shall be explicitly specified' OK; 5.2.7 OK), so a written pair holds at least one argument. inlineInvocationSegment is now `COLONCOLON literal (LPAREN argumentList RPAREN)?`; `A1 :: "GETNAME" ( )` (which compiled and ran, W=ACCOUNT) is refused with COBOLNET2994 named by CobolErrorStrategy. The drift test pins the required list. The format's '::' punctuation carries the 8.7.4 separator-space rule (cite.py --check 8.7.4 'shall be immediately preceded and followed by a separator space' OK), now decided by SeparatorRule as COBOLNET2993 (with its 8.7.3 '&' twin); positive golden pb1430_operator_separator_spaces pins line-end separators and both argument separators.

subject: Object-view
notes: kb/Work PB1425 (w1019a). The general format, rendered from the canonical PDF (printed page 134): `identifier-1 AS { [FACTORY OF] object-class-name-1 [ONLY] | interface-name-1 | UNIVERSAL }`, one brace, AS/FACTORY/ONLY/UNIVERSAL underlined, OF not. Grammar `objectView : objectReferenceTerm objectViewPhrase+`, `objectViewPhrase : AS UNIVERSAL | AS (FACTORY OF?)? className ONLY?` (interface-name and class-name are one word; the binder refuses FACTORY/ONLY on an interface, COBOLNET2872). UNIVERSAL is a new token, 8.9-reserved 2002+ (cobol-words.json). The view is an object-reference ATOM, reached by every object-reference position (INVOKE receiver, inline receiver, SET Format 5 sender, RAISE). Was COBOLNET0901 on AS in every position. [editions: the OO facility, 2002+]

subject: EXCEPTION-OBJECT
notes: Format: the bare word <u>EXCEPTION-OBJECT</u> (cite.py --check 8.4.3.6.2 "EXCEPTION-OBJECT" OK). IsExceptionObjectRegister = edition>=2002 AND no dataReferenceSuffix AND spelling EXCEPTION-OBJECT, so only the bare form is the register; resolver returns ExceptionObjectPlace, rendered as CobolNet.Runtime.Exceptions.ExceptionState.ExceptionObject from every sending position (relation condition, SET source). At --std 85 the word stays a user word (conformance:85/pb922_exception_object_user_word_85). Probe out/probe/exception-object/p1.cob compiles and runs at 2002/2014/2023 with the bare word in IF relations, in a declarative and in a separately compiled program. The spec-derived golden pb922_exception_object_reference exercises the bare word in sending positions at the introducing edition. [code-location note: (ExceptionObjectPlace arm, ~l.460); code-location note: (ExceptionObjectPlace => RuntimeApi.ExceptionObjectRead)] || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (object-orientation facility introduced in ISO/IEC 1989:2002; at 85 the spelling is an ordinary user-defined word)

subject: NULL object reference
notes: kb/Work PB1137 (landed w61j). Format: the underlined word NULL (cite.py --check 8.4.3.7.2 OK), an identifier (8.4.3.1.3 SR7). It now parses in every INVOKE identifier-5 slot: keyword-less and BY CONTENT (the literal alternative's figurativeConstant) and BY VALUE (invokeArgument's BY VALUE brace gained `literal`, the printed literal-2 that also carries NULL; before it `USING BY VALUE NULL` was COBOL0001). Binding: BY CONTENT / keyword-less NULL into an object-reference formal crosses as the null reference (golden: NULL LO=NULL twice). A BY VALUE NULL reaches the BY VALUE formal refusal that kb/Work PB1051 owns (COBOLNET0899 / 0828 SR5b) rather than a parse error. The 1985 non-reserved spelling is unchanged (NULL_ is a reservedGatedWord).

subject: SELF and SUPER
notes: kb/Work PB1425 (w1020c). The general format `{ SELF | [ object-class-name-1 OF ] SUPER }` is ONE rule, `selfAndSuper`, and it is now an identifier of the expression tier (`primaryExpression`), besides the object-reference operand rule (INVOKE / inline receiver, SET Format 5, RAISE, the GOBACK / EXIT RAISING phrase). So every sending position spells it: relation and EVALUATE operands (`IF O = SELF`), INVOKE and inline-invocation arguments, SET senders, RAISING SELF - each was a parse error (COBOL0001 / COBOLNET0901 'SELF is a reserved word'). The binder's one door is OoBinder.OoBindOoIdentifier; SELF binds to an ACTIVE-CLASS temporary filled with the method's object (BoundSelfReference). The object of an object-property identifier (`BAL OF SELF`) is Format 7's identifier-3, owned by FMT-8.4.3.9.2. [editions: the OO facility, 2002+]

subject: Object property
notes: kb/Work PB1425 (w1021a). 8.4.3.9.2 prints `property-name-1 OF {object-class-name-1 | identifier-1}` and 8.4.3.1.3 SR1 makes identifier-1 any identifier (cite.py --check 8.4.3.1.3 -> OK 1)). The property binder no longer takes one bare word: ReferenceResolver.ResolveObjectProperty splits the written chain - the head word is property-name-1, identifier-1 is the rest less the reference modifiers (8.4.3.1.4 GR1 a) before d), g) last) - and resolves identifier-1 through the ordinary resolver, so a qualified and subscripted object reference (BAL OF A OF T(2), BAL OF AR(2), which used to name the compiler's temporary), a chained property (NM OF NXT OF D), and the forms a word cannot spell (the grammar's propertyObject suffix: SELF, SUPER, object-class-name-1 OF SUPER, an object-view BAL OF U AS C, a function-identifier BAL OF FUNCTION F (5)) are all the object. The class-name arm (factory accessors) is unchanged. [editions: the OO facility, 2002+] retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/ReferenceResolver.cs#OoTryBindPropertyReference (the one-word property binder ReferenceResolver.OoTryBindPropertyReference is deleted by kb/Work PB1425 (w1021a): a property reference is resolved by ReferenceResolver.ResolveObjectProperty, which splits the chain and resolves identifier-3 through the ordinary resolver)

subject: NULL address pointer and message tag content
notes: kb/Work PB1427 LANDED (wave 68 Y). The general format is the single word NULL; the grammar spells it by ONE rule, predefinedNull : NULL_ (carried by nonNumericLiteral, the SET senders setAddressSender / objectReference, callByReference and invokeArgument's BY REFERENCE arm), no longer an arm of figurativeConstant — the drift test fails if NULL_ is spelled in any other parser rule (the reservedGatedWord COBOL-85 user-word gate excepted).

subject: Data-address-identifier
notes: kb/Work PB1407. The one shape the format refused, a reference-modified identifier-1 (legal per 8.4.3.11.3 SR4 a)), is admitted through the ONE ref-mod admission (ReferenceResolver.ReadScreenedRefMod) and addresses its leftmost position (8.4.3.11.4 GR1 over 8.4.3.3.4 GR5), range-checked by the same CobolString test as a read. The OF-omitted, qualified, subscripted, relation-operand and CALL/INVOKE shapes were already witnessed.

subject: Function-address-identifier
notes: kb/Work PB1416 (landed w1014 group S). 8.4.3.12.2 `ADDRESS OF FUNCTION { function-prototype-name-1 | identifier-1 }` (OF not underlined); identifier-1 is any identifier format (8.4.3.1.3 SR1). The lexer no longer types the '(' after `ADDRESS [OF] FUNCTION word` as the 8.4.3.2.3 SR6 argument paren (a prototype name takes no argument list), so a subscripted (`WS-NAME(2)`, `WS-NAME (N)`, OF omitted) and a reference-modified identifier-1 parse and resolve to the function their content names (golden: SUBSCRIPT-OK, NO-OF-OK, REFMOD-OK).

subject: Program-address-identifier
notes: kb/Work PB1452 landed (wave 1009 B). Printed format `ADDRESS OF PROGRAM { identifier-1 | literal-1 | program-prototype-name-1 }`, ADDRESS/PROGRAM underlined, OF not. The grammar rule is `ADDRESS OF? PROGRAM (nonNumericLiteral | functionCall | inlineMethodInvocation | dataReference)`: identifier-1 is ANY identifier format (8.4.3.1.3 SR1, cite.py --check OK), so a function-identifier (8.4.3.1.2 Format 1) and an inline method invocation (Format 4) stand beside the data reference, ahead of it because an invocation's first element is itself a data reference. One dataReference still covers identifier-1 and program-prototype-name-1, split at bind (BindProgramAddressOperand). Reached as the SET Format 9 sender and, as identifier Format 9 via addressIdentifier, as a CALL argument and a relation operand: the golden drives a function-identifier operand through all three, plus group, national-group and reference-modified operands. --std 85 is gated by the program-pointer family (COBOLNET0900). The function twin (functionAddressIdentifier) takes the same operand set.

subject: LINAGE-COUNTER
notes: Format: LINAGE-COUNTER [ {IN|OF} file-name-1 ]. Grammar alternative `LINAGE_COUNTER ((OF | IN) cobolWord)?` is exactly the diagram (qualifier optional, exactly one of IN/OF). LinageFileOf treats the cobolWord as the file-name. Probes (probe/linage-counter/Q1, Q5, g4) at --std 85 and 2023: `LINAGE-COUNTER OF LPF`, `LINAGE-COUNTER IN LPG` and bare `LINAGE-COUNTER` all bind and read the right file's counter (Q1/Q5 print their OK line). The covering test writes both `OF LP1` and `IN LP2`. cite.py --check 8.4.3.14.3 "Qualification requirements for LINAGE-COUNTER are defined by 8.4.2.2, Qualification." -> OK. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85 2002 2014 2023

subject: Report counters
notes: kb/Work PB1456 landed. The format {PAGE-COUNTER | LINE-COUNTER} [{IN | OF} report-name-1] is accepted in every position the standard gives it, including report-name-1 naming a DIFFERENT report inside a report section SOURCE (PAGE-COUNTER OF R1, LINE-COUNTER OF R2) and inside its arithmetic expression.

subject: Condition-name
notes: Rule: §8.4.4.2 Format 1 'condition-name-1' (switch-status, bare word) and Format 2 'qualified-condition-name-with-subscripts-1' (cite.py --check 8.4.4.2 'Format 2 (qualified-condition-name-with-subscripts)' OK; the production is §8.4.2.3.2 'qualified-condition-name-1 [ ( subscript … ) ]', --find OK). Code: ConditionBinder.AnalyzeBareOperand tries level-88 resolution (Format 2, through ctx.Refs.ResolveForItem with qualifiers+subscripts) then SetAlterBinder.SwitchCondOf, which admits a switch-status condition-name ONLY when dataReferenceSuffix() is empty (Format 1 has no qualifier/subscript). Probes (pinned cobol.exe, out/probe/condition-name): p1.cob --std 2023 and --std 85 -> 'IF V-ONE OF T OF G (2)' TRUE, 'IF V-ONE (1)' FALSE, 'IF SW-ON' TRUE after SET SW1 TO ON, 'IF SW-OFF' FALSE, EVALUATE TRUE WHEN SW-OFF, and a contained program reading the container's SW-OFF (SPECIAL-NAMES inheritance, DataBinder.InheritConfiguration) all correct. n1 'IF SW-ON OF G' and n2 'IF SW-ON (1)' rejected (COBOLNET1639); n3 'IF SW1' (the mnemonic) rejected COBOLNET2318. Cosmetic only: the 1639 wording says 'no declaration gives the name SW-ON' although SW-ON IS declared as a switch-status condition-name — correct rejection, imprecise message (no harm). Coverage: Format 1 by conformance:85/pb390_procedure_and_condition_operands (SW-ON true after SET SW-M TO ON) and 85/nested_special_names_inheritance; Format 2 by conformance:85/pb567_condition_name_qualification and conformance:85/pb1030_reference_answers (IF C-THREE (I)). No negative golden pins the qualified/subscripted switch-status rejection. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (both kinds of condition-name present in every edition; §8.4.4.1)

subject: Relational operators

notes: Both printed formats reduce to `operand IS? NOT? (POSITIVE|NEGATIVE|ZERO)`: comparisonExpression alt 3 (written form) and partialComparison alt 2 (EVALUATE SR5 elided operand). subject: Simple omitted argument condition
notes: Rule: §8.8.4.8.2 general format 'data-name-1 IS [ NOT ] OMITTED' with NOT and OMITTED underlined and IS not underlined (cite.py --check 8.8.4.8.2 "data-name-1 IS" -> OK; the Markdown form carries the <u> marks), so IS is optional, NOT is an optional bracketed word, OMITTED required. Grammar comparisonExpression alt 1 'comparisonOperand IS? NOT? OMITTED' spells exactly that (superset operand; ConditionBinder.BindComparison then requires the operand text to name a formal of the current element, method formals inside a method, else LinkageFormals, COBOLNET1686 per SR1 -- cite.py --check 8.8.4.8.3 'Data-name-1 shall be a formal parameter defined in the source element in which this condition is specified' OK -- so a subscripted/expression/non-formal operand is refused). NOT yields BoundOmittedCondition(formal, not) -- one condition per GR2 (cite.py --check 8.8.4.8.4 'When used, NOT and the keyword OMITTED specify one condition' OK). Edition gate: VersionConformancePass.VisitComparisonExpression Check(OmittedArguments2002). PROBE (pinned cobol.exe, out/probe/simple-omitted/p1.cob): 'l-a OMITTED' (no IS, lower case), 'L-B NOT OMITTED' (no IS), 'L-C IS NOT OMITTED AND L-A IS OMITTED', 'NOT L-C IS OMITTED' against CALL USING W-A OMITTED (+trailing) and USING OMITTED W-A W-A -> A-PRESENT/B-OM then A-OM/B-PRESENT/C-PRES-A-OM/C-PRESENT2, exactly the GR1a/GR1b truth values, at --std 2023 and 2002; --std 85 -> COBOLNET0900 on every condition; p2.cob: working-storage item and a linkage item not in USING -> COBOLNET1686. Covering golden pb133_omitted_args spells IS OMITTED and IS NOT OMITTED (IS-less spellings verified by probe only). [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the omitted-argument condition is a COBOL-2002 introduction; absent from 1985)]

subject: Complex negated conditions
notes: Rule: §8.8.4.10.2 general format `NOT condition-1`; §8.8.4.10.1 'A condition is negated by use of the logical operator 'NOT', which reverses the truth value of the condition to which it is applied. Including a negated condition in parentheses does not change its truth value.' (cite.py --check 8.8.4.10.1 OK). Code: grammar unaryLogicalExpression : NOT primaryCondition | primaryCondition, where primaryCondition includes LPAREN condition RPAREN, so NOT applies to a simple condition or a parenthesized complex condition; NOT sits below AND/XOR/OR tiers, giving §8.8.4.11.3 precedence NOT>AND>XOR>OR. Binder wraps BoundNot; ConditionRenderer emits !(operand). Table 5 / §8.8.4.11.3 NOTE 'the pair 'NOT (' is permissible while the pair 'NOT NOT' is not permissible' (cite.py --check 8.8.4.11.3 OK) is realized structurally (NOT primaryCondition cannot recurse) — probe `IF NOT NOT A = 1` -> COBOL0001 unexpected 'NOT'. Abbreviation interplay §8.8.4.12.4 GR1 'NOT a = b OR c' => '(NOT (a = b)) OR (a = c)' (cite.py --find -> §8.8.4.12.4 1)). Probe (pinned cobol.exe, probe/complex-negated-conditions/negc.cob, --std 2023; negc85.cob at 85/2002/2014) A=1,B=2,C=3,X='Z',88 F-ON false: NOT A=B ->T1; NOT(A=B OR B=C)->T2; NOT(A=1 OR B=C)->F3; NOT cond-name->T4; NOT (X NUMERIC)->T5; NOT A POSITIVE->F6; A=9 OR NOT B=2 AND C=3 ->F7 (precedence); NOT (NOT A=1)->T8; NOT A=2 OR 1 ->T9; NOT A=1 OR 2 ->F10 (NOT scopes only the first relation per §8.8.4.12.4); NOT(A=1 AND B=2) AND C=3 ->F11; A=1 XOR NOT B=2 ->T12 (2023; XOR correctly 0900 below 2023); PERFORM UNTIL NOT A<3 -> A=3; NOT (((A=3)))->F13. All outputs equal the spec-derived expectations at every edition. Covering spec-derived golden: 2023/l1_perform_until_condition_forms (`PERFORM UNTIL NOT (CX IS NUMERIC)`, expected count derived from §8.8.4.4); sibling 2023/l1_search_when_condition_forms (`WHEN NOT (WS-K(IX) < 7)`). No clause-citing source (dossier) — code implements the rule without citing §8.8.4.10; not a defect. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the clause carries no edition qualification; negated conditions are base COBOL; the XOR operand context is 2023-only per §8.8.4.9)

subject: Complex Combined conditions
notes: cite.py --check 8.8.4.11.2 "AND, OR, EXCLUSIVE-OR, and XOR are underlined in the printed standard (required words). Both" OK. kb/Work PB1162 re-verdicted (wave 73 group A): the finding was a '(' after XOR / EXCLUSIVE-OR lexed in SUBSCRIPT mode at 2023; PB1465's reservation-aware trigger fixed it (both words are reserved at 2023). subject: Abbreviated combined relation conditions
notes: kb/Work PB1390 landed (wave 68 s). Printed format (PDF p233): relation-condition-1 { {AND|OR|EXCLUSIVE-OR|XOR} {NOT|simple-relational-operator|extended-relational-operator} object-1 } ... — ONE group, any connective in any position (cite.py --check 8.8.4.12.2 "relation-condition-1" OK; --check 8.8.4.12.1 "any relation condition except the first may be abbreviated by" OK). The grammar now spells the tail ONCE: the leading tiers hold the first simple condition and every connective's operand (OR, XOR, AND alike) is a succeeding tier whose leftmost element is succeedingCondition = abbreviatedRelation | unaryLogicalExpression; the EVALUATE partial spine uses the same succeeding tails. Probed on the w68s build: A = B OR < C AND D -> F, OR < C AND NOT D -> T, A = B XOR < C -> T, XOR NOT < C -> F, OR < C XOR = D -> F, OR < D AND C = 1 -> F, A = 1 XOR = 2 -> T (all were COBOL0001/0901). Goldens run each shape over all 81 tuples of A..D in 1..3 against the GR1 expansion: 0 disagreements. The connective '(' after XOR / EXCLUSIVE-OR (e.g. A = B XOR (C + 1)) is still mis-lexed as a subscript opener — the lexer's edition-blind subscript trigger, kb/Work PB1162, which owns FMT-8.8.4.11.2 (the connective row); it fails before any rule of this clause is reached. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4#abbreviatedAndChain (kb/Work PB1390 deleted the OR-only abbreviatedAndChain rule; its job is the succeeding tiers, now witnessed on this row)

subject: COBOL compilation group
notes: kb/Work PB1507 (wave 1012 J). The printed 10.6.1 page was rendered by the adjudicator (cite.py --check 10.6.1 'procedure-division [ program-definition ]' OK). The source-unit SHAPE is now screened for every unit kind from ONE table (SourceUnitShape, COBOLNET2274 - the prototype-only screen it generalizes is deleted): a unit is contained only if it is a program definition, only a program definition prints the contained slot, the slot sits inside the procedure-division bracket, END PROGRAM closes the program kinds and END FUNCTION the function kinds, and the end marker is required wherever the format prints it unbracketed (every kind but the program definition). notes: kb/Work PB829. X.` as a unit's first line, and a header-less NESTED program, compile at 2002+ (the 2002 golden); X3.23-1985 required the header, so below 2002 it is the named relaxation gate identification-header-optional-2002 (COBOLNET0900, the 85 negative). notes: kb/Work/PB759.md landed w46i3. Every phrase of the printed format parses: AS literal-1 (PB303), IS FINAL, INHERITS [FROM] {name}... (PB695; repetition semantics are the documented 0849), and now USING {parameter-name-1}... (PB759).

subject: FACTORY paragraph
notes: Rule: `FACTORY. [ IMPLEMENTS { interface-name-1 } ... . ]` (cite.py --check 11.4.2 "FACTORY" -> OK §11.4.2 General format). Grammar: factoryParagraph = (IDENTIFICATION DIVISION DOT)? FACTORY DOT implementsClause? ...; implementsClause = IMPLEMENTS interfaceName+ DOT - FACTORY required, IMPLEMENTS optional, repetition via +, trailing separator period required. IMPLEMENTS FPJ.` compiles+runs (J-F 0042); p7 drops the trailing period -> COBOL0307 (correctly rejected); p5 bare `FACTORY.` runs at --std 2002/2014/2023 (CHILD-F 0042); at --std 85 the OO source is rejected COBOLNET0900 (FACTORY is a user word at 85, pinned by the OoSpineTests FACTORY-at-85 test). notes: §11.5.2 prints Format 1 `FUNCTION-ID. user-function-name-1 [ AS literal-1 ] .` and Format 2 `FUNCTION-ID. function-prototype-name-1 [ AS literal-1 ] IS PROTOTYPE.` (IS not underlined => optional; FUNCTION-ID, AS, PROTOTYPE underlined; both periods required). cite.py --check 11.5.2 "Format 1 (definition)" OK; --check 11.5.2 "Format 2 (prototype)" OK. PROTOTYPE`, externalizedNamePhrase = `AS literal` (narrowed by ExternalizedName.Screen, the §11.5.3 SR1 row owned by landed PB303). Probes with the pinned cobol.exe (out/probe/fid): p1 Format 2 with AS + IS (`FUNCTION-ID. FIDPA AS "FIDREAL" IS PROTOTYPE.`) compiles+runs at 2002 and 2023 (P=000049); p2 Format 2 with IS omitted (`FUNCTION-ID. FIDPB PROTOTYPE.`) compiles+runs at 2002/2023; p4 missing period after FUNCTION-ID rejected (COBOL0307); p5 reversed order `IS PROTOTYPE AS "X"` rejected (COBOLNET0901 on AS — rejection correct, message names reservation rather than position); --std 85 rejects the prototype tail, the AS phrase and function reference with COBOLNET0900 (edition gate). Not in COBOL-85.

OBJECT DOT implementsClause? ...`, implementsClause `IMPLEMENTS interfaceName+ DOT` - one-or-more repetition and the clause's own trailing period, exactly as printed. IMPLEMENTS IA` / `IC.` spanning two lines compiles and runs (CB8-PA, CB8-PC); p2 missing trailing period -> COBOL0307; p11 `IMPLEMENTS .` (empty list) -> COBOL0001; --std 85 -> COBOLNET0900 (OO gated), 2002/2014 run. subject: OPTIONS paragraph
notes: kb/Work PB1508 (landed w1032d). Rule (PDF p302 / folio 272, rendered and inspected): 'OPTIONS. [ arithmetic-clause ] [ default-rounded-clause ] [ entry-convention-clause ] [ float-binary-clause ] [ float-decimal-clause ] [ initialize-clause ] [ intermediate-rounding-clause ] [.]' - seven SEPARATE brackets in a fixed sequence, no choice indicators, no ellipsis, and an independent [.]. cite.py --check 11.9.2 "[ intermediate-rounding-clause ]" -> OK; --check 5.2.1 "shall be written in the compilation group in the sequence given in the general format, unless otherwise specified by the rules of that format" -> OK (11.9.3 has one rule, the period, and frees no order); --check 5.2.6.2 "may be explicitly specified or that portion of the general format may be omitted" -> OK; --check 5.2.7 "applies to the portion of the format between the determined pair of delimiters" -> OK. CODE: the grammar keeps the order-free `optionsClause+` superset (each clause opens on a distinct keyword) and ClauseCardinalities.ByClauseContext[OptionsClauseContext] narrows it - Repeatable empty, Sequence = the seven clause contexts in printed order - read by ClosedFormatPass.ScreenClauseRepetition: an element written after one the figure prints later is COBOLNET2987 (format-element-out-of-order, at the misplaced clause), a repeat is COBOLNET2423 (at the second occurrence). The independent [.] is `optionsParagraph : OPTIONS DOT (optionsClause+ DOT | DOT)?` - the bracket plus SR-11.9.3-1 - so `OPTIONS. .` and `OPTIONS.` + a lone `.` line compile (2002 golden). MEASURED (w1032d build): reorder.cob -> COBOLNET2987 at 2014/2023 (was clean, printed 1); dup.cob -> COBOLNET2423 (was clean, last clause won, printed 2); twodots.cob / twolines.cob -> compile and run (were COBOL0001); all seven clauses in printed order compile and run B=1 W=[ZZZZ] (2023 golden). The edition gate is unchanged: 85 refuses the paragraph (COBOLNET0804), 2002 refuses the 2014 clauses (COBOLNET0900). || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (not 85): the OPTIONS paragraph is a 2002 element (its ARITHMETIC clause's Standard Arithmetic was obsolete in 2014 and removed per Annex E.2 item 21); the seven-clause list is the 2023 format - initialize-clause is new in 2023 (Annex E.3 item 33), the other five non-ARITHMETIC clauses 2014

subject: ARITHMETIC clause
notes: Rule: `ARITHMETIC IS {NATIVE | STANDARD-BINARY | STANDARD-DECIMAL}`, ARITHMETIC and the three phrases underlined, IS not underlined, plain braces = exactly one (cite.py --check 11.9.5.1 "STANDARD-DECIMAL" -> OK §11.9.5.1 General format; cite.py --check E.2 "Standard Arithmetic" -> OK §E.2 21)). Code: arithmeticClause = ARITHMETIC IS? arithmeticMethod; arithmeticMethod = NATIVE | STANDARD_BINARY | STANDARD_DECIMAL | STANDARD. Probed with the pinned cobol.exe (probe/arithmetic-clause/p_*.cob) at --std 85/2002/2014/2023: every alternative with and without IS compiles at 2014/2023 and selects the right engine (FUNCTION SQRT(2) into PIC 9V9(30): NATIVE/absent -> binary64 1.414213562373095145474621858738, STANDARD-DECIMAL -> 34-digit 1.414213562373095048801688724209); `ARITHMETIC IS NATIVE STANDARD-DECIMAL` -> COBOL0307 (exactly one); `ARITHMETIC IS.` -> COBOL0001 (one required); STANDARD-DECIMAL at 2002 -> COBOLNET0900; OPTIONS at 85 -> COBOLNET0804; the 2002 STANDARD phrase compiles at 2002, warns obsolete (0903) at 2014, is rejected at 2023 (0807, Annex E.2 item 21 removal) - edition-correct dual window. STANDARD-BINARY is refused by COBOLNET0806 at every edition: a documented processor-dependent decline (A.3 item 2, cite --check A.3 OK; docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 2, kb/Work PB198), not a syntax defect; at 2023 it additionally draws the NOTE 2 obsolete warning 0903 (cite --check 11.9.5.2 "The STANDARD-BINARY mode of arithmetic is an obsolete feature" OK). Grammar comment calls bare STANDARD 'a common vendor spelling' - it is in fact the ISO 2002 phrase; the gating is right, the comment is stale. No single existing test exercises the IS-omitted spelling plus each alternative, so test-ref is empty (candidates: conformance:2023/l1_native_arithmetic_intermediate writes ARITHMETIC IS NATIVE; conformance:2014/arithmetic_standard_decimal writes ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL). || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002 (clause introduced with the OPTIONS paragraph; NATIVE | STANDARD); 2014 (STANDARD-BINARY, STANDARD-DECIMAL added; STANDARD obsolete); 2023 (NATIVE | STANDARD-BINARY | STANDARD-DECIMAL; Standard Arithmetic removed - Annex E.2 item 21); not in 1985

subject: DEFAULT ROUNDED clause
notes: Format: DEFAULT ROUNDED MODE IS {8 modes}; DEFAULT, ROUNDED and the mode words underlined, MODE and IS not (optional words). cite.py --check 11.9.6.2 "DEFAULT" -> OK (diagram line '<u>DEFAULT</u> <u>ROUNDED</u> MODE IS'). Grammar `DEFAULT ROUNDED MODE? IS? roundingModeName` with the shared 8-mode roundingModeName matches exactly. Probed with pinned cobol.exe: 'DEFAULT ROUNDED NEAREST-EVEN' (both optional words omitted), 'DEFAULT ROUNDED IS PROHIBITED', 'DEFAULT ROUNDED MODE TOWARD-LESSER', 'DEFAULT ROUNDED TOWARD-GREATER' all accepted and applied; 'DEFAULT ROUNDED MODE IS .' (no mode) -> COBOL0001; 'DEFAULT MODE IS NEAREST-EVEN' (ROUNDED missing) -> COBOL0001; two modes -> COBOL0307. Edition gate: --std 2002 -> COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014'; 2014/2023 accepted (negative golden options-default-rounded-at-2002 also covers the gate). Clause uniqueness/order inside OPTIONS is §11.9.2's concern, not this row. Covering golden exercises the full MODE IS spelling; the optional-word omissions are verified by probe only (untested). || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2014, 2023 (clause of the 2002 OPTIONS paragraph; 2023 Annex E lists no change to it, D.17.2/D.17.3 describe it as the enhancement over earlier standards; absent from 1985/2002)

subject: ENTRY-CONVENTION clause
notes: Rule: ENTRY-CONVENTION IS { COBOL | entry-convention-name-1 } (cite.py --check 11.9.7.2 "ENTRY-CONVENTION" -> OK General format); ENTRY-CONVENTION and COBOL required, IS optional. Probes (pinned cobol.exe, out/probe/ec/): p1 `entry-convention cobol.` (no IS, lower case) compiles and runs 'P1 OK'; n3 `ENTRY-CONVENTION IS.` -> COBOL0001 unexpected '.' (operand required); the entry-convention-name-1 arm parses and is then refused by GR3 semantics (COBOLNET2385, conformance:negative/pb232-entry-convention-name) -- the documented A.1 item 64 'Not provided' choice (CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-64), legal since GR3 leaves the meaning implementor-defined. At --std 2002/85 COBOLNET0900 (edition gate, see editions). Side observation outside this clause: optionsParagraph is `optionsClause+`, so two ENTRY-CONVENTION IS COBOL clauses (probe n2) compile silently; §11.9.2 lists each clause once -- a §11.9.2 question, recorded as a dossier gap, not charged here. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2014, 2023 (the 2023 Annex E lists no introduction or change of the clause, so it predates 2023; whether ISO 1989:2002 carried it is not derivable from specs/ISO_COBOL.md -- the code gates it 2014 as a recorded conservative choice, constructs.json options-entry-convention-2014)

subject: INITIALIZE clause
notes: kb/Work PB1508 (landed w1032d). Format: INITIALIZE {ALL | {|LOCAL-STORAGE|SCREEN|WORKING-STORAGE|}} [SECTION] [TO] {BINARY ZEROES | HIGH-VALUES | literal-1 | LOW-VALUES | SPACES}; SECTION and TO not underlined. Verified (probes under out/probe/initialize-clause): ALL SECTION TO HIGH-VALUES -> both sections 0xFF; ALL BINARY ZEROES (SECTION and TO omitted) -> NULs; WORKING-STORAGE LOCAL-STORAGE SECTION X"5A" (reverse order, TO omitted) -> both ZZZZ; singular SPACE refused COBOLNET1727 naming the keyword spelling; ALL mixed with a section name refused (outer braces are exclusive); empty target refused; --std 85/2002/2014 refused COBOLNET0900 (E.3.3 item 33). SCREEN leg refused by name via ScreenFacility (declined A.4.2 module, PB260 owns). THE ONCE-ONLY HALF of the choice-indicator group (was the defect): cite.py --check 11.9.10.2 "The storage-section group is enclosed in CHOICE INDICATORS" -> OK; --check 5.2.6.4 "any single alternative shall be specified only once" -> OK. The grammar's optionsInitializeSection+ is the any-order half; OptionsBinder.SectionsOf groups the written targets by alternative and reads each through ChoiceIndicators.AtMostOnce (COBOLNET2104, at the repeat), binding the first - it used to fold them with a bitwise OR, so `INITIALIZE WORKING-STORAGE WORKING-STORAGE TO X"5A".` compiled clean and ran W=[ZZZZ]. subject: INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING clause
notes: Rule: INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING IS {NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO|NEAREST-EVEN|PROHIBITED|TRUNCATION}, IS optional (not underlined), exactly one of four (cite.py --check 11.9.11.1 "INTERMEDIATE" -> OK, the general-format line). IS AWAY-FROM-ZERO` (ROUNDED-phrase-only modes) are rejected COBOL0001; at --std 2002 the clause draws COBOLNET0900 'OPTIONS INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING requires COBOL-2014', at --std 2014 it compiles. notes: kb/Work PB78 / PB64 T5 (2026-08-19) + PB830 (2026-09-22). RENDERED (PDF p315 / folio 285): OBJECT-COMPUTER. subject: Input-output section
notes: Format: 'INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION. [ file-control-paragraph ] [ i-o-control-paragraph ]' (cite.py --check 12.4.2 "INPUT-OUTPUT" -> OK §12.4.2 General format). Grammar `inputOutputSection : INPUT_OUTPUT SECTION DOT fileControlParagraph? ioControlParagraph?` is the format verbatim: both words required, period required, both paragraphs optional, FILE-CONTROL before I-O-CONTROL. environmentDivision places it after configurationSection? (the §12.2 order). Bound by DataBinder.BindFileControl (env.inputOutputSection()?.fileControlParagraph()) and BindIoControl. Probes (pinned cobol.exe, E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec/scratchpad/adj-d1/out/probe/iosec): p1 both paragraphs -> runs 'OK' at 2023; p2 empty INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION. -> runs 'EMPTY' at 2023 and at --std 85; p3 I-O-CONTROL before FILE-CONTROL -> COBOL0001 unexpected 'FILE-CONTROL', exit 65 (correct: the format orders them). Edition note: the 2023 spec carries no edition difference for this format, so the uniform acceptance is what the spec derives; whether COBOL-85 required FILE-CONTROL inside the section is not stated in ISO_COBOL.md and is not a basis for a verdict here. test-ref left empty: goldens exercise the both-paragraph shape (e.g. conformance:2023/l1_release_same_record_area) but none pins the optional-paragraph arms (empty section / I-O-CONTROL only) or the ordering refusal. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (no Annex E row names the input-output section; the 2023 format is the only one the spec states)]

subject: FILE-CONTROL paragraph

The contents of each file-control-entry belong to §12.4.5 rows, not this one. No spec-derived golden targets the empty-paragraph form or the missing-period rejection, so test-ref is empty (test-needed). [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (no Annex E change entry for the FILE-CONTROL paragraph format)]

subject: File control entry
notes: kb/Work PB829. Grammar: BLOCK CONTAINS? integerLiteral (TO integerLiteral)? (CHARACTERS | RECORDS)? - exact. Placement: fileDescriptionClause alternative (FD only; SD excluded per sortMergeDescriptionEntry). Probed pinned cobol.exe at --std 85 and 2023: 'BLOCK CONTAINS 2 RECORDS', 'BLOCK 100', 'BLOCK CONTAINS 10 TO 100 CHARACTERS', 'BLOCK CONTAINS 10 TO 20' all compile and run; '+5' and '5.5' refused (COBOL0001, integer-n required); 'CHARACTERS RECORDS' refused (COBOL0307, braces choose one); zero refused COBOLNET2386 (§5.5 1) nonzero default). conformance:2023/pb829_closed_formats_legal exercises only the 'BLOCK CONTAINS 1 RECORDS' arm, so it is not a covering test for the whole format -> test-ref empty. cite.py --check 13.18.10.1 "The BLOCK CONTAINS clause specifies the size of a physical record." -> OK. || Editions (adjudicator): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (clause present unchanged in every edition; Annex E records no change to 13.18.10)

subject: CLASS clause
notes: docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 row A.4.14 (VALIDATE — Not claimed) + §4 item 3. Licence: Annex A.4.1 and its second sentence. OWNER DECISION kb/Work PB375, 2026-09-02. The GENERAL FORMAT row: the grammar RECOGNIZES the printed format — `CLASS IS { NUMERIC | ALPHABETIC | ALPHABETIC-LOWER | ALPHABETIC-UPPER | BOOLEAN | alphabet-name-1 | class-name-1 }`, RENDERED at PDF p412 / folio 382 (CLASS and the five keywords underlined, IS not; a plain required choice with no choice indicators) — and refuses it by name rather than failing to parse it. BOOLEAN has no lexer token and rides the class-name-1 arm, which is unobservable because the clause is refused whichever arm matched. The negative fixture exercises BOTH arms (a class-name and a keyword, the latter without the optional word IS).

subject: COLUMN clause
notes: (kb/Work PB1220, wave 1005 A). Format 1 rendered from the PDF (printed p386): {COLUMN NUMBER|COLUMN NUMBERS|COLUMNS|COL NUMBER|COL NUMBERS|COLS} [LEFT|CENTER|RIGHT] [IS|ARE] {integer-1 | {PLUS|+} integer-2}... The grammar is now (COLUMN|COLUMNS|COL|COLS) (NUMBER|NUMBERS)? (LEFT|CENTER|RIGHT)? (IS|ARE)? reportColumnOperand+, CENTER a context-sensitive token (8.10, a user word elsewhere). The alignment brace is OPTIONAL in the grammar though the diagram prints a brace, because SR9 states 'If any of the operands is absolute and neither LEFT, CENTER, nor RIGHT is specified, LEFT is assumed' (cite.py --check 13.18.14.3 OK 9)). The alignment phrase gates 2002 with the other COLUMN forms (construct report-multi-column-2002; the 85 form is COLUMN NUMBER IS integer-1 alone).

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: kb/Work PB483 LANDED (wave 58). The rendered figure (PDF p422) prints {CONTROL IS | CONTROLS ARE} { {data-name-1}... | FINAL [data-name-1]... }: FINAL once, FIRST, the ellipsis on the data-name bracket alone (5.2.7). subject: LINAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB489 LANDED. The printed shape was already matched token for token (the figure was rendered from the canonical PDF, printed folio 417, and the transcription is faithful); what diverged was the OPERAND EXTRACTION, and it no longer does. BindLinageClause captured `d.cobolWord()?.GetText()` - the FIRST word of the written dataReference - so a qualified data-name-1 bound the WRONG item and, for the register alternative, the first word is the FILE-NAME QUALIFIER, so `LINAGE IS LINAGE-COUNTER OF LPF LINES` recorded the file name as the clause's data-name. Both operand slots now go through DataBinder.ClauseDataName, which keeps the whole written reference and REFUSES the three shapes a data-name-n position does not admit (COBOLNET2024): a special register (8.4.3.1 Format 10/11 identifiers, confined to the procedure division by 8.4.3.14.3 SR1 / 8.4.3.15.3 SR1), a subscript (8.4.2.3's with-subscripts form is an identifier), and a reference-modifier (8.4.3.3.3 NOTE). THE FORMAT'S REMAINING COVERAGE IS ALSO CLOSED, and the adjudication named it open: the positive fixture writes ALL THREE optional phrases - WITH FOOTING AT, LINES AT TOP, LINES AT BOTTOM - on two files at once, one with every optional word OMITTED (`LINAGE 2 FOOTING 2 TOP 3 BOTTOM 2`, 8.3.2.4.3) and one with every optional word written and all four operands qualified, and asserts the two files are byte-identical on the medium and branch-identical at every end-of-page; the new negative pins the PHRASE ORDER. Grammar unchanged - the defect was never in the .g4.

subject: LINE clause
notes: (kb/Work PB1221, wave 1021 F). IS?) | LINES ARE?), exactly the brace, so LINES NUMBER IS, LINE NUMBER ARE, LINES IS, LINES NUMBERS ARE and LINE NUMBERS IS are refused by the parser (COBOL0001 / COBOL0307), and LINE ARE, LINE IS, LINE NUMBER, LINE NUMBERS, LINES and LINES ARE compile and print on their lines (conformance:2002/pb1221_report_keyword_prefixes). The OPERAND half is unchanged (reportLineOperand; PB951 reportRelativeSign; PB1001 ON NEXT PAGE). ReportClauseKeywordPrefixTests enumerates all 18 (LINE|LINES, NUMBER|NUMBERS, IS|ARE) combinations. The 85 gate now names the written form (the LINES spelling, the multiple LINE clause form) instead of calling a single-operand LINES 3 a multiple LINE clause. Format 2 (screen) is the declined A.4.2 module, refused by name COBOLNET1560 (PB260). || Editions: Format 1 in every edition; the LINES / NUMBERS / ARE spellings and the multi-operand form are 2002 (report-multi-line-2002, COBOLNET0900 at 85).

subject: RECORD clause
notes: Three printed formats: F1 RECORD [CONTAINS] integer-1 [BYTES|CHARACTERS]; F2 RECORD [IS] VARYING [IN] [SIZE] [[FROM] integer-2] [TO integer-3] [BYTES|CHARACTERS] [DEPENDING [ON] data-name-1]; F3 RECORD [CONTAINS] integer-4 TO integer-5 [BYTES|CHARACTERS]. Grammar alt 1 `RECORD CONTAINS? integerLiteral (TO integerLiteral)? (CHARACTERS|BYTES)?` covers F1+F3 (TO required in F3, optional word CONTAINS), alt 2 covers F2 with every optional word optional and DEPENDING ON as its own bracket. BYTES/CHARACTERS braces: all words unmarked, so the whole group is optional - grammar matches. Probed (probe/record-clause/fm.cob) at --std 2014 and 2023: `RECORD 20`, `RECORD 5 TO 20`, `RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE TO 20 CHARACTERS`, `RECORD IS VARYING FROM 5` compile clean at both; `RECORD CONTAINS 20 BYTES` and `RECORD VARYING 5 TO 20 BYTES DEPENDING L` compile at 2023 and draw COBOLNET0900 at 2014 (BYTES is the 2023 addition). VARYING compiles at --std 85 (probe/record-clause/p3.cob) - correct: the 1985 RECORD clause had the VARYING format (note: docs/COBOLNET_FILES_DESIGN.md ~L2108 claims VARYING is a 2002 introduction rejected at 85; that doc text is stale, the code is right). || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 85,2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (BYTES spelling 2023 only - Annex E.3.3 item 13)

subject: REDEFINES clause

The grammar is a SUPERSET (dataReference admits OF/IN and subscripts, and clause order is free) - those residues are SR1/SR5/SR6 questions and are recorded on those rows, not here. || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 85,2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the REDEFINES clause is in the base language of every edition; the 2023 Annex E lists no change to this rule) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Cst/DataDescriptionCst.cs#RedefinesTargetName (kb/Work PB1281 replaced the glued-text accessor RedefinesTargetName with RedefinesTarget, which hands the binder the written dataReference; DataBinder.RedefinesDataName2 decides the operand's shape)

subject: ALLOCATE statement
notes: Read the format at specs/ISO_COBOL.md 22600-22604 (no 'Figure notes' block accompanies this diagram, so the transcribed <pre> IS the authority): ALLOCATE { arithmetic-expression-1 CHARACTERS | data-name-1 } [ INITIALIZED ] [ RETURNING data-name-2 ], with ALLOCATE / CHARACTERS / INITIALIZED / RETURNING underlined and no optional noise words. Read grammar rule `allocateStatement`: two alternatives, `ALLOCATE arithmeticExpression CHARACTERS INITIALIZED? (RETURNING dataReference)?` and `ALLOCATE dataReference INITIALIZED? (RETURNING dataReference)?` — arm-for-arm identical to the diagram, both optional phrases optional in both arms, and no scope terminator / conditional phrase (matching Table 12's empty ALLOCATE row at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:20867). Alternative order is safe because alt 1 requires the CHARACTERS token, so a bare data-name falls to alt 2 under ALL(*) prediction. The binder's `PtrBinder.BindAllocate` reads `al.dataReference()` (DIRECT children only, so data-names inside arithmeticExpression are not in the list) and indexes drefs[0] for data-name-1 / drefs[^1] for RETURNING — correct for all four legs, and the RETURNING()-null guard precedes the index so the no-RETURNING form cannot index an empty list. All five surface legs have goldens: `ALLOCATE G INITIALIZED RETURNING P`, `ALLOCATE W INITIALIZED`, `ALLOCATE 6 CHARACTERS INITIALIZED RETURNING P2` (2002/allocate_initialized), `ALLOCATE B` and `ALLOCATE 5 CHARACTERS RETURNING P` (2002/pointer_alloc). Editions: ALLOCATE appears in neither the 2023 new-features list (specs/ISO_COBOL.md 1100-1130) nor Annex E, so there is no 2014->2023 delta; it cannot be COBOL-85 because SR1 requires the BASED clause and SR3 requires category data-pointer, neither of which the 1985 standard has. || UPHELD: I re-read specs/ISO_COBOL.md 22598-22604 myself — the <pre> reads exactly `ALLOCATE ┤ arithmetic-expression-1 CHARACTERS | data-name-1 ├ [ INITIALIZED ] [ RETURNING data-name-2 ]`, brackets with NO choice-indicator bars, so INITIALIZED-before-RETURNING is a fixed order and the grammar's `INITIALIZED? (RETURNING dataReference)?` tail matches it in both arms. I re-read `allocateStatement` at CobolParserCore.g4:1244-1247 and `PtrBinder.BindAllocate` at PtrBinder.cs:99-138: for form 1 with RETURNING drefs has ONE element and drefs[^1] is it; for form 2 without RETURNING drefs has ONE element and drefs[0] is it; for form 2 with RETURNING drefs is [based, returning] and both indexes are right — all four index legs re-derived, not taken on trust. I do NOT rest on the ALL(*) prediction argument: `ALLOCATE B.` and `ALLOCATE G INITIALIZED RETURNING P.` are ENABLED goldens with byte-compared .out, which is empirical proof alt 2 is reachable. Edition re-derived independently of the code catalog: ALLOCATE is absent from Annex E (§E.2/§E.3, specs/ISO_COBOL.md 42858-44000), and §13.18.x SR16 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:15101 — 'The BASED clause may be specified only in data description entries in the linkage section, in the working-storage section, and in the local-storage section. The level number of such data description entries shall be 1 or 77') plus §13.18.60.4 GR23's data-pointer are both post-85 constructs, so 2002,2014,2023. Not downgraded: the format-surface row is about which token sequences the grammar admits, and the BASED-record storage-shape gap found on GR3/GR4/GR7 is a data-model gap, not a surface one.

subject: CONTINUE statement
notes: Re-read the format in specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 23190 and validated it mechanically (`cite.py --check 14.9.9.2 "CONTINUE"` -> OK, returning the whole format line). Derived expectation BEFORE reading code, from the repaired Figure-notes block: CONTINUE is a required word (the printed missing underline is the C2 typo), the bracket makes the whole phrase optional, and AFTER / SECONDS carry underline rules so they are REQUIRED inside the phrase; the operand is arithmetic-expression-1 (a full 8.8.1 arithmetic expression, not a mere identifier/literal). READ: `continueStatement : CONTINUE (AFTER arithmeticExpression SECONDS)? ;` (CobolControlFlow.g4:361-363). Token-for-token identical to the derived shape: CONTINUE mandatory (so `AFTER 5 SECONDS` alone cannot parse as a CONTINUE, the Figure-notes' second argument), the group is `( ... )?` (bracket), AFTER and SECONDS are hard tokens inside it (not `AFTER?` / `SECONDS?`), so `CONTINUE 5` is rejected. The operand nonterminal is the SHARED `arithmeticExpression` (CobolExpressions.g4:208 -> additiveExpression -> multiplicative -> power), i.e. the same 8.8.1 rule PERFORM VARYING uses, so a parenthesized/compound expression, a literal, an identifier and a function reference are all admitted -- not a narrowed operand. The grammar's own header comment (CobolControlFlow.g4:359-360) records the same page-604-vs-page-732 contradiction the Figure notes do and resolves it the same way (the defining occurrence governs), so the transcription and the grammar agree rather than one having inherited the other's typo. Wired into the single `statement` rule at CobolParserCore.g4:719. EDITION (derived from Annex E, NOT from the registry's own IntroducedIn column): Annex E.3.3 item 14 at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:43957 -- "Additional functionality added to the CONTINUE statement. The CONTINUE statement has been enhanced to provide the ability to pause runtime execution for a specified period of time" -- so the bracketed phrase is 2023-only while bare CONTINUE is 85-continuous. The compiler gates exactly that split: VersionConformancePass.VisitContinueStatement fires COBOLNET0900 only when `ctx.arithmeticExpression()` is present (Validation/VersionConformancePass.cs:584-589), i.e. on the PHRASE, never on the verb -- confirmed by 85/wavef_dbg_proc.cob and 85/index_name_r7_windows.cob compiling bare CONTINUE at --std 85. TESTED: 2023/continue_after exercises both operand forms (a literal `AFTER 0` and a data item `AFTER WS-N`); the constructs.json row `continue-after-2023` drives VersionMatrixTests.Construct_MatchesEditionExpectation and IntroducedConstruct_IsRejectedUnderPermissive, so the below-2023 rejection is asserted at 85/2002/2014 and is not waived by --permissive. NOT exercised anywhere: a COMPOUND arithmetic-expression-1 (`CONTINUE AFTER N + 1 SECONDS`); that is a shared-nonterminal reuse rather than a private parse, so it does not cost the verdict. || UPHELD (independent re-derivation): I re-ran all three cite checks myself -- `cite.py --check 14.9.9.2 "CONTINUE"` -> OK (General format), and read the format + Figure notes at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:23189-23212 before opening any code. I re-read CobolControlFlow.g4:361-363 and CobolParserCore.g4:719 directly. I additionally checked the two edges the adjudicator did not: (a) `unaryExpression : addOp unaryExpression | primaryExpression` (CobolExpressions.g4) admits a LEADING SIGN, so `CONTINUE AFTER -1 SECONDS` -- the literal spelling of the GR1a negative case -- parses, and `primaryExpression` admits numericLiteral / ZERO_ARITH / functionCall / dataReference / `( arithmeticExpression )`, so the operand really is the full 8.8.1 rule; (b) the SECONDS terminator cannot be swallowed by the operand, because `additiveExpression` stops at a non-addOp token and `dataReference` is single-word except for OF/IN qualification. I verified the test-refs are LIVE rather than merely present: tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json lists `continue_after` at enabled[22], and tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/VersionMatrixTests.cs:79/:124 are the two named methods; the constructs.json row `continue-after-2023` carries source `CONTINUE AFTER 0 SECONDS.` with expectDiagnostic COBOLNET0900. || REFUTED (edition-basis citation, verdict unchanged): the adjudicator wrote "E.2's new-reserved-word list at :43951 adds SECONDS". That is WRONG on both counts and I did not inherit it. Line 43951 sits inside Annex **E.3.3 item 13** (heading at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:43225 `E.3.3 Not affecting`), whose lead sentence is "**Context-sensitive words.** In order to provide enhanced functionality, the following words have either been added to the list of context-sensitive words or the context in which they are reserved has been expanded" -- SECONDS is in the CONTEXT-SENSITIVE list, not a reserved-word list. The 8.10 context-sensitive-words table at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:9578 confirms it: `| SECONDS | RETRY phrase, CONTINUE statement |`. The compiler agrees with the STANDARD and not with the adjudicator's note: CobolLexer.g4:562-568 comments SECONDS as "8.10 context-sensitive (user-legal at every edition)" and CobolWords.g4:89 re-admits it as a user word. This does not move the verdict -- the AFTER phrase's 2023 introduction rests on E.3.3 item 14, which I checked and which stands -- but the note's edition evidence was an uncited (and false) claim, exactly the failure mode CLAUDE.md rule 1 names, and is replaced above.

subject: DISPLAY statement
notes: CLOSED 2026-09-09 (kb/Work PB258 golden round) - both halves this row held open are landed or licensed, and both are now witnessed. || FORMAT 1 (device), re-derived element for element against 14.9.11.2's printed format and CobolParserCore.g4#displayStatement as it stands today: the operand brace repeats with '...' (the grammar's operand loop), UPON is optional, WITH is an OPTIONAL word before NO ADVANCING (it is not underlined - 5.2.3), END-DISPLAY is optional, and identifier-1 admits a function-identifier per 8.4.4.1. conformance:2002/l1_display_format1_elements pins every one of those in four derived lines - A=0042|abc (one statement, a mixed identifier/literal operand LIST, 14.9.11.4 GR1's 'in the order listed'), S=[ ] (GR3 - a figurative constant contributes ONE occurrence, not the width of a neighbour), F=ABC (the function-identifier operand) and N1N2! (NO ADVANCING written with WITH and without it). conformance:2023/l1_display_standard_device pins the UPON element and discriminates SYSERR from the standard display device. || THE END-DISPLAY EDITION ASYMMETRY IS FIXED (kb/Work PB134). The terminator used to be accepted at --std 85 with no gate at all while its END-ACCEPT twin had one - one of two twin terminators gated, which was the defect whatever edition number the derivation assigned. constructs.json now carries the ACTIVE row end-display-2002 with diagnosticCode COBOLNET0816 and the version matrix runs it at all four editions (conformance-test:VersionMatrixTests.Construct_MatchesEditionExpectation). MEASURED here: DISPLAY WS-X END-DISPLAY draws COBOLNET0816 'the END-DISPLAY scope terminator requires COBOL-2002 (targeting COBOL-85)' at 85 and compiles clean at 2002, 2014 and 2023. || FORMAT 2 (screen) IS DECLINED, NOT MISSING, AND THE DECLINE IS LOUD. Annex A.4.2 (ACCEPT and DISPLAY screen handling) is recorded 'Not claimed' in docs/CONFORMANCE.md, and Annex A.4.1 admits an optional element's syntax 'only when support for that language element is claimed by the implementor' - so screen-name-1, the AT LINE/COLUMN phrase and the [NOT] ON EXCEPTION pair are refused BY NAME with COBOLNET1707 through ScreenFacility (kb/Work PB260). The grammar's screenTail arm and its {!screenPositionAhead()}? guard exist precisely so DISPLAY SG COLUMN 5 is DIAGNOSED rather than silently binding as a three-operand device DISPLAY, which is what it used to do. Witnesses: conformance:negative/a42-display-screen-minimal and conformance:negative/a42-display-screen-positioned. That half of the format is therefore UNREACHABLE rather than unverified - the same disposition GR-8.8.1.2-6 already carries for the declined standard-binary arithmetic mode. The repaired Figure notes' choice-indicator claims (the AT phrase's braces, the exception pair's brackets) are content OF that declined format and are recorded as A.4.2 posture, not as debt on this row. || Editions: batch default; Annex E carries no DISPLAY item.

subject: EVALUATE statement
notes: kb/Work/PB396.md — ALL FOUR recorded divergences are closed, and each was re-measured on this tree rather than inherited. (1) range-expression's trailing [ IN alphabet-name-1 ]: `valueRange : valueOperand (THRU|THROUGH) valueOperand (IN cobolWord)?` — `EVALUATE WS-C WHEN "A" THRU "M" IN MY-ALPHA` now runs (probe fmt_rest.cob prints RANGE-IN-ALPHA). (2) partial-expression-1: `evaluateWhenItem` carries `| partialExpression` — `EVALUATE WS-N WHEN > 5` now runs (same probe, PARTIAL-GT5). Those two were closed by earlier landings; re-probed here because a note's word is not evidence. (3) imperative-statement-1 sits INSIDE the outer brace group, unbracketed, so §5.2.6.3 makes it required and §5.2.6.2 gives the omission licence to brackets only: `evaluateWhenClause` now reads `evaluateWhenPhrase+ statementBlock` (statementBlock IS statement+), and `EVALUATE X WHEN 3 END-EVALUATE` is refused COBOLNET2072 where it used to compile in silence. The outer `{ … } …` is itself unbracketed, so at least one ordinary WHEN group is required and an EVALUATE whose only clause is WHEN OTHER is no longer a spelling of this statement. (4) `[ WHEN OTHER imperative-statement-2 ]` is ONE bracketed phrase FOLLOWING the repetition — §5.2.7 scopes an ellipsis to the portion between the delimiters immediately to its left, which the OTHER phrase is outside of — so it is a trailing `evaluateWhenOther?` on `evaluateStatement` rather than a second alternative of the repeated clause. A repeated or mispositioned WHEN OTHER is refused COBOLNET2073; it used to be admitted at any position any number of times, with EvaluateBinder's `other = body` discarding all but the last. The positive control at the introducing edition writes every position WITH its imperative and pins the values from the general rules, so the tightening cannot have been "satisfied" by refusing the construct.

subject: GENERATE statement
notes: Format: GENERATE {data-name-1 | report-name-1} (cite.py --check 14.9.16.2 "GENERATE" OK). The grammar parses one operand, `GENERATE reportGroupReference` = cobolWord [(IN|OF) reportName]. The optional qualifier is SR1's "It may be qualified by a report-name". BindGenerate tells the two alternatives apart by resolution. An unqualified name that resolves to a report is report-name-1 (summary reporting); otherwise it resolves through ReportGroupResolution to a report group (data-name-1). A name that matches neither is COBOLNET1757. Both alternatives were compiled and run in probe out/probe/generate/g1.cob (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023): `GENERATE DE-1` and `GENERATE R-1`. The data-name alternative is also exercised by conformance:2023/pb365_report_group_qualified and 85/pb365_report_group_qualified_85, which include the qualified form. No spec-derived test exercises the report-name alternative, so test-ref is left empty. || editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (Report Writer is present in every edition; the 2023 Annex E lists no change to GENERATE)

subject: GO TO statement
notes: kb/Work/PB412.md landed w41. PDF page 660 (printed folio 630) re-rendered at 190 dpi, the diagram being load-bearing: Format 1 is 'GO TO procedure-name-1' with only GO underlined, so TO is an optional word (5.2.3) and procedure-name-1 is unbracketed and therefore singular and required (5.2.6.2); Format 2 is 'GO TO { procedure-name-1 } ... DEPENDING ON identifier-1' -- one or more names (5.2.7), DEPENDING underlined and required (5.2.2), ON optional. The transcription matches the page. THE REPAIR IS STRUCTURAL: goToStatement now carries ONE ALTERNATIVE PER PRINTED FORMAT plus the edition-gated ANSI-85 target-less arm, so the complement is a syntax error in the parser; GoToFormats.Of is the ONE classifier every reader asks (the binder's total three-arm switch, the BareGotoRemoved2002 gate, and the ALTER sole-GO-TO-paragraph test), replacing three separate reconstructions from optional children; and CobolErrorStrategy re-codes the resulting parse error as COBOLNET2172 naming the format's own cardinalities. WHAT WAS WRONG: the rule was the single union 'GO TO? procedureName? (procedureName)* (DEPENDING ON? dataReference)?', so 'GO TO A B.' compiled at every edition and the Format-1 bind arm read names[0] and DISCARDED B in silence, while 'GO TO DEPENDING ON X.' compiled clean and aborted the run unit on a BoundUnsupported loud stage -- that stage is now deleted. Measured after the fix: both shapes refused with COBOLNET2172 at 85/2002/2014/2023, the bare form still gated by name (COBOLNET0811) at 2002+ and accepted at 85, and the six legal spellings (TO omitted, ON omitted, one and three procedure-names, a section target, a qualified name) plus GR2's out-of-range fall-through all correct.
