subject: MOVE statement
notes: kb/Work/PB421.md landed w41. Both general formats were already faithfully implemented and the diagram was verified as PRINTED (PDF p.694): Format 1 'MOVE {identifier-1|literal-1} TO {identifier-2}...' and Format 2 'MOVE {CORRESPONDING|CORR} identifier-3 TO identifier-4'. The whole divergence was ONE over-accepting alternative: moveReceivingPhrase carried '(CORRESPONDING | CORR) dataReference TO dataReference', which composed with 'MOVE moveSendingOperand moveReceivingPhrase' to admit 'MOVE <sending-operand> CORRESPONDING id-3 TO id-4' -- a shape neither format prints, which the binder could not build, so MoveBinder fell through to BoundUnsupported and the compiler EMITTED A PROGRAM that died at run time claiming an unimplemented COBOL feature. The alternative is DELETED (Format 2 is spelled whole by moveStatement's first alternative), the shape is now a parse error re-coded as COBOLNET2173 naming both formats, and the fall-through message no longer says 'MOVE CORRESPONDING'. All FOUR spellings of the over-acceptance (identifier/literal sender x CORRESPONDING/CORR) are refused at all four editions, and the six legal spellings still compile. The drift guard is stated over the WHOLE grammar: a format-selecting CORRESPONDING/CORR keyword may be named only by a statement rule, never by a phrase rule it composes with. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4#moveSendingOperand (kb/Work PB2114 unified the sending operand into the one sendingOperand rule; moveSendingOperand no longer exists)

subject: MULTIPLY statement
notes: kb/Work PB1142 landed (w65c). Both formats parse and bind; the union grammar (multiplyByOperand: receivingOperand roundedPhrase? | functionCall | inlineMethodInvocation) is narrowed per format by the ONE ArithmeticOperandRole classification all four arithmetic verbs ask: Format 1 `BY {identifier-2 [rounded-phrase]}` accepts only a data reference placed through a receiving rule (positive definition), so a literal, a function-identifier (8.4.3.2.3 SR1) and an inline method invocation (8.4.3.4.3 SR1) are each COBOLNET1689 - before, the invocation receiver was silently DROPPED (MULTIPLY A BY B OB::"GETX" printed B=8.2 with the second operand ignored). Format 2 `BY {identifier-2 | literal-2}` + GIVING binds every identifier format (2002 golden rows 1-4). ArithmeticOperandRoleDriftTests pins the mixed-rule set and the receiving-rule set against the .g4.

subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB316 (LANDED) after kb/Work PB236 (landed). The general format's OUTER brace pair, with its own trailing ellipsis, encloses the whole group '{open-mode} [sharing-phrase] [retry-phrase] {file-name-1 [WITH NO REWIND]}' - re-verified this session by RENDERING the printed page (PDF p.705) rather than reading the transcription, and the transcription's figure note matches it. The grammar was already that format's exact image (openStatement: OPEN openClause+; openClause: openMode (sharingPhrase)? (retryPhrase)? openFileSpec+), and REVERSED is edition-gated out at >=2002 (conformance:negative/open-reversed). Defect (b), file-name-1 resolution, was fixed by PB236 (COBOLNET1639; conformance:negative/pb236-open-undeclared-file). Defect (a) - the repeated group's SCOPE discarded at bind - is FIXED HERE: the binder no longer hoists the two phrases out of the openClause loop, and the bound tree carries the format's own shape as BoundOpenFile(File, Mode, Sharing, Retry, Unsupported), one entry per file-name, which is 14.9.27.4 GR20's normal form. The two-group probes that motivated the row now agree with their GR20 reference forms: 'OPEN INPUT FA INPUT SHARING WITH NO OTHER FB' prints A=00 B=00, the same as the two-statement form (it printed A=00 B=61 before), and 'OPEN OUTPUT SHARING WITH ALL OTHER F1 OUTPUT F2' with an unlocked F2 now compiles, as its reverse ordering always did. Witness: conformance:2002/pb316_open_group_scope pins both orderings and both phrases; conformance:negative/pb316-open-sharing-group-below-2002 pins the 2002 introduction gate on a phrase written on a group OTHER than the first.

subject: PERFORM statement
notes: kb/Work PB431 + PB432 (landed). The DIVERGES verdict rested on FOUR shape errors in this figure and all four are now closed, each against the PRINTED page (682-683 / PDF 712-713), not the OCR. (1) The inline head's CARDINALITY: Format 2 prints ONE bracket over three stacked loop-control alternatives and Format 3 prints none, while the grammar spelled the head a repetition and BindPerformControl read FirstOrDefault() - PERFORM 3 TIMES UNTIL X > 100 ran three times, PERFORM UNTIL X > 4 3 TIMES ran five (the FIRST phrase always won), PERFORM 3 TIMES UNTIL ... VARYING I ... left I never initialized, and PERFORM 3 TIMES ... WHEN EC-ALL ... ran its body ONCE; ONE screen above the Format-2/Format-3 split now reports COBOLNET2117 / COBOLNET2118 at every edition. (2) The varying-phrase FROM/BY slots were typed arithmeticExpression, WIDER than the printed brace group - FROM A + B BY B * 2 compiled and ran at every --std, now COBOLNET2119. (3) The same typing was NARROWER: the figurative FROM ZERO, which 8.3.3.6.3 SR1 a) permits because 14.9.28.3 SR3 restricts the literal to numeric, was a hard parse error; the slot is now the shared valueOperand and FROM ZERO / FROM ZEROS compile and initialize to 0 (conformance:85/pb432_varying_brace_group legs A and B). (4) The empty imperative-statement-1 half, which PB431 recorded as unowned, was closed earlier by kb/Work PB396 and is RE-MEASURED here on this tree: PERFORM UNTIL X > 5 END-PERFORM is refused COBOLNET2072 naming 5.2.6.2, and a Format-3 PERFORM with no imperative-statement-1 is refused structurally at the parse. RESIDUE, and it is a message-quality one rather than a conformance gap: the Format-3 empty-body refusal is a bare COBOL0001 where the Format-2 one names the rule (registered as a lead in the PB432 implementer report).

subject: RAISE statement
notes: kb/Work PB1197 (landed with PB1425, w1019a). RAISE { EXCEPTION exception-name-1 | identifier-1 }: identifier-1 takes the shared objectReference rule, which now carries every identifier format that can yield an object reference - a data-name, SELF, an inline invocation and a function-identifier (w1018d) and the object-view (this landing): `RAISE OU AS PB1425VA` raises the object and the class's USE AFTER EXCEPTION OBJECT declarative selects it (RAISED-OBJECT). NULL and SUPER stay 14.9.29.3 SR2's COBOLNET0848. [editions: the OO facility, 2002+]

subject: READ statement
notes:
kb/Work PB331 LANDED (and PB332's format half rides the same grammar). THE PRINTED FIGURE WAS MEASURED, NOT INHERITED. `clause_page.py 14.9.30.2` -> PDF page 722 / folio 692, RENDERED with `render-spec-page.py 722`; `figure_geometry.py 722` reports, in printed order: Format 1 = a plain bracket y=280.90 h=48.79 over THREE stacked alternatives (ADVANCING ON LOCK / IGNORING LOCK / retry-phrase) and a SEPARATE plain bracket y=339.26 h=31.98 over TWO (WITH LOCK / WITH NO LOCK); Format 2 = the same pair at y=507.57 and y=547.48, then the KEY bracket at y=589.03. Neither lock bracket carries choice indicators - contrast the AT END group at y=377.08 and the INVALID KEY group at y=634.55, which the same tool flags `<-- CHOICE INDICATORS (5.2.6.4)`.
THREE RULES, ALL THREE NOW MODELLED. 5.2.6.2 (`--check` OK, 'or one of the alternatives contained within the brackets') makes each bracket AT MOST ONE alternative; 5.2.6.1 (`--check` OK, 'a unique combination of possibilities from a series of brackets') makes the two brackets INDEPENDENT; 5.2.1 (`--check` OK, 'shall be written in the compilation group in the sequence given in the general format') makes the printed ORDER normative, so the KEY phrase follows both brackets.
WHAT WAS WRONG, MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER ON THIS WORKTREE'S cobol.exe. (1) ORDER: `READ IXF RECORD WITH NO LOCK KEY IS IX-KEY ...` was `error COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input 'KEY'` (identically with IGNORING LOCK and with RETRY 3 TIMES), because `readKey?` sat BEFORE the lock slots and ANTLR takes the first matching alternative in written order; all three now compile and run, and the unprinted reverse `KEY IS IX-KEY WITH NO LOCK` - which used to compile - is now rejected (negative/pb331-read-key-before-lock). (2) CARDINALITY, INVERTED BOTH WAYS BY ONE MERGED RULE: `recordLockPhrase : IGNORING LOCK | WITH? NO LOCK | WITH? LOCK` reached through three free optionals made the LEGAL pair `IGNORING LOCK WITH NO LOCK` a syntax error (`no viable alternative at input 'WITH'`) while accepting `ADVANCING ON LOCK RETRY 3 TIMES IGNORING LOCK`, three alternatives out of one bracket. Now `readLockContentionPhrase` is bracket 1 and `recordLockPhrase` is bracket 2 - one grammar object per printed bracket - so the legal pair compiles (conformance:2002/pb331_read_lock_brackets, line S1) and the three-alternative spelling is rejected (negative/pb331-read-two-from-one-lock-bracket). (3) THE MERGE LEAKED INTO TWO OTHER STATEMENTS: WRITE and REWRITE reference the same rule, and 14.9.51.2 (pages 815/816) and 14.9.35.2 (page 740) print `[ retry-phrase ]` and `[ WITH LOCK | WITH NO LOCK ]` with NO IGNORING LOCK alternative at all; `WRITE R IGNORING LOCK` and `REWRITE R IGNORING LOCK` compiled and are now rejected (negative/pb331-write-ignoring-lock, negative/pb331-rewrite-ignoring-lock). (4) ONE OPTIONAL WORD: `figure_extract.py 722` measures the underlines as `_ADVANCING_ ON _LOCK_`, so by 5.2.3 ON is an optional word and `READ ... ADVANCING LOCK` is conforming; it was `error COBOL0001: missing token before 'LOCK'` and now compiles (golden line S2). The transcription of this figure was already CORRECT on all four points - the grammar had diverged from it, so nothing in specs/ISO_COBOL.md needed repair.
THE MODEL FOLLOWS THE FIGURE END TO END, which is the part that keeps it fixed: `BoundRecordLock` lost its IgnoringLock member and is now the retention bracket alone, `BoundRead`/`BoundKeyedRead` carry `IgnoringLock` beside `AdvancingOnLock`/`Retry` for bracket 1, and the runtime's `FileRecordLock` / `CobolFile.ReadShared` / `ReadLockGovern` take the two facts separately - because a single enum cannot say `IGNORING LOCK WITH NO LOCK`, which is exactly why that spelling could not reach 14.9.30.4 GR11 b)'s release before. Unit witness: conformance-test:CobolFileLockTests.ReadShared_IgnoringLockWithNoLock_ReadsTheLockedRecord_AndReleasesThisConnectorsOwnLock, with its falsifying control arm. Design: docs/COBOLNET_FILES_DESIGN.md D15. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: the general format itself is present at all four editions; its lock phrases are Annex A.4.7 2002 introductions and are COBOLNET0900-gated at 85 (measured at --std 85 for IGNORING LOCK, WITH NO LOCK and ADVANCING LOCK - the split kept every gate, VersionConformancePass.VisitReadIgnoringLock being the new site the split required).
 (5) ONE MORE OPTIONAL WORD, WRITTEN DOWN TWICE: the statement's single printed RECORD lived in BOTH `readDirection : (NEXT|PREVIOUS) RECORD?` and `readStatement`'s own `RECORD?`, so the grammar accepted it TWICE - `READ SQF NEXT RECORD RECORD ... END-READ` compiled clean, exit 0, no diagnostics. 14.9.30.2 Format 1 prints it once, after the {NEXT|PREVIOUS} braces, and 5.2.3 makes a non-underlined word one that may be omitted, not repeated. `readDirection` is now `NEXT | PREVIOUS` and the word lives in one place (negative/pb331-read-record-word-twice). Found by sweeping the whole figure rather than only the two defects the note named - the row is the FORMAT, so a second over-acceptance of it would have made this CONFORMS false.

subject: RECEIVE statement
notes: kb/Work R43 (owner, 2026-09-24): an unsupported facility is unsupported entirely. kb/Work R43 (owner, 2026-09-24) over docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 Annex A.3 row 4 'Asynchronous messaging (MCS) facility | Not claimed' + §4 item 1. subject: RELEASE statement
notes: kb/Work PB347 LANDED. FORMAT, rendered from the licensed PDF rather than read from the OCR (scripts/render-spec-page.py, PDF page 734 = printed 704): `RELEASE record-name-1 [ FROM { identifier-1 | literal-1 } ]`, with RELEASE and FROM the underlined required words -- the transcription at 14.9.32.2 is faithful, and the operand IS record-name-1, not identifier-1. THE DIVERGENCE THIS ROW CARRIED (over-acceptance of the record-name-1 POSITION) IS CLOSED: `RELEASE SRT-REC(1:3)` used to compile with NO diagnostic at any --std and emit CobolSort.Release(..., CobolString.RefMod(SRT_REC.AsImage(), 1, 3)), releasing a 3-character record into an 8-byte sort file; it is now COBOLNET1757 at every edition. The rule behind it: a record-name is a user-defined word (8.3.2.2.25) and 5.2.4's operand table gives that operand type 'User-defined word, including qualification and subscripting if needed' and nothing further, while 8.4.3.3.3 SR5 permits reference modification only 'anywhere an identifier referencing a data item of class alphanumeric, boolean, or national is permitted' -- its NOTE drawing the consequence, 'where data-name-n is used in a general format or syntax rule, then reference-modification is not permitted' (all three --check OK). The refusal is at BIND, not in the grammar: `releaseStatement : RELEASE dataReference` stays general because the subordinate-item half of the same rule cannot be decided by a grammar, and one rule belongs in one place. THE ACCEPTED SURFACE IS UNCHANGED and still verified in both positive goldens: FROM omitted; FROM identifier; FROM subscripted identifier; FROM reference-modified identifier (an IDENTIFIER position, where 8.4.3.3.3 SR5 does permit it); FROM alphanumeric literal; FROM figurative constants (8.3.3.6.3 SR1). EDITION LEG unchanged: the literal-1 arm is gated 2002+ (`release-from-literal-2002` -> COBOLNET0871); the functionCall arm (the deliberate PB10 addition, legal by 8.4.3.1.2) carries no gate. Annex E lists no substantive change to 14.9.32, so 2014 and 2023 are identical; the 85/2002 boundary for either FROM arm is not derivable from this document -- a dossier gap, not a verdict.

subject: RESUME statement
notes: General format: RESUME [AT] { NEXT STATEMENT | procedure-name-1 }, with RESUME, NEXT and STATEMENT underlined and AT not underlined (figure notes; the rendered figure's underlining is what the transcription records). Grammar: `resumeStatement : RESUME AT? (NEXT STATEMENT | procedureName)` - AT optional, one of the two operands required, NEXT STATEMENT both required. PROBED with the pinned cobol.exe: `RESUME M3` and `RESUME NEXT STATEMENT` (no AT) compile and run under --std 2002/2014/2023; under --std 85 both are refused with COBOLNET0876 ('the RESUME statement requires COBOL-2002'). The unit theory parses all four spellings (with/without AT x NEXT STATEMENT/procedure-name) at 2023; its expected values are the figure's own optional-word reading. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the RESUME statement belongs to the exception model introduced by ISO 1989:2002; absent from 1985)]

subject: RETURN statement
notes: kb/Work PB351 LANDED (w1015c): the residue after PB350 is closed. imperative-statement-1 / -2 of RETURN admit no conditional statement - an IF with no END-IF after AT END is refused COBOLNET2796 at every edition by the ONE screen of every non-IF statementBlock (ISO 14.5.1: 'Any statement with a conditional phrase that is not terminated by its explicit scope terminator is a conditional statement'; cite.py --check 14.5.1 OK). PB350's mandatory AT END half stays as landed (COBOLNET1850).

subject: REWRITE statement
notes: Every optional phrase of the record-name-1 arm, alone and combined, is pinned via GR7/GR23/§9.1.14. The 85 golden uses the 85 subset. The FILE arm is declined (A.4.13) and witnessed by the a413 negative.

subject: ROLLBACK statement
notes: General format is the single keyword ROLLBACK (cite.py --check 14.9.36.2 "ROLLBACK" -> OK, <u>ROLLBACK</u>). Grammar: rollbackFacilityStatement : ROLLBACK, reached from `statement` under {facilityWord("ROLLBACK")}? so it is a statement exactly where §8.9 reserves the word. Editions from the spec: Annex E.3.2 item 2 'Commit and rollback facility' (cite.py --check E.3.2 "Commit and rollback facility." -> OK §E.3.2 2)) - a COBOL-2023 addition; below 2023 ROLLBACK is a user word and there is no ROLLBACK statement. Probed on the pinned cobol.exe (out/probe/rollback/rb9_2014.cob): a bare ROLLBACK statement compiles and runs at --std 2023, and at 85/2002/2014 is rejected as an undefined user word (COBOLNET1639) - correct, no such statement exists there. The goldens pin a bare ROLLBACK parsing as a statement in sentence and imperative positions. FMT under an unclaimed module: the derived selector commit-and-rollback-only excludes FMT rows by KIND and records that the shipped grammar matches the printed format, which this confirms.

subject: SEARCH statement

subject: SEND statement
notes: kb/Work R43 (owner, 2026-09-24): an unsupported facility is unsupported entirely. kb/Work R43 (owner, 2026-09-24) over docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 Annex A.3 row 4 'Asynchronous messaging (MCS) facility | Not claimed' + §4 item 1. subject: SET statement
notes: kb/Work PB450 half 2 - the LAST printed general format of 14.9.39.2 whose grammar shape was not the figure's. The printed Format 7 was RE-RENDERED here (specs-private PDF p760 / folio 730 at 300 dpi) rather than taken from the transcription: `SET { ADDRESS OF data-name-1 | identifier-5 } ... TO identifier-6`, the brace a PLAIN required choice, the `...` OUTSIDE it, ADDRESS and TO underlined and OF NOT - and the figure note says the same in words, "The braces are a plain required choice - exactly one of the two alternatives - and the following `...` repeats the braced receiving operand" (cite.py --check 14.9.39.2 OK). The grammar held TWO fixed productions split on the SENDER's spelling, each hard-coding arity one, so four cells of the printed cross-product were a bare COBOL0001 at every edition. MEASURED on this worktree's own build BEFORE the fix: `SET ADDRESS OF B1 ADDRESS OF B2 TO P1` -> `COBOL0001: unexpected 'ADDRESS'`; `SET P1 P2 TO ADDRESS OF REC1` -> `cannot parse construct near 'REC1'`; `SET ADDRESS OF B1 P1 TO P2` -> `unexpected 'P1'`; `SET ADDRESS OF B1 TO ADDRESS OF R1` -> `unexpected 'ADDRESS'`. AFTER: all four compile and answer the values 14.9.39.4 GR12/GR13 and 8.4.3.11.4 GR1 compute (B1A=[AAAA] B2A=[AAAA] / B1A=[BBBB] / B1A=[CCCC] / B1A=[DDDD]). The rule is now ONE production whose repeated unit is a NAMED rule, `setAddressStatement : SET setAddressReceiver+ TO setAddressSender`, and the receiver carries its own kind (`ADDRESS()` present = data-name-1, absent = identifier-5) instead of a binder re-deriving it from token positions - the discipline half 1 landed for Formats 3 and 4, now held for this one by the same drift test. setObjectReferenceStatement moved AHEAD of it in setStatement, pinned by unit:PrintedFormatAlternativeDriftTests.SetObjectReferenceStatement_IsOfferedBeforeSetAddressStatement: Format 7's identifier-6 may be the predefined address NULL (SR19) and Format 5's identifier-4 the predefined object reference NULL (SR9), so `SET X TO NULL` is token-identical and only the receiver's category tells them apart, which is a BIND question. The other sixteen formats' shapes were swept and none carries a hard-coded arity: Formats 8, 9, 15 and the ENTRY extension already write `dataReference+`, Format 16's printed receiving operand IS one operand, and Format 6 is refused by name (COBOLNET1707).

subject: SORT statement
notes: kb/Work PB994 + PB1175 landed: the two legal operand shapes the refuter named as not compiling to working code now do - a Format-2 table inside a REDEFINES view / a nested table (PB1175, PB1055) and a relative or indexed USING/GIVING file (this note); the syntax surface the adjudicator measured stands (phrase order, Format-1 KEY arity, the 2002 gate of Format 2, the FOR forms, DUPLICATES, the OCCURS KEY default), and COLLATING is an optional word (printed page 745; PB1139).

notes: kb/Work PB333 LANDED (wave 56) RESIDUE (a) CLOSED; the screen moved by kb/Work PB1034 (wave 1005 D). subject: STOP statement
notes: Figure §14.9.42.2: STOP RUN [WITH? {ERROR|NORMAL} STATUS? [identifier-1|literal-1]], only STOP/RUN/ERROR/NORMAL underlined. Grammar statusPhrase = WITH? (ERROR|NORMAL) STATUS? (dataReference|literal)? matches exactly. Probed with pinned cobol.exe (probe dir out/probe/stop-statement/): 'STOP RUN.' exit 0; 'STOP RUN WITH ERROR.' 1; 'WITH NORMAL.' 0; 'WITH ERROR STATUS 16.' 16; 'STOP RUN ERROR 5.' (WITH+STATUS omitted) 5; 'STOP RUN NORMAL STATUS.' 0; 'STOP RUN STATUS 3.' rejected COBOL0307 and 'STOP RUN WITH STATUS 3.' rejected COBOL0001 (brace requires ERROR|NORMAL - correct). Edition: 'STOP RUN WITH ERROR.' at --std 85 -> COBOLNET0900, accepted at 2002/2014/2023; STOP literal accepted at 85 and rejected COBOLNET0902 at 2023 (2023 format has no literal arm). Doc drift only: an orphaned doc comment in StatementBinder.cs above the File I/O banner still says 'The phrase has no runtime effect in this compiler' - false since the exit-code wiring. [editions as adjudicated: STOP RUN: 1985/2002/2014/2023; the WITH {ERROR|NORMAL} [STATUS] phrase predates 2023 (Annex E item 32: GOBACK 'now allows the same status phrase as the STOP statement'); its 2002 introduction is the project's VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE datum, not re-derivable from the 2023 text]

subject: STRING statement
notes: General format: STRING {{identifier-1|literal-1}... [DELIMITED BY {identifier-2|literal-2|SIZE}]}... INTO identifier-3 [WITH POINTER identifier-4] [choice-indicator ON OVERFLOW / NOT ON OVERFLOW] [END-STRING]. Grammar: stringStatement : STRING stringSendingPhrase+ stringIntoPhrase stringWithPointer? stringOnOverflow? END_STRING?; stringSendingPhrase : strUnstrOperand delimitedByPhrase?; delimitedByPhrase : DELIMITED BY? (ALL)? (strUnstrOperand|SIZE) (the non-ISO ALL token is parsed only to be rejected at bind under SR2 - verified: sr2b.cob 'DELIMITED BY ALL SPACE' -> COBOLNET1757); stringOnOverflow carries both orders of the choice-indicator pair (5.2.6.4). Underlined/optional words verified by probe gr2.cob ('DELIMITED SIZE' with BY omitted, 'NOT OVERFLOW' with ON omitted, 'DELIMITED BY SPACES') -> C[ABX.......] NOV. identifier-1 admits a function-identifier (§8.4.3.1.2 Format 1) via strUnstrSender; INTO/POINTER are dataReference only (receivers). phrase_order_overflow golden pins the reversed NOT/ON order with DELIMITED BY SIZE runs. SR9 (omission only before INTO) is structurally unviolable by this grammar: any phraseless run merges into the next run. Edition note: whether COBOL-85 already allowed the DELIMITED phrase to be omitted is NOT derivable in-repo (see dossier_gaps); the binder applies it at every edition. [editions as adjudicated: 2023 text (ISO/IEC 1989:2023 §14.9.43); Annex E lists no STRING change 2014->2023; the earlier-edition edge is not derivable in-repo (no 2002/2014 text)]

subject: SUBTRACT statement
notes: All three printed formats implemented and measured. PRINTED PAGE RENDERED (licensed PDF p.762, ISO/IEC 1989:2023) and matched against specs/ISO_COBOL.md line-for-line: F1 `SUBTRACT {identifier-1|literal-1}... FROM {identifier-2 [rounded-phrase]}...`; F2 adds `FROM {identifier-2|literal-2}` + `GIVING {identifier-3 [rounded-phrase]}...`; F3 `{CORRESPONDING|CORR} identifier-4 FROM identifier-5 [rounded-phrase]`; each with the bracketed CHOICE-INDICATOR size-error group and `[END-SUBTRACT]`. Underlining measured off the render: ON is NOT underlined in either size-error line (optional word) and the grammar has `ON?` in both arms (CobolParserCore.g4:840,842). MEASURED (probe dir probe/subtract): p1 F1 multi-operand + multi-receiver + per-receiver ROUNDED; p2/g6 F2 with literal-2 and with several GIVING receivers each carrying its own ROUNDED; p3/p4/m3 F3 with both CORR and CORRESPONDING, ROUNDED after identifier-5, both size-error branches, END-SUBTRACT; g7 the REVERSED phrase order (5.2.6.4 choice indicators - zero or more, each at most once, any order); h5 END-SUBTRACT as a scope terminator inside IF; h1 the FROM sender as a data reference; g9/g10 a function-identifier in both sending positions (8.4.3.1.2 makes it an identifier). The format-mixing violations the union grammar admits are narrowed back at bind and REJECTED AT COMPILE TIME with COBOLNET1689: two FROM operands under GIVING (g1), ROUNDED on the F2 sending operand (g2), operands with no FROM (g3), a literal receiver in F1 (g4), GIVING with no FROM (g5), a function-identifier F1 receiver (g11). Verified at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 (h2); ROUNDED MODE IS gates 2014+ (h3, COBOLNET0803 - 14.7.4's row, not this one). Additional spec-derived goldens touching this row: conformance:85/optional_on_size_error (ON omittable, SUBTRACT leg), conformance:2023/pb134_giving_sending_operands (F2 one sending literal), conformance:2023/pb45_function_in_sending_operands (F2 function sender). DEFECT ATTACHED (does not change the verdict - it is comment text, not behaviour): the grammar's own section banner for SUBTRACT cites the WRONG clause and UNSTRING's banner claims SUBTRACT's - see finding subtract-clause-citation-drift.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:897 subtractStatement; src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:902-923 subtractOperandList/subtractOperand/subtractFromPhrase/subtractFromOperand/subtractGivingPhrase; src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:809-817 receivingArithmeticOperand/roundedPhrase; src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:839-844 arithmeticOnSizeError; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/ArithmeticBinder.cs:71-99 BindSubtract; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/ArithmeticBinder.cs:215-236 Format2SendingOperand/Format1Receivers; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/CorrespondingBinder.cs:33-37 BindSubtractCorresponding retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4#subtractOperandList (kb/Work PB2114: subtractStatement names sendingOperand+ directly; the subtractOperandList wrapper no longer exists)

subject: SUPPRESS statement
notes: Format '<u>SUPPRESS</u> PRINTING' (cite.py --check 14.9.45.2 "SUPPRESS" OK); PRINTING is not underlined so it is optional. Grammar 'suppressStatement : SUPPRESS PRINTING? ;' admits both forms; conformance:2023/rw_suppress (SUPPRESS PRINTING) and conformance:2023/rw_suppress_bare (bare SUPPRESS) cover both. Probe ed.cob: bare SUPPRESS compiles and runs at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 (no edition gate, per row 130d accept-everywhere posture). [editions as adjudicated: 2014, 2023 (not an Annex E 2014->2023 addition, so present in 2014); 85/2002 availability not derivable from the 2023 text (VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE row 130d, RW accepted at every edition)]

subject: TERMINATE statement
notes: Format `TERMINATE { report-name-1 } ...` (cite.py --check 14.9.46.2 "TERMINATE" -> OK §14.9.46.2 General format). Grammar `terminateStatement : TERMINATE reportName+ ;` admits one-or-more report-names, ungated (Core grammar); BindTerminate resolves each name (SR1 COBOLNET1757 on an unknown one). Probed: single-report TERMINATE compiles and runs at --std 85, 2002, 2023 (out/probe/terminate-statement/q85.cob, q2002.cob, p1.cob); three-name `TERMINATE R-C R-B R-A` compiles and runs at 2023 (p2.cob). No spec-derived test targets the general format itself; Terminate_Gr2/ControlBreak tests exercise only the one-name form. [editions as adjudicated: 1985 (Report Writer module), 2002, 2014, 2023]

subject: UNLOCK statement
notes: kb/Work PB236 (landed). SHAPE: unchanged and correct -- `UNLOCK file-name-1 [ RECORD | RECORDS ]` with only UNLOCK underlined, rendered from the printed page (scripts/render-spec-page.py 798) and matched exactly by `unlockStatement : UNLOCK fileName (RECORD | RECORDS)? ;`; RECORD/RECORDS are optional words carrying no semantics (5.2.3), the whole bracketed group is omissible (5.2.6.2), and all three spellings were measured behaviourally identical. Edition identity: recognition-gated at COBOL-2002 (COBOLNET0900 at --std 85). THE OPERAND HALF -- THE ONE REASON THIS ROW WAS PARTIAL -- IS NOW ENFORCED. The format writes file-name-1 and cite.py --check 8.4.2.1 'In order to use a resource, a statement shall contain a reference that uniquely identifies that resource.' -> OK; `UNLOCK NOSUCH.` used to compile clean (exit 0, zero diagnostics) and abort at run time with 'a COBOL feature that is not yet implemented ... UNLOCK of undeclared file'. The finding said the mechanism was shared with six sibling binder sites and the fix was one dispatch change rather than seven -- and that is what landed: StatementValidation.ResolveFile is the ONE file-name resolution step for a statement operand, reporting the EXISTING undefined-reference descriptor COBOLNET1639, and the seven sites now have no BoundUnsupported arm at all. Measured: `error COBOLNET1639: 'NOSUCH' is not defined as a file -- UNLOCK names file-name-1 in its general format ...`. The witness deliberately puts the UNLOCK on a path the flow GO TOs past, because that is the shape on which the defect was worst: the run-time loud never fired either, so illegal source compiled AND ran to normal completion. Witness: conformance:negative/pb236-unlock-undeclared-file-unreached.

subject: UNSTRING statement
notes: kb/Work PB1183 (landed, wave 1019 F). cite.py --check 14.9.48.2 "INTO" -> OK §14.9.48.2: `INTO { identifier-4 [ DELIMITER IN identifier-5 ] [ COUNT IN identifier-6 ] } …` — the ellipsis follows the braced receiver group, so it repeats the receivers, never the INTO keyword. The grammar read `unstringIntoPhrase+` and compiled `UNSTRING S DELIMITED BY "," INTO A INTO B` at every edition (A=[AB  ] B=[CD5E]); it now reads ONE `unstringIntoPhrase` (`INTO unstringIntoTarget+`) and the second INTO is COBOL0307 at 85/2002/2014/2023 (negative/pb1183-unstring-into-repeated). The one-INTO-many-receivers form stays pinned by conformance:85/l1c35_unstring_receiving_operands (three receivers with DELIMITER IN). GnuCOBOL 3.2 (-std=cobol2014 and default) refuses the same source: 'syntax error, unexpected INTO'. Every other facet of the format was verified by the d1-14c adjudication (optional BY/IN/WITH/ON words, the ON/NOT ON OVERFLOW choice indicators, POINTER/TALLYING order, identifier-only sender); unchanged. The legacy binder's per-phrase loop collapsed with it (StringStatementBinder).

subject: USE statement
notes: kb/Work PB332 (divergence 1) and PB365 (divergence 2), both LANDED. Divergence 2: Format 4's second brace group prints {object-class-name-1 | interface-name-1} and DeclBindUse resolved only the class arm, so half the format's operand alternatives were unreachable; PB365 landed the interface alternative (SR17) and the two-pass GR14 selector behind it. subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB1189 landed (w1031 group G). Format 1 prints ADVANCING as `{identifier-2 | integer-1} [LINE | LINES]` OR `{mnemonic-name-1 | PAGE}` - LINE/LINES belong ONLY to the count alternative (cite.py --check 14.9.51.2 'mnemonic-name-1' OK). A mnemonic-name parses as dataReference, so the grammar cannot tell it from identifier-2; SequentialIoBinder.BindAdvancing's mnemonic arm now refuses a trailing LINE/LINES by name (COBOLNET2269, statement-format-shape) where it used to drop the word in silence (`WRITE R AFTER ADVANCING TOP-OF-FORM LINES` and `WRITE R BEFORE TOP-OF-FORM LINE` compiled rc=0). `AFTER ADVANCING PAGE LINES` stays the parse error COBOL0307. The keyed arm (KeyedIoBinder.BindWrite) refuses any ADVANCING phrase (SR3), so the sequential arm is the only one. Negative pb1189-advancing-mnemonic-lines (85..2023); the legal mnemonic arm is pinned by FileIoDifferentialTests. Everything else verified: EOP / NOT EOP both orders and both spellings, AT optional (ws1eop runs); INVALID KEY both orders in grammar; WITH optional on LOCK/NO LOCK, the two lock alternatives mutually exclusive (ws1lock2 COBOL0307); FROM must precede ADVANCING (ws1order COBOL0307); `BEFORE BEFORE` rejected (ws5dup); the BEFORE+AFTER pair rejected at 2014 (COBOLNET0900) and accepted at 2023 (ws1pair); retry-phrase and lock phrase rejected at 85 (ws5lk, ws5rt COBOLNET0900) and accepted in format order at 2023 (ws5rt23). Choice-indicator reading per §5.2.6.4 (cite.py --check 5.2.6.4 'The alternatives may be specified in any order.' OK); §E.3.3 item 2 --check OK; §14.9.51.2 'where retry-phrase is described in 14.7.9, RETRY phrase' --check OK. The FILE file-name-1 alternative is Annex A.4.13, declined (COBOLNET1706, PB282 landed). Format selection by organization is SR2/SR3 (part 2/3). [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 for the base format; the BEFORE+AFTER word pair is 2023-only (§E.3.3 item 2, 'Both BEFORE and AFTER are allowed together in WRITE ADVANCING'); the retry-phrase and WITH [NO] LOCK bracket are post-1985 (edition of introduction not derivable from the 2023 text; the code gates them at 2002)]

subject: BASECONVERT function
notes: UPHELD after INDEPENDENT re-verification rather than by accepting the prior report. PRINTED PAGE RE-RENDERED AND READ (python scripts/render-spec-page.py 851 = printed folio 821): the format is 'FUNCTION BASECONVERT ( argument-1 argument-2 argument-3 )' with separate underline rules under FUNCTION and under BASECONVERT and none under the parentheses or the arguments -- exactly three arguments, no brackets, no braces, no choice indicators, no ellipsis, so nothing is optional and nothing is repeatable. specs/ISO_COBOL.md:30184 now carries the matching <u>FUNCTION</u> <u>BASECONVERT</u> markup, so the transcription is faithful and the earlier reconciliation defect is repaired. GRAMMAR READ, NOT INFERRED: BASECONVERT is not a lexer token anywhere under src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/, so it arrives through `functionName : IDENTIFIER` and the generic `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?`, with `functionArgList : functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*`. Acceptance AND rejection re-run in both directions: BASECONVERT("FF" 16 10) (the printed juxtaposition form) -> 255; BASECONVERT("FF", 16, 10) (the §8.3.5 comma separator) -> 255; lowercase 'function baseconvert(...)' -> 255; argument-2/argument-3 as PIC 99 DATA ITEMS -> 255; as a DISPLAY operand and nested inside another BASECONVERT -> correct. Arity is enforced by BindIntrinsicCore against the IntrinsicCatalog Fixed 3,3 row: 2 arguments, 4 arguments and the bare 'FUNCTION BASECONVERT' with no parentheses each draw 'error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION BASECONVERT takes 3 argument(s); N given (ISO 15.3)', and BASECONVERT(OMITTED, 16, 10) draws COBOLNET1544 per §8.4.3.2 SR7. EDITION taken from Annex E.3.3 item 22, NOT from the catalog row, and confirmed at the CLI: --std 85 / 2002 / 2014 each reject with COBOLNET1502 naming 2023. COVERING TEST verified on disk: tests/conformance/2023/intrinsics_string_2023.cob writes the three-argument format three times against tests/conformance/2023/intrinsics_string_2023.out, whose BASECONVERT lines (DEC=255, HEX=FF, BIN=A) I recomputed by hand from §15.12.4 -- spec-derived, not a legacy or GnuCOBOL comparison. ADJACENT, outside this rule's text and NOT counted against it: reference modification of the function result, FUNCTION BASECONVERT("FF", 16, 10)(1:2), is a PARSE ERROR ('COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input (') although §8.4.3.3.4 SR2 says 'If identifier-1 is a function-identifier, it shall reference an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function' -- an §8.4.3.3.4 grammar gap affecting every alphanumeric intrinsic, for whoever adjudicates that clause.

subject: BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER function
notes:
ADVERSARIAL PASS 2 - I tried to overturn this and could not; the CONFORMS is upheld on evidence I generated myself, not on the prior report. SCOPE OF THE CLAIM (stated so this row cannot be misread as 'BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER is done'): per scripts/spec/extract_rule_catalog.py, an FMT row is 'the unit of verify this diagram against the grammar rule that implements it' - it is the SYNTAX question only. The SEMANTICS of this function DIVERGE; see RV-15.13.4-1, which is DIVERGES on three independent sites.

(a) TRANSCRIPTION - I did not take the prior report's word for it. I extracted the PDF text layer independently (specs-private/ISO+IEC+1989-2023..., 0-based page 851 = printed folio 822) AND RENDERED THE PAGE IMAGE at 300 dpi (scripts/render-spec-page.py 852) because the standing rule is that OCR'd DIAGRAMS were systematically lossy toward falsely-restrictive syntax. The rendered diagram reads 'FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER ( argument-1  argument-2 )' with FUNCTION and BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER UNDERLINED and nothing else underlined, NO brackets, NO braces, NO ellipsis, one Format only. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 30217 is faithful. §15.13.2 validated with scripts/spec/cite.py --check.

(b) ACCEPTANCE - every case below re-run by ME on src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe at --std 2023, all yielding 00000101: space-only '(5 8)'; comma '(5, 8)'; semicolon '(5; 8)'; spaces inside the parens '( 5 8 )'; identifier arguments '(IV LN)'; arithmetic-expression argument '(IV - 0, LN)'; SUBSCRIPTED argument '(E(2), 8)'; nested function argument '(FUNCTION INTEGER(5.2), 8)'; and the two forms the prior report did NOT test, which were my best shot at breaking it - SPACE-SEPARATED PARENTHESIZED arguments '((2 + 3) (4 * 2))' and a data-name-headed expression followed by a space-separated parenthesized argument '(N + 0 (4 + 4))', both of which stress the FNARG_SEPARATOR / SUBSCRIPT-mode boundary described in the CobolExpressions.g4 comment. Both accept correctly. Also verified: a USER DATA ITEM NAMED 'BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER' coexists with 'FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5, 8)' in the same program and both resolve correctly (the intrinsic-function-name is not wrongly reserved); the format binds in a STRING sending position; and the §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 FUNCTION-omitted form under 'REPOSITORY. FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER INTRINSIC.' works.

(c) REJECTION (the diagram's other half - no bracket means no other arity is legal): 0, 1 and 3 arguments and the bare no-parenthesis form all reject with COBOLNET1504 'FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER takes 2 argument(s); n given (ISO 15.3)', emitted in IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsicCore off the IntrinsicCatalog Fixed(2,2) row; OMITTED in an argument position rejects with COBOLNET1544 (§8.4.3.2 SR7). All four re-run by me.

(d) EDITIONS - NOT taken from the IntrinsicCatalog row (I verified that independently of the code). Annex E of the 2023 standard is the SUBSTANTIVE CHANGES list 'between the previous COBOL standard and this Working Draft' (i.e. 2014 -> 2023) and BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER appears nowhere in it - its only post-Annex-E occurrence in specs/ISO_COBOL.md is the Index entry - so 2014 and 2023 are identical. The 85 exclusion is EXTERNAL knowledge, honestly flagged: the 2023 text carries no introduction-edition statement, and the COBOL-85 + 1989 intrinsic-function amendment set of 42 functions contains no boolean function (boolean/bit data - PICTURE 1, USAGE BIT, B"..." literals - is a COBOL-2002 addition, and §15.13.1 makes this function's type boolean).

(e) test-needed (partial). tests/conformance/2002/intrinsics_boolean_conv.cob exists on disk, is registered in tests/conformance/2002/manifest.json AND in tests/CobolSharp.Tests.Integration/ConformanceTests.cs, and is spec-derived (expected values hand-derived from §15.13.4 r1 and the Annex D.10 544 -> low-6-bits example - not a characterization/nist/legacy asset); I re-ran it through the CLI and it reproduces its golden exactly. It covers the format POSITIVELY and only in the comma-separated style. The SPACE-separated form as actually printed in the diagram, and the whole wrong-arity/OMITTED rejection half, appear in NO test asset (COBOLNET1504 and COBOLNET1544 are in no test) - those halves rest on my manual CLI runs above.

(f) CHECKED AND CORRECTLY OUT OF SCOPE (I re-tested the prior report's two dismissals rather than accepting them). (i) 'MOVE BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5, 8) TO B8' with NO REPOSITORY entry compiles silently and dies at run time with an UNHANDLED NotImplementedCobolFeatureException instead of a bind-time 'undefined data item'. This is NOT a §15.13.2 leniency: I ran the control 'MOVE ZZ-UNDEFINED-THING(5, 8) TO B8' and 'MOVE UPPER-CASE("abc") TO B8' and BOTH are equally undiagnosed, so the missing diagnostic is the generic undefined-subscripted-reference gap, not this function's. (ii) Reference modification of a function-identifier is a parse error for UPPER-CASE too, so it is a §8.4.3.1.2 / §8.4.3.2 diagram gap, i.e. a different FMT row.

subject: DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD function
notes: SUSTAINED. RPAREN)?` in CobolExpressions.g4, so no per-function rule can be falsely restrictive, and the arity comes from the catalog row via IntrinsicBinder's `if (args.Count < sig.MinArgs || args.Count > sig.MaxArgs)` -> COBOLNET1504. subject: DISPLAY-OF function
notes: UPHELD. I did NOT take the rendering on trust - I re-rendered the printed page myself (python scripts/render-spec-page.py 872 -> printed folio 842) and read it: the format is exactly 'FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF ( argument-1 [ argument-2 ] )', FUNCTION and DISPLAY-OF underlined, only argument-2 bracketed, no ellipsis, no repetition, no third operand. specs/ISO_COBOL.md 15.26.2 matches the printed page, so there is no falsely-restrictive OCR residue. Grammar: functionCall is the generic superset 'FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?' (read at CobolExpressions.g4:264), so the per-function shape is the catalog arity - IntrinsicArity.OptionalTrailing, MinArgs 1 / MaxArgs 2 - enforced in BindIntrinsicCore. RAN MYSELF at --std 2023: 1 argument accepted; 2 arguments accepted; the bare keyword-only form FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF with no parentheses at all -> COBOLNET1504 'takes 1..2 argument(s); 0 given'; 3 arguments -> COBOLNET1504 '3 given'; and the 15.3 ALL-subscript shape FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N-E(ALL)) over an OCCURS 3 table -> COBOLNET1504 '3 given', i.e. rejected, which is the right outcome since 15.26 does not permit a repeated argument. conformance:2002/national_intrinsics verified on disk with its golden and its tests/conformance/2002/manifest.json entry, and it exercises both admissible shapes. NOTED, and deliberately NOT charged to this rule: FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N-SRC)(2:3) is a parse error (COBOL0001 'no viable alternative at input (') - the reference-modifier belongs to the 8.4.3.2 function-identifier format, not to the 15.26.2 general format, so it is out of scope here but is a real gap for whoever adjudicates 8.4.3.2.

subject: EXCEPTION-FILE-N function
notes: Re-verified independently, not inherited. I rendered printed folio 846 (PDF page 876) myself with scripts/render-spec-page.py: the format is `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE-N [(argument-1)]` with FUNCTION and EXCEPTION-FILE-N underlined and the parenthesized argument bracketed — the transcription is faithful, no OCR over-restriction, and `python scripts/spec/cite.py --check 15.29.2` matches it. Grammar: `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?` admits both shapes. Ran every shape against the built CLI: 0 args -> `00`; empty parens `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE-N()` -> `00` (the ISO §8.4.3.2.3 SR6 NOTE's `FUNCTION RANDOM ()` shape, validated with cite.py — not a §15.29.2 over-acceptance); 1 arg -> accepted; a SPACE before the left parenthesis (`FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE-N (INF)`) still binds as the argument form, per SR6; 2 args rejected `COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE-N takes 0..1 argument(s); 2 given (ISO 15.3)`. The bracketed argument is correctly introduction-gated at 2023 (`COBOLNET0900 ... requires COBOL-2023 (targeting COBOL-2014)` observed at --std 2014) per Annex E.3.3 item 26 (cite.py-checked); the whole function is gated below 2002 by COBOLNET1502 (tests/conformance/negative/exception_file_n_below_2002.cob, verified on disk). Editions are the national-function window (national data and the -N exception twins are ISO/IEC 1989:2002 additions), NOT read off the IntrinsicCatalog row. COVERAGE GAP (does not change the verdict): the cited case exercises only the ZERO-argument shape; the one-argument shape — the only thing 2023 added to this format — has no spec-derived case for EXCEPTION-FILE-N (tests/conformance/2023/exception_file_arg.cob covers the alphanumeric sibling only). ADJACENT, OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS RULE: reference modification of a function-identifier does not parse at all (`FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE-N(INF)(1:1)` and even `FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(WS-A)(1:2)` both give `COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input '('`), although ISO §8.4.3.3.3 SR2 permits it for an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function and EXCEPTION-FILE-N is national (§15.29.1). That is a general §8.4.3.3 grammar row, not a §15.29.2 format defect.

subject: MAX function
notes: VERDICT UPHELD after an independent attack on each of the format's three obligations. `FUNCTION MAX ( { argument-1 } … )`: both words underlined (required), parentheses required, braces-plus-ellipsis = one or more with no upper bound. (1) REQUIRED WORDS AND PARENTHESES - the grammar deliberately parses the parenthesized list as a SUPERSET, `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? refModPart*` (read at source, both symbols exist), and the omission is caught at bind with a COBOL diagnostic rather than a parse error, which is a conforming rejection either way. (2) THE ELLIPSIS IS GENUINELY UNBOUNDED - the original record asserted 'Variadic, 1, inf' from the row; re-derived at source, the row is `Add(new("MAX", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "p", "MaxScaled", ...))` and `const int inf = int.MaxValue;` (IntrinsicCatalog.cs), so no hidden ceiling truncates the ellipsis. (3) THE ARGUMENT SEPARATOR - `functionArgList : functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*` admits the §8.3.5 comma separator and bare juxtaposition alike. No optional phrase words exist in this format, so there is no unverified half. NOTE ON SCOPE: the FUNCTION-keyword-omitted form is §8.4.3.2's grant, not this format's - §15.59.2 underlines FUNCTION as required - so it is out of scope here and is not what this CONFORMS rests on. EDITION WINDOW as in AR-15.59.3-1, from Annex E only. EVIDENCE: PROBED, --std 2023. ACCEPTS: E:/Temp/pbmax/maxfmt2.cob `FUNCTION MAX(N1)` -> ONE=000C (3) and `FUNCTION MAX(N1, N2, N3, N4, N5)` -> FIVE=000I (9), exit=0. E:/Temp/pbmax/maxfmt3.cob with a space before the paren as the format renders it: `FUNCTION MAX (N1 N2)` -> SP=000I; subscripted arguments `FUNCTION MAX (T(1) T(2) T(3))` -> SUB=000H; arithmetic-expression argument `FUNCTION MAX (N1 + 100, N2)` -> EXPR=010C. Refuter additions, E:/Temp/rfmax/refm.cob (RFMAXREFM): reference-modified argument `FUNCTION MAX(S9(1:3) T3)` accepted, RM1=[ZZZ|********]; nested function-identifier argument `FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION MAX(S9(1:3) T3))` accepted, RMLEN=0003. REJECTS: E:/Temp/pbmax/maxfmt.cob `FUNCTION MAX()` -> `error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION MAX takes at least 1 argument(s); 0 given (ISO §15.3)`, exit=70; E:/Temp/pbmax/maxbare.cob `FUNCTION MAX.` (no parentheses) -> the same COBOLNET1504, exit=70. Corroboration only, not closing: tests/conformance/negative/func-omitted-arg.cob pins `FUNCTION MAX(OMITTED, 4)` -> COBOLNET1544 for §8.4.3.2 SR7. subject: MIN function
notes: REFUTER RE-EXAMINED AND SUSTAINED — the one row that survived attack, and the format DIAGRAM was rendered from the PDF rather than trusted from the transcription (CLAUDE.md rule 1: a general format is a load-bearing diagram). Printed folio 888 / PDF page 918 renders as `FUNCTION MIN ( { argument-1 } … )` with FUNCTION and MIN both UNDERLINED and nothing bracketed — exactly what specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.63.2 carries, so the transcription is faithful and no falsely-restrictive OCR residue is in play here. The grammar rule `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? refModPart*` is a deliberate SUPERSET — the parenthesised group is optional there and the per-function arity is the binder's job. For MIN the catalog row is Variadic with a minimum of 1 (`Add(new("MIN", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "p", "MinScaled", ...))`) and the binder enforces it, so the composite behaviour matches the printed format: FUNCTION required, MIN required, the parenthesised list required, at least one argument required, repetition unbounded. The repeat-brace `…` also picks up §15.3's ALL-subscript expansion, which works. ⚠ RESIDUE (unchanged, and it is a corpus gap not a conformance defect): no spec-derived test pins the two REJECTION shapes (bare `FUNCTION MIN`, empty `FUNCTION MIN()`) — test-ref is deliberately left EMPTY rather than closed on the differential. ⚠ SCOPE NOTE the refuter adds: §15.63.1's TYPE TABLE (Index ⇒ Index, All arguments integer ⇒ Integer) is visible on the same rendered page and is NOT covered by any rule in this batch — the catalog hardcodes IntrinsicType.Numeric and the binder only ever re-derives Alphanumeric/National. Whether the Integer and Index rows of that table are honoured is an UNADJUDICATED row, and it should be added to the inventory rather than assumed closed by this FMT verdict. EVIDENCE: PDF page rendered: `python scripts/spec/clause_page.py 15.63.1 15.63.2 15.63.3` → PDF page 918 / printed folio 888; `python scripts/render-spec-page.py 918` → E:/Temp/spec_p918.png, read and compared against the transcription. Editions re-derived from E.3.3 item 29, not from the catalog row (rule 4).

subject: SQRT function
notes: CONFORMS. The general format, read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:33307-33309, is `FUNCTION SQRT ( argument-1 )` with FUNCTION and SQRT both UNDERLINED — required words — and exactly one argument inside required parentheses; there is no optional phrase, no ellipsis, and no second format. READ, GRAMMAR: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4 line 333 — `: FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*` — so the FUNCTION keyword and the name are both required at this production, and the argument list's '(' is lexed in the dedicated FNARG mode so §8.4.3.2 SR6 ('that ( is ALWAYS the argument list') holds rather than the '(' being read as a subscript or a grouping paren. The optionality of the paren group in the grammar is deliberate (it serves the zero-argument functions) and does NOT leak into SQRT: the arity is the CATALOG's. READ, ARITY: IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build line 133 — Add(new("SQRT", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "n", "Sqrt", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, true, 85)) — MinArgs = MaxArgs = 1, enforced at IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsicCore lines 572-579: `if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs)` -> COBOLNET1504 'FUNCTION SQRT takes 1 argument(s); N given (ISO §15.3)'. So a bare `FUNCTION SQRT` (given 0) and `FUNCTION SQRT(A B)` (given 2) are both rejected with the §15.3 citation. The FUNCTION-omitted spelling (§8.4.3.2.3 SR2, a REPOSITORY INTRINSIC declaration) is gated the same way — IntrinsicBinder.cs lines 301 and 339 both refuse to route a name written without an argument list unless sig.MinArgs == 0, which SQRT's is not. The row's IntrinsicType.Numeric matches §15.84.1's 'The type of this function is numeric'. GOLDEN: conformance:2023/pb52_intrinsic_argument_stage writes the format both ways argument-1 can be spelled (a data item, `FUNCTION SQRT(NI)`, and a literal, `FUNCTION SQRT(4)`), each pinned to 2.00 in the .out. NOT COVERED: there is no SQRT-specific arity negative fixture; the COBOLNET1504 guard is catalog-driven and generic, so a SQRT-specific one could only re-test the shared guard. EDITIONS: the format is unchanged across the four editions (SQRT is a 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment function); batch default.

subject: STANDARD-COMPARE function
notes: kb/Work PB101 T7 (2026-08-18): FUNCTION STANDARD-COMPARE ( argument-1 argument-2 [ ordering-name-1 ] [ argument-4 ] ) — the bespoke binder takes the two operands, then a bare ordering-name and/or an integer level in either order the format admits; ArgKinds ssoi ('o' = §15.3 argument type 12). Below 2002 the function is COBOLNET1502 (standard-compare-2002).

subject: STANDARD-DEVIATION function
notes: Format read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.86.2: `FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION ( { argument-1 } … )` — FUNCTION and STANDARD-DEVIATION underlined (required keywords), the parenthesised list NOT bracketed (required), and the brace-ellipsis making argument-1 one-or-more. Both halves of the format located and read. HALF 1, the keyword/name/paren shape: the grammar carries no STANDARD-DEVIATION production (grep of src/Cobol.Net.Frontend for the name returns nothing) because the form is generic — CobolExpressions.g4#functionCall is `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*`, and CobolExpressions.g4#functionName admits IDENTIFIER. Checked the lexer for the hyphen hazard, since CobolLexer.g4 does carry STANDARD (:536), STANDARD_BINARY/STANDARD_DECIMAL (:264-265) and STANDARD_1/STANDARD_2 (:669-670) but no STANDARD_DEVIATION token: ANTLR maximal munch gives IDENTIFIER the full 18-character 'STANDARD-DEVIATION' over STANDARD's 8, which is the documented behavior at CobolLexer.g4:261-262 ('a bare STANDARD still lexes as STANDARD, and WC-COBOL still lexes as one IDENTIFIER'). The argument-list paren is retyped FNARG_LPAREN per §8.4.3.2.3 SR6, so the list is never read as a grouping or subscript paren. HALF 2, the one-or-more arity: IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build:139 declares Add(new("STANDARD-DEVIATION", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "n", "StandardDeviation", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, true, 85)) — MinArgs 1, MaxArgs int.MaxValue, matching `{ argument-1 } …` exactly; IntrinsicBinder.cs:572-579 computes `given` and raises COBOLNET1504 'takes at least 1 argument(s)' when given < MinArgs, which catches both the bare `FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION` and the empty-parens `()` form the grammar's optional group admits. IntrinsicType.Numeric matches §15.86.1 ('The type of this function is numeric'). Closing test: tests/conformance/2023/pb56_dec_carrier_intrinsics.cob line 45 writes the format `FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION(2, 2, 2)`, it is registered in tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json:123, and tests/conformance/2023/pb56_dec_carrier_intrinsics.out line 8 pins SD=0.0 — so the format demonstrably lexes, parses and binds. The fixture is spec-derived (its header derives every line from §15.4.1 r1 and the functions' own EAEs), not a characterization or legacy-match. Editions: Annex E (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:42847 onward) carries no STANDARD-DEVIATION entry and the clause has no edition-varying content, so the batch default stands; the editions field was NOT read off IntrinsicCatalog's own IntroducedIn column.

subject: SUBSTITUTE function
notes: kb/Work PB81 (2026-08-18): FUNCTION SUBSTITUTE ( argument-1 { [ANYCASE] [FIRST | LAST] argument-2 argument-3 } … ) — the pair repeats, so §15.3's table(ALL) is admissible among the pairs and its elements form the pairs by position at run time (the FLAT form: CobolIntrinsics.SubstituteFlat pairs the enumerated elements; a keyword before an enumeration attaches to the pair its first element opens). Written pairs pair at bind as before (SubstituteModes per pair). The ALL argument was the staged COBOLNET0899 (`substitute-all-subscript-argument`, retired).

subject: SUM function
notes:
Format read directly from specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.88.2 (line 33495-33499): `FUNCTION SUM ( { argument-1 } … )` — FUNCTION and SUM underlined (required), the argument-list parentheses present, and the braced argument-1 followed by an ellipsis, i.e. ONE OR MORE. Both halves READ and verified. (1) THE REFERENCE SHAPE: CobolExpressions.g4#functionCall `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*`, with SUM present in CobolExpressions.g4#functionName (line 458) — needed because SUM is one of the §8.9 reserved words that is also a §8.11 intrinsic name. The keyword-omitted twin `SUM(…)` rides CobolExpressions.g4#reservedIntrinsicArgFn (`SIGN | SUM`), and IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsic lines 54-63 enforces §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 on it (COBOLNET1543 unless REPOSITORY declares SUM / FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC) — so the abbreviated form is not accepted unconditionally. Arguments juxtapose or take the §8.3.5 separator via functionArgList. §8.4.3.2.3 SR6 is decided from the DEFINITION before binding (DefinitionPermitsArguments("SUM") is true since MaxArgs > 0), so `FUNCTION SUM (1:4)` draws Sr6ArgumentListError, not a bogus arity error; §8.4.3.3.3 SR2 rejects reference-modifying SUM's numeric result (ResultRefMod, COBOLNET1629). (2) THE 1..n MULTIPLICITY: IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build line 152 `Add(new("SUM", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "n", "SumScaled", …))` — MinArgs 1, MaxArgs int.MaxValue; IntrinsicBinder.cs line 573 raises COBOLNET1504 ("takes at least 1 argument(s); 0 given (ISO §15.3)") for `FUNCTION SUM` written with no list or an empty one, and the unbounded max means no upper rejection. The ellipsis also licenses the §15.3 table(ALL) argument: IntrinsicSig.RepeatsAnArgument (MaxArgs == int.MaxValue) gates TryBindAllArgument, and its own diagnostic text names SUM as an example of a `{ argument } …` format. TESTS: tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit/IntrinsicRepeatedArgumentDriftTests.cs re-reads §15.88.2's `<pre>` block out of specs/ISO_COBOL.md and asserts the catalog's unboundedness EQUALS the presence of the '…' character — spec-derived in the strict sense (the assertion's oracle is the standard's own text, not a hand list). tests/conformance/2023/pb62_all_subscript_runtime_ranges.cob exercises the repeated-argument format over ALL (fixed, ODO, dynamic-capacity, two-level, and a mixed `SUM(F(ALL) WS-E(ALL))`); pb58_argument_predicates_legal.cob exercises the plain 3-argument written form. NOT covered by a dedicated fixture: a zero-argument `FUNCTION SUM` negative case — the COBOLNET1504 arm was read in source but has no SUM-specific golden; that is a test gap, not a behavior gap (the arm is shared and exercised by other MinArgs rows).

REFUTER (verdict SUSTAINED after independent attack): the format was re-read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:33494-33499 and §8.4.3.2.3 re-read whole at :6020ff. SR2 ("If intrinsic-function-name-1 or the ALL phrase is specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph … the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier; otherwise the word FUNCTION is required") and SR6 ("If a function's definition permits arguments and a left parenthesis immediately follows … the left parenthesis is always treated as the left parenthesis of that function's arguments") both check out against IntrinsicBinder.cs:57 (COBOLNET1543) and :88 (Sr6ArgumentListError, via DefinitionPermitsArguments reading MaxArgs > 0 from the catalog row). The keyword-omitted alternative `reservedIntrinsicArgFn subscriptPart refModPart*` (CobolExpressions.g4:334-346) REQUIRES the subscript group, so a bare `SUM` can never be read as a function reference — which is correct precisely because §15.88.2 has no zero-argument form, and is what keeps the report-writer `SUM OF` clause and the `SIGN` data-description clause from being swallowed. The drift test was read in full and is genuinely spec-derived: it re-scans every `#### 15.x.2 General format` block out of specs/ISO_COBOL.md, keys on the '…' character, asserts a ≥79-row floor on BOTH the spec scan and the catalog scan so the scanner cannot silently find nothing, and asserts the equivalence in both directions — it closes the UNBOUNDED half of `{ argument-1 } …`. The at-least-one half rests on reading only (IntrinsicBinder.cs:573, MinArgs 1) with no SUM-specific fixture, which rule 3 expressly permits for CONFORMS. ONE RESIDUE FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT COUNTED AGAINST THIS ROW: with a runtime-ranged table(ALL) the compile-time count is `all.StaticCount ?? 1` (IntrinsicBinder.cs:572), so an OCCURS DEPENDING object of 0 satisfies MinArgs at compile time and the enumerated list reaches the runtime EMPTY — CobolIntrinsics.Dec.cs#SumDec would then throw IndexOutOfRangeException on `xs[0]` and CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#SumScaled would return 0. §15.3 makes exactly that case undefined ("The evaluation of an ALL subscript shall result in at least one argument, otherwise the result of the reference to the function-identifier is undefined"), so it is not a violation of this format rule; it is worth a robustness note elsewhere, not a downgrade here. Verdict held at CONFORMS.

subject: TAN function
notes: 15.89.2 'FUNCTION TAN ( argument-1 )' written over every 15.3 type-10 argument shape (tan(0)=0 exactly by 15.89.4 r1) with the eighth-turn +1/-1 pins as the discriminator against a return-zero stub; the complement, a second argument, rejects with COBOLNET1504 at all four editions. There is no no-argument form here, unlike 15.75.2 RANDOM.

subject: TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD function
notes: cite.py --check 15.90.2 "TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD" => OK (General format, FUNCTION and TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD both underlined = required, one parenthesized argument-1, no brackets anywhere). READ: CobolExpressions.g4#functionReference `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*` with `functionName : IDENTIFIER | DISPLAY | LENGTH | MERGE | NATIONAL | BIT | RANDOM | SIGN | SORT | SUM` — TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD is not a reserved word so it lexes IDENTIFIER and the format parses; the lexer's FUNCTION suppression keeps the '(' in the argument region (SR6) so 20240229 is an argument, not a subscript. READ: IntrinsicCatalog.cs line 274 `Add(new("TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "i", "TestDateYyyymmdd", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 2002))` — Fixed 1..1 makes the parenthesized single argument MANDATORY: the grammar's optional arg-list and the empty-parens form both reach IntrinsicBinder.cs:573 with given=0 and raise COBOLNET1504 "takes 1 argument(s); 0 given (ISO §15.3)", so the no-argument shape the format does not offer is rejected. IntrinsicType.Integer matches §15.90.1 "The type of this function is integer" and Table 21 line 29995 (Int1 -> Int). EDITIONS derived from the spec, NOT from the catalog row: Annex E item 13 (line 42993) enumerates the intrinsic functions NEW in 2023 (BASECONVERT, CONCAT, CONVERT, FIND-STRING, MODULE-NAME, SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC, SUBSTITUTE) and TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD is absent, so it predates 2023; it is not in the COBOL-85 + Amendment-1 intrinsic set, and D.31.3.8 presents it in the 2002 date-function family — hence 2002,2014,2023. The edition gate is live and pinned: conformance:negative/test_validators_below_2002 carries `reject-at: 85` and expects COBOLNET1502 (IntrinsicBinder.cs:494 "was introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:{sig.IntroducedIn}"). Positive golden intrinsics_test_validators writes the format seven times and is registered in tests/conformance/2002/manifest.json and ConformanceTests.cs:179. || REFUTED: VERDICT SURVIVES — CONFORMS confirmed, but the record's EDITIONS EVIDENCE is corrected and one over-claim in the note is withdrawn. (1) Citation re-derived independently: cite.py --check 15.90.2 "TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD" => OK, §15.90.2 (General format), text `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD</u> ( argument-1 )` — both words underlined, no bracketed element, exactly one argument. (2) The grammar claim was NOT taken on trust: CobolExpressions.g4:333 is verbatim `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*`, and the FNARG re-typing is real — CobolLexer.g4:14 `tokens { FNARG_LPAREN, FNARG_RPAREN }` and CobolLexer.g4:119 `if (PreviousIsFunctionName()) Type = FNARG_LPAREN;` — so §8.4.3.2.3 SR6 is mechanically enforced, not asserted. (3) The arity gate was read at source, not quoted: IntrinsicBinder.cs `long given = args.Sum(...)` then `if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs) ctx.Edition.Error("COBOLNET1504", ...)`, sitting AFTER BindIntrinsicArgs and BEFORE every per-function arm; and `grep TEST-DATE IntrinsicBinder.cs` returns NOTHING, so there is no bespoke arm that could divert this row past the gate. Both halves of the format (accept the one shape it offers / reject the shapes it does not) are therefore verified. (4) ⛔ EDITIONS — RULE 4 HAZARD, PARTIALLY REALIZED. Annex E item 13 is real and I re-read it (lines 42993–43001: BASECONVERT, CONCAT, CONVERT, FIND-STRING, MODULE-NAME, SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC, SUBSTITUTE), so the UPPER bound ("predates 2023") IS spec-derived. The LOWER bound is NOT. The note's two supports for 2002 do not carry it: "not in the COBOL-85 + Amendment-1 intrinsic set" is asserted with no citation and no --check, and D.31.3.8 (line 42650, re-read in full) is informative prose about the verdict codes that makes NO edition statement whatsoever — it neither says nor implies 2002. The 2023 transcription's Annex E records the delta from 2014 ONLY, so the 2002-vs-2014-vs-85 boundary is not derivable from `specs/ISO_COBOL.md` at all. The value 2002 is left standing because it is very likely correct and the rule-4 fallback ("85,2002,2014,2023") would be affirmatively WORSE — it would assert availability in an edition the function demonstrably post-dates — but it is recorded here as NOT spec-derived, and it coincides exactly with the `2002` field of the IntrinsicCatalog row under review, which is the shape rule 4 exists to catch. If the edition gate is ever challenged, the evidence must come from the 2002 or 2014 edition's own annex, not from this transcription.

subject: TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD function
notes: CITATION RE-DERIVED: cite.py --check 15.91.2 "FUNCTION</u> <u>TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD" -> OK, General format; the printed format is exactly 'FUNCTION TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD ( argument-1 )' - one REQUIRED argument, parenthesised, no optional phrase, no ellipsis, no keyword. READ: (1) src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4 functionCall ('FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*') accepts the written form generically - the name needs no grammar token, which is why grep finds none in the Frontend; (2) IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build carries Add(new("TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "i", "TestDayYyyyddd", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 2002)) so MinArgs==MaxArgs==1 and IntrinsicBinder.cs (the 'given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs' guard) raises COBOLNET1504 on 0 or 2 arguments - the format's arity is enforced, not merely declared; (3) the result is IntrinsicType.Integer so a refModPart on the call is rejected by IntrinsicBinder's RefModFunctionResultClass arm ('is not an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function', ISO 8.4.3.3.3 SR2) - the grammar's optional refModPart* cannot over-accept here. POSITIVE FORM EXERCISED: tests/conformance/2002/intrinsics_test_validators.cob writes FUNCTION TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD(...) six times (J1-J6) and is registered in tests/conformance/2002/manifest.json. EDITIONS derived from the SPEC, not from the catalog's own IntroducedIn: cite.py --check D.31.3.1 "Two additional functions were added by ISO/IEC 1989:2002 as complements to these basic functions." -> OK, and D.31.3 lists exactly nine subclauses of which the last two are D.31.3.8 TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD and D.31.3.9 TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD (the other six being the COBOL-85 basic date functions), so the two additions are these; tests/conformance/negative/test_validators_below_2002.cob (reject-at: 85, registered in negative/manifest.json) pins the COBOLNET1502 window rejection below 2002. REFUTED: VERDICT UPHELD - CONFORMS survives independent re-reading, but the test-ref is TRIMMED and the evidence chain is re-grounded. (a) Citation re-derived from scratch: cite.py --check 15.91.2 "TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD" -> OK, and specs/ISO_COBOL.md 33617-33622 shows the format is one line, one bracket-free argument. (b) The grammar text was read directly rather than taken from the adjudicator: CobolExpressions.g4:332-336 is verbatim as quoted, and functionName (448-459) is IDENTIFIER plus nine reserved-word alternatives, so the hyphenated word lexes on the IDENTIFIER arm (longest-match beats any TEST prefix token). (c) The ADJACENCY question the adjudicator never asked was measured in the lexer, because the spec prints the format WITH spaces ('( argument-1 )') and a whitespace-sensitive argument-paren would REJECT legal source: CobolLexer.g4:61 PreviousIsFunctionName() tests _prevNonWsTokenType == FUNCTION, and NextToken() (143-152) advances _prev/_last only on non-WS tokens with WS itself '-> skip', so at the '(' of 'FUNCTION TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD ( 2024366 )' _last is the name and _prev is FUNCTION regardless of intervening spaces - OnDefaultLParen (101-120) therefore types it FNARG_LPAREN. No whitespace defect. (d) THE REJECT HALF was verified arm by arm, not inferred: arity at IntrinsicBinder.cs:573-579 (COBOLNET1504, reached because TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD matches no bespoke arm between the 493 edition gate and the 565 generic path, and ArgKinds "i" does not end in 'l'); the ALL subscript at TryBindAllArgument (2553-2587) rejects with AllSubscriptNotRepeatable because sig.RepeatsAnArgument is MaxArgs == int.MaxValue and this row's MaxArgs is 1; the result ref-mod at FinishIntrinsic (132-149) -> ResultRefMod (169-195), whose category comes from IntrinsicSig.CategoryOf (93-99) mapping IntrinsicType.Integer to PicCategory.Numeric - not one of Alphanumeric/National/Boolean, so SR2 fires. IntrinsicSig's positional record header (IntrinsicCatalog.cs:52-57) was read to confirm the row's 1,1 really are MinArgs,MaxArgs. Both halves of the format are verified by reading, so rule 5's PARTIAL cost is not owed. (e) TEST-REF CORRECTED: conformance:negative/test_validators_below_2002 was REMOVED from this row. It exercises the D8 catalog edition window (COBOLNET1502 at --std 85), which is IntrinsicBinder.cs:493's gate, not anything in the 15.91.2 general format; keeping it here would credit the format rule with coverage it does not have. The fixture is still the evidence for the `editions` field and is cited above by name. NOTE for the row's residual exposure: no fixture anywhere pins the format's REJECT half for THIS function (0 args, 2 args, ALL, ref-mod) - the pb58 negative set's nearest neighbour is pb58-testdate-frac.cob, which is TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD (15.90) and screens the argument rule, not the format.

subject: TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes:
THE FORMAT READ OFF THE PRINTED CLAUSE (specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.92.2, lines 33665-33668): `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME ( argument-1 argument-2)`. FUNCTION and the function-name are UNDERLINED, so both are required key words; the two argument operands are unbracketed and carry no ellipsis, so exactly two arguments, both required, and no repetition (feedback_underlining_not_bracketing — I measured the <u> markup, I did not infer from brackets).

GENERIC HALF — the keyword/name/parenthesised-list shape. Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4: `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart* | ...` and `functionArgList : functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*`. The separator rule is what matters for THIS format: it admits BOTH the bare juxtaposition §15.92.2 itself prints and the §8.3.5 comma separator, and the corpus exercises both spellings (below). TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME is not a §8.9 reserved word, so it arrives through the ordinary functionName/cobolWord slot; hyphens are COBOL-word characters, so the name lexes whole.

PER-FUNCTION HALF — the name, the arity and the edition window — is the catalog row at IntrinsicCatalog#Build (IntrinsicCatalog.cs:310): Add(new("TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 2, 2, "ss", "TestFormattedDatetime", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 2014)). ⚠ I READ THE IntrinsicSig RECORD DECLARATION (IntrinsicCatalog.cs:52-57) to confirm the POSITIONAL meaning of `2, 2` (MinArgs, MaxArgs) and of `2014` (IntroducedIn) instead of counting commas. The grammar's paren group is OPTIONAL, i.e. a superset parse; what actually makes both arguments REQUIRED and forbids a third is BindIntrinsicCore's arity gate — `if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs) ctx.Edition.Error("COBOLNET1504", ...)` — so a bare `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME` (0 given) and a 3-argument call are both rejected against MinArgs=MaxArgs=2.

RESULT TYPE, since the format's clause head fixes it: §15.92.1 "The type of this function is integer" — the row's IntrinsicType.Integer, and IntrinsicRenderer.cs:334 `case "TestFormattedDatetime": return new NumX(RuntimeApi.DateFn(...), 0)` renders it at SCALE 0, i.e. as an integer.

TESTS: both separator spellings of the printed format are pinned by spec-derived programs. conformance:2023/pb23_week_date_beyond_integer_date_form writes `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYWwwD" "9999W526")` — the exact space juxtaposition §15.92.2 prints, which is the harder half and is easy to leave untested; conformance:2014/formatted_datetime and the AssertSpec theory write the §8.3.5 comma form. ⚠ NOT TESTED under this function's name: the arity REJECTIONS. The COBOLNET1504 gate is generic and catalog-driven (read at IntrinsicBinder.cs:572-579) and is exercised elsewhere (tests/conformance/2023/pb24_length_physical_keyword pins it for FUNCTION LENGTH), but no fixture gives TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME one or three arguments.

EDITIONS from the standard: Annex E (the 2014->2023 change record) carries no occurrence of the name, so the general format is unchanged at 2023; 2014 is the introduction edition the family is gated at, and the landed sibling row AR-15.92.3-2 records the same window. Not derived from the catalog row.

subject: TEST-NUMVAL function
notes:
Citation re-derived: cite.py --check 15.93.2 "FUNCTION" -> OK (§15.93.2 General format), the printed form being FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL ( argument-1 ) — one required argument, no optional phrase, no keyword, no repetition. READ: (1) the grammar, CobolExpressions.g4:332 functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart* — functionName is the generic word slot, so TEST-NUMVAL needs no bespoke production and the written form parses; (2) IntrinsicCatalog.Build line 276, Add(new("TEST-NUMVAL", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "s", "TestNumval", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 2002)) — MinArgs = MaxArgs = 1 matches the format's single non-optional argument, and IntrinsicType.Integer matches §15.93.1 (cite.py --check 15.93.1 "The type of this function is integer." -> OK); (3) the arity is ENFORCED, not merely declared — IntrinsicBinder.cs:573 raises COBOLNET1504 "FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL takes 1 argument(s); N given (ISO §15.3)" for any other count. TEST-NUMVAL is NOT an OptionalTrailing/Variadic row, so no phrase the format does not print can be written. TEST: conformance:2002/intrinsics_test_validators writes the call in exactly the form §15.93.2 prints, ten times, and asserts the §15.93.4 returned values (N1..N10 in the .out). NOT VERIFIED and named honestly: no negative fixture pins the COBOLNET1504 two-argument rejection for THIS function specifically (siblings do), and the format rule itself states nothing about arity beyond the one printed operand, which the catalog row expresses. EDITIONS: batch default, same derivation limit recorded on AR-15.93.3-1 (the compiler's 2002 window and the test-numval-2002 construct row are code, not the spec).

REFUTED: (verdict SUSTAINED; the ZERO-argument path — rule 5's second famous miss, "every zero-argument intrinsic failing at run time" — probed independently and found closed at COMPILE time, which the adjudicator did not check): I traced all three routes by which a TEST-NUMVAL reference with no argument list can arrive. (a) `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL` bare: fc.functionArgList() is null, ArgsOf yields [], given = 0 < MinArgs = 1, so IntrinsicBinder.cs:573-579 issues COBOLNET1504 and returns BoundExprError — a diagnostic, never a LoudValue that survives to run time.
