subject: TEST-NUMVAL-C function
notes:
PB250 LANDED — the format was already correct (the printed page was re-rendered, scripts/render-spec-page.py 958 = printed folio 928, and all eight legal shapes trace through BindNumvalCFamily's positional walk); the PARTIAL was owed to (a) the >>COBOL-WORDS interaction with this format's two keywords and (b) four missing test shapes. Both are closed.

(a) THE DEFECT AND ITS ROOT CAUSE. ANYCASE and LOCALE are ISO 8.9 RESERVED words (cite.py --check 8.9 OK on both; neither is in the 8.10 table) and 7.3.10.3 SR3 therefore admits both as the EXISTING word of a >>COBOL-WORDS directive. The directive was applied by ONE mechanism only — the post-lex token retype (CobolWordsRewriter), which can reach a word solely when the lexer makes it a keyword TOKEN — and both of these words are deliberately left as bare IDENTIFIERs so the 15.94.2 / 15.68.2 phrase parses as ordinary space-separated arguments. So the directive was ACCEPTED and SILENTLY INERT in both directions: `EQUATE "LOCALE" WITH "LOCALITY"` then `TEST-NUMVAL-C(X LOCALITY FR)` rejected legal source with a COBOLNET1504 arity error naming the renamed keyword (measured), and `UNDEFINE "ANYCASE"` still ate the user's own data item as the keyword, switching on case-insensitive currency matching and injecting the compilation-unit currency with no diagnostic (measured: a wrong TEST-NUMVAL-C answer of 1 where 0 is required by 15.94.4 1)a)).

THE FIX IS THE SECOND MECHANISM, ONCE, FOR THE WHOLE CLASS. CobolWordsMap.Resolve is now the ONE reading of 7.3.10.4 GR2/GR3/GR4 (canonical for an EQUATE/SUBSTITUTE synonym, null for an UNDEFINE'd or SUBSTITUTE'd-away word, the word itself otherwise), and every by-name classifier calls it: IntrinsicBinder.KeywordWordOf — the single funnel through which EVERY section-15 phrase word is read, so TRIM, FIND-STRING, SUBSTITUTE, CONVERT, MODULE-NAME, LENGTH and NUMVAL-C/TEST-NUMVAL-C are all covered by one change — plus the parser's text predicates, the SET-statement locale categories, the ALPHABET coded-set names and CALL ... AS NESTED. CobolWordsRewriter.CanonicalWordOf/TokenIs keep the directive applied to a word EXACTLY once (the retype already re-spells what it reaches). Measured population behind the sweep: of the 552 words in 8.9 union 8.10, 447 were in the token map, 17 are lexed but were invisible to it (a multi-spelling rule publishes no ANTLR literal name) and 88 are no token at all.

TWO SIBLING DEFECTS OF THE SAME MECHANISM, ALSO CLOSED. The token map now resolves multi-spelling keywords by asking the lexer itself, and the de-reserve retype matches the token TEXT so `UNDEFINE "ZERO"` frees ZERO without freeing ZEROS and ZEROES (7.3.10.3 SR3 names one COBOL word). And SR3/SR4's category test could only ask the lexer vocabulary, so it rejected every legal directive naming one of the 31 section-8.10 context-sensitive words this compiler does not tokenize (HEX, CURRENT, LC_ALL, ANUM, BYTE, ACTIVATING, STACK, TOP-LEVEL, UCS-4, UTF-8, UTF-16 and the rest) — a generated 8.10 table now answers it, single-sourced from the spec section and drift-tested against it.

(b) TESTS. The three positive shapes the row owed (argument-1 ANYCASE; argument-1 LOCALE ANYCASE; argument-1 LOCALE locale-name-1 ANYCASE) are 2002/pb250_test_numvalc_remaining_shapes, all three verified 0 per 15.94.4 1)a); the stack-exclusion negative under this function's OWN name is negative/pb250-test-numvalc-locale-and-argument2-are-alternatives (15.94.2 + 5.2.6.2, COBOLNET1504). The >>COBOL-WORDS goldens the row asked for are 2023/pb250_cobol_words_phrase_word_equate (GR2 synonym for ANYCASE) and 2023/pb250_cobol_words_phrase_word_undefine (GR3, the user's data item bound as argument-2), with negative/pb250-cobol-words-undefined-keyword-syntax-withdrawn pinning that the withdrawn syntax is no longer available. All eight shapes of the format now have a fixture or a traced derivation, and nothing in the format binds by a rule stated in more than one place.

THE STALE COMMENT the row recorded (IntrinsicBinder.cs, "The LOCALE phrase is the A.4.9 documented non-support") is corrected in the same change set, as is the neighbouring claim that ANYCASE and LOCALE are 8.10 context-sensitive words — they are 8.9 reserved, and the argument-1 exclusion is positional, not a context-sensitivity allowance. EDITIONS unchanged at 2002,2014,2023.

FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*` -- with functionArgList = `functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*`, so space- and comma/semicolon-separated repeats both parse; VARIANCE is not in reservedIntrinsicArgFn (only SIGN and SUM are) so it takes the generic FUNCTION-keyword arm. (2) The VARIANCE-specific half is the catalog row read at IntrinsicCatalog.cs line 140: Add(new("VARIANCE", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "n", "Variance", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, true, 85)) -- MinArgs 1, MaxArgs int.MaxValue. NOT tested for VARIANCE specifically: the table(ALL) form (pb62_all_subscript_runtime_ranges does not name VARIANCE) and the zero-argument rejection. || REFUTER (independently re-derived; verdict UPHELD as CONFORMS). Format re-read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 33974 -- FUNCTION and VARIANCE underlined, list unbracketed, `{ argument-1 } ...`. Grammar confirmed at CobolExpressions.g4 line 333 (functionCall) and lines 351-353 (functionArgList); reservedIntrinsicArgFn at line 343 is SIGN and SUM only, so VARIANCE takes the FUNCTION-keyword arm as claimed. subject: COBOL character repertoire (encoding of, mapping of, substitute graphics)
notes: Rule: A.1 item 25 'COBOL character repertoire (encoding of, mapping of, substitute graphics) ... required ... documented (8.1.3; 8.1.3 GR1 and 5)'. cite.py --check 8.1.3.2 "The implementor shall define a mapping of each basic letter, basic digit, basic special character, and extended letter" -> OK §8.1.3.2 1) (General rules). cite.py --check 8.1.3.2 "substitute graphics may be specified by the implementor to replace the characters not represented" -> OK §8.1.3.2 5). cite.py --check 8.3.3.2.3 "Character-1 may be any character in the coded character set that the implementor has chosen for source code representation" -> OK §8.3.3.2.3 2) (Syntax rules). Determination reasoning: ISO leaves the mapping and the source encoding to the implementor (GR1) but a literal may hold only characters of the chosen source set (8.3.3.2.3 SR2); U+FFFD substitution silently changes a literal's content, so it is not a choice to document (PB1535). Two candidate fixes were on the table in PB1397 step 3 — a strict decoder with an error, or byte pass-through. Rule-1 precedence settles it: GnuCOBOL (next after ISO) accepts such source and preserves each byte as one character (no iconv on source), so rejecting it would be less conforming to the precedence than preserving it; in a UTF-16 repertoire the unique byte-preserving decoding is ISO/IEC 8859-1 (code point = byte, so FUNCTION ORD equals GnuCOBOL's byte+1 for every such byte). Whole-file (not per-sequence) fallback keeps DOC-A.1-26's one-encoding-per-file model; the warning keeps a CP1252 source (0x80 -> U+0080, not €) from being reinterpreted invisibly. PARTIAL: the ISO 10646/UTF-16 mapping and the BOM-selected encodings hold (DOC-A.1-26 probe, item 32/74 goldens); the malformed-UTF-8 arm diverges (probe). Owning defect kb/Work PB1397 (open, keeps DOC-A.1-25 per its step-3 section). The fix: CompilationInputs.ReadAllText detects BOM itself, decodes with UTF8Encoding(throwOnInvalidBytes: true), on DecoderFallbackException re-decodes the file as Latin-1 and records a warning (needs an allocated COBOLNET code). Witness needed: a golden reading a no-BOM file with a raw 0xE9 in a literal, expecting DISPLAY é and ORD 234 plus the warning in .err. Row stays GAP until then. COBOL.NET provides 1,073,741,791 characters (0x3FFFFFDF) for every dynamic-length elementary item, alphanumeric or national: the CARRIER's own ceiling, since the item IS a native System.String whose maximum length is that value - the same "the carrier's headroom IS the implementor maximum" reading CobolDynTable<T>.MaxOccurrences already records for a dynamic-capacity table. A LIMIT phrase below it is the maximum size; one above it cannot raise the maximum and is REPORTED (COBOLNET2027, a warning - 13.18.19.3 bounds integer-1 only when a dynamic-length-structure-name is written too, SR4, so the entry is legal source). The second candidate never applies: the PREFIXED phrase rides a dynamic-length-structure-name, refused by COBOLNET1562. ONE producer computes it (CobolDynString.MaxSizeOf) and DataItem.DynMaxSize carries it, so the value cannot differ between the binder, the emitters and the runtime; DynamicLengthTests.ImplementorMaximum_IsTheNumberPublishedInConformanceSection7 reads the number back out of the section 7 row in both published spellings, so the determination and the constant cannot drift apart. Before this landing the item had no maximum at all and the section 7 register said only that a branch was unreachable - a determination about code nobody had checked, which is how a SET SIZE past 2**32 came to wrap to its low bits.

subject: Line sequential character set
notes: A.1 item 115 -- 'Line sequential character set. This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (14.9.30, READ statement, General rule 16, 9.1.13.2, Successful completion, I-O Status = 09; 14.9.35, REWRITE statement, General rule 17d; 14.9.51, WRITE statement General rule 23; and 9.1.13.10, Record with invalid content with unsuccessful completion, I-O Status = 71)'. The determination is made and documented (kb/Work PB329): the set is every character at code point U+0020 or above; the C0 controls U+0000-U+001F are outside it, the two line delimiters CR and LF and the tab HT among them; DEL and the Latin-1 supplement are inside, so an ordinary 8-bit text file reads without 09. The delimiters are FORCED out by 9.1.7.2's definition of a line sequential record's extent; the set cannot be only 'everything but the delimiters' because the reader consumes CR/LF as the framing and GR16's 09 would then be unreachable by construction; the remaining C0 controls are the stream/device repertoire, not text, and a line sequential file exists to be plain text. Surveyed, not assumed: GnuCOBOL's COB_LS_VALIDATE defaults to TRUE 'per COBOL 2022' and validates data read (status 09) and written (status 71) against the same below-SPACE boundary. ONE type carries the set for all four cross-referenced rules, so the READ and WRITE directions cannot disagree; the test is character-wise (national record areas two bytes at a time as UTF-16BE) rather than byte-wise. Pinned at all three editions the LINE SEQUENTIAL organization exists in. kb/Work PB688 (2026-09-05): ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL is a COBOL-2023 INTRODUCTION - the Foreword's list of the main changes this third edition makes over ISO/IEC 1989:2014 names "Line Sequential file organization", and 9.1.6 / 9.1.7.1 still name exactly three organizations with 9.1.7.2 splitting the sequential one into its record- and line-delimited types. The organization therefore does not exist below 2023 (the pass now rejects it with COBOLNET0900, registry row file-organization-line-sequential-2023), the 2002 and 2014 copies of the golden were deleted as programs no edition below 2023 can express, and this row's editions are 2023 alone.

subject: OPEN statement (validation of fixed file attributes)
notes: The A.1 item 129 determination is made and documented, and was RE-DECIDED on 2026-09-07 (kb/Work PB802, owner decision verbatim: 'Let's match GNUCobol's implementation in spirit. No sidecar of any type.'). THE DETERMINATION IS NOW ONE RULE: the validated set is exactly what each organization's PHYSICAL FORMAT ENCODES, using the latitude GR10 grants in its own words ('The implementor defines which of the fixed-file attributes are validated during the execution of the OPEN statement. The validation of fixed-file attributes may vary depending on the organization or storage medium of the file.'). Fixed-length record sequential and line sequential record nothing and validate nothing (9.1.7.2; 9.1.13.2 items 3, 5 and 7 answer the disagreements with the successful '04', '06' and '09'). A RECORD VARYING record-sequential file records its record type in 9.1.7.2's record-length header, so that header must PARSE - and only that: a prefix outside the RECORD clause's bounds is item 3's '04', not a '39'. RELATIVE and INDEXED record the organization, record type, the two logical record sizes and the key table in the framed store's header, IN the data file; an unreadable header is '39' and a zero-byte file is the one tolerated exception. THE KEY CHECK HAS A DOCUMENTED RUNTIME OPT-OUT, COBOLNET_KEYCHECK=OFF - GnuCOBOL's COB_KEYCHECK under this repository's naming (COBOLNET_, never COBOL_, which is the external-switch family's prefix), read once per run unit in FileRegistry and registered in RuntimeConfig; it narrows the set by exactly the key table and is part of the determination rather than an escape from it. The set is still NOT the empty set item 50 answers for DELETE FILE. The code set is still outside the set, on PB793's ground (13.18.13.4 GR7 vs GR2/GR6 really can differ now, so it is a determination and not an observation that the value is constant): a CODE-SET clause exists to read a file some OTHER system wrote, which carries no COBOL.NET header, and reading a converted file through a description with no CODE-SET clause is GR7's own default. The physical record sizes (no blocking; BLOCK CONTAINS inert under A.3 item 5) and the record delimiter (no compiler surface; the realized distinction is a sequential-organization attribute whose format records nothing) are outside it too. 9.1.6's last sentence is still answered NO - shareability is per file connector (14.9.27.4 GR21-GR23), arbitrated live (9.1.15 Table 19). subject: SET statement (value in NaN payload)
notes: DOCUMENTED (kb/Work PB452, 2026-09-09) IN THE SAME CHANGE SET AS THE GENERAL RULES IT RIDES. A.1 item 176 is a REQUIRED documentation obligation on 14.9.39.4 GR34 and GR35 - the NaN PAYLOAD a SET CONTENT OF ... TO FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER / FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER-SIGNALING stores - and it had no row while the general rules themselves had no implementation at all; a required implementor-definition with no documentation row is not 'implemented'. The determination: payload ZERO for the quiet form and ONE for the signaling form, giving binary32 0x7FC00000 / 0x7F800001 and binary64 0x7FF8000000000000 / 0x7FF0000000000001, with the sign bit set from GR34/GR35's own SIGN phrase and positive when the phrase is absent. Zero is the canonical NaN every IEEE implementation produces; one is the smallest payload that keeps the significand nonzero once ISO/IEC 60559:2020 6.2.1's quiet bit is cleared, which a signaling NaN requires. 14.9.39.3 SR32 confines the receiver to a STANDARD floating-point usage and the two COBOL.NET provides are binary32 and binary64 EXACTLY, so the basic interchange format the rules name IS the carrier. The values are emitted as BIT PATTERNS through BitConverter, never as a CLR constant: double.NaN carries a SET sign bit, so the positive default would otherwise be spelled -double.NaN and depend on constant folding, and the CLR has no signaling-NaN constant at all because every managed arithmetic path quiets one. IeeeSpecials is one table serving as both the documented encoding and the emitted one, and IeeeSpecialsTests asserts the two agree by DECODING them rather than string-matching. The COBOL-observable witness can see that a NaN is unequal to itself but not which kind it is: the class condition that would expose the distinction (8.8.4.4's FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER-QUIET / -SIGNALING) is kb/Work PB225 and unimplemented. kb/Work/PB961 (2026-09-22): RE-RECORDED ON THE STORED IMAGE. The prior CONFORMS rested on the emitted EXPRESSION (unit:IeeeSpecialsTests.TheEmittedExpression_EvaluatesToTheDocumentedBits), while the pipeline stored a binary32 signaling NaN as the QUIET 0x7FC00001 - the JIT carried the inline BitConverter constant as a double, and the binary32 image lane widened through double. The value now reaches the item through CobolFloat.FromBinary32Bits (opaque to the JIT) and CobolNum.FormatImageSingle/ParseImageSingle (no binary64), and a same-usage MOVE copies on the carrier (14.9.25.4 GR6 c)). Witness: conformance:2014/pb961_signaling_nan_binary32 reads 0x7F800001 = 2139095041 back through a BINARY-LONG UNSIGNED REDEFINES and asks GR3 k) of every copy; unit:IeeeSpecialsTests.TheStoredImage_CarriesTheDocumentedBits follows the emitted text to the stored image in both byte orders. IeeeSpecials.Text is deleted (Bits is the one table; RuntimeApi.FloatFromBits spells it). docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-176 corrected in the same change set (the "cannot quiet the value" sentence was true of the expression and false of the pipeline). retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/IeeeSpecials.cs#Text (IeeeSpecials.Text was deleted by kb/Work PB961 (the emitted expression is RuntimeApi.FloatFromBits over IeeeSpecials.Bits) and TheEmittedExpression_EvaluatesToTheDocumentedBits was replaced by TheStoredImage_CarriesTheDocumentedBits, which asserts the stored image rather than the expression) retired-witness: unit:IeeeSpecialsTests.TheEmittedExpression_EvaluatesToTheDocumentedBits (IeeeSpecials.Text was deleted by kb/Work PB961 (the emitted expression is RuntimeApi.FloatFromBits over IeeeSpecials.Bits) and TheEmittedExpression_EvaluatesToTheDocumentedBits was replaced by TheStoredImage_CarriesTheDocumentedBits, which asserts the stored image rather than the expression)

subject: SIGN clause (valid sign when SEPARATE CHARACTER phrase not present)
notes: DOCUMENTED (kb/Work PB803). The row states the valid sign set as a RULE over the program's convention rather than as a character list: at the sign position a plain digit 0-9 plus both tables of the selected convention, every other position a plain digit. It records the three things a user has to know and could not previously look up -- that a PLAIN DIGIT is valid and means positive (so a group MOVE of raw characters, and every positive value under the `ascii` convention, is well formed); that a punched character carries a DIGIT as well as a sign, so it fixes the value (`12{` is +120, and at the leading position `C23` is +323); and that the SEPARATE characters `+` and `-` are 13.18.52.4 GR6 b)'s and are NOT valid here. GR5 a) is documented alongside b) although it is not latitude, because it is what makes the width answer 3 and a reader looking up the sign set is exactly the reader who needs it. What a numeric operation makes of a character outside the set stays 14.6.13.2's obligation and is not filed here.

subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, ALPHABET clause, code-name-1 (alphanumeric coded character set and collating sequence; ordinal
notes: A.1 item 183 - the code-name-1 coded character set and collating sequence, the ordinal number of characters, and the correspondence with the native alphanumeric character set (12.3.7.4 GR7 i). CONDITIONALLY REQUIRED 'because it is conditioned upon the existence of a code-name', and the condition became TRUE with owner decision kb/Work PB793, so the item is LIVE and the determination is written out in full at docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 7. ASCII: ISO/IEC 646 IRV, 128 ordinals, ordinal n = native character U+(n-1), the identity correspondence, the native collating positions. EBCDIC: IBM CCSID 37, 256 ordinals, ordinal n = the native character that page assigns to code unit n-1, the correspondence being the page itself and the collating position of a native character being its code unit in it; the 65,280 native characters the page does not spell are not members of the set and take the collating position 12.3.7.4 GR7 k3 gives an unspecified character. Surveyed rather than assumed (survey_compilers_on_latitude): CCSID 37 is the canonical registered complete single-byte EBCDIC page and the z/OS default; GnuCOBOL's own default table corresponds to no registered CCSID and its named alternates are CCSID 500 variants, so its LATITUDE is followed and its tables are not (they are GPL and are not read here). The whole table is DERIVED from Encoding.GetEncoding(37) at bind time, so nothing is transcribed and there is no 256-entry literal to drift.

subject: USAGE BINARY-CHAR, BINARY-SHORT, BINARY-LONG, BINARY-DOUBLE (allow wider range than minimum specified)
notes: OWNER DECISION Q30, 2026-09-09 (kb/Work PB592), verbatim: "provided, the native range." It REPLACES the premise this row previously closed on. The row carried DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT through the `a1-optional-not-provided` derived selector (kb/Work PB280 Q1) because docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 7 said "Not provided. Each usage holds exactly the GR12 minimum range for its width" - and that determination was FALSE for all four SIGNED usages. 13.18.60.4 GR12's printed table is ASYMMETRIC and the asymmetry is the whole content of the rule: every SIGNED row prints a STRICT '<' on BOTH sides (-128 [-2**7] < n < 128 [2**7]) while every UNSIGNED row prints '<=' on the left (0 <= n < 256 [2**8]) - re-rendered from the canonical PDF for this landing (printed page 507), independently of the reading the note inherited. So the minimum SIGNED band EXCLUDES -2**(w-1), which this compiler stores; 15.58.4's NOTE concedes the same thing from inside the standard ("BINARY-CHAR SIGNED | -128 (assuming an 8-bit twos-complement representation)"). The optional element of A.1 item 206 - "allow wider range than minimum specified" - is therefore PROVIDED, by exactly one value per signed usage, and A.1's preamble ("Documentation required: If the element is provided by the implementor, the implementor's user documentation shall document the element ...", cite.py --check A.1 OK) read with 4.2.5 (the conformance clause that governs the A.1 list, cite.py --check OK) makes documenting it an obligation rather than an option. NOTE the ground named here is 4.2.5, NOT 4.2.7: 4.2.7's own first sentence scopes it to A.4 (kb/Work PB593). THE DETERMINATION, stated structurally here and ENUMERATED ONCE in the row's own register anchor (docs/CONFORMANCE.md#DOC-A.1-206, which the code-location above names): the full native two's-complement band of each usage's byte width - so each SIGNED usage expresses exactly ONE value beyond the GR12 minimum and the four UNSIGNED usages are exactly the minimum. The band is written down ONCE, as the byte width per usage (PicInfo.StorageWidth, 1/2/4/8) under the BinaryCapacity discipline (PicInfo.Truncation), and read by the runtime store bound (CobolNum.InBinaryRange / TryStoreU) and the compile-time HIGHEST/LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC fold (IntrinsicBinder.BindAlgebraicFold), which AlgebraicFoldContainerAgreementTests holds in agreement - which is why the two sites named above are the whole implementation and not a sample. WITNESS conformance:2002/pb592_binary_usage_range_bounds measures all three claims at the introducing edition: Part A round-trips both endpoints of all EIGHT GR12 minimum bands (0 included, since the unsigned bands are CLOSED at 0); Part B measures GR12's nesting sentence at BOTH extremes of each narrower signed usage through FUNCTION LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC (15.58.1) and FUNCTION HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC (15.43.1), the leg the wider signed band actually puts at risk; Part C measures both edges of all eight PROVIDED bands and one step beyond each, reading its disposition from 14.7.5 (case 3 and GR2 make an ON SIZE ERROR firing mean "not expressible in this usage") and reporting, for the four unsigned -1 legs, WHICH value landed - the magnitude, per 14.9.25.4 GR6 d)2.b. No compiler change was needed: every edge already behaved as the documented band, measured on this tree at --std 2002 and --std 2023.

ALIGNMENT: none - a function-pointer occupies no character positions and rides a managed slot (StorageForm.FunctionPointerRef, image width 0), so there is no boundary to align on, and 13.18.60.3 SR14 confines it to a level-1/77 elementary item or a STRONG type declaration where no sibling can be displaced. Name) - deliberately SEPARATE from ProgramPointer, because 8.4.3.10.4 gives each category its own NULL and 14.9.39.3 SR20/SR21 forbid mixing them, so one shared struct would make the two assignment-compatible in the GENERATED C#, the one place a binder screen cannot reach.
